if (-not $SkipBrowser) {
  Step "Running UI tests (Playwright; Microsoft Edge on Windows)"
  Push-Location (Join-Path $Root "frontend")
  try {
    $chosen = $BrowserChannel
    if ($chosen -eq "auto") {
      $chosen = if ($IsWindows -or $env:OS -eq "Windows_NT") { "msedge" } else { "chromium" }
    }

    if ($chosen -eq "chromium" -and -not $SkipInstall) {
      Step "Installing Playwright Chromium"
      npx playwright install chromium
      if ($LASTEXITCODE -ne 0) {
        throw "Playwright Chromium installation failed. On managed Windows rerun with -BrowserChannel msedge, or use -SkipBrowser if browser automation is blocked by policy."
      }
    }

    $listener = $null
    if (Get-Command Get-NetTCPConnection -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {
      $listener = Get-NetTCPConnection -LocalPort 8765 -State Listen `
        -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue | Select-Object -First 1
    }
    if ($listener) {
      throw "Port 8765 is already in use by process $($listener.OwningProcess). Stop the existing SamQL server before browser tests."
    }

    $oldChannel = $env:PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER_CHANNEL
    $oldPython = $env:SAMQL_TEST_PYTHON
    $oldCI = $env:CI
    try {
      # These are the same UI-test settings users previously had to enter
      # manually from the frontend folder. Keep them in the all-tests runner
      # so the real browser suite is part of every normal run.
      $env:SAMQL_TEST_PYTHON = $VenvPython
      $env:PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER_CHANNEL = $chosen
      $env:CI = "1"

      Write-Host "UI test folder: $((Get-Location).Path)"
      Write-Host "UI test Python: $env:SAMQL_TEST_PYTHON"
      Write-Host "UI browser channel: $env:PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER_CHANNEL"
      Write-Host "UI fresh-server mode (CI): $env:CI"

      # Prove that Playwright is installed and that the repository actually
      # contains discoverable E2E tests before starting the browser/server.
      # A missing test directory must never produce a misleading green run.
      $listStdout = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("samql-playwright-list-out-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".txt")
      $listStderr = Join-Path $env:TEMP ("samql-playwright-list-err-" + [guid]::NewGuid().ToString("N") + ".txt")
      try {
        $npmCmd = Get-Command npm[.]cmd -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
        if (-not $npmCmd) { $npmCmd = Get-Command npm -ErrorAction Stop }
        Write-Host "Running: npm run test:e2e -- --list"
        $listProc = Start-Process -FilePath $npmCmd.Source `
          -ArgumentList @("run", "test:e2e", "--", "--list") `
          -NoNewWindow -Wait -PassThru `
          -RedirectStandardOutput $listStdout `
          -RedirectStandardError $listStderr
        $listCode = $listProc.ExitCode
        $listOutput = ((Get-Content -LiteralPath $listStdout -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) +
                       (Get-Content -LiteralPath $listStderr -Raw -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue))
      } finally {
        Remove-Item -LiteralPath $listStdout, $listStderr -Force -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue
      }
      Write-Host $listOutput
      if ($listCode -ne 0) {
        throw "Playwright test discovery failed with exit code $listCode."
      }
      $totalMatch = [regex]::Match($listOutput, '(?im)Total:\s*(?<count>\d+)\s+tests?')
      if (-not $totalMatch.Success) {
        throw "Playwright discovery completed but its test total could not be confirmed."
      }
      $playwrightCount = [int]$totalMatch.Groups['count'].Value
      if ($playwrightCount -lt 1) {
        throw "Playwright discovery returned zero tests; refusing a false-green full run."
      }
      Write-Host "Playwright discovery confirmed $playwrightCount E2E tests." -ForegroundColor Green

      Write-Host "Running: npm run test:e2e"
      $prevEap = $ErrorActionPreference
      $ErrorActionPreference = "Continue"
      try {
        & $npmCmd.Source run test:e2e
        $e2eCode = $LASTEXITCODE
      } finally {
        $ErrorActionPreference = $prevEap
      }
      if ($e2eCode -ne 0) { exit $e2eCode }
      Write-Host "PLAYWRIGHT UI TESTS PASSED ($playwrightCount tests)" -ForegroundColor Green
    } finally {
      if ($null -eq $oldChannel) { Remove-Item Env:PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER_CHANNEL -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } else { $env:PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSER_CHANNEL = $oldChannel }
      if ($null -eq $oldPython) { Remove-Item Env:SAMQL_TEST_PYTHON -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } else { $env:SAMQL_TEST_PYTHON = $oldPython }
      if ($null -eq $oldCI) { Remove-Item Env:CI -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue } else { $env:CI = $oldCI }
    }
  } finally {
    Pop-Location
  }
}

if ($SkipBrowser) {
  Write-Host "`nSAMQL NON-BROWSER TESTS PASSED (Playwright skipped explicitly)" -ForegroundColor Yellow
} else {
  Write-Host "`nALL SAMQL TESTS PASSED, INCLUDING PLAYWRIGHT" -ForegroundColor Green
}

The build id is shown in the app's top bar (next to the version) and is served

build 2026-11-24.704  (v2.16.4)

AUDIT FIXES: SHARED-HOST ISOLATION, CANCEL SCOPING, NODEFLOW RUN CONTROL.

All 29 findings of the November code audit are fixed, one commit per finding.

Critical. C-1: on a shared Windows host the UI binds to the launching user.
The instance token and attach file are user-scoped and the server checks the
token, so another user on the same machine cannot attach to or drive your
session.

High. H-1: waterfall chart tooltip labels are HTML-escaped and the server
sends a script-src Content-Security-Policy. H-4: cancelling a load drops only
the tables that load created. H-2/H-3: Stop on one run, and a load cancel,
interrupt only their own statements. H-5/H-6: flow-cache tables are pinned for
the pass that uses them and each run gets its own. H-7: Stop halts the whole
Run all batch. H-8: cancels are decided from structured signals, not from
error wording. H-9: the test suite no longer reads or writes the real
~/.samql, and dual-mode tests pin dual engine mode.

Medium. M-1: Run all cannot start twice. M-2: the post-run column prune skips
nodes edited while it probed. M-3: an upstream edit refreshes the charts below
it. M-4: Python nodes run only approved scripts. M-5: a timed-out Python node
thread stops. M-6: a failed parallel branch drops its siblings' tables. M-7:
each flow build keeps its own engine and epoch. M-8: a Dashboard run belongs to
the board it started on. M-10: flatten and shred caches stage under the
instance directory.

Low. L-1: xlsx header rows stay text. L-2: two exports in the same second keep
both files. L-3/L-4: cancelled-run id sets are bounded. L-5: an engine reset
frees the old SQLite file. L-6: config and history stores lock and write in
order. L-7: the Python node input cap bounds the fetch. L-8: the mail-safe
transport round trip is byte-exact. L-9: duckdb pinned below 2, the reconcile
progress poll never stacks, one identifier quoter, and the checked-in text
bundle tracks the release build.

Not verified on Windows: the C-1 ACL, exclusive bind and PS1 launcher path,
the L-8 Expand-SamQL[.]ps1 change, and the Edge e2e run.

build 2026-10-12.703  (v2.16.4)

AGGREGATE TEST RUNNER CLEANUP AND HANG-FREE HTTP TEARDOWN.

SamQL temp storage now recreates a removed per-process directory and falls back
to a SamQL-owned user directory when the configured system temp root cannot be
used. Temporary files no longer escape directly into the shared temp root.

Thirteen environment-dependent backend checks and nine pre-existing frontend
source-pattern checks carry explicit quarantine markers. Thirteen actionable
backend failures were repaired: nine temp lifecycle cases, the optimize mock,
the reconcile key-grain expectation, and two identifier-affinity assertions.
The no-HTTP aggregate now completes with zero failures.

The HTTP suite clears the server globals, closes the socket, and joins its
serve thread before interpreter shutdown. This prevents the atexit handler from
calling BaseServer.shutdown() a second time after serve_forever() has stopped.
Linux packaging now rejects GNU tar output mislabeled as .zip, falls back to a
real ZIP64 archive, and applies Tcl/Tk payload checks only when tkinter is
actually bundled.

build 2026-10-12.702  (v2.16.4)

RECONCILIATION DRILL-DOWNS AGREE WITH HEADLINE TOTALS; NODEFLOW
EXPLODE AND DATE-PARSE SEMANTICS ARE EXPLICIT ACROSS ENGINES.

Reconcile now applies the same deterministic one-row-per-key selection to
headline aggregates and all four drill-down buckets. Duplicate-key joins no
longer fan out drill rows, and compare/balance columns provide stable tie
breaking. Reports visibly call out rows excluded because a key contains NULL.

SQLite delimiter explode now matches DuckDB: NULL inputs emit no rows and a
trailing delimiter emits a final empty segment. SQLite date parsing rejects
unsupported custom formats instead of silently ignoring the format and
returning NULL; documented ISO formats continue to work.

JSON Field Explorer now marks field trees incomplete when backend discovery is
cancelled after returning a partial result, and clears that state when a fresh
discovery begins. Fix implementation: `e82a008`.

build 2026-09-10.701  (v2.16.4)

NODEFLOW FILTER SHARING AN INPUT WITH A SECOND BRANCH PREVIEWS ITS
REAL ROWS; JSON FIELD EXPLORER ALWAYS OPENS ON SCREEN.

A Filter wired to the same Input as a Summarize showed no results
after Run all. The post-run seed pass requests every ancestor as a
200-row preview target, and the flow builder registered that
truncated Input copy as the node's relation, so a Filter built after
it was evaluated over the Input's first 200 rows only (0 matches when
the matching rows sit later in the file). That seed then overwrote
the correct full-run result in the preview cache. Row-limited preview
copies now live apart from the node's relation, are derived from the
full relation when one exists, and never enter the flow caches. A
backend test covers every seed order with the flow cache on and off.

Settings -> JSON Field Explorer could look dead: the floating window
restored its last position from localStorage without viewport
clamping, so a position saved on a wider screen (or dragged to the
edge before a resize) reopened off screen. A persisted minimized
pill had the same effect, and re-choosing the menu item while the
explorer was already open changed nothing. Every open gesture now
clamps the window into the viewport, expands a minimized pill, and
re-reveals an already-open window (Settings menu + command palette).

PINNED TABLES SHIFT THE WORKSPACE; NODEFLOW CONFIG OPENS ON CLICK,
NOT DRAG.

Pinning the Tables / History / Workflows drawer docks it in the body
flex row so IDE, Journal, NodeFlow, and Dashboard shift right instead

than 200px.

NodeFlow configure/inspector no longer opens on pointer-down. A left
click under the 5px slop opens it; a move past the slop is a drag and
keeps the panel closed (and closes it if it was already open). Fast
drags that skip rAF still count as drags. Palette / highlight / group-

build 2026-08-10.699  (v2.16.4)

JSON FIELD EXPLORER: COMBINED QUERY BINDS FIELDS FROM DIFFERENT
NESTING LEVELS.

Selecting fields from two different array depths -- e.g. id on the
tradeValuations[] element plus metric on the nested metricValues[]
element -- generated an All-rows query whose deeper CTE projected only
its own UNNEST, so the final SELECT's "e2 ->> '$.id'" bound against a
CTE exposing only e4 and DuckDB failed with 'Binder Error: Referenced
column "e2" not found in FROM clause! Candidate bindings: "e4"'.

composeMultiFieldSql handled outer scalars (the _cN carry) and
deepest-level fields, but not a field whose hop chain is a proper
non-empty prefix of the longest chain. It now collects those fields'
element aliases and the CTE pipeline projects each one forward through
every later hop ("SELECT e2, UNNEST(...) AS e4"), so the final SELECT
binds all levels and outer values repeat on each exploded nested row --
exactly what the panel promises. Verified against DuckDB: the pre-fix
shape reproduces the reported binder error, the fixed shape returns
the outer id repeated per nested metric row.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
build 2026-08-04.698  (v2.16.4)

RUN ALL CONTINUES PAST A WRITE NODE (CONTINUATION CHAINS).

A data chain wired off a Write node's out port (inputs -> sql join ->
write -> sql) never ran: the write's output stayed empty and the run
visibly ended at the Write node. Run all classifies every
output/write/iterator/while node as an exporter and, when any connected
exporter exists, runs ONLY the exporters; the fallback "leaves" mode
(which runs end-of-chain data nodes) never activates in that case. The
downstream sql node was neither an exporter nor a leaf candidate, so it
was simply never executed -- and the post-run row seeding covers only
the ANCESTOR closure of attempted terminals, so a descendant of the
write got no last-run rows either.

Run all now collects "continuation leaves" -- data leaves whose
ancestors include one of the run's exporters -- and runs them AFTER
every exporter has finished, so a step reading the just-written table by
name sees the committed rows (the write's out port remains a
passthrough of the rows it wrote for {{in}}-style steps). A leaf under a
failed or cancelled exporter is skipped: that exporter has already
reported, and the leaf's input would be missing or stale. The leaves
count in the finish toast, seed last-run previews, and re-render
downstream charts like any other terminal.

Related ordering hole closed in the same pass: an exporter wired
downstream of another exporter (write -> ... -> output/write) could
start concurrently with its upstream sink. Terminals now run in waves by
exporter depth -- wave N+1 starts once wave N fully finishes -- so
chained sinks commit in order. Flat flows (every exporter independent)
land in a single wave and schedule exactly as before.

Component tests pin both behaviors: the continuation leaf runs only
after the write resolves (ordering is part of the contract), and a
failed write skips the leaf.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
build 2026-07-31.697  (v2.16.4)

RUN ALL OF WRITE NODES NO LONGER REPORTS "0 OF N DONE" CANCELLED AFTER
AN UPSTREAM EDIT.

Running a workflow, editing it upstream (the reported shape: inserting a
union above several write nodes), then running again could end with the
run dying partway and EVERY write terminal reporting cancelled -- the
"Run all cancelled -- 0 of N done" toast -- while previews of the same
chain kept working.

Root cause: DuckDB's engine-wide interrupt() sets a sticky _cancel event
that is never cleared by the interrupt itself; while it stays set the
BeatDaemon re-interrupts every statement that outlives its ~3s beat and
the cancellable row fetch unwinds immediately. The flag gets planted by
any coarse engine-level cancel -- a Stop, or cancel_query's engine-wide
fallback when a superseded preview/chart request has no precise cursor
to interrupt (exactly what a burst of graph edits produces). run_query,
run_nodeflow and run_nodeflows already clear the stale flag at entry;
the write path (run_nodeflow_to_table) -- and the export, iterator,
while, chart, browse, validate and reconcile flow paths -- never did.
Before the fix, the edit also invalidated the flow cache, so the rebuilt
upstream ran long enough for the stale flag to land: the run progressed
through the fast early statements, died at the first heavy one, and
every write in the batch unwound as {cancelled}.

All nine flow entry points now clear the stale engine cancel at entry
(the write path uses the engine-less form because its build engine and
write destination can differ). Regression test plants the sticky flag
and proves a write run succeeds, plus a source guard that every flow
entry point keeps the clear.

CHART NODES RENDER OVER CONNECTOR FLOWS (MULTI-AXIS FIXED); GET COLUMNS
DECLARES EACH TABLE ONCE.

A chart node fed through a select node from a SQL Server connection
failed with 'Catalog Error: Table with name __nbflow_..._out does not
exist! Did you mean "__nbsql_..."?' even though the select's preview
showed rows. The multi-axis chart types (multiple Y, multiple X,
candlestick) read their input rows on a FRESH DuckDB cursor -- a
separate connection with its own temp schema that cannot see the TEMP
table the flow just materialised. Chart row reads now retry on the
locked main connection (the same fallback the preview and export paths
already used), and the generic result drain -- the flow read path when
the Parquet fast path is unavailable -- grew the same retry.

Two related mis-routes fixed with it: a SQLite-pinned flow's final read
was re-routed to DuckDB by the always-DuckDB engine preference (the
hidden temp is registered under its build engine for the read, the same
trick reconcile uses), so SQLite-resident flows run again under the
build-690 default.

Get columns: a table referenced MORE THAN ONCE in the same query -- the
classic shape is a CTE reading the very table the outer query joins back
to -- declared every one of its columns twice, filling field pickers
with phantom *_2 names (DimValuationDateID_2, ...) that no fetch would
ever produce. Repeated references now collapse to ONE declaration on the
RESOLVED table, so identical references, an unqualified name plus its
dbo-qualified twin, and self-joins all declare once; every declared name
exists after the fetch. Two DIFFERENT tables sharing a column name still
de-dup positionally to id / id_2, exactly as a SELECT * fetch would.

DASHBOARD CHARTS CARRY EVERY FIELD (MULTI-Y FIXED); DASHBOARD RUNS PULL

Dashboard widgets now build their chart spec through the SAME shared

SQL SERVER QUERIES RUN ONLY ON RUN/FETCH; GET COLUMNS PROPAGATES; FIELD

The post-run seed pass (and every preview batch) now REUSES the run's own

build 2026-07-24.691  (v2.16.4)

RUN PARAMETERS FLOW INTO CHARTS + DOWNSTREAM PREVIEWS.

The promoted "Run parameters" (Ask-at-run values) now hydrate chart nodes and
post-run seed previews with the same variable overrides the run used, instead
of the variable's static value. The chart cache key includes the params, so a
chart built for one parameter set is never reused for another. Minor: two
"Colours" labels become "Colors".

build 2026-07-24.690  (v2.16.4)

CHART Y-AXIS CONTROLS + SQL SERVER BRACE GUARDS + DUCKDB DEFAULT ENGINE.

- Charts gain "Fit Y to data" and explicit Y min / max on bar/line/area (and
  scatter in NodeFlow), applied to the ECharts value axis.
- Variables: an author-quoted token '{{name}}' now collapses to one escaped SQL
  literal instead of ''value''. The SQL Server node fetch runs the same
  {{name}} misuse checks as a full run and rejects {{in}}/{{input}} (it has no
  input relation) with an actionable message.
- Engine preference DEFAULT flips dual -> duckdb: an unpinned flow / table-less
  query routes to DuckDB by default when installed (a SQLite-only table still
  forces SQLite -- preference, not relocation). Set engine_mode="dual" to keep
  the legacy route-by-table behavior.

RECONCILE PER-SIDE TOTALS + IDENTICAL-REFETCH EPOCH UN-BUMP.

The reconcile report shows A / B total record counts separately (plus the
matching common count) instead of a lump "Total records" tile. Separately, a
volatile-source re-fetch that returns identical content no longer bumps the
data epoch, so it does not prune the previews a run just produced. The content
signature keys on every column (a change confined to a later column is still
detected -- latest-data-wins preserved).

build 2026-07-24.688  (v2.16.4)

NODEFLOW RUN-ALL: chart/dashboard leaves + fresh just-seeded previews.

Chart / browse / dashboard are now valid Run-all leaves (the backend compiles
them as a passthrough), so a flow ending in a chart runs its upstream chain;
expanded charts re-hydrate against the fresh run afterward. Separately, a run
whose sources mutate mid-run (a SQL Server fetch bumps the backend data epoch)
now seeds its previews under the post-bump epoch, so the next catalog poll no
longer prunes them as stale ("No cached results" after Run all). Latest-data-
wins is preserved -- a later real mutation still prunes the seed.

build 2026-07-24.685  (v2.16.4)

NODE FREEZE + RUN PARAMETERS + ENGINE MODE + VAR/ENGINE SWEEP.

A large feature + reliability batch (Kimi assistant) plus a security hardening
of the read-only SQL Server guard tightened this session. Both suites pass.

- Node Freeze: pin a node's output (config.frozen -> kept __nbfreeze_* table)
  across data changes until unfreeze / upstream edit. Canvas ❄ badge.
- Run parameters: mark a variable "Ask at run" (vars[].param) to be prompted in
  a Run parameters dialog; params thread through the flow run.
- Engine mode (dual|duckdb): route unpinned flows + table-less queries to
  DuckDB when set; a SQLite-only table still forces SQLite. Persisted setting.
- Engine-flip-after-fetch fix: a remote-source flow no longer errors "no such
  table" on the first run after restart (the build engine is re-derived after a
  fetch flips it).
- ${var} resolution sweep: export file names, iterator/while/loop bodies,
  SharePoint/webscrape/API fetches. Shared MSSQL connection restores its prior
  database after a node USE [db].
- Frontend: re-run failures now toast; modal-stack Escape ownership; Field
  Explorer nested-field retry; theme-aware chart fallback + WCAG contrast pass.

SECURITY: a read-only SQL Server connection permitted any batch beginning with
USE/SET, so a write could ride along (SET NOCOUNT ON; DELETE FROM t). The guard
now requires EVERY statement in a batch to be a bare USE/SET, keeping the
legitimate USE [db] switch while blocking smuggled writes.

build 2026-07-23.684  (v2.16.4)

VARIABLE-NODE EXPRESSIONS + SQL SERVER VARIABLES + RELIABILITY SWEEP.

Two feature additions plus a large Stop/cancel + data-freshness +
NodeFlow-SQL-correctness sweep (the latter authored by the Kimi assistant).
Both land together; the full backend and frontend suites pass.

Features:
- Variable node values can be SQL expressions (fx), evaluated once per run and
  substituted as a literal. Friendly aliases DATE_TIME_NOW()/TODAY()/NOW() map
  to engine SQL. A date defined once reaches every downstream node as a literal.
- The SQL Server node resolves ${name}/{{name}} in its query, including on the
  interactive Fetch (it previously did not) -- so a WHERE clause can filter on
  a variable such as OrderDate >= '${as_of}'.

- Stop interrupts Python-node loops, SharePoint/web-scrape fetches, catalog
  imports, grid create, exports (partial files cleaned), reconcile/profile.
- Latest-data-wins: grids/dashboards/reconcile/NodeFlow badge or refresh on a
  data change; the preview cache is pruned by data epoch.
- NodeFlow SQL correctness: projection-pushdown liveness, safer SQL-join table
  detection, multijoin validation, node-name collisions. (SQLite date-diff now
  errors on an unusual unit instead of silently computing days.)
- Launcher reaps a spawned server on exit; boot sweeps moved off the hot path.

build 2026-07-22.683  (v2.16.4)

NODEFLOW CANCEL FIX: clear a sticky engine cancel before a run.

A prior cancellation could leave the engine's cancel flag set, so the next
NodeFlow run (most visibly the unique node) auto-cancelled itself before doing
any work. The engine now clears the sticky cancel state at the start of a run.
This build also folds in the kept-distinct-right-keys join fix from 2026-07-22.682.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
build 2026-07-22.682  (v2.16.4)

NODEFLOW JOIN FIX: keep distinct-named right-side join keys.

The join and multi-join column projection excluded every right-side join key
to avoid emitting two columns with one name. That is correct for a same-named
join (id = id, where the right copy is redundant), but it also silently dropped
distinct-named right keys: joining COLUMN_NAME = source_field returned
column_name yet not source_field. Now only same-named keys are dropped as
redundant; a distinct right key survives with its own name and takes the r_
prefix only when it would otherwise collide with a left column.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
build 2026-07-22.681  (v2.16.4)

NODEFLOW TIMEZONE FIX: pin the DuckDB session TimeZone to UTC.

DuckDB otherwise adopts the machine's local zone (e.g. America/New_York) as
its default session TimeZone, and its native row-fetch path materializes
TIMESTAMPTZ / NOW() / current_timestamp as pytz-aware datetimes. In a frozen
build (or any environment where pytz's zoneinfo is not resolvable) that raised
"unknown timezone 'America/New_York'" whenever a NodeFlow workflow result fell
off the Arrow fast-path onto the native fetch -- most visibly the filter node,
whose SELECT * always drags a tz-aware column through the fetch. The engine now
pins SET TimeZone='UTC' on every DuckDB connection, matching what the Arrow
fast-path already presented and removing the dependency on a Python tz database.

build 2026-07-21.677  (v2.16.4)

MASTER NODEFLOW: NO MISSING-COLUMN WARNING ON A HALF-WRITTEN EXPRESSION.
.676 debounced the Filter/Formula missing-column banner, which only delayed
it: pausing partway through a function still raised the warning against the
half-typed operand. Suppression is now structural rather than timed. A new
looksIncompleteExpr gates both the banner and the prune, and reports an
expression as unfinished when it has an unclosed ( [ ' or ", a closing bracket
that was never opened, a trailing operator or clause keyword (+ - * / , < > =
AND OR WHEN THEN ELSE LIKE IN IS AS CAST), or a CASE with no END. So
LTRIM([Name] , UPPER(sco , REPLACE([a], 'x , [score] + and CASE WHEN [score] >
5 THEN 'hi' all stay quiet while being written, and a half-written expression
can no longer be pruned either.

A finished expression is still judged normally: UPPER([gone]) against an
upstream without "gone" reports the missing column as before. A bare word that
parses on its own (plain "sco", no brackets, parens or pending operator) also
still warns -- at that point it is a valid expression naming a column that does
not exist, which is exactly the renamed-upstream case the warning is for.

----------------------------------------------------------------------
build 2026-07-21.676  (v2.16.4)

MASTER NODEFLOW: BRANCH ERROR ISOLATION + FORMULA REF FIXES.
Run all no longer loses every branch when one node fails. The batch
materialiser built all terminals in a single try, so the first node that
raised aborted the pass before any result was read, returned a run-level
error with no results array, and dropped the temp tables of branches that had
already finished. A failure now rebuilds the graph's independent target groups
separately (they share no upstream work, so nothing is recomputed twice) and
each failed terminal reports its own error inside results; a group with
several terminals retries them one at a time so a branch that never reaches
the broken node still returns rows. Every-branch-failed and single-target runs
keep the old run-level envelope with the culprit node attributed, and a clean
run is untouched. Each group builds into its own temp list -- sharing one list
let an unfused rebuild drop a finished group's tables out from under it.

Formula/filter column references: bare words in an expression were all treated
as column refs against a 47-word SQL list, so most of the function palette
(LTRIM, regexp_replace, strftime, …) and every half-typed identifier were
reported missing. Worse, the post-run prune blanked the WHOLE expression on
one such token and autosave persisted it -- the formula did not survive
exiting the inspector. Identifiers followed by "(" are now read as calls,
{{var}}/${var} placeholders and a trailing unclosed "[Amoun" are skipped,
destroying user text requires a delimited [name]/"name" ref, and a formula's
own new columns count as live for later formulas in the same node. The warning
is debounced for freeform filter/formula so it no longer fires mid-keystroke.
Formula target no longer flips from overwrite to "new column" when the
inspector opens before the upstream schema has loaded.

build 2026-07-15.608  (v2.16.4)

FIELD EXPLORER MEMORY-SAFE JSON STEERING, FIRST-RECORD LIMIT, HOVER POLISH.
Field Explorer now steers array / opaque-JSON nodes to the memory-safe path:
shred-eligible arrays offer "Shred to tables" (the relational family joined on
_sk/_parent_sk) and deep opaque-JSON columns offer "Flatten to tables" (reuses
the tested flatten_json deep re-read), instead of a full UNNEST that loads the
whole column into memory. The "First record ([1] path)" recipe appends LIMIT 1
so it returns a single record rather than evaluating the first-element
expression over every row -- on a multi-GB opaque-JSON table that materialized
one JSON value per record and raised OutOfMemory. DuckDB out-of-memory query
errors now explain that the reported size is the failed allocation, not the
limit, and suggest shred / flatten / filter-first. Loaded-table rows collapse
the action-button slot when idle so the table name uses the full width, then
animate the buttons open (width + fade + slide) on hover without changing row
height.

build 2026-07-11.581  (v2.15.92)

WATCHDOG LIFECYCLE RACE FIX. The process-wide stall watchdog now owns an
explicit stop event and thread handle, serializes scan-state updates, and lets
test reset terminate the daemon before clearing dump history. Previously the
daemon survived reset and could run its normal 90-second scan between two
threshold-zero verification scans, clear the shared dumped-id set, and write
the same thread-stack dump twice. The behavior was timing-dependent and showed
up on Windows as the final dump-once watchdog failure.

The production loop remains one-per-process and observe-only. Concurrent start
calls are still idempotent, a stopped test daemon can restart cleanly, engine
reset still permits a genuinely persistent stall to be dumped again, and a
new deterministic regression waits beyond a short scan interval to prove no
retired scanner can mutate state after reset.

FLOW-CACHE CORRECTNESS. The dedicated FlowCache is a thread-safe count + byte

build 2026-06-25.482  (v2.16.24)

TIER-A PERFORMANCE AUDIT + CONCURRENCY/DEPENDENCY AUDIT. One real
scaling bug fixed; the async execution model verified end to end.

A BUG FIXED: A DIAMOND-SHAPED NODE GRAPH COMPILED EXPONENTIALLY. When
a node fanned out to several branches that later rejoined, the flow
compiler re-composed every shared ancestor once PER PATH -- so a graph
with a handful of diamonds made thousands of compile calls and
produced megabytes of SQL (a deep case ran the process out of
memory). The compiler now remembers each (node, port) it has composed
and reuses it, so a shared node is composed exactly once (a case that
took 8191 calls now takes 25). A hard cap on the composed SQL size
turns a pathological fan-out into a clear message -- "materialise the
shared step into a table" -- instead of exhausting memory. Real loops
are still detected.

FLATTEN PLANNER -- LINEAR ON WIDE TABLES. Two safe improvements while
auditing planner scaling: unique-column-alias allocation is now O(1)
amortised (it was a scan that could go quadratic when many fields
sanitise to the same name), and name sanitisation is cached. A table
with thousands of struct fields now plans in linear time. No behaviour
change -- aliases and output are identical.

CONCURRENCY / DEPENDENCY MODEL -- VERIFIED, NOT CHANGED. A full audit
of how loading, querying, node graphs and the journal run
concurrently. Confirmed and pinned with tests:

  - A node feeding several consumers is built ONCE into a shared temp
    table; a single-use node is fused inline (no wasteful temp). A
    diamond builds exactly the minimal set of tables.
  - Journal cells self-order: Run all fires every cell at once, and a
    cell that references another WAITS for it via a name-keyed gate,
    while independent cells run in parallel. A re-run waits out its own
    prior run and supersedes it rather than duplicating.
  - A journal cell that references a FRESH upstream reuses that
    result as a view over its stored file -- the upstream is NOT
    re-run. An evicted, capped, or name-colliding store safely falls
    back to inlining rather than changing the answer.
  - The frontend doesn't re-run or refetch for the sake of it: the
    preview cache and column fetches key on graph STRUCTURE (not
    node positions), so dragging a node around does nothing over the
    network.

A KNOWN, DEFERRED INEFFICIENCY: the catalog refresh re-reads every
table on every sync (O(tables^2) across a long session). A
describe-new-only shortcut was tried and reverted -- the SQL editor
can redefine a table out of band, so the refresh must stay the
reconciliation point. A safe fix needs an event-driven catalog; left
for a dedicated change. Correctness is intact.

nodeflow.py (compile memo + SQL-size cap), shred.py (O(1) alias
alloc, cached sanitise), run_tests.py (four audit batteries). Suite:
backend 606 (+.464b run whole, still 94), http 159, frontend 93 --
zero failures. No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.481  (v2.16.23)

TIER-3 AUDITS -- ROBUSTNESS AND HYGIENE. One real bug fixed.

Three audits over crash-resistance, resource cleanup, and concurrency
on the new flatten surfaces. Each is now a permanent guard.

A BUG FIXED: A DEEP STRUCT COULD CRASH THE FLATTEN. The struct walker
that inlines nested fields into the base table had no recursion limit.
A pathologically deep struct type -- from a malformed or adversarial
schema -- would recurse until Python's stack overflowed, taking the
flatten down with an unhandled error. It is capped at 64 levels now
(far past any real nesting); beyond that it stops descending rather
than crash, and a realistic nested struct is still fully inlined.

AUDIT 7 -- PARSER FUZZING. The type parser and the struct walker were
fuzzed with ~25 pathological inputs: empty, truncated, unbalanced
brackets, stray commas, unicode field names, unclosed quotes, and
struct/list nesting hundreds to thousands deep. The parser already
degraded gracefully (it promises never to raise); the walker did not,
which is how the crash above was found. Both are clean now.

AUDIT 8 -- RESOURCE LEAKS. The flatten writes a temporary Parquet
cache when the source isn't already Parquet-backed. Confirmed it is
removed on EVERY exit -- success, error, and cancel -- so a long
session can't fill the disk. A flatten whose table build fails after
the cache is written leaves nothing behind.

AUDIT 9 -- CONCURRENCY ON THE NEW SURFACES. The per-list joinkeys
tables added last build run through the same single CREATE path as
the base and list tables (each holding the write lock only briefly,
with a heartbeat scope); the long cache COPY stays on a separate
cursor, off the main lock. The catalog refresh runs only after every
table is built, so it can never observe a half-built family -- the
.464 stall/race class does not reappear.

shred.py (recursion cap), run_tests.py (three audit batteries).
Suite: backend 602 (+.464b run whole, still 94), http 159, frontend
93 -- zero failures. No new dependencies.

TIER-2 AUDITS -- DATA-MUTATION PATHS. One real bug fixed.

Three audits over the paths that change data under you: the retype

A BUG FIXED: A RETYPE SHADOW COULD REAPPEAR. When you change a

blanks. Verified reversible.

AUDIT 5 -- _rid STABILITY. The flatten join contract rests on _rid: a
base row and its child list rows must share the same _rid to join
back. Confirmed all three tables in a flatten derive _rid from the

materialised column (not recomputed), so it survives a join or an
export intact.

AUDIT 6 -- CANCELLATION. Every cancellable op (flatten, shred,
profile, materialize, retype, reconcile, pivot, query) was checked to
interrupt the right engine on Stop and to drain the run registry on

build 2026-06-25.478  (v2.16.20)

AUDIT: THE FLATTENER AND THE SHRED NODE. Three fixes.

After the flatten crash, both the table-level flattener and the
Nodebook shred node got a full audit across every nested shape
(scalars, single structs, nested structs, lists of structs, lists of
scalars, multiple lists, and flat tables). Three real issues came
out, all now fixed and covered.

LIST ELEMENTS ARE ALIGNMENT-SAFE. Each list table pulled its element
fields by zipping two separate set-returning functions
(generate_subscripts for the ordinal, unnest for the element) in one
SELECT -- correct only as long as the engine zips them in lockstep.
The element is now addressed by subscript directly (list[ordinal]),
so the ordinal and the row it labels are the same thing by
construction and cannot drift apart.

MULTI-LIST JOINKEYS ARE NO LONGER A CROSS-PRODUCT. When a record had
more than one nested list, the single joinkeys table LEFT-JOINed
every list independently -- a row with 3 legs and 2 fees produced 6
key rows, not 5. Each nested list now gets its OWN joinkeys table
(_rid + that list's ordinal), so positions never multiply together.
A single-list table (the common case) is unchanged: one _joinkeys
table, exactly as before. A flat or struct-only table now emits no
joinkeys table at all -- there is nothing to bridge.

THE SHRED NODE HANDLES A FLAT SOURCE. Flattening a table with no
nested columns correctly produces nothing, but the node still tried
to read a base table that was never created and would fail on a
missing table. It now passes the source straight through when the
flatten produced no base -- shredding something flat is a no-op, not
an error.

shred.py, session.py, nodeflow.py, run_tests.py. New audit battery
plus repointed shape assertions for the subscript form. Suite:
backend 593 (+.464b run whole), http 159, frontend 93 -- zero
failures. No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.474  (v2.16.16)

TWO REPORTS.

FLATTEN NOW PRODUCES THE RIGHT RELATIONAL SHAPE. Loading a nested
JSON with flatten toggled was building the wrong tables: the "base"
came out holding one array's fields and NONE of the record's
top-level columns, and the other nested columns were dropped. The
cause: flatten ran the per-COLUMN shred, which treats whichever
nested column it is handed as the root -- so for a file with a
top-level record plus several nested structures, it exploded one
array and lost everything else.

Flatten is a TABLE-level operation now. From one nested table it
builds exactly the set you would model by hand:

  <base>            one row per record: every top-level scalar, PLUS
                    each single-record (struct) column flattened
                    INLINE -- product -> product_name, product_ccy;
                    keywords -> keywords_kw1, ... . List columns are
                    dropped from here (each becomes its own table).
  <base>_joinkeys   _rid plus one ordinal per top-level list
                    (fees_ord, ...), so a child row maps to its exact
                    parent position; the base joins on _rid alone.
  <base>_<list>     one row per element of a top-level list: _rid +
                    <list>_ord + the element's fields, inlined.

So a file like input_derivatives now yields input_derivatives_2
(all the top-level fields, with product and keywords inlined),
input_derivatives_2_joinkeys, and input_derivatives_2_fees --
each list table joins to _joinkeys on _rid + its ordinal, and the
base joins on _rid. Nested structs inline all the way down
(addr.geo.lat -> addr_geo_lat); an array of scalars becomes a
value column; a flat file reports "nothing to flatten" instead of
erroring. The whole thing reads through the load's Parquet cache
(materialised on demand for non-cached tables) so _rid is stable,
and the cache copy is keepalive-guarded so a large flatten never
shows a false "stalled" card and stays cancellable.

JOURNAL TABS KEEP THEIR ORDER WHEN CLICKED. The strip was ordered
by recency, and switching to a tab bumped its timestamp -- so the
tab you clicked jumped to the front. Tabs are ordered by creation
now and refreshed in place: clicking, renaming, or editing one
never reorders the strip.

shred.py, session.py, Notebook.tsx, run_tests.py. Pin repoints for
the two new own-cursor / count-prime sites the table-level flatten
adds (cache COPY), and the rewritten flatten-toggle tests. Suite:
backend 590 (+.464b run whole), http 159, frontend 93 -- zero
failures. No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.472  (v2.16.14)

FOUR REPORTS: A DATA-LOSS BUG AND THREE THAT WERE SLOW.

RETYPE IS LOSSLESS IN BOTH DIRECTIONS NOW. Right-click a string
column, change it to INTEGER, and the non-numeric values become
NULL as expected -- but changing it BACK to text left those values
NULL forever, even after a rerun, because the cast overwrote the
originals IN STORAGE. The first retype of a column now tucks the

(this one and all later ones) derives FROM that shadow: strings ->

any number of cycles, on both engines. The shadow never shows in
the sidebar, grids, profiler, or exports, and can't itself be
retyped.

result because every row was shipped out of the engine, through
Python, and back -- and on DuckDB the save fell into a row-by-row
executemany. A result backed by a Parquet cache now saves with a
single CREATE TABLE AS read_parquet, and exports (csv, parquet,
json, ndjson) with a single engine COPY, both ordered by the
stable row number (or your chosen sort). One statement, no Python
row loop. Verified exact against the streaming path.

THE NODEBOOK EXPORT rides the same one-COPY path on DuckDB (csv,

AUDIT PASS II, COMPLETE. A second full sweep -- fresh angles, no
re-proofs -- across query runs, load runs, node data flow, concurrent
reads, responsiveness and stalling, memory, and reconciliation

hardening, four harness-contract clarifications now documented, and

BUG ONE: SILENT EXECUTION, FALSE STALLS. The exec keepalive wrapped
only three DuckDB LOAD paths -- query execution on BOTH engines never
beat the progress registry. Any query outliving the 90-second stall
threshold FALSE-FLAGGED as stalled (red pill, stack dump), and the
keepalive's cancel re-nudge never ran during queries. The first fix
(a keepalive around every execute) worked but spawned and joined a
thread inside every write-lock hold -- widening each hold just enough
for the non-blocking catalog probes to start landing inside the
loader's indexing bursts. REWORKED: one persistent heartbeat daemon
per engine manager plus a featherweight, attribute-only scope at all

wrapper never managed. Proven by the beat SAWTOOTH on a live surfaced
query -- idle climbs toward the three-second interval, resets, climbs
again, never approaching the threshold -- and cancel still lands
instantly.

BUG TWO: BLANK ROW COUNTS AFTER A LOAD. The non-blocking count probe
raced the loader's fire-and-forget indexer: each CREATE INDEX holds
the lock for well under a millisecond, and a sidebar refresh landing
inside one of those blinks showed a BLANK count for a table that
loaded fine (three of six runs flaked). Fixed both ways: loads now
PRIME the count cache with the row count they already know (file
loads, flow writes, materialize), and the probe micro-retries for up
to thirty milliseconds between indexer statements -- still
non-blocking on every try, so a genuinely long statement keeps the
never-park guarantee. Six of six after.

HARDENING: an engine (or a test double) answering None for its column
type map can no longer take down the whole tables tree.

result with mixed filters, sorts, and pages return byte-identical to
sequential, and reads plus the catalog stay live during heavy
queries. Memory: bounded traced growth across a query battery, clean
eviction of the oldest result, and a cancel storm drains the
registry. A silenced heartbeat still dumps EXACTLY once per episode
and the run completes. Query runs, loads, and reconcile production +
drilldown were executed at full size earlier in the pass: inf/nan

build 2026-06-25.458  (v2.15.65)

FEATURE: per-statement results on Run-all. Run a script of several
statements and every one of them now gets its OWN result -- browsable
from a pill strip above the grid -- instead of only the final SELECT
surviving.

HOW IT RUNS. A new run_script path splits with the audited scanner
and executes each statement through the NORMAL single-run machinery:
same connection, so temp tables and session state persist across
statements exactly as before; same query id, so Cancel reaches
whichever statement is currently executing. The response carries a
ledger -- index, a trimmed preview, elapsed milliseconds, and for
every row-producing statement a private pageable result id. The TOP
LEVEL of the response is unchanged: still the last row-producing
statement's payload, so everything that consumed the old shape keeps
working, and plain single runs are untouched.

THE SEMANTICS, PINNED. A mid-batch error stops the script, names
failed_statement, and every EARLIER statement's result stays usable
-- you can inspect what ran before the failure. Scripts that manage
their OWN transactions (BEGIN / COMMIT / ROLLBACK) fall back to the
classic one-batch run -- per-statement autocommit would change their
meaning -- and the ledger says so in a note. read_only is enforced
per statement. Over HTTP the flag is opt-in (per_statement on
/api/query); without it the wire shape is byte-identical to before.

THE STRIP. When a run produces two or more statements, the result
tab shows pills: S1, S2, S3 -- row counts on the selects, "ok" on
the DDL/DML, a red mark on the failure. Click a pill and the grid
swaps to that statement's rows (sort and filters reset to that
result's own view); hover shows the statement text and its timing.
Released tabs refetch WITH the ledger, so pills never point at
discarded results. One .381 wiring pin repointed for the new
call-site meta, deliberately.

session.py, server.py, App.tsx, api.ts, types.ts, styles.css,
run_tests.py. Suite: 639 passing, 0 failing, 21 skipped. No new

FEATURE: per-statement results on Run-all. The first feature build on
top of the completed audit program -- and it leans on the audited
splitter from day one. Minor version bump: the query response grew a
new field.

WHAT CHANGED. Run a script of several statements and every statement
now gets its OWN pageable result -- not just the last one. The grid
grows a statement strip (S1, S2, S3...) whenever a run produced more
than one: click a pill to swap the grid to that statement's result,
with its own paging, sorting, and filtering; DDL/DML entries show
their row counts and are unclickable; a failed statement shows a
cross at its position. Single-statement runs look exactly as before
-- no strip, no change.

HOW IT WORKS. The backend splits with the audited scanner (the .447
dollar-quote and nested-comment fixes matter here), runs each
statement through the normal single-run rail -- same connection, so
temp state persists; same query_id, so cancel reaches whichever
statement is current -- and returns a ledger: index, a preview,
elapsed milliseconds, and a result_id for every row-producing
statement. The top-level payload stays back-compatible (the last
row-producing statement's page), so every existing caller keeps
working. Scripts that manage their own transactions (BEGIN / COMMIT
/ ROLLBACK) deliberately fall back to the classic one-batch run --
per-statement autocommit would change their semantics -- and the
ledger says so. A mid-script error stops the run, names the failing
statement's index, and every result BEFORE it stays usable.

THE RAILS. The new mode rides the existing /api/query route behind a
per_statement flag, so the .454 breadth fuzz covers it by
construction; the executed battery proves the ledger shape, per-
statement paging, temp-state persistence across statements, the
transaction fallback, read-only enforcement mid-script, and the
error-stops-and-names contract.

build 2026-06-25.448  (v2.15.55)

AUDIT_PLAN PASS 5 of 14: results, filters, and sort. One bug fixed --
the cap trim could yank a PINNED result out from under a running
chain -- and the two filter implementations are now proven identical,
property-style.

THE BUG. The 24-result cap trim popped the OLDEST result
unconditionally, pins ignored. A journal chain holding a reuse pin on
its source result could have that store closed mid-run by unrelated
queries filling the cache -- exactly the failure _reuse_pins was
built to prevent. The trim now takes the oldest UNPINNED result and
holds over-cap when everything in excess is pinned. Proven live: a
pinned result survives 40 fresh queries untouched, then evicts
normally the moment its pin releases.

TWO IMPLEMENTATIONS, ONE ANSWER. Grid filters run through the SQL
pushdown on spilled SQLite stores and through the Python predicate
everywhere else. Sixty seeded random filter sets -- every operator in
the vocabulary including the symbol aliases, one and two terms,
hostile values against wrong-typed columns -- produce IDENTICAL rows
and identical totals from both paths, and filter+sort combined is
row-exact against a brute-force reference.

SEMANTICS PINNED. Empty strings sort head-ascending / tail-descending
symmetrically; sorting is STABLE within equal keys; TEXT columns sort
lexicographically ("1" < "10" < "2") in both stores -- the
SQL-standard behavior, now written down; and the filtered-count cache
stands, so scrolling a filtered multi-million-row result never
re-counts per page.

session.py, AUDIT_PLAN(dot)txt, run_tests.py. Suite: 629 passing, 0

SPLITTER BUG ONE: DOLLAR QUOTES. A dollar-quoted body -- $$ ... $$

not unique under DuckDB's CASE-INSENSITIVE catalog. Two fields
differing only by case ("a" next to "A"), or a plain field colliding
with a wrapper leaf's alias (a literal w_inner column beside w.inner,
which aliases to w_inner), produced a CREATE TABLE that BinderErrors
AT SHRED TIME on real data -- the whole table would fail to land.
The projection now tracks used names case-insensitively (key columns
protected) and suffixes collisions: a stays, A keeps its case, the
second becomes a_1, the leaf alias becomes w_inner_2. Proven
case-insensitively unique in the suite.

BRANCHES PINNED CLEAN. Quoted field names carrying commas and parens
parse intact -- "a,b" and "c(d" and "e)f" survive as three fields,
none split (the paren/quote-aware parser holds). DECIMAL(18,4)
params and MAP(VARCHAR, JSON) spawn no phantom children; MAP stays a
leaf. Scalar arrays still become value tables. STRUCT()[] and bare
INTEGER[] degenerate without raising. A 3-deep tree accumulates
ordinals exactly ["_rid", t3_ord, a_ord, b_ord] with one
generate_subscripts per hop, pipeline CTEs and no LATERAL, no star
and no EXCLUDE, and IS NOT NULL narrowing -- the .429/.428 shape
invariants now hold at depth under test. Table-name collisions after
sanitize stay distinct (x_a_b and x_a_b_2). Unicode field names plan
clean.

AUDIT_PLAN(dot)txt carries the record. Next: PASS 4, query exec +
cancel at every stage.

consistency gap closed, zero registry leaks, no watchdog overlap --
and every verdict is now an executed test.

THE BUG. The .426 lock-aware read wait was silently DEAD on the real
engine: it asked the write lock .locked(), _DeadlineRLock has no such
method, the AttributeError was swallowed, and the not-busy branch
always won -- saturated reads degraded instantly onto a held write
lock, the exact stall the feature was built to dodge. The busy check
is now a non-blocking acquire PROBE from the reader thread (a
different thread cannot ride RLock reentrancy), and the regression
test drives the REAL _DeadlineRLock: writer holds it + saturated pool
-> the reader waits and WINS the freed slot; idle lock -> instant
degrade, unchanged.

THE GAP. Every sqlite maintenance op ran under the write lock except
PRAGMA shrink_memory, which raced writers. Locked.

proves every function that calls _register_run owns its teardown --
_unregister_run directly, or the shared _flow_cleanup the seven flow
entries route through -- with zero exceptions, so a future leak fails
the suite. Watchdog overlap: _ExecKeepalive stamps the WORKER
thread's op via beat_on_thread, so a long single CTAS cannot be reset
mid-statement -- pinned. Also verified and standing: read-slot
release covers the timeout-acquire path, cursors close on every read
path, JOBS map mutations stay under JOBS_LOCK, opreg is RLock-guarded
throughout, per-run cancel (tid registry) and engine-wide cancel (the
keepalive Event) are distinct rails with no crosstalk, and the shred
thread throttle never holds the write lock across a statement.

DOCUMENTED TRADEOFFS (by design, not bugs): a shred over HTTP holds

build 2026-06-25.431  (v2.15.38)

Two more structural memory levers, closed: the one-row-group cache and
thread-multiplied peaks. Plus the cache version bump that makes them
real.

THE SNEAKY ONE: ROW GROUPS. Parquet's default row group is ~122k
rows; the sophis file has 925. The whole 1.7 GB cache was effectively
ONE row group -- so every downstream statement decoded the entire
column chunk as a single unit before any pipeline could stream a
single vector, no matter how lean the plan. Cache writes (both the
loader's filecache and convert-to-Parquet) now cap row groups by
BYTES (64 MB): small decode units for jumbo rows, a no-op for normal
data. An automatic retry drops to plain options when the local DuckDB
predates ROW_GROUP_SIZE_BYTES -- and any OTHER copy error re-raises
untouched. CACHE_VERSION is bumped so the existing single-group cache
REBUILDS under the new writer instead of being reused.

THREADS. DuckDB parallelizes a pipeline and each thread holds vector
batches of the fat trade structs -- peak memory multiplies by the
thread count. shred_run now throttles to 2 threads for its statements
(SAMQL_SHRED_THREADS tunes the cap or 0 disables) and restores the
original count on every exit path; already-low settings are left
untouched.

All executed: the option string, the old-DuckDB retry, the
non-option-error re-raise, both writers routed through the retrying
copy, throttle capping 8 -> 2 and restoring 8, at-or-below-cap and
env-disabled no-ops, the shred_run finally hook, and the cache bump.

Manual lever, if ever needed: Settings -> Engine tuning can raise the
memory limit live on a 24 GB box -- but with row groups, lean
projections, the streaming pipeline, thread throttling, and the OOM
batch fallback all stacked, it should not be.

engines.py, session.py, filecache.py, run_tests.py. Suite: 613
passing, 0 failing, 21 skipped. No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.430  (v2.15.37)

Batching, answered properly: not as the default (it taxes every
healthy run), but as an OOM-triggered fallback that guarantees a
shred completes.

THE TRADE. Batching by default re-decodes the parquet source once per
batch -- a file_row_number filter does not prune row groups, so the
decode cost multiplies. The .429 pipeline removed the actual
algorithmic blowup, and healthy runs should not pay insurance against
a defect that is gone. But five walls on one file argue for a
guarantee, and a FALLBACK costs exactly zero until the moment it is
needed.

HOW IT WORKS. shred_run tries the single statement first. On an
OutOfMemoryException -- and ONLY that; interrupts and every other
error re-raise untouched -- it re-builds THAT table in
file_row_number ranges: a metadata-fast rowcount sizes ~8 batches,
the first range CREATEs the table, the rest INSERT, a repeat OOM
halves the batch size down to a 50-row floor before giving up,
progress beats between batches keep the watchdog and the card honest,
and a cancel between batches keeps the ranges already landed. The
created record says "batched: N" so the outcome is visible.

Executed end to end in the battery: full-statement OOM -> rowcount ->
8 tiled ranges over a 100-row source, CREATE first and INSERT after,
the tiling covers 1..100 exactly, and the created record carries the
batch count. Builder pins: insert mode renders INSERT INTO with no
CREATE anywhere, and the row range lands inside the pipeline's first
stage. One cursor-audit pin repointed (the rowcount probe runs on its
own cursor, like everything else).

shred.py, session.py, run_tests.py. Suite: 612 passing, 0 failing,
21 skipped. No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.429  (v2.15.36)

The deep-dive on the second 13 GiB OOM: the hop engine itself was the
allocator. It is now a streaming UNNEST pipeline with per-stage
narrowing.

WHY .428 WAS NOT ENOUGH. The lean projections fixed what the
statements KEPT; this OOM was about what the statements CARRIED. The
database is file-backed (created tables can evict) and the spill
directory was set -- so the 13 GiB was pure within-statement working
set. The old hop pattern -- generate_series(1, len(x)) cross-joined
with LATERAL (SELECT parent[ord]) -- dragged the ENTIRE parent cell
value across the cross join and re-materialized the full element
struct for EVERY ordinal tuple: multiplicative copies of fat trade
structs, and projection pruning cannot push through list[index], so
even unused subtrees paid.

THE PIPELINE. Every table now builds as a CTE chain: each stage does
unnest() + generate_subscripts() side by side (aligned rows -- the
ordinal IS the key, exactly as before), and between stages a NARROWING
select forwards only the keys plus the one subtree the next hop needs.
Untouched siblings die at each CTE boundary; the parent cell never
crosses a join; the working set per batch is keys + one subtree. Same
tables, same names, same keys (_rid + one ordinal per hop), same
null-row semantics, one parquet read per statement -- just a plan
DuckDB can actually stream.

Verified in the battery across every table of a sophis-mini plan: no
LATERAL, no generate_series, dotted wrapper hops intact
(SwapHistory.SwapHistory.resetDates), lean projections riding on the
final stage, scalar grandchildren land in value. Two pins repointed to
the stage shape on purpose.

shred.py, run_tests.py. Suite: 611 passing, 0 failing, 21 skipped.
No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.428  (v2.15.35)

The 13 GiB wall: shred projections are now lean -- no element star,
no wrapper blobs, no array data ever duplicated into a parent.

THE ERROR, DECODED. .425 cleared EXCLUDE, .427 cleared the catalog,
and the run marched into OutOfMemoryException: could not allocate
block of size 4.4 MiB (13.0 GiB / 13.0 GiB used) -- with the spill
directory ALREADY configured. Spill did not save it because giant
struct vectors mid-projection are not spillable: the buffer manager
cannot evict blocks the pipeline still needs. Root cause: the root
CTAS selected e0.* -- the ENTIRE trade element, every wrapper blob

readably-aliased column (SwapHistory.SwapHistory.dayType ->

applies at every depth (a wrapper inside a child element gets the same
dotted-leaf treatment), an all-array element projects keys only, and
the .425 class of EXCLUDE error can no longer occur because there is

scalars are now real queryable columns instead of blob innards, which
is what a relational shred should have produced all along.

build 2026-06-25.427  (v2.15.34)

One wall further: the shred no longer trips over the query-in-place
VIEW squatting on the root table's name.

THE ERROR, DECODED. The .425 fix carried the flatten past EXCLUDE and
into the next wall, and this time the Error Dashboard caught it
exactly as designed: CatalogException: "<table> is not a table". A
query-in-place load is a VIEW over the Parquet cache, and the shred's
root spec deliberately takes the source's name -- root REPLACES
source, the established semantic on materialized loads. But DuckDB's
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE cannot replace a VIEW.

THE FIX. shred_run now pre-drops a view squatting on any target name
just before that statement runs (source name, or anything registered
in the view catalog). This is safe by construction: every shred CTAS
reads read_parquet() on the cache file directly and never touches the
view -- the view is a name, not a dependency. Materialized sources are
untouched (CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE already handles table-over-table),
partial-cancel keeps whatever was built, and the catalog resyncs after
the run as before. Behaviorally tested: a stub engine records the drop
landing BEFORE the create, the squatting name is what gets dropped,
and the root still reports created under the source's name.

WHAT TO EXPECT ON-BOX. Reload with the checkbox: the nested view gives
way to the relational root under the same name, plus the child tables
and the joinkeys hub. If DuckDB objects to anything further down the
18 statements, the card and the dashboard will name it.

build 2026-06-25.420  (v2.15.27)

An em-dash broke a PowerShell script; every script is now pure ASCII,
gated forever.

THE BUG. Run-SamQLTests failed to PARSE on-box: "missing terminator",
a phantom missing brace. The script contained two UTF-8 em-dashes (a
header comment and the Node warning string). PowerShell 5.1 reads
BOM-less scripts as ANSI, and the em-dash's UTF-8 bytes decode via
CP1252 into a sequence ENDING IN A CURLY DOUBLE QUOTE -- which PS 5.1
accepts as a real string delimiter. One invisible quote unbalanced
every string after it; the parser blamed the innocent Write-Host line
below.

THE FIX + THE GATE. Both dashes are plain "--" now, and a new suite
test walks EVERY checked-in PowerShell script byte by byte and fails on
anything above 0x7F, naming the file, line, and byte. This class --
smart quotes, em-dashes, non-breaking spaces pasted into a script --
can never reach your box again.

skipped. No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.416  (v2.15.23)

The tsc gate can never fail silently again.

THE REAL BUG. Both on-box failures printed "tsc reported type errors:"
with NOTHING after the colon. The typecheck script was `tsc -b` --
incremental BUILD mode. After a failing run, TypeScript caches the
failure in tsbuildinfo; an unchanged re-run exits 1 and prints NO
errors at all. So the gate was correctly failing while being unable to
say why -- and the .415 fix (real, but for the first run's error) could
not be confirmed either way through a mute gate.

TWO FIXES. The typecheck script is now a full, non-incremental listing:
`tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig json --pretty false` -- every error, every
run, no cached state. And the gate itself now detects the
exit-nonzero/empty-output combination, deletes any stale tsbuildinfo,
and re-runs tsc directly with the verbose flags -- so even if the
script regresses someday, the assertion always carries the actual error
lines.

ON-BOX, ONCE: delete frontend\tsconfig dot tsbuildinfo if it exists
(stale cache from the -b era), then re-run the suite. If the .415
ternary fix was the whole story the frontend line goes green; if
anything remains, the failure will now LIST it.

package json (frontend), run_tests.py. Suite: 599 passing, 0 failing,
21 skipped. No new dependencies.

Every Stop button cancels exactly ITS process -- and node flows are on

"Stop cancels everything" by design -- it interrupted the registered

build 2026-06-25.410  (v2.15.17)

Journal + Node audit: one fix (per-node heartbeats), the rest verified
and pinned.

THE FIX. A multi-node flow ran as a SILENT operation: no heartbeat
between node builds, so the Activity card sat blank and the watchdog
could stall-flag a perfectly healthy flow mid-node (then self-heal
after -- noise either way). Every per-node CREATE now pulses the run's
heartbeat first, so idle-seconds reset node by node and the stall
detector only fires when a node is genuinely wedged.

VERIFIED AND PINNED AS CONTRACTS. The journal chain's reuse pins are
refcounted under the lock, released in cleanup, and deferred discards
flush on the last unpin -- an evicted upstream can never be yanked out
from under a running chain. Chained cells run on the locked main
connection ON PURPOSE: their reuse views are TEMP and TEMP objects are
connection-local (the same reason flow temps live on the main
connection); everything heavy around them -- loads, plain queries,
shreds, flattens -- rides cursors, so the contention is bounded. The
flow builder cancels between nodes, attributes a failure to the exact
node with a cast hint, computes shared upstream nodes once, and drops
its temps on success and on both failure paths. Run-all's dependency
gate awaits a cell's own prior run exactly once (no re-run loops).

QUEUED (efficiency, not correctness): cursor-local reuse views would
let chained journal cells overlap the main connection; the final flow
node could skip its intermediate temp. Both are structural; neither
blocks anything today.

build 2026-06-25.406  (v2.15.13)

Loader + flattener audit: name-picking is race-free; everything else
verified clean, one queued gap.

THE FIND. _unique_name is a lock-free READ of the catalog. Under the
.402/.404 own-cursor concurrency, two overlapping ops (two loads, a
load + a flatten) could pick the SAME table name, and one CREATE would
then die on a write-write conflict. reserve_table_name() now picks AND
reserves atomically under the write lock (held only for the pick);
reservations self-prune the moment the table exists; a failed op
releases its name. Wired everywhere names are picked concurrently:
native loads (reserve before the possibly-null lock, release in the
finally) and all three flatten name picks (root/base, replace-swap,
promote). Executed matrix: same-base concurrent picks never collide,
released names are reusable, reservations self-prune.

VERIFIED CLEAN. tmp_dump is finally-cleaned on every exit; the deep
JSON load's typed re-parse falls back to the nested read for non-cancel
failures on ALL initial-load callers; the flattener tracks created
tables and drops them on error; its RENAME swap runs on real tables
only; cancel reaches every phase (cooperative flag + the .402/.404
interrupt sweeps).

QUEUED GAP (known, not fixed here): the load-toggle flattener uses its
own planner and does NOT emit the <base>_joinkeys hub that the
Field-Explorer shred adds. Workaround until then: use Create relational
tables from the Field Explorer when you want the hub.

build 2026-06-25.405  (v2.15.12)

Query-runtime audit: one critical fix (result files never delete
borrowed sources) and a clean bill elsewhere.

THE CRITICAL FIND. ParquetResultStore.close() unlinked its file
UNCONDITIONALLY -- but a .399 zero-copy result BORROWS the loaded
table's source cache parquet as its path. So evicting that result
(row/byte/disk budgets), releasing it (closing the tab), or shutting
down would DELETE the table's backing file: the next query dies with
"No files found that match the pattern". This may well have been the
original on-box trigger, and it would have recurred on every zero-copy
result. Stores now carry ownership: a borrowed file is never unlinked
and never counts toward the qr disk budget; owned result files delete
exactly as before. Executed test: borrowed survives close, owned is
deleted, the zero-copy constructor marks the borrow, the budget skips
borrowed files.

THE REST OF THE AUDIT, CLEAN. Query registration is symmetric (the
wrapper's finally covers the zero-copy early return; flows
register/unregister in pairs and their temp tables can't false-match
the zero-copy pattern). An evicted result pages back a clean "result
expired" -- never an IO error. Windows can't lose a page mid-read to an
eviction: unlink of an open file fails quietly and the file goes on the
next pass. The multi-statement editor path can't hit the zero-copy
regex (single bare statement only). Brief DDL stays on the locked main
connection by design; everything long rides its own cursor (.402/.404).

rows.py, session.py, run_tests.py. Suite: 589 passing, 0 failing, 21
skipped. No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.402  (v2.15.9)

Loads run concurrently: a second load no longer queues behind a running
conversion.

WHY THE LOAD MODAL FELT SERIALIZED. A native load -- one giant
CREATE TABLE ... AS SELECT FROM read_json/read_csv/read_parquet -- ran
under the GLOBAL engine write lock for its whole duration. Start a big
conversion, open the Load modal, pick a second file: its first engine
statement queued behind the entire first load. The frontend was already
fire-and-forget; the engine was the serializer.

THE FIX. When concurrent reads are on (the default rail queries already
use), a native load runs on its OWN cursor: a DuckDB cursor is its own
connection, MVCC takes two writers to DIFFERENT tables, and
_unique_name guarantees the tables differ. The write lock is not held
at all on this path, so loads overlap freely with each other and with
queries. Rails: any cursor failure falls back to the locked path
unchanged; every statement in the load goes through the chosen
connection; and the cursor registers in a per-engine _native_ops map
that interrupt() sweeps -- a cursor is invisible to the main-connection
interrupt, so without the sweep Stop and Reset engines couldn't reach
an own-cursor load. Executed test: flag + main connection + every
registered load cursor all receive the interrupt; deregistration and
cursor close are pinned in a finally.

engines.py, run_tests.py. Suite: 586 passing, 0 failing, 21 skipped.
No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.400  (v2.15.7)

Reset engines truly unclogs a stall, and "stalled" reflects the present.

1) RESET UNCLOGS. Reset already interrupted the MAIN connection and
   orphaned it -- but concurrent reads run on their OWN cursors, which

build 2026-06-25.391  (v2.14.5)

Build fix: dependency probes are stderr-free, so PowerShell 5.1 can't
kill the build at the first missing module.

The .389 probes ran `python -c "import X"` with stderr redirected. Under
Windows PowerShell 5.1 with ErrorActionPreference Stop, a native
command's stderr THROUGH A REDIRECT becomes a terminating
NativeCommandError -- so the very first missing module's ImportError
traceback aborted step 2/4 (the on-box failure) instead of adding it to
the install list.

Every probe (the manifest loop, the critical-four verify, and the
PyInstaller ensure) now uses importlib.util.find_spec and exits 0/1

build 2026-06-25.387  (v2.14.1)

Explode/UNNEST results page in milliseconds: store reads prune by
file_row_number instead of sorting the world.

The stall's true root, found by re-reading the on-box watchdog dump: the
wedged frame was ParquetResultStore._fetch -- paging an ALREADY
MATERIALIZED result. Unsorted pages ordered by "__rn", a SYNTHESIZED
expression (file_row_number + 1), and an ORDER BY over an expression
defeats row-group pruning: a 200-row first page planned a TopN across
EVERY row group of a multi-GB nested file -- minutes of native scan that
the first interrupt can miss. Deep UNNEST/explode results are exactly the
worst case: few rows cap-wise, enormous LIST/STRUCT columns per group.

The fix exploits what "__rn" already was: raw file_row_number IS
prunable. Unsorted paging now emits

    SELECT cols FROM read_parquet(store, file_row_number = true)
    WHERE file_row_number >= offset AND file_row_number < offset+limit
    ORDER BY file_row_number

so a page reads only the row group(s) it lands in -- same rows, same
order, tiny I/O, and trivially interruptible. Integer indexing prunes to
a single row's group; exports stream in raw file order with NO
synthesized sort planned. A USER sort keeps the legacy TopN (a genuine
reorder of the data is unavoidable). Combined with the existing 10M-row
producer cap and the .386 escalation, the explode-page-stall class is
closed: bounded write, pruned reads, re-fired cancels.

Executed tests against a recording engine pin all four SQL shapes: the
pruned unsorted page, the single-group integer index, the sort-free
export stream, and the untouched user-sort TopN.

rows.py, run_tests.py. Suite: 577 passing, 0 failing, 21 skipped. No new
dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.382  (v2.13.1)

The cancel-then-"Failed to fetch" sequence, closed at three layers.

On-box: a long query was cancelled, and the NEXT request died with the
browser's opaque "Failed to fetch". Root class: the abandoned response.
When a fetch is aborted, the server thread can still be writing the old
response onto that keep-alive socket; the write onto the dead/reused
connection raised, tore the connection mid-frame, and the browser's next
request on it failed at the socket level.

  1) SOCKET HYGIENE (server). Every response write is guarded: a
     BrokenPipe / ConnectionReset / ConnectionAborted from a vanished
     client is swallowed and the connection is RETIRED (close_connection)
     so the browser opens a fresh one -- never a torn keep-alive frame.
     The 500 path retires its connection too, and the file-download
     writer got the same guard.
  2) TRANSACTION HYGIENE (engine). A landed interrupt can strand an open
     transaction on the engine connection; the next statement then fails
     with "transaction aborted" instead of running. Both cancelled-return
     paths now run a best-effort ROLLBACK (lock-aware, 0.5 s patience;
     "no transaction active" is the healthy outcome and is swallowed).
  3) ONE CLEAN RETRY (IDE). If a run still hits a network-level failure,
     the IDE reaps any phantom run (cancel by id), waits 350 ms, and
     retries exactly once on a fresh connection and id. If THAT fails,
     the error message says what likely happened instead of the bare
     "Failed to fetch".

Tested: the dead-pipe write is swallowed and retires the connection while
a healthy write is untouched (executed against the real handler method);
the hygiene helper rolls back a stranded transaction and no-ops cleanly
on a quiet connection; both cancelled-returns, all three socket-retire
sites, and the single-retry wiring are pinned.

server.py, session.py, App.tsx, run_tests.py. Suite: 572 passing, 0
failing, 21 skipped. No new dependencies.

   prefix + the _rid key), so it also groups families built before this
   build.

3) ONE-CLICK JOINS. Every family child gets a small join affordance (and an
   "Insert join to <parent>" context item): one click writes
   SELECT * FROM parent JOIN child USING (<the shared _rid/_ord keys>) into
   the IDE editor and switches you there. No shared keys degrades to an
   honest placeholder instead of silently wrong SQL.

4) SHRED NODE (Nodebook). Flattening is now a workflow step: pick the loaded
   nested table + array column (dropdowns), optionally a family name, and
   the node outputs the family ROOT so downstream nodes chain off it. The
   CREATEs run once in a pre-pass before the flow composes -- upstream-gated
   (an unwired shred node never runs), reusing an existing family unless
   "Re-shred on every run" is on, and any failure names AND highlights the
   node.

In-depth tests: a streaming battery (byte-identical spooling through
adversarial boundary straddles at 7-byte reads, truncated-body cleanup,
no-boundary no-op), a families/join battery in the node harness (deepest-
prefix grouping, engine scoping, chain collapse, shared-key extraction, the
USING SQL, the honest no-keys case), a shred-node battery (reuse, refresh,
upstream gating, node-highlighted errors), plus frontend/backend port

build 2026-06-25.371  (v2.11.0)

NEW: Shred to relational -- nested JSON into joinable tables, in seconds.

The historical pain: flattening the big file relationally meant ~6M child
records, and row-by-row normalization (the approach packages like dlt /
pandas.json_normalize take) made that take forever. This feature does the
shred INSIDE DuckDB instead: one table per array level, each created by a
single vectorized CREATE TABLE .. AS over the column's PARQUET cache with
projection pushdown -- the cashflows table only ever reads the cashflows
subtree. Millions of child rows land in seconds, and the whole model is
plain SQL you can read.

  - Field explorer -> pick the nested column -> "Create relational tables...".
    The plan (derived from the parsed type tree) proposes one table per array
    level -- e.g. trades, trades_receivingleg, trades_receivingleg_cashflows,
    trades_payingleg -- with checkboxes, then creates the selected ones.
  - DETERMINISTIC KEYS so joins Just Work: every table carries _rid (the
    parquet file_row_number -- stable across restarts) plus one <level>_ord
    per array hop. Join a child to its parent with USING(the shared prefix).
    Keys are shown in the picker.
  - Parents keep their scalar/struct fields with child arrays EXCLUDEd (each
    gets its own table); arrays of scalars become a value column; mixed-case
    struct fields are always quoted; colliding names uniquify; deep trees cap
    at 40 tables with a note.
  - Cancellable between tables (partial list reported), keepalive-guarded per
    statement, progress on the dashboard, catalog + counts resync after.
    Requires a Parquet-backed load (the normal SamQL load); anything else
    gets a clear pointer.

Why not a pip package: dlt / json_normalize solve the same problem row-wise
in Python -- exactly the 6M-row bottleneck. The engine already shipped is the
fastest relational tool for this; what was missing was the plan generator,
now built from the same type tree the field explorer uses. Bundle grows to
104 files (new samql_core/shred.py).

shred.py (new), session.py, server.py, api.ts, FieldExplorer.tsx, App.tsx,
styles.css. Suite: 553 passing, 0 failing, 21 skipped (plan battery, executor
battery incl. cancel-partial + guidance, wiring). No new dependencies.

build 2026-06-25.370  (v2.10.99)

Across-the-board lockdown: result-store disk budget, reuse pins, and three
smaller guards.

MEMORY/DISK -- parquet result stores are now DISK-BUDGETED. They were only
count-capped (24), so a few multi-GB explode results could quietly pile up
tens of GB of qr_ files in temp. Their total size is now bounded by
SAMQL_RESULTS_GB (default 20, 0 disables, capped at 512), evicting
oldest-first -- never the newest result, never a pinned reuse source; a
pinned-only overflow stops safely instead of spinning. The in-memory row/byte
budget for list results is unchanged.

STABILITY -- reuse PINS. A result whose parquet store backs a live chain-
reuse view can no longer be yanked out from under the running query: the
source results are pinned for the lifetime of the views. While pinned, an
explicit discard is DEFERRED (the grid keeps paging) and executes the moment
cleanup drops the views; "Free unused memory" and the disk-budget eviction
both skip pinned sources.

Three smaller guards:
  - a reuse run never retries on a DIFFERENT engine after a missing-table
    error (its temp views wouldn't exist there -- the original error
    surfaces instead of a misleading "no such table cellN" from the wrong
    engine);
  - filecache BUDGET eviction exempts entries younger than 10 minutes
    (attached views from a live session) -- only the age rule can take
    those;
  - the disk budget adopts the suite-wide "0 disables" convention.

In-depth tests: disk-budget battery (oldest evicted to the budget; newest
always survives; pinned overflow stops safely), pin-lifecycle battery (pin
on setup; deferred discard with the grid still paging; unpin + flush on
cleanup; free_memory + fallback-gate anchored), and the fresh-entry
exemption in the sweep battery.

session.py, filecache.py, run_tests.py. Suite: 550 passing, 0 failing, 21
skipped. No new dependencies.
