    def t_mei_orphan_sweep():
        # Storage audit: onefile launch leftovers (_MEI*) are reclaimed at
        # open -- except the CURRENT extraction and anything young enough to
        # be another instance mid-launch.
        import tempfile as _tf
        import shutil as _sh
        from samql_core import tmputil as T
        root = _tf.mkdtemp(prefix="meiroot_")
        real_root, real_mei = T.mei_root, getattr(sys, "_MEIPASS", None)
        try:
            T.mei_root = lambda: root

            def mk(name, age_sec, size=1000):
                p = os.path.join(root, name)
                os.makedirs(p)
                with open(os.path.join(p, "lib.bin"), "wb") as f:
                    f.write(b"x" * size)
                t = time.time() - age_sec
                os.utime(p, (t, t))
                return p
            old = mk("_MEIold1", 7200, 5000)
            fresh = mk("_MEIfresh", 120, 5000)
            cur = mk("_MEIcurrent", 7200, 5000)
            sys._MEIPASS = cur
            other = mk("notmei", 7200)
            n, freed = T.sweep_mei_orphans()
            need(n == 1 and freed >= 5000 and not os.path.exists(old),
                 "an old orphan is removed and counted (n=%d freed=%d)"
                 % (n, freed))
            need(os.path.exists(fresh) and os.path.exists(cur)
                 and os.path.exists(other),
                 "fresh, current and non-MEI dirs are untouched")
        finally:
            T.mei_root = real_root
            if real_mei is None:
                try:
                    del sys._MEIPASS
                except AttributeError:
                    pass
            else:
                sys._MEIPASS = real_mei
            _sh.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_zombie_instance_sweep():
        # Storage audit: pid reuse. A pid-named dir whose process LOOKS alive
        # but whose liveness marker is ancient is a zombie -> removed; a
        # fresh marker (a real live instance) is never touched.
        import tempfile as _tf
        import shutil as _sh
        from samql_core import tmputil as T
        root = _tf.mkdtemp(prefix="samqlroot_")
        real_root, real_alive = T._ROOT, T.pid_alive
        try:
            T._ROOT = root
            T.pid_alive = lambda p: True   # every pid "alive": reuse world

            def inst(pid, marker_age):
                p = os.path.join(root, str(pid))
                os.makedirs(p)
                open(os.path.join(p, "qr_x.parquet"), "wb").write(b"d")
                mp = os.path.join(p, T._ALIVE)
                open(mp, "w").close()
                t = time.time() - marker_age
                os.utime(mp, (t, t))
                return p
            zombie = inst(11111, 3 * 24 * 3600)
            live = inst(22222, 60)
            # legacy dir (pre-marker build): falls back to the dir mtime
            legacy = os.path.join(root, "33333")
            os.makedirs(legacy)
            t = time.time() - 3 * 24 * 3600
            os.utime(legacy, (t, t))
            n = T.sweep_zombie_instances()
            need(n == 2 and not os.path.exists(zombie)
                 and not os.path.exists(legacy),
                 "zombies (ancient marker OR legacy old dir) are removed")
            need(os.path.exists(live), "a fresh marker is never touched")
            # touch_alive refreshes the marker for THIS instance
            T.touch_alive()
            mp = os.path.join(T.instance_dir(), T._ALIVE)
            need(os.path.exists(mp)
                 and time.time() - os.path.getmtime(mp) < 60,
                 "touch_alive keeps this instance fresh")
        finally:
            T._ROOT = real_root
            T.pid_alive = real_alive
            _sh.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_storage_endpoints():
        # Storage audit: the report measures every class honestly and the
        # clean action reclaims orphans + (explicitly) the conversion cache.
        import tempfile as _tf
        import shutil as _sh
        import server as _srv
        from samql_core import tmputil as T
        from samql_core import filecache as FC
        root = _tf.mkdtemp(prefix="samqlroot_")
        mroot = _tf.mkdtemp(prefix="meiroot_")
        fcd = os.path.join(root, "filecache")
        os.makedirs(fcd)
        saves = (T._ROOT, T.mei_root, T.pid_alive, FC._DIR)
        try:
            T._ROOT, FC._DIR = root, fcd
            T.mei_root = lambda: mroot
            T.pid_alive = lambda p: False
            dead = os.path.join(root, "99999")
            os.makedirs(dead)
            open(os.path.join(dead, "qr_a.parquet"), "wb").write(b"x" * 500)
            open(os.path.join(fcd, "fc_abc.parquet"), "wb").write(b"c" * 700)
            mei = os.path.join(mroot, "_MEIdead")
            os.makedirs(mei)
            open(os.path.join(mei, "l.bin"), "wb").write(b"m" * 300)
            t = time.time() - 7200
            os.utime(mei, (t, t))
            rep = _srv.Api.storage_report(None, None, {"fresh": 1}, None)
            need(rep["other_instances"]["count"] == 1
                 and rep["other_instances"]["dead"] == 1
                 and rep["other_instances"]["bytes"] >= 500,
                 "dead instances are measured: %r" % rep["other_instances"])
            need(rep["filecache"]["count"] == 1
                 and rep["filecache"]["bytes"] == 700
                 and rep["filecache"]["budget_gb"] > 0,
                 "the cache is measured with its budget")
            need(rep["mei_orphans"]["count"] == 1
                 and rep["mei_orphans"]["bytes"] == 300,
                 "launch leftovers are measured")
            # a YOUNG leftover (2 min): skipped by the automatic sweep's
            # hour guard, but a user-clicked clean takes it (60s guard)
            mei2 = os.path.join(mroot, "_MEIyoung")
            os.makedirs(mei2)
            open(os.path.join(mei2, "y.bin"), "wb").write(b"y" * 200)
            t2 = time.time() - 120
            os.utime(mei2, (t2, t2))
            r = _srv.Api.storage_clean(None, None, {"orphans": True}, None)
            need(r["freed"]["orphans"] >= 1000
                 and not os.path.exists(dead) and not os.path.exists(mei)
                 and not os.path.exists(mei2),
                 "the user clean takes dead instances + leftovers, young "
                 "ones included: %r" % r["freed"])
            need(r.get("note") is None,
                 "a full reclaim carries no caveat")
            # an unremovable leftover -> honest note, never a silent 0
            mei3 = os.path.join(mroot, "_MEIstuck")
            os.makedirs(mei3)
            open(os.path.join(mei3, "s.bin"), "wb").write(b"s" * 400)
            t3 = time.time() - 7200
            os.utime(mei3, (t3, t3))
            real_rm = T._rmtree
            T._rmtree = lambda p: None
            try:
                r = _srv.Api.storage_clean(None, None, {"orphans": True},
                                           None)
            finally:
                T._rmtree = real_rm
            need(r["freed"]["orphans"] == 0
                 and "in use" in (r.get("note") or ""),
                 "an unremovable leftover explains itself: %r"
                 % r.get("note"))
            import shutil as _sh2
            _sh2.rmtree(mei3, ignore_errors=True)
            need(os.path.exists(os.path.join(fcd, "fc_abc.parquet")),
                 "orphan cleaning NEVER touches the conversion cache")
            r2 = _srv.Api.storage_clean(None, None, {"filecache": True},
                                        None)
            need(r2["freed"]["filecache"] == 700
                 and not os.listdir(fcd),
                 "clearing the cache is explicit and reports the bytes")
        finally:
            T._ROOT, T.mei_root, T.pid_alive, FC._DIR = saves[0], saves[1], \
                saves[2], saves[3]
            _sh.rmtree(root, ignore_errors=True)
            _sh.rmtree(mroot, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_suite_temp_hygiene():
        # The runner's temp canary + teardown: every temp path the suite
        # creates is registered and reclaimed at the end, with the tally
        # printed -- leaky tests can never litter the box again.
        import tempfile as _tf
        # the canary is live in THIS process (main installed it)
        need(getattr(_tf, "_samql_canary", False),
             "the canary wraps tempfile for this run")
        d = _tf.mkdtemp(prefix="hyg_")
        f = _tf.NamedTemporaryFile(prefix="hyg_", delete=False)
        f.write(b"x" * 10)
        f.close()
        import __main__ as M
        need(d in M._TEMP_REGISTRY and f.name in M._TEMP_REGISTRY,
             "created paths are registered")
        n, freed = M._sweep_registered({d, f.name, d + "_ghost"})
        need(n == 2 and freed >= 10
             and not os.path.exists(d) and not os.path.exists(f.name),
             "the sweeper removes what exists and counts the bytes "
             "(n=%d freed=%d)" % (n, freed))
        src = open(os.path.abspath(M.__file__), encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("_install_temp_canary()" in src.split("def main(")[1]
             and "_sweep_registered(_TEMP_REGISTRY)" in src
             and "tmputil.sweep_stale()" in src.split("finally:", 1)[1]
             and "temp cleanup:" in src,
             "the runner installs the canary, sweeps, and prints the tally")

    def t_run_surface_meta():
        # .381: every run registers WHERE it came from (ide/journal/node) and
        # a human label; the stat modal groups running queries by these.
        from samql_core import progress as P
        P.begin("query", op_id="qq1", engine="duckdb",
                surface="ide", label="Tab 3")
        try:
            row = [o for o in P.snapshot() if o["id"] == "qq1"][0]
            need(row["surface"] == "ide" and row["label"] == "Tab 3",
                 "opreg snapshot carries surface + label: %r" % row)
        finally:
            P.end(op_id="qq1")
        # through the session's register path
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s._register_run("qq2", s.db, surface="journal", label="cell7")
            row = [o for o in P.snapshot() if o["id"] == "qq2"][0]
            need(row["surface"] == "journal" and row["label"] == "cell7",
                 "_register_run threads the meta through")
            s._unregister_run("qq2")
            # .516: a finished op lingers observable; it must be FINISHED
            # and no longer active
            _q2 = [o for o in P.snapshot() if o["id"] == "qq2"]
            need(all(o["finished"] for o in _q2) and P.count() == 0,
                 "unregister finishes it (linger-visible, not active)")
            # flow label helper: label > type > id
            g = {"nodes": [{"id": "n9", "type": "filter",
                            "config": {"label": "keep big"}}]}
            eq(s._flow_node_label(g, "n9"), "keep big", "cfg label wins")
            eq(s._flow_node_label({"nodes": [{"id": "n9",
                                              "type": "filter"}]}, "n9"),
               "filter", "type is the fallback")
            eq(s._flow_node_label({}, "zz"), "zz", "id is the last resort")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
        # run_query accepts and forwards the meta (signature-level)
        import inspect
        ps = set(inspect.signature(
            __import__("samql_core.session",
                       fromlist=["Session"]).Session.run_query
        ).parameters)
        need({"surface", "label"} <= ps,
             "run_query carries surface/label")
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('surface=b.get("surface")' in srv
             and 'label=b.get("label")' in srv,
             "the query handler passes both through")
        sess = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(sess.count('surface="node"') >= 5
             and "_flow_node_label(graph, node_id)" in sess,
             "flow runs register as node-surface with the node's label")

    def t_duckdb_timestamptz_pytz():
        # DuckDB's Python bindings hard-require pytz when converting
        # TIMESTAMPTZ to Python (current_timestamp / NOW() / tz columns).
        # Without it, NodeFlow and query fetch raise
        # "Required module 'pytz' failed to import". Packaging must list
        # and collect pytz; runtime must import it when DuckDB is present.
        req = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "requirements-optional.txt"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(any(ln.strip() == "pytz" for ln in req.splitlines()),
             "requirements-optional.txt installs pytz")
        spec = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql.spec"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('"pytz"' in spec and '"tzdata", "pytz"]' in spec,
             "samql.spec REQUIRES pytz (collect_all + refuse if missing)")
        from samql_core.engines import HAS_DUCKDB
        if not HAS_DUCKDB:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        import importlib.util as _ilu
        need(_ilu.find_spec("pytz") is not None,
             "pytz is importable alongside DuckDB")
        import duckdb as _ddb
        row = _ddb.connect().execute("SELECT current_timestamp").fetchone()
        need(row is not None and row[0] is not None,
             "DuckDB TIMESTAMPTZ fetch succeeds with pytz installed")

    def t_socket_hygiene():
        # The cancel-then-"Failed to fetch" sequence (on-box 2026-07-02):
        # a response write onto a dead/aborted client socket must never
        # escape (it tears the keep-alive connection mid-frame); the 500
        # path retires its connection; a landed interrupt leaves the engine
        # connection clean; and the IDE retries ONCE on a network failure.
        import server as _srv
        import types as _types

        class _DeadPipe:
            def write(self, b):
                raise BrokenPipeError("client went away")

        class _H:
            command = "POST"
            close_connection = False
            headers = {}
            wfile = _DeadPipe()

            def send_response(self, *_a):
                pass

            def send_header(self, *_a):
                pass

            def end_headers(self):
                pass

            def _cors(self):
                pass
        h = _H()
        h._send_bytes_raw = _types.MethodType(
            _srv.Handler._send_bytes_raw, h)
        _types.MethodType(_srv.Handler._send_bytes, h)(
            200, b"x" * 10, "application/json")
        need(h.close_connection is True,
             "a dead-client write is swallowed and retires the connection")
        # success path still writes
        got = []

        class _OkPipe:
            def write(self, b):
                got.append(b)
        h2 = _H()
        h2.close_connection = False
        h2.wfile = _OkPipe()
        h2._send_bytes_raw = _types.MethodType(
            _srv.Handler._send_bytes_raw, h2)
        _types.MethodType(_srv.Handler._send_bytes, h2)(
            200, b"ok", "text/plain")
        need(got == [b"ok"] and h2.close_connection is False,
             "a healthy write is untouched")
        # post-interrupt hygiene: swallows everywhere, rolls back where a
        # transaction is stranded
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s._post_interrupt_hygiene("local")   # no txn: healthy no-op
            calls = []

            class _Eng:
                conn = type("C", (), {"execute":
                                      staticmethod(
                                          lambda q: calls.append(q))})()
                write_lock = threading.Lock()
            real = s._engine_obj
            s._engine_obj = lambda t: (_Eng(), "duckdb")
            try:
                s._post_interrupt_hygiene("duckdb")
            finally:
                s._engine_obj = real
            eq(calls, ["ROLLBACK"], "a stranded transaction is rolled back")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
        # wiring: both cancelled-returns call the hygiene; the 500 path and
        # the download writer retire their connections; the IDE retries once
        sess = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        eq(sess.count("self._post_interrupt_hygiene(first_target)"), 2,
           "both cancelled-returns leave the connection clean")
        srv_src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                       encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(srv_src.count("self.close_connection = True") >= 3,
             "write guard + 500 path + download writer all retire sockets")
        app = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "App.tsx"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("if (network && !_retry && !wasCancelled(queryId))" in app
             and "return runResolved(trimmed, true, previewLimit, tabId)" in app,
             "the IDE retries a network-failed run once -- never for a "
             "run the user cancelled (.519)")

    def t_flatten_deep_recursion():
        # .423 deep audit conclusion, pinned. WHY it "still" would not
        # flatten: (a) the load toggle NEVER used the engine -- it
        # streamed the file through the Python flattener, which failed
        # on the sophis shape and silently fell back to a nested load;
        # (b) the sophis json column is a top-level LIST of records, so
        # ONE unnest level still leaves records nested inside the
        # child. Fixes: the toggle now rides nested-load-then-
        # in-engine-flatten (behavior test above), and the unnest
        # flatten RECURSES: any child still carrying LIST/STRUCT
        # columns is flattened again in place, each level with its own
        # synthesized key (_rowkey, _rowkey2, ...), depth-capped, with
        # a hard table budget, sharing the run registration (one
        # dashboard op, one precise cancel).
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        i = src.index("def _duckdb_unnest_flatten")
        # .501 widened: the replace-mode family handling grew the function
        body = src[i:i + 18000]
        checks = [
            ("depth + registration guards in the signature",
             "replace=False, depth=0," in body
             and "max_depth=3, _registered=False" in body),
            ("per-depth synthesized keys",
             '"_rowkey" if depth == 0' in body
             and '"_rowkey%d" % (depth + 1)' in body),
            ("recursion re-enters on nested children, in place",
             "self._duckdb_unnest_flatten(\n                        "
             "child, query_id=query_id," in body
             and "replace=True, depth=depth + 1," in body),
            ("hard table budget + cancel propagation",
             "len(mgr.table_columns) > 200" in body
             and 'sub.get("cancelled")' in body),
            ("one registration across the whole recursion",
             "if not _registered:" in body
             and body.count("if not _registered:") == 2),
            ("the hub is renamed with the tree and reported",
             "hub_name = plan.get(\"hub\")" in body
             and "([hub_name] if hub_name else [])" in body),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "deep recursion: " + "; ".join(missing))
        # the planner honors a per-depth synthesized key name (pure)
        from samql_core import flatten as F
        pl = F.duckdb_unnest_plan(
            "c", {"x": "BIGINT", "arr": "STRUCT(v BIGINT)[]"},
            "c_flat", detect=False, synth_key="_rowkey2")
        blob = " ".join(st["sql"] for st in pl["statements"])
        need('"_rowkey2"' in blob and pl["key"] == "_rowkey2",
             "planner threads the depth key: %s" % pl["key"])

    def t_shred_after_load_visible():
        # .423 deep audit of "it's still not flattening!!": the modal
        # checkbox is the SHREDDER-after-load, and its pipeline was
        # green at every hop EXCEPT the last two -- (a) the eligibility
        # gate was a storage-string allowlist that could skip an item
        # silently (no note, no shred), and (b) only the SUCCESS branch
        # was ever surfaced on the load card: shred_error, the
        # nothing-to-shred note, and cancels were stamped on items and
        # shown NOWHERE. Now: the gate is simply "a DuckDB table" (the
        # candidate scan decides the rest, with an HONEST note when the
        # type scan itself fails), the job records that flatten was
        # requested, and EVERY branch lands on the card note.
        import types as _t
        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            calls = []
            _saved_duck = sess.duckdb
            sess.duckdb = object()  # non-None gate
            # .474: flatten is TABLE-LEVEL -- _shred_after_load calls
            # flatten_table(table) once per item, not a per-column loop.
            sess.flatten_table = lambda tbl, base=None, **kw: (
                calls.append((tbl, base))
                or {"ok": True, "created": [
                    {"name": tbl, "kind": "base"},
                    {"name": tbl + "_flattened", "kind": "joinkeys"},
                    {"name": tbl + "_fees", "kind": "list"}]})
            loaded = [{"engine": "duckdb", "name": "soph"}]  # NO storage
            out = sess._shred_after_load(loaded)
            need(calls == [("soph", "soph")]
                 and out[0].get("shredded")
                 == ["soph", "soph_flattened", "soph_fees"],
                 "a storage-less DuckDB item flattens (the allowlist is "
                 "gone): %r" % out)
            # a flatten error lands on the item, never silently
            sess.flatten_table = lambda *a, **k: {"error": "boom"}
            out2 = sess._shred_after_load(
                [{"engine": "duckdb", "name": "x"}])
            eq(out2[0].get("shred_error"), "boom",
               "a flatten error is surfaced, not 'nothing to do'")
        finally:
            sess.duckdb = _saved_duck   # restore so shutdown() works
            sess.shutdown()
        import server as _srv
        job = {"shred": True}
        _srv._shred_note(job, [{"shred_error": "kapow"}])
        eq(job["note"], "flatten failed: kapow",
           "errors reach the card")
        job = {"shred": True}
        _srv._shred_note(job, [{"shred_note": "no nested array columns "
                                "to flatten"}])
        need(job["note"].startswith("flatten: no nested"),
             "the nothing-to-do note reaches the card")
        job = {"shred": True}
        _srv._shred_note(job, [{}])
        need("flatten requested" in job.get("note", ""),
             "even a fully silent item leaves a diagnosable note")
        job = {"shred": True}
        _srv._shred_note(job, [{"shredded": ["a", "b", "c"]}])
        eq(job["note"], "+3 relational tables", "success still counts")
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(srv.count('"shred": bool(locals().get("shred"))') == 2,
             "both load jobs record the request")
        shared = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src",
                                   "components", "ActivityShared.tsx"),
                      encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("{t.note ? ` · ${t.note}` : \"\"}" in shared,
             "the card renders the note")

    def t_flatten_wrapper_descent():
        # .422: BOTH on-box flatten complaints were one planner bug --
        # duckdb_unnest_plan scanned TOP-LEVEL columns only, and sophis
        # tables carry a single top-level STRUCT with every array buried
        # inside. Flatten-on-load planned nothing ("won't flatten") and
        # right-click hit the struct-only branch that kept the blob
        # nested (the "partial JSON"). The planner now DESCENDS plain
        # struct wrappers: every LIST at a dotted path becomes a child
        # table (UNNEST on the dotted source), every scalar/MAP leaf
        # becomes a readable dotted root column (the root is actually
        # flat), and a <root>_joinkeys hub carries the row key plus
        # identifier-ish leaves -- the .406 promise. All pure-SQL
        # planning, executed here on a sophis-mini schema.
        from samql_core import flatten as F
        coltypes = {
            "json": ('STRUCT(code BIGINT, '
                     'identifier MAP(VARCHAR, JSON), '
                     'quote STRUCT("last price" DOUBLE, ric VARCHAR), '
                     'SwapHistory STRUCT(resetDates STRUCT(items '
                     'STRUCT(d DATE, v DOUBLE)[]), dayType VARCHAR), '
                     'tags VARCHAR[])'),
            "loaded_at": "TIMESTAMP",
        }
        plan = F.duckdb_unnest_plan("t", coltypes, "t_flat")
        kinds = [st["kind"] for st in plan["statements"]]
        eq(kinds, ["staging", "root", "child", "child", "hub"],
           "plan shape: keyed staging, flat root, two children, hub")
        blob = " ".join(st["sql"] for st in plan["statements"])
        checks = [
            ("nested struct-array child unnests the DOTTED path",
             '"json"."SwapHistory"."resetDates"."items"' in blob),
            ("nested scalar-array child too",
             'UNNEST("json"."tags")' in blob),
            ("root carries dotted leaves with readable aliases",
             '"json"."code" AS "json_code"' in blob
             and '"json"."quote"."last price" AS '
                 '"json_quote_last_price"' in blob),
            ("MAP stays a leaf column (keys are data, not schema)",
             '"json"."identifier" AS "json_identifier"' in blob),
            ("the wrapper blob itself is excluded from the root",
             'EXCLUDE ("json")' in blob),
            ("the hub joins on the row key and carries idents",
             plan["hub"] == "t_flat_flattened"
             and '"json"."code"' in [st["sql"] for st in
                                     plan["statements"]
                                     if st["kind"] == "hub"][0]),
            ("children map reports dotted sources",
             all("." in v or v == "tags"
                 for v in plan["children"].values())
             and any(v == "json.SwapHistory.resetDates.items"
                     for v in plan["children"].values())),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "wrapper descent: " + "; ".join(missing))
        flat = F.duckdb_unnest_plan("p", {"a": "BIGINT"}, "p_flat")
        need(flat["children"] == {} and flat["hub"] is None,
             "a truly flat table keeps the old single-copy branch")
        fs = F._split_struct_fields(
            'STRUCT("we""ird" MAP(VARCHAR, JSON), ok BIGINT)')
        eq(fs, [('we"ird', 'MAP(VARCHAR, JSON)'), ('ok', 'BIGINT')],
           "the type-string splitter survives quoted names + nesting")

    def t_plan_pass13_packaging_launcher():
        # .456 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 13 (packaging + launcher). VERDICT:
        # CLEAN x17 on the sandbox-executable half -- the fifth clean
        # subsystem -- with the Windows-only half turned into an
        # explicit on-box checklist (WINDOWS_BUILD_CHECKLIST, file
        # 112) so the manual steps are as unambiguous as the
        # automated ones. EXECUTED HERE: port_open answers true on a
        # live listener and false on a closed port -- the launcher's
        # single-instance-by-port contract rides on it (the main flow
        # is pinned: a live port SKIPS start_server and opens the
        # window onto the running instance; a dead one starts, waits
        # 30 s, then fails VISIBLY; --no-server never starts). The
        # launcher log rotates at exactly 200 lines keeping the
        # newest, timestamped. clean_child_env scrubs _MEIPASS2 and
        # every _PYI_* variable and drops the launcher's own MEIPASS
        # from PATH while keeping everything else -- the .421 fix for
        # frozen children pinning the extraction dir, now enforced.
        # server_candidates matches Start-SamQL-AppWindow[.]ps1: source
        # backend/server.py first (current UI/API), then exe beside the
        # launcher, then dist\\, then frozen self-serve last. The temp
        # root honors SAMQL_TMP and defaults under the system tempdir.
        # DRIFT PINS: the VERSION header equals __version__ and BUILD.
        # THE PIPELINE: the ship-email defang is REVERSIBLE byte-exact on
        # the real expand script, and the spec bundles samql_core, names
        # the exe SamQL, and treats the icon as optional.
        import re as _re, socket as _sk, tempfile as _tf
        _tmp = _tf.mkdtemp()
        _old_env = os.environ.get("SAMQL_TMP")
        os.environ["SAMQL_TMP"] = _tmp
        import launcher_app as LA
        import importlib as _il
        _il.reload(LA)
        try:
            srv = _sk.socket()
            srv.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
            srv.listen(1)
            live = srv.getsockname()[1]
            need(LA.port_open(live) is True,
                 "port_open sees a live listener")
            srv.close()
            probe = _sk.socket()
            probe.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
            deadp = probe.getsockname()[1]
            probe.close()
            need(LA.port_open(deadp) is False,
                 "port_open sees a closed port")
            for i in range(250):
                LA.write_log("line-%03d" % i)
            with open(LA.launcher_log_path(),
                      encoding="utf-8") as f:
                lines = f.readlines()
            need(len(lines) == 200 and "line-249" in lines[-1]
                 and not any("line-000" in l for l in lines),
                 "the log rotates at 200 keeping the newest")
            need(_re.match(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2} "
                           r"\d{2}:\d{2}:\d{2} ", lines[0]),
                 "log lines are timestamped")
            # .465: build PATH with os.pathsep -- on the real Windows
            # box the ':'-joined fixture read as ONE entry, so the
            # (correct, per-platform) scrub emptied it and the pin
            # blamed the product.
            poison = {"_MEIPASS2": "x",
                      "_PYI_APPLICATION_HOME_DIR": "y",
                      "PATH": os.pathsep.join(
                          ["/usr/bin", "/fake/_MEI123"]),
                      "KEEP": "1"}

            class _FS:
                _MEIPASS = "/fake/_MEI123"
            real_sys = LA.sys
            LA.sys = _FS
            try:
                out = LA.clean_child_env(poison)
            finally:
                LA.sys = real_sys
            need("_MEIPASS2" not in out
                 and not any(k.startswith("_PYI_") for k in out)
                 and out["PATH"] == "/usr/bin"
                 and out["KEEP"] == "1",
                 "child env scrubbed of the PyInstaller runtime")
            kinds = [(k, os.path.basename(p))
                     for k, p in LA.server_candidates(base="/app")]
            need(kinds[0] == ("py", "server.py")
                 and ("exe", "SamQL[.]exe") in kinds
                 and kinds.index(("py", "server.py"))
                 < kinds.index(("exe", "SamQL[.]exe")),
                 "candidate order py -> exe -> dist (matches PS1)")
            eq(LA._temp_root(), _tmp, "temp root honors SAMQL_TMP")
            src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                       encoding="utf-8").read()
            need("if not port_open(args.port):" in src
                 and src.index("if not port_open")
                 < src.index("find_browser(args.browser)"),
                 "a live port REUSES the instance, never restarts")
            need("def wait_for_server_ready" in src
                 and "SERVER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_S = 300" in src
                 and "SERVER_BOOT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S = 90" in src
                 and "wait_for_server_ready(args.port, splash)" in src
                 and "did not come up" in src
                 and "exited before it was" in src
                 and "--no-server" in src
                 and "_server_alive_now(port)" in src
                 and "Waiting for SamQL to be ready" in src,
                 "heartbeat boot wait: child-death fail, idle+absolute "
                 "ceilings, /api/health readiness (not TCP alone)")
            need('background_color=CHROME_BG' in src
                 and 'CHROME_BG = "#16181d"' in src
                 and 'webview.create_window("SamQL"' in src,
                 "native window uses a dark WebView2 background "
                 "(avoids the white first-open flash)")
            need(LA.SERVER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_S == 300,
                 "absolute boot ceiling is 300 s (close-stops-server "
                 "colder starts + OneDrive/AV)")
            need(LA.SERVER_BOOT_IDLE_TIMEOUT_S == 90,
                 "boot idle timeout is 90 s (no heartbeat)")
            need(LA._MUTEX_BOOT_WAIT_S == float(LA.SERVER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_S),
                 "mutex boot wait tracks the server boot budget "
                 "(no stale-mutex second-server race)")
            need(LA.APP_WINDOW_WAIT_S >= 75.0
                 and LA._MUTEX_WINDOW_GRACE_S >= 100.0,
                 "window wait / grace budgets cover WebView2 cold start")
            from samql_core import __version__, BUILD
            vh = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION"),
                      encoding="utf-8").read()
            need(("Product version: %s" % __version__) in vh
                 and ("Current build:   %s" % BUILD) in vh,
                 "VERSION header tracks __init__ exactly")
            exp = open(_root_script("Expand-SamQL[.]ps1"),
                       encoding="utf-8").read()
            _bd = "[" + "." + "]"   # built, never literal: refang-safe
            # The distributed helper intentionally keeps executable/script
            # extensions defanged inside its own examples. Validate the full
            # transport round-trip from that canonical representation rather
            # than requiring an obsolete raw-extension source fixture.
            refanged = _re.sub(
                r"\[\.\](exe|dll|msi|bat|cmd|scr|vbs|ps1|jar)"
                r"(?![A-Za-z0-9])",
                lambda m: "." + m.group(1), exp)
            d = _re.sub(r"\.(exe|dll|msi|bat|cmd|scr|vbs|ps1|jar)"
                        r"(?![A-Za-z0-9])",
                        lambda m: _bd + m.group(1), refanged)
            need(refanged != exp and d == exp and _bd in refanged,
                 "the ship defang is reversible without rewriting literal "
                 "bracketed-dot markers")
            spec = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql.spec"),
                        encoding="utf-8").read()
            need('hiddenimports = ["samql_core", "samql_instance"]' in spec
                 and 'name="SamQL"' in spec
                 and "_brand.app_ico()" in spec
                 and "overwrite unconditionally" in spec,
                 "the spec bundles the core and regenerates the icon from "
                 "_brand every build (overwriting any stale file)")
            need(os.path.isfile(os.path.join(
                ROOT, "WINDOWS_BUILD_CHECKLIST.txt")),
                "the on-box checklist ships with the repo")
        finally:
            if _old_env is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_TMP", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_TMP"] = _old_env

    def t_plan_pass12_fe_state():
        # .455 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 12 (frontend state machines).
        # VERDICT: CLEAN -- the fourth clean subsystem; four sweeps,
        # zero fixes needed, four invariants enforced dir-wide so it
        # stays that way. (1) DRAG CANNOT STRAND: every file that
        # starts a drag (drag.current = { / resizing.current =) must
        # either listen for mouseup/pointerup on WINDOW or use pointer
        # capture with an onPointerUp -- releasing outside the element
        # always ends the drag (FloatingPanel rides capture; NodeFlow,
        # DataGrid, ActivityShared ride window listeners). (2) ASYNC
        # EFFECTS ARE GUARDED: every useEffect that awaits the api and
        # sets state carries a liveness/sequence guard (alive /
        # cancelled / AbortController / seq token / poll gate) -- the
        # .439 latest-wins discipline, now enforced for every FUTURE
        # effect. (3) REF MAPS GET CLEANED: every useRef<Map|Record>
        # has at least one delete/clear/reassign site in its file, so
        # per-entity caches cannot grow forever across a long session.
        # (4) STORAGE KEYS ARE FROZEN: the exact localStorage key
        # inventory is pinned (all samql.-prefixed); adding a key is a
        # conscious act that updates this list.
        import re as _re, glob as _g
        FE = os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src")

        def _production_ts(path):
            # Wave 2 added rendered-component fixtures under frontend/src.
            # They intentionally seed localStorage with migration values and
            # must not become part of the PRODUCT storage-key inventory.
            norm = path.replace("\\", "/")
            base = os.path.basename(path)
            return ("/test/" not in norm
                    and not _re.search(
                        r"(?:\.component)?\.test\.[tj]sx?$", base))

        files = [f for pat in ("*.tsx", "*.ts")
                 for f in _g.glob(os.path.join(FE, "**", pat),
                                  recursive=True)
                 if _production_ts(f)]
        drag_bad, eff_bad, map_bad = [], [], []
        keys = set()
        storage_call = _re.compile(
            r'(?:window\.)?localStorage(?:\?\.|\.)'
            r'(?:getItem|setItem|removeItem)\(\s*["\']([^"\']+)["\']',
            _re.S)
        for f in files:
            src = open(f, encoding="utf-8").read()
            name = os.path.basename(f)
            if f.endswith(".tsx") and _re.search(
                    r"(drag|resizing)(Ref)?\.current = \{", src):
                winup = _re.search(
                    r'addEventListener\("(mouse|pointer)up"', src)
                capture = ("setPointerCapture" in src
                           and "onPointerUp" in src)
                if not (winup or capture):
                    drag_bad.append(name)
            if f.endswith(".tsx"):
                for m in _re.finditer(
                        r"useEffect\(\(\) => \{(.*?)\n  \}, \[",
                        src, _re.S):
                    body = m.group(1)
                    if ("api." in body
                            and _re.search(r"\bset[A-Z]", body)
                            and ("await " in body or ".then(" in body)):
                        if not any(k in body for k in (
                                "alive", "cancelled", "AbortController",
                                "Seq.current", "polling.current",
                                "my ==")):
                            eff_bad.append(
                                (name, src[:m.start()].count("\n") + 1))
                owner_src = (
                    _nodeflow_source()
                    if (name == "NodeFlow.tsx"
                        or "/components/nodeflow/" in f.replace("\\", "/"))
                    else src
                )
                for m in _re.finditer(
                        r"const (\w+) = useRef<(?:Map|Record)", src):
                    nm = m.group(1)
                    if not _re.search(
                            nm + r"\.current\.(delete|clear)\(|"
                            r"delete " + nm + r"\.current\[|"
                            + nm + r"\.current = (new Map|\{\})", owner_src):
                        map_bad.append((name, nm))
            keys |= set(storage_call.findall(src))
        need(not drag_bad,
             "every drag ends outside the element too: %r" % drag_bad)
        need(not eff_bad,
             "every awaiting effect is liveness-guarded: %r"
             % eff_bad)
        need(not map_bad,
             "every ref map has a cleanup site: %r" % map_bad)
        # Visual toggles: Sphere nodes (default on), Node Snap (default off),
        # Hover-open tables drawer (default off).
        eq(keys, {"samql.editorIvory", "samql.reduceMotion",
                  "samql.eyeCare", "samql.nodeFlowDense",
                  "samql.nodeSphere", "samql.nodeSnap",
                  "samql.tablesDrawerHoverOpen",
                  "samql.nbMinimapMini", "samql.nb2.paletteHidden",
                  "samql.canvasIvory", "samql.theme"},
           "the direct storage-key inventory is frozen and namespaced")
        model = open(os.path.join(FE, "lib", "nodeFlowModel.ts"),
                     encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('"samql.nodeflow.favorites.v1"' in model
             and '"samql.nodebook.favorites.v1"' in model,
             "NodeFlow keeps a canonical favorites key and an explicit "
             "legacy Nodebook migration key")

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_per_statement_run_all():
        # .458 FEATURE: per-statement results on Run-all. run_script
        # splits with the audited scanner and runs each statement
        # through the NORMAL single-run path -- same connection so
        # temp state persists, same query_id so cancel reaches the
        # current statement -- and returns a LEDGER: index, trimmed
        # preview, elapsed ms, and a private pageable result_id for
        # every row-producing statement. BACK-COMPAT: the top level is
        # still the last row-producing statement's payload byte-for-
        # byte shape-wise, and plain run_query is untouched (no
        # "statements" key). SEMANTICS: a mid-batch error stops the
        # script, names failed_statement, and earlier statements'
        # results stay usable; scripts managing their OWN transactions
        # (BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK) fall back to the classic one-batch
        # run -- per-statement autocommit would change their meaning
        # -- and the ledger carries a note saying so; read_only is
        # enforced per statement; a single statement gains a trivial
        # one-entry ledger. Over HTTP, /api/query grows an opt-in
        # per_statement flag; without it the wire shape is unchanged.
        import json as _json, time as _tm, threading as _th
        import urllib.request as _ur
        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            r = sess.run_script(
                "CREATE TABLE m(x); INSERT INTO m VALUES (1),(2); "
                "SELECT x FROM m; "
                "SELECT x*10 AS y FROM m ORDER BY x DESC",
                target="auto")
            st = r["statements"]
            eq(len(st), 4, "four ledger entries")
            eq(sum(1 for e in st if e.get("result_id")), 2,
               "two row-producing statements")
            need(r["rows"] == [[20], [10]]
                 and r["result_id"] == st[3]["result_id"],
                 "top level = the LAST select (back-compat)")
            eq(sess.page(st[2]["result_id"], limit=10)["rows"],
               [[1], [2]],
               "an earlier statement's result is its own page")
            need(st[1].get("result_id") is None
                 and st[1]["total_rows"] == 0,
                 "DDL/DML entries carry counts, not results")
            need(all(isinstance(e.get("ms"), int) for e in st),
                 "every entry is timed")
            r2 = sess.run_script(
                "SELECT 1 AS a; SELECT * FROM missing_t; SELECT 2",
                target="auto")
            need(len(r2["statements"]) == 2
                 and r2.get("failed_statement") == 1
                 and "missing_t" in str(r2.get("error")),
                 "a mid-batch error stops, names its statement")
            eq(sess.page(r2["statements"][0]["result_id"])["rows"],
               [[1]], "results before the failure stay usable")
            r3 = sess.run_script(
                "BEGIN; INSERT INTO m VALUES (9); COMMIT; "
                "SELECT count(*) AS n FROM m", target="auto")
            need(len(r3["statements"]) == 1
                 and "transaction" in str(
                     r3["statements"][0].get("note"))
                 and r3.get("rows") == [[3]],
                 "txn scripts run as ONE batch, and say so")
            r4 = sess.run_script("SELECT 42 AS v", target="auto")
            need(len(r4["statements"]) == 1
                 and r4["rows"] == [[42]],
                 "a single statement gains a trivial ledger")
            r5 = sess.run_script("SELECT 1; CREATE TABLE ro2(x)",
                                 target="auto", read_only=True)
            need(r5.get("failed_statement") == 1
                 and "read-only" in str(r5.get("error")).lower(),
                 "read_only is enforced per statement")
            r6 = sess.run_query("SELECT 1; SELECT 2", target="auto")
            need("statements" not in r6 and r6["rows"] == [[2]],
                 "plain run_query is untouched")
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()
        import server as _sv
        httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port = httpd.server_address[1]
        _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm.sleep(0.2)
        try:
            def post(body):
                rq = _ur.Request(
                    "http://127.0.0.1:%d/api/query" % port,
                    data=_json.dumps(body).encode(),
                    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                    method="POST")
                with _api_urlopen(httpd, rq, timeout=25) as x:
                    return _json.loads(x.read().decode())
            w = post({"sql": "SELECT 1 AS a; SELECT 2 AS b",
                      "per_statement": True})
            need(len(w.get("statements") or []) == 2
                 and w["rows"] == [[2]],
                 "the flag rides the wire: %r"
                 % list(w.get("statements") or []))
            wo = post({"sql": "SELECT 1 AS a; SELECT 2 AS b"})
            need("statements" not in wo,
                 "without the flag the wire shape is unchanged")
        finally:
            httpd.shutdown()
        app = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "App.tsx"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        css = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "styles.css"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("per_statement: true" in app
             and "const openStmt" in app
             and app.count("openStmt(") >= 1
             and "stmtStrip(activeResultTab)" in app
             and app.count("statements:") >= 3
             and ".stmt-pill" in css,
             "the IDE requests the ledger, renders the strip, and "
             "every tab-write site stores it")

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_audit2_464_engines():
        # .464 AUDIT PASS II (1/2): fresh angles on query runs, loads,
        # and reconcile -- nothing here re-proves an old pin. QUERY
        # RUNS: infinities survive the JSON wire as "inf"/"-inf"
        # strings, never a crash; the full-cell fetch contract
        # (cell_value takes the column NAME) returns the whole value
        # with its keys; cancelling a script mid-flight lands a ledger
        # whose later statements never ran while the finished one
        # still pages; a script and a query racing on one session
        # both land. RECONCILE PRODUCTION: currency-string balances
        # ("$1,000.50") parse into exact matching sums; a matching
        # drill REQUIRES a field (documented contract, clean error)
        # and with one produces [key, A, B] columns keyed exactly,
        # even for hostile table names; summaries carry null_keys; no
        # __samql temp tables survive. LOADS: two concurrent loads
        # into the SAME base name land as name + name_2, both intact.
        import json as _json, time as _tm, threading as _th
        import csv as _csv, tempfile as _tf, os as _os
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            from samql_core.session import LOCAL_TARGET as _LT
            r = s.run_query("SELECT 9e999 AS pinf, -9e999 AS ninf, "
                            "1.5 AS ok", target=_LT)
            row = s.page(r["result_id"], 0, 1)["rows"][0]
            wire = _json.dumps(row)
            need("inf" in wire.lower() and "1.5" in wire,
                 "infinities ride the wire as strings: %s" % wire)
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE bigcell AS SELECT 1 AS k, "
                        "REPLACE(HEX(ZEROBLOB(500000)), '0', 'x') "
                        "AS huge", target=_LT)
            rr = s.run_query("SELECT * FROM bigcell", target=_LT)
            cv = s.cell_value(rr["result_id"], 0, "huge")
            need(len(cv.get("value") or "") == 1000000
                 and set(cv) >= {"value", "column", "row"},
                 "cell_value(name) returns the WHOLE value + keys")
            out = {}

            def scr():
                out["r"] = s.run_script(
                    "SELECT 41 AS a; "
                    "WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL "
                    "SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<20000000) "
                    "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c; "
                    "SELECT 43 AS z", query_id="a3")
            th = _th.Thread(target=scr)
            th.start()
            _tm.sleep(0.5)
            s.cancel_query("a3")
            th.join(30)
            led = (out.get("r") or {}).get("statements") or []
            need(led and not th.is_alive(), "cancel landed a ledger")
            first = led[0]
            need(first.get("result_id")
                 and s.page(first["result_id"], 0, 1)["rows"]
                 == [[41]],
                 "the finished statement still pages [[41]]")
            need(len(led) < 3 or not (led[2] or {}).get("result_id"),
                 "the statement after the cancel never ran")
            race = {}

            def q():
                race["q"] = s.run_query("SELECT 7 AS s", target=_LT)

            def sc():
                race["s"] = s.run_script("SELECT 8 AS t", target=_LT)
            t1, t2 = _th.Thread(target=q), _th.Thread(target=sc)
            t1.start(); t2.start(); t1.join(20); t2.join(20)
            need(not race["q"].get("error")
                 and not race["s"].get("error"),
                 "a script and a query race cleanly on one session")

            s.run_query('CREATE TABLE "A side" AS '
                        "SELECT 1 AS k, '$1,000.50' AS bal UNION ALL "
                        "SELECT 2, '$20.25' UNION ALL "
                        "SELECT 3, '$5.00'", target=_LT)
            s.run_query('CREATE TABLE "B;side" AS '
                        "SELECT 1 AS k, '$1,000.50' AS bal UNION ALL "
                        "SELECT 2, '$99.75' UNION ALL "
                        "SELECT 7, '$1.00'", target=_LT)
            spec = {"left": "A side", "right": "B;side",
                    "keys": ["k"], "compare": ["bal"],
                    "balance": "bal"}
            rep = s.reconcile(spec)
            need(not rep.get("error"),
                 "hostile-name currency reconcile runs: %s"
                 % rep.get("error"))
            summ = rep.get("summary") or rep
            need("null_keys" in _json.dumps(summ),
                 "the summary carries null_keys")
            sm = _json.dumps(summ)
            need("1000.5" in sm or "1,000.50" in sm,
                 "currency parsed: the matching balance is exact")
            bad = s.reconcile_drilldown({**spec,
                                         "bucket": "matching"})
            need("field" in str(bad.get("error", "")).lower(),
                 "matching drill without a field: clean contract "
                 "error")
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({**spec, "bucket": "matching",
                                       "field": "bal"})
            need(d.get("result_id"), "matching drill with field "
                 "produces a result")
            pg = s.page(d["result_id"], 0, 10)
            ks = sorted(int(r0[0]) for r0 in pg["rows"])
            eq(ks, [1], "only the truly matching key drills")
            eq(len(pg["rows"][0]), 3,
               "drill columns are [key, A value, B value]")
            names = _json.dumps(s.tables_tree())
            need("__samql" not in names.lower(),
                 "no reconcile temp tables leak")

            import server as _sv
            httpd, _pp = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
            port = httpd.server_address[1]
            _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever,
                       daemon=True).start()
            _tm.sleep(0.2)
            import urllib.request as _ur

            def hit(method, path, body=None):
                data = (_json.dumps(body).encode()
                        if body is not None else None)
                rq = _ur.Request(
                    "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (port, path),
                    data=data, method=method,
                    headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
                with _api_urlopen(httpd, rq, timeout=30) as r0:
                    return r0.status, _json.loads(r0.read() or b"{}")
            try:
                # the load path names the table from the FILE STEM
                # (base_name is advisory) -- so the twin test names
                # the file itself.
                d0 = _tf.mkdtemp(prefix="a2_")
                pth = _os.path.join(d0, "dupload.csv")
                with open(pth, "w", newline="") as f:
                    w = _csv.writer(f)
                    w.writerow(["a", "b"])
                    for i in range(2000):
                        w.writerow([i, "r-%d" % i])
                jids = []
                for _ in range(2):
                    st, bd = hit("POST", "/api/load/start",
                                 {"path": pth,
                                  "destination": "sqlite",
                                  "base_name": "dupload"})
                    jids.append(bd["job_id"])
                deadline = _tm.time() + 30
                states = {}
                while _tm.time() < deadline:
                    states = {}
                    for j in jids:
                        st, pgj = hit("GET",
                                      "/api/load/progress/" + j)
                        states[j] = pgj.get("state")
                    if all(v in ("done", "error", "cancelled")
                           for v in states.values()):
                        break
                    _tm.sleep(0.1)
                need(all(v == "done" for v in states.values()),
                     "both concurrent same-name loads land: %r"
                     % states)
                st, tb = hit("GET", "/api/tables")
                nm = _json.dumps(tb)
                need('"dupload"' in nm and '"dupload_2"' in nm,
                     "the twin got the _2 suffix; both intact")
            finally:
                httpd.shutdown()
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_audit2_464_runtime():
        # .464 AUDIT PASS II (2/2): node data flow, concurrent reads,
        # responsiveness, memory -- and THE FINDING OF THE PASS, fixed
        # here. THE STALL: execute_cursor (the streaming path every
        # long SELECT rides) holds NO write_lock by design, so the
        # catalog's .464 busy-probes sailed past it and then parked
        # inside sqlite's per-connection mutex behind the running
        # statement -- the sidebar froze for the DURATION of any big
        # query (measured 2.5s behind a 25M-row CTE; unbounded in
        # general). THE FIX: the engine now keeps a statement-
        # in-flight counter (stmt_busy), marked around every
        # cur.execute on BOTH the locked and streaming paths, and
        # every catalog walker (sync_catalog, types_cached,
        # _cached_count, the reader busy-probe) consults it FIRST and
        # serves its cache instead of joining the queue -- proven
        # live below: the catalog answers in milliseconds DURING a
        # heavy query, stays name-stable, and reconciles for real
        # once the engine frees. ALSO EXECUTED: a nodeflow chain
        # (filter -> formula -> summarize) matches brute SQL exactly;
        # a diamond join lands the k%10 population; a flow cancel is
        # honest and the flow layer stays healthy with no temp
        # tables; an iterator in children-form accumulates three
        # passes to an exact checksum; 8 threads x 60 mixed row-exact
        # reads (pages, sorts, filters, cell fetches) with zero
        # errors and a 10-way identical filtered read stays coherent;
        # and a bounded six-query retained-row battery grows the Python
        # heap by under 40 MB while a deliberately small result cap forces
        # repeated eviction and keeps dependent caches tracking the store.
        import time as _tm, threading as _th, gc as _gc
        import tracemalloc as _tr
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            from samql_core.session import LOCAL_TARGET as _LT
            import engines as _eng_mod  # noqa: F401 (path check)
        except Exception:
            from samql_core.session import LOCAL_TARGET as _LT
        try:
            eng = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core",
                                    "engines.py"),
                       encoding="utf-8").read()
            need(eng.count("_mark_busy(+1)") == 3
                 and "self.stmt_busy = 0" in eng
                 and eng.count('stmt_busy", 0) > 0') == 2,
                 "the stmt-busy counter wraps BOTH execute paths and "
                 "gates the engine-side walkers")
            sess = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core",
                                     "session.py"),
                        encoding="utf-8").read()
            # .464 pass II: the count probe gained a bounded micro-retry

            need(sess.count("_stmt_stepping(") == 4
                 and "int(getattr(engine, \"stmt_busy\", 0) or 0)"
                 in sess,
                 "the session-side count cache and reader probe "
                 "consult stmt_busy first (int-coerced for doubles)")

            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE nf_src AS WITH RECURSIVE c(k) "
                        "AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT k+1 FROM c "

            g1 = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "L", "type": "input",
                 "config": {"table": "nf_src"}},
                {"id": "F", "type": "filter",
                 "config": {"condition": "k % 3 != 0"}},
                {"id": "X", "type": "formula", "config": {
                    "formulas": [{"name": "w", "expr": "v*2 + k"}]}},
                {"id": "S", "type": "summarize", "config": {

            g2 = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "L", "type": "input",

                 "to": {"node": "A", "port": "in"}},

            gslow = {"nodes": [{"id": "Q", "type": "sql", "config": {

            th.start()
            _tm.sleep(0.6)
            s.cancel_query("c3f")

            e = str((fout.get("r") or {}).get("error", "")).lower()
            need(not th.is_alive()
                 and ("cancel" in e
                      or (fout.get("r") or {}).get("cancelled")),

            r3 = s.run_nodeflow(g1, "S", "out")
            need(not r3.get("error"),
                 "the flow layer is healthy after a cancel")
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE it_nums AS WITH RECURSIVE "
                        "c(n) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT n+1 "

            git = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "V", "type": "input",

            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE big AS WITH RECURSIVE c(k) AS "
                        "(SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT k+1 FROM c "

                        "FROM c", target=_LT)
            rid = s.run_query("SELECT * FROM big ORDER BY k",
                              target=_LT)["result_id"]
            N = 60000
            errs = []
            lk = _th.Lock()

            def reader(w):
                for i in range(10):
                    try:
                        off = (w * 997 + i * 7919) % (N - 60)
                        pg = s.page(rid, off, 50)
                        assert int(pg["rows"][0][0]) == off + 1
                        pg2 = s.page(rid, 0, 5, sort_col="k",
                                     descending=True)
                        assert int(pg2["rows"][0][0]) == N
                        pg3 = s.page(rid, 0, 5, filters=[
                            {"column": "k", "op": "<=",
                             "value": 1000}])
                        assert int(pg3["rows"][0][0]) == 1
                        cv = s.cell_value(rid, off, "v")
                        assert cv["value"] == "v-%d" % (off + 1)
                    except Exception as ex:
                        with lk:
                            errs.append((w, i, repr(ex)[:50]))
            ths = [_th.Thread(target=reader, args=(w,))
                   for w in range(8)]
            for t in ths:
                t.start()
            for t in ths:
                t.join(90)
            need(not errs and all(not t.is_alive() for t in ths),
                 "8x10 mixed reads row-exact, zero errors: %r"
                 % errs[:2])
            same = []

            def racer():
                try:
                    pgq = s.page(rid, 0, 3, filters=[
                        {"column": "k", "op": "<=", "value": 777}])
                    same.append(int(pgq["rows"][0][0]))
                except Exception as ex:
                    same.append(repr(ex)[:30])
            rs = [_th.Thread(target=racer) for _ in range(10)]
            for t in rs:
                t.start()
            for t in rs:
                t.join(30)
            eq(same, [1] * 10,
               "a 10-way identical filtered read stays coherent")

            pre = sorted(x["name"] for x in s.tables_tree())
            hout = {}

            def heavy():
                hout["r"] = s.run_query(
                    "WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL "

            th = _th.Thread(target=heavy)
            th.start()
            _tm.sleep(0.35)
            worst = 0.0
            stable = True
            for i in range(3):
                t0 = _tm.monotonic()
                tt = s.tables_tree()
                worst = max(worst, _tm.monotonic() - t0)
                stable = stable and sorted(
                    x["name"] for x in tt) == pre
                _tm.sleep(0.1)
            need(worst < 0.4,
                 "THE STALL FIX, live: catalog answers in %.3fs "

                 "real")

            _gc.collect()
            # Keep this release rail strong but bounded on constrained CI.
            # A cap of four means six 300k-row results force multiple real
            # evictions; retaining fourteen 600k-row stores under tracemalloc
            # tested the allocator more than the SamQL ownership contract and
            # could take many minutes on the stdlib SQLite fallback.
            s.MAX_CACHED_RESULTS = 4
            _tr.start()
            base = _tr.take_snapshot()
            for i in range(6):
                rr = s.run_query(
                    "WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL "
                    "SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<300000) "
                    "SELECT x, 'pad-'||x AS t FROM c",
                    query_id="m-%d" % i)
                s.page(rr["result_id"], 0, 100)
            _gc.collect()
            growth = sum(st0.size_diff for st0 in
                         _tr.take_snapshot().compare_to(
                             base, "filename")) / 1e6
            _tr.stop()
            need(growth < 40.0,
                 "heap growth bounded: %.1f MB after six retained-row "
                 "queries" % growth)
            need(len(s._results) <= 4,
                 "the results store stays capped by repeated eviction")
            ncc = len(getattr(s, "_count_cache", {}) or {})
            need(ncc <= len(s._results) + 6,
                 "the count cache tracks the store, not history")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_audit2_464():
        # AUDIT PASS II (.464), fresh angles across seven domains. THE
        # ONE PRODUCT BUG: _ExecKeepalive wrapped only three DuckDB
        # LOAD paths -- query execution on BOTH engines never beat the
        # progress registry, so any query outliving the 90-second
        # stall threshold FALSE-FLAGGED as stalled (red pill + dump),
        # and the keepalive's cancel re-nudge never ran during
        # queries. FIXED: all five execute paths (sqlite execute /
        # execute_cursor pre+main, duckdb execute / execute_cursor /
        # execute_read) now wear the keepalive, each interrupting the
        # connection that is actually executing. Proven below by the
        # beat SAWTOOTH on a live surfaced query. HARNESS-CONTRACT
        # RECLASSIFICATIONS (documented, not bugs): registry
        # visibility requires the surface= the UI always sends;
        # nodeflow sources are type "input"; filter emits port "true";
        # iterator vars bind as ${var}; fixtures must load with
        # target="auto"; cell_value takes a column NAME; reconcile
        # matching/non-matching drills REQUIRE a field. CLEAN
        # DOMAINS, executed: chain-vs-brute and a diamond join
        # row-exact; iterator append == brute union; 8-thread
        # concurrent reads byte-identical to sequential; reads and
        # the catalog live during heavy queries; memory bounded over
        # a query battery with clean eviction; a cancel storm drains
        # the registry; a silenced beat still dumps EXACTLY once and
        # the run completes.
        import time as _tm, threading as _th, gc as _gc
        import tracemalloc as _tr, tempfile as _tf
        from samql_core.session import Session
        from samql_core import watchdog as _wd, progress as _op
        sess = Session()

        def q(sql, **kw):
            return sess.run_query(sql, target="auto", **kw)

        def rows(res, lim=6000):
            need(not res.get("error"), "run clean: %r"
                 % res.get("error"))
            return sess.page(res["result_id"], offset=0,
                             limit=lim)["rows"]
        q("CREATE TABLE a2src AS WITH RECURSIVE c(k) AS (SELECT 1 "
          "UNION ALL SELECT k+1 FROM c WHERE k<6000) "
          "SELECT k, k*2 AS v, k%7 AS g FROM c")

        # C: chain vs brute
        g = {"nodes": [
            {"id": "t", "type": "input",
             "config": {"table": "a2src"}},
            {"id": "f", "type": "filter",
             "config": {"condition": "k <= 4000"}},
            {"id": "fx", "type": "formula",
             "config": {"formulas": [{"name": "s",
                                      "expr": "v + g"}]}},
            {"id": "agg", "type": "summarize",
             "config": {"group_by": ["g"],
                        "aggs": [{"col": "s", "func": "sum",
                                  "name": "ss"},
                                 {"col": "k", "func": "count",
                                  "name": "n"}]}},
        ], "edges": [
            {"id": "e1", "from": {"node": "t", "port": "out"},
             "to": {"node": "f", "port": "in"}},
            {"id": "e2", "from": {"node": "f", "port": "true"},
             "to": {"node": "fx", "port": "in"}},
            {"id": "e3", "from": {"node": "fx", "port": "out"},
             "to": {"node": "agg", "port": "in"}},
        ]}
        flow = sorted(tuple(x) for x in
                      rows(sess.run_nodeflow(g, "agg", "out",
                                             query_id="a2c1")))
        brute = sorted(tuple(x) for x in rows(q(
            "SELECT g, SUM(v+g), COUNT(*) FROM a2src "
            "WHERE k<=4000 GROUP BY g")))
        eq(flow, brute, "C1 chain == brute, row-exact")

        g2 = {"nodes": [
            {"id": "t", "type": "input",
             "config": {"table": "a2src"}},
            {"id": "a", "type": "filter",
             "config": {"condition": "k % 2 = 0"}},
            {"id": "b", "type": "filter",
             "config": {"condition": "k % 3 = 0"}},
            {"id": "j", "type": "join",
             "config": {"keys": [{"left": "k", "right": "k"}],

        q("CREATE TABLE a2vars AS SELECT 2 AS lo UNION SELECT 4 "
          "UNION SELECT 6")
        q("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS a2acc")
        g4 = {"nodes": [
            {"id": "vt", "type": "input",
             "config": {"table": "a2vars"}},

        need(r4.get("ok") and r4.get("passes") == 3
             and not r4.get("errors"),
             "C4 iterator drove three passes clean: %r" % r4)
        got = rows(q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a2acc"))[0][0]
        want = rows(q("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM a2src "
                      "WHERE g IN (2,4,6)"))[0][0]
        eq(got, want, "C4 iterator append == brute union")

        # D: concurrent reads row-exact
        rd = q("WITH RECURSIVE c(k) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT "
               "k+1 FROM c WHERE k<40000) SELECT k, k%13 AS m, "

        rid = rd["result_id"]
        specs = [dict(offset=0, limit=300),

        derrs = []

        def reader(i):
            try:
                for _ in range(3):
                    if sess.page(rid, **specs[i])["rows"]                             != base[i]:

        for t in ts:

        for t in ts:
            t.join(30)
        eq(derrs, [], "D1 concurrent reads byte-identical")

        # E: THE BUG, pinned by its sawtooth. A ~4s surfaced query
        # must BEAT: idle climbs toward the 3s keepalive interval,
        # resets, climbs again. Before the fix it climbed forever.
        hold = {}

        def heavy():
            hold["r"] = q("WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION "
                          "ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<34000000) "

        idles = []
        t0 = _tm.monotonic()
        while th.is_alive() and _tm.monotonic() - t0 < 15:
            sn = [o for o in _op.snapshot()
                  if o.get("id") == "a2-beat"]
            if sn:

        need(not hold["r"].get("error"), "beat probe ran clean")
        saw = any(b < a - 0.5 for a, b in zip(idles, idles[1:]))
        need(saw and idles and max(idles) < 3.9,

             % (max(idles) if idles else -1))
        eq(_op.count(), 0, "registry drains after the beat probe")

        # E: a genuinely dead beat still dumps exactly once, live

        real = _op.beat
        real_bot = _op.beat_on_thread
        try:
            _op.beat = lambda *a, **k: None
            _op.beat_on_thread = lambda *a, **k: None
            log = os.path.join(_tf.mkdtemp(), "a2wd.log")
            h2 = {}

            def stall():
                h2["r"] = q("WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 "
                            "UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE "
                            "x<30000000) SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c",
                            query_id="a2-stall", surface="ide")
            t2 = _th.Thread(target=stall)
            t2.start()
            # deflake (.467): under full-suite CPU contention a fixed
            # sleep raced the query's own lifetime. Wait until the op

            t0 = _tm.monotonic()
            while _tm.monotonic() - t0 < 5:
                if any(o.get("id") == "a2-stall"
                       for o in _op.snapshot()):
                    break
                _tm.sleep(0.05)
            _tm.sleep(0.5)
            _wd.scan_once(0.3, log)
            sz1 = os.path.getsize(log) if os.path.exists(log)                 else 0
            _wd.scan_once(0.3, log)
            sz2 = os.path.getsize(log) if os.path.exists(log)                 else 0
            t2.join(60)
        finally:
            _op.beat = real
            _op.beat_on_thread = real_bot
        need(sz1 > 0 and sz2 == sz1 and not h2["r"].get("error"),
             "a true live stall dumps once and the run completes")

        # F: memory ledger + cancel storm
        _gc.collect()
        _tr.start()
        snap0 = _tr.take_snapshot()
        for i in range(20):

        delta = sum(st.size_diff for st in
                    _tr.take_snapshot().compare_to(

        need(delta < 90, "F1 20-query traced growth bounded "

        for i in range(5):
            qid = "a2storm-%d" % i
            t = _th.Thread(target=lambda qq=qid: sess.run_query(
                "WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL "
                "SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<8000000) "
                "SELECT COUNT(*) FROM c",
                target="auto", query_id=qq, surface="ide"))
            t.start()
            _tm.sleep(0.05)
            sess.cancel_query(qid)
            t.join(30)
        eq(_op.count(), 0, "F3 cancel storm drains the registry")

        # engines: all five paths wear the keepalive
        eng = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core",
                                "engines.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        # REWORKED: the per-execute keepalive spawned+joined a thread
        # inside every write_lock hold, widening holds enough for the
        # non-blocking catalog probes to land inside the loader's
        # indexing bursts. Now: ONE persistent _BeatDaemon per manager
        # plus an attribute-only _BeatScope at all six exec sites (the
        # legacy load paths keep their _ExecKeepalive).
        # .472: the save-as-table CTAS (add_table_from_parquet) is a
        # seventh keepalive-wrapped exec site -- a long CREATE TABLE AS
        # read_parquet must beat the progress registry too.
        need(eng.count("_BeatScope(self,") == 7
             and eng.count("_BeatDaemon(self)") == 2
             and eng.count("_ExecKeepalive(") == 3,
             "beat daemon + six featherweight scopes; legacy load "
             "keepalives intact")
        # .465: the daemon holds its manager WEAKLY and retires when
        # the manager is collected -- otherwise every Session the
        # suite created left two ticking threads behind, and the
        # timing-heavy stations crawled.
        need("self._mgr = weakref.ref(mgr)" in eng
             and "if m is None:" in eng,
             "the beat daemon weak-refs its manager and retires with "
             "it")
        import gc as _gc2, threading as _th2, time as _tm2
        before = [t for t in _th2.enumerate()
                  if t.name.startswith("samql-beat")]
        probe = Session()
        probe.run_query("SELECT 1", target="auto")
        probe.shutdown()
        del probe
        _gc2.collect()
        _tm2.sleep(3.4)
        after = [t for t in _th2.enumerate()
                 if t.name.startswith("samql-beat")]
        need(len(after) <= len(before),
             "a dropped session's beat threads retire within one tick "
             "(%d -> %d)" % (len(before), len(after)))
        sess_src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core",
                                     "session.py"),
                        encoding="utf-8").read()
        # .474: flatten_table primes the count for each relational
        # table it creates -- a fourth priming site (same fire-and-
        # forget indexer race the load paths guard against).
        need("def _prime_count" in sess_src
             and sess_src.count("self._prime_count(") == 4
             and "deadline = time.monotonic() + 0.006" in sess_src,
             "loads PRIME the count cache (now 4 paths incl. flatten) "
             "and the probe micro-retries past indexing bursts")
        need("types = types or {}" in sess_src,
             "a None type-map can never take down the tables tree")

    def t_progress_anim_compositor_482():
        # .482 animation audit: the THREE continuous progress animations --
        # shown during every query / pivot / load, so the most-seen motion
        # in the app -- previously slid via `left` / `margin-left`, which
        # force a layout on every frame (janky bars). They now animate
        # `transform: translateX`, which the compositor handles without
        # layout or paint, and carry `will-change: transform`. This guards
        # against a future edit reintroducing the layout-triggering form.
        css = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "styles.css"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()

        import re as _re11

        def _kf_body(name):
            m = _re11.search(r"@keyframes %s\s*\{(.*?)\n\}" % _re11.escape(name),
                             css, _re11.DOTALL)
            return m.group(1) if m else ""

        for name in ("indet", "run-indeterminate", "pv-indeterminate"):
            body = _kf_body(name)
            need(body, "the %s progress keyframe still exists" % name)
            need("translateX" in body,
                 "%s animates transform:translateX (compositor-only)" % name)
            # must NOT animate layout-triggering box-offset properties
            for bad in ("left:", "right:", "margin-left:", "margin-right:",
                        "top:", "width:"):
                need(bad not in body,
                     "%s must not animate `%s` (forces per-frame layout)"
                     % (name, bad.rstrip(":")))

        # the animated elements hint the compositor with will-change
        need(css.count("will-change: transform;\n  animation") >= 2,
             "the sliding progress fills declare will-change: transform")

        # reduced-motion still fully covers animation (the escape hatch for
        # motion sensitivity AND slow machines)
        need("prefers-reduced-motion: reduce" in css
             and "animation-duration: 0.01ms !important" in css,
             "a global reduced-motion guard disables animation")
        need("body.motion-reduced" in css,
             "an in-app motion-reduced toggle also disables animation")
