    def t_anim_integrity_462():
        # .462 ANIMATION AUDIT. The sweep across every motion build
        # (.433-.437, .459, .460) found the system structurally sound
        # and four real defects, all fixed: (1) @keyframes node-in was
        # defined TWICE -- the later definition silently won the
        # cascade for both consumers; deduped to one; (2) the ripple /
        # snap / born one-shots re-set the SAME state value on
        # back-to-back events, so a second run finishing inside the
        # window never replayed -- they now drop the class for a frame
        # (requestAnimationFrame) before re-arming, the refresh-spin
        # pattern; (3) SELECTION runs went through onRunAll with no
        # range, so they never flashed and never err-pinged -- a
        # dedicated onRunSelection channel now carries the range and
        # honors the same flash + red-ping contract, and the CLIENT
        # statement fallback err-pings too; (4) the .460 changelog
        # promised an invalid-submit shake class that never shipped --
        # modal-shake exists now, documented-unused until a form modal
        # validates. GENERIC INVARIANTS, enforced forever: every
        # @keyframes is referenced by an animation rule; no keyframe
        # name is defined twice; every animation-bearing selector's
        # class tokens appear somewhere in the markup (documented
        # allowlist: shake); the stylesheet's braces balance.
        import re as _re, glob as _glob
        css = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src",
                                "styles.css"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        markup = ""
        for f in _glob.glob(os.path.join(
                ROOT, "frontend", "src", "**", "*.tsx"),
                recursive=True):
            markup += open(f, encoding="utf-8").read()
        markup += open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend",
                                    "index.html"),
                       encoding="utf-8").read()
        names = _re.findall(r"@keyframes\s+([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)", css)
        dups = sorted({n for n in names if names.count(n) > 1})
        eq(dups, [], "no keyframe name is defined twice")
        kfs = set(names)
        used = set()
        for m in _re.findall(r"animation(?:-name)?\s*:\s*([^;]+);",
                             css):
            for tok in _re.split(r"[\s,]+", m):
                if tok in kfs:
                    used.add(tok)
        eq(sorted(kfs - used), [],
           "every keyframe is used by an animation rule")
        ALLOW_UNWIRED = {"shake"}  # promised utility, wired later
        missing = set()
        for sel in _re.findall(
                r"([^{}]+)\{[^{}]*animation[^{}]*\}", css):
            for cls in _re.findall(r"\.([A-Za-z0-9_-]+)", sel):
                if cls in ALLOW_UNWIRED:
                    continue
                if cls not in markup:
                    missing.add(cls)
        eq(sorted(missing), [],
           "every animated selector's class exists in markup")
        eq(css.count("{") - css.count("}"), 0,
           "stylesheet braces balance")
        nb = _nodeflow_source()
        # Phase 9 moved the one-shot animation owners into focused hooks and
        # added frame-handle cleanup. Match the behavior rather than requiring
        # the old single-line spelling: each repeated effect drops its class,
        # re-arms on the next frame, and retains the canvas snap contract.
        ripple_rearm = _re.search(
            r"setRipple\(false\);.*?rippleFrame\.current\s*=\s*"
            r"(?:window\.)?requestAnimationFrame\(\(\)\s*=>\s*\{.*?"
            r"setRipple\(true\);.*?\}\);", nb, _re.S)
        born_rearm = _re.search(
            r"setBornId\(null\);.*?bornFrame\.current\s*=\s*"
            r"(?:window\.)?requestAnimationFrame\(\(\)\s*=>\s*\{.*?"
            r"setBornId\(id\);.*?\}\);", nb, _re.S)
        need(bool(ripple_rearm)
             and "requestAnimationFrame(() => setSnapId(id))" in nb
             and bool(born_rearm),
             "ripple/snap/born re-arm through a frame so they replay")
        app = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src",
                                "App.tsx"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("const runSelection = async" in app
             and app.count('flashRange(start, end, "err")') == 1
             and app.count('flashRange(span.start, span.end, "err")')
             == 2,
             "selection runs and BOTH statement branches flash and "
             "err-ping")
        ed = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src",
                               "components", "SqlEditor.tsx"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("onRunSelection(ta.selectionStart, ta.selectionEnd)"
             in ed, "the editor routes selections through the new "
             "channel")
        need("@keyframes modal-shake" in css and ".shake" in css,
             "the promised shake utility exists")

    def t_server_stability_462():
        # .462 SERVER STABILITY AUDIT. VERDICT: CLEAN, nine executed
        # stations, zero findings -- the transport layer joins the
        # certified-clean list. The paper posture (a 60s socket
        # timeout, daemon threads, HTTP/1.1 keep-alive with
        # Content-Length on every frame, a 413 body cap, and
        # broken-pipe writes retiring the connection instead of
        # tearing it) is now PROVEN: a 200-request mixed hammer from 8
        # threads lands with zero >=500s; worker threads settle back
        # to baseline; a naked idle socket and a Content-Length LIAR
        # both free their threads the moment the client closes; forty
        # mid-response aborts on a large payload leave the server
        # healthy with no thread residue; keep-alive serves two
        # requests on one connection; an oversized header line gets an
        # honest 431; and shutdown under live load returns in well
        # under five seconds.
        import json as _json, time as _tm, socket as _sk
        import threading as _th
        import urllib.request as _ur, urllib.error as _ue
        import http.client as _hc
        import server as _sv
        httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port = httpd.server_address[1]
        _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm.sleep(0.25)
        base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % port
        try:
            rq = _ur.Request(
                base + "/api/query",
                data=_json.dumps(
                    {"sql": "WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION "
                            "ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<15000) "
                            "SELECT x, 'pad-pad-pad-' || x AS t "
                            "FROM c",
                     "target": "auto"}).encode(),
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"})
            rid = _json.loads(_api_urlopen(
                httpd, rq, timeout=30).read())["result_id"]
            base_threads = _th.active_count()
            errs = []
            lk = _th.Lock()
            paths = ["/api/tables", "/api/saved", "/api/history",
                     "/api/result/%s/page?offset=50&limit=200" % rid,
                     "/favicon.ico"]

            def w(wi):
                for i in range(25):
                    p = paths[(wi + i) % len(paths)]
                    try:
                        with _api_urlopen(httpd, base + p, timeout=20) as r:
                            r.read()
                            if r.status >= 500:
                                with lk:
                                    errs.append((p, r.status))
                    except _ue.HTTPError as e:
                        if e.code >= 500:
                            with lk:
                                errs.append((p, e.code))
                    except Exception as e:
                        with lk:
                            errs.append((p, repr(e)[:40]))
            ts = [_th.Thread(target=w, args=(k,)) for k in range(8)]
            for t in ts:
                t.start()
            for t in ts:
                t.join(60)
            need(not errs and all(not t.is_alive() for t in ts),
                 "hammer: 200 mixed requests, zero >=500 (%r)"
                 % errs[:3])
            _tm.sleep(0.8)
            need(_th.active_count() <= base_threads + 3,
                 "threads settle after the hammer")
            s = _sk.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port))
            _tm.sleep(1.0)
            s.close()
            _tm.sleep(0.4)
            eq(_api_urlopen(httpd, base + "/api/tables",
                           timeout=10).status, 200,
               "a naked idle socket harms nothing")
            s = _sk.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port))
            s.sendall(b"GARBAGE NONSENSE\r\n\r\n")
            s.recv(200)
            s.close()
            eq(_api_urlopen(httpd, base + "/api/tables",
                           timeout=10).status, 200,
               "a garbage request line harms nothing")
            s = _sk.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port))
            liar = ("POST /api/query HTTP/1.1\r\n"
                    "Host: 127.0.0.1:%d\r\n"
                    "X-SamQL-Token: %s\r\n"
                    "Content-Type: application/json\r\n"
                    "Content-Length: 5000\r\n\r\n{\"sq"
                    % (port, httpd.samql_api_token)).encode("ascii")
            s.sendall(liar)
            _tm.sleep(0.5)
            s.close()
            _tm.sleep(1.0)
            need(_th.active_count() <= base_threads + 3,
                 "a Content-Length liar frees its thread on close")

            def aborter():
                try:
                    c = _hc.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", port,
                                           timeout=10)
                    c.request("GET",
                              "/api/result/%s/page?offset=0"
                              "&limit=5000" % rid,
                              headers={"X-SamQL-Token":
                                       httpd.samql_api_token})
                    r = c.getresponse()
                    r.read(1500)
                    c.sock.close()
                except Exception:
                    pass
            ab = [_th.Thread(target=aborter) for _ in range(40)]
            for t in ab:
                t.start()
            for t in ab:
                t.join(20)
            _tm.sleep(0.8)
            need(_api_urlopen(httpd, base + "/api/tables",
                             timeout=10).status == 200
                 and _th.active_count() <= base_threads + 4,
                 "40 mid-response aborts leave no residue")
            c = _hc.HTTPConnection("127.0.0.1", port, timeout=10)
            c.request("GET", "/api/tables", headers={
                "X-SamQL-Token": httpd.samql_api_token})
            r1 = c.getresponse()
            r1.read()
            cl = r1.getheader("Content-Length")
            c.request("GET", "/api/saved", headers={
                "X-SamQL-Token": httpd.samql_api_token})
            r2 = c.getresponse()
            r2.read()
            need(r1.status == 200 and r2.status == 200
                 and cl is not None,
                 "keep-alive: two on one connection, CL framed")
            c.close()
            s = _sk.create_connection(("127.0.0.1", port))
            s.sendall(b"GET /api/tables HTTP/1.1\r\nHost: x\r\n"
                      b"X-Big: " + b"A" * 200000 + b"\r\n\r\n")
            resp = s.recv(200)
            s.close()
            need(b"431" in resp,
                 "an oversized header line answers an honest 431")
            stop = []

            def bg():
                while not stop:
                    try:
                        _api_urlopen(httpd, base + "/api/tables",
                                     timeout=5).read()
                    except Exception:
                        return
            bgs = [_th.Thread(target=bg, daemon=True)
                   for _ in range(5)]
            for t in bgs:
                t.start()
            _tm.sleep(0.3)
            t0 = _tm.monotonic()
            httpd.shutdown()
            stop.append(1)
            need(_tm.monotonic() - t0 < 5.0,
                 "shutdown under load returns promptly")
        finally:
            stop = [1]
            try:
                httpd.shutdown()
            except Exception:
                pass

    def t_window_branding_469():
        # .469: the on-box window and taskbar wore the EDGE logo. Two
        # causes, both fixed. (1) The Edge --app frame adopts the page
        # favicon only if the favicon service may cache it -- our
        # no-store starved it; brand images are max-age=60 now.
        # (2) The PowerShell app-window flow never stamped the window
        # at all -- it now mirrors the packaged launcher natively:
        # WM_SETICON + AppUserModelID via a compiled helper, with
        # timed restamps so ours is the LAST writer; the launcher
        # gained the same restamps. The header mark inside the app
        # also wears the SAME art (/app-icon.png) as the window. The
        # server names its art source in an X-SamQL-Brand header and
        # ships an exe-adjacent brand ladder, so "why is it the
        # default?" is one curl away -- proven LIVE below, custom art
        # in and out. The exe-adjacent frontend_dist may only take
        # over the whole UI when it is a REAL dist (index.html
        # present); an icons-only folder brands without blanking.
        import struct as _st, zlib as _zl, tempfile as _tf
        import threading as _th, time as _tm
        import urllib.request as _ur
        import server as _sv

        def _png(w, h, rgb):
            def chunk(t, d):
                c = t + d
                return (_st.pack(">I", len(d)) + c
                        + _st.pack(">I", _zl.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff))
            raw = b"".join(b"\x00" + bytes(rgb) * w
                           for _ in range(h))
            return (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
                    + chunk(b"IHDR", _st.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8,
                                              2, 0, 0, 0))
                    + chunk(b"IDAT", _zl.compress(raw))
                    + chunk(b"IEND", b""))
        d = _tf.mkdtemp()
        art = _png(8, 8, (200, 60, 40))
        with open(os.path.join(d, "app-icon.png"), "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(art)
        old = _sv._FRONTEND_DIR
        _sv._FRONTEND_DIR = d
        try:
            httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
            port = httpd.server_address[1]
            _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever,
                       daemon=True).start()
            _tm.sleep(0.2)
            base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % port
            r = _ur.urlopen(base + "/favicon.ico", timeout=10)
            need(r.headers.get("X-SamQL-Brand")
                 == "derived from bundled app-icon.png"
                 and r.headers.get("Cache-Control") == "max-age=60",
                 "favicon names its source and is cacheable "
                 "(Edge's adoption path)")
            r2 = _ur.urlopen(base + "/app-icon.png", timeout=10)
            need(r2.headers.get("X-SamQL-Brand")
                 == "bundled app-icon.png"
                 and r2.read() == art,
                 "the header mark's art serves byte-exact, named")
            os.remove(os.path.join(d, "app-icon.png"))
            r3 = _ur.urlopen(base + "/favicon.ico", timeout=10)
            eq(r3.headers.get("X-SamQL-Brand"), "embedded",
               "no custom art -> the header says so plainly")
            httpd.shutdown()
        finally:
            _sv._FRONTEND_DIR = old
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("def _brand_lookup" in srv
             and '"exe-adjacent"' in srv
             and 'os.path.isfile(os.path.join(adj, "index.html"))'
             in srv,
             "brand ladder + the icons-only folder can't blank the UI")
        ps1 = open(_root_script("Start-SamQL-AppWindow[.]ps1"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("WM_SETICON" in ps1
             and "SHGetPropertyStoreForWindow" in ps1
             and "window icon source" in ps1
             and "foreach ($delay in 2, 3, 5, 8, 15, 30, 60)" in ps1,
             "the PS1 flow stamps icon + AppUserModelID and restamps")
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("def _restamp():" in la
             and "for delay in (2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 8.0, 15.0, 30.0, 60.0):"
             in la,
             "the packaged launcher restamps too (.526 long schedule)")
        app = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "App.tsx"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        # .469 (same build): the mark tries app-icon.png THEN
        # logo.png -- the user's first custom file was logo.png and
        # that must be enough on its own.
        need('["/app-icon.png", "/logo.png"]' in app,
             "the in-app header mark wears the same art (either "
             "custom name)")

    def t_reports_476():
        # .476, three on-box reports. FLATTEN CRASHED: flatten_table
        # called _shred.sql_path, but sql_path lives in sqlutil -- an
        # AttributeError on every real flatten (the mocks never entered
        # the body, so the sandbox missed it). Fixed + now covered by a
        # real run in the .474 battery. LOGO WHITESPACE: the embedded
        # icon is regenerated FULL-BLEED (cropped to its content, zero
        # transparent margin), so it fills the box with no scale hack.
        # EDGE ICON: WM_SETICON alone loses to Edge's repaint, so the
        # launcher now also sets PKEY_AppUserModel_RelaunchIconResource
        # -- the property Windows reads for the TASKBAR button icon --
        # which Edge can't repaint away.
        from samql_core import _brand
        import struct as _stt

        # the flatten crash: sql_path resolves from sqlutil, not shred
        sess = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("_shred.sql_path(" not in sess,
             "flatten_table no longer calls the non-existent "
             "shred.sql_path")
        _ftw = sess.split("def flatten_table", 1)[1]
        _ft = _ftw[:_ftw.find("\n    def ", 10)]
        need("sqlutil.sql_path(parquet)" in _ft,
             "the flatten cache COPY uses sqlutil.sql_path")

        # full-bleed icon: content fills the whole 256x256 frame
        png = _brand.app_icon_png()
        need(png[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n", "icon is a PNG")
        try:
            from PIL import Image as _Img
            import io as _io
            im = _Img.open(_io.BytesIO(png)).convert("RGBA")
            bb = im.getbbox()
            fill = (bb[2] - bb[0]) / im.size[0]
            need(fill >= 0.99,
                 "the icon is full-bleed (content fills %.0f%% of the "
                 "frame)" % (fill * 100))
        except ImportError:
            pass  # PIL not present in this env; the byte checks still ran

        # the ICO is regenerated from the full-bleed PNG (>=4 sizes)
        ico = _brand.app_ico()
        eq(ico[:4], b"\x00\x00\x01\x00", "ICO magic")
        need(_stt.unpack("<H", ico[4:6])[0] >= 4,
             "the ICO carries several sizes")

        # the taskbar RelaunchIconResource override, both launchers
        lap = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("def set_relaunch_icon(" in lap
             and "set_relaunch_icon(hwnd, ico)" in lap
             and "_set_window_prop(hwnd, 3," in lap,
             "the packaged launcher sets the taskbar icon via "
             "RelaunchIconResource (pid 3)")
        ps1 = open(_root_script("Start-SamQL-AppWindow[.]ps1"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("SetRelaunchIcon" in ps1
             and "SetProp(hwnd, 3," in ps1,
             "the PS1 launcher sets the taskbar icon override too")
