    def t_lifecycle_544():
        # .544: the SHIPPING-PRODUCT lifecycle audit. Every startup path
        # of SamQL-AppWindow[.]exe, asserted: (A) cold start; (B) window
        # closed, server alive -> reattach; (C) plain restart; (D) a
        # second click WHILE THE FIRST IS BOOTING -- the .537 10s heal
        # regressed this: it "continued" mid-cold-boot and started a
        # SECOND server; the wait is port-aware now and reuses instead;
        # (E) click while open -> focus; (F) after a crash -> stale
        # mutex heals, startup sweeps. Plus the cleaning contract:
        # past sessions reclaimed on EVERY start (sweep_stale was
        # exit-only -- a crash never reached it) and on exit
        # (cleanup_instance + sweep_stale, already present), with the
        # launcher's hard-exit _MEI orphans reclaimed by a maintenance
        # ping on each successful attach/boot.
        import types as _tl4
        import time as _tm4
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            import launcher_app as _LA
            from samql_core import tmputil as _TU
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)

        # ---- the cleaning contract, behaviorally ----
        # a dead-pid instance dir from a "crashed" past session
        ghost = os.path.join(_TU._ROOT, "999983")
        os.makedirs(ghost, exist_ok=True)
        open(os.path.join(ghost, "spill.parquet"), "wb").write(b"x" * 64)
        n = _TU.sweep_stale()
        need(n >= 1 and not os.path.exists(ghost)
             and os.path.isdir(_TU.instance_dir()),
             "a dead session's dir is reclaimed; our own is not (%d)" % n)
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        boot = srv.split("tmputil.touch_alive()")[1][:600]
        need("tmputil.sweep_stale()" in boot,
             "startup sweeps past sessions (crashes never reach the "
             "exit sweep)")
        need("tmputil.cleanup_instance()" in srv
             and srv.index("SESSION.shutdown()")
             < srv.index("tmputil.cleanup_instance()"),
             "exit removes this session's own temp dir after shutdown")
        need('"mei_min_age"' in srv
             and "sweep_mei_orphans(min_age_sec=age)" in srv,
             "the maintenance route reclaims recent _MEI orphans on ask")
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        rt = read_test_sources(ROOT)
        need("SystemExit(%r) escaped the test" in rt,
             "the runner converts a test's SystemExit into a FAIL")
        need("def _ping_maintenance" in la
             and la.count("_ping_maintenance(args.port)") == 2
             and 'name="samql-startup-maintenance"' in la,
             "the launcher pings housekeeping after reuse AND boot "
             "(daemon thread; never blocks the window handoff)")

        # ---- the six scenarios' anchors all present ----
        for frag, scen in (
            ("Starting the SamQL server...", "A cold start"),
            ("reusing the SamQL server already on port", "B reattach"),
            ("SamQL is already open -- brought its window", "E focus"),
            ("SamQL is already starting...", "D second click"),
            ("waiting for the first launch's server", "D port-aware"),
            ("treating it as stale", "F crash-stale mutex"),
            ("ignored a phantom", "ghost windows"),
            # .622: close stops the server we started (no lingering Task
            # Manager / llama-server) unless Exit → keep server marked
            # keep_on_close. Reattach reuses that left-up backend.
            ("stopped the server on port", "close stops server we started"),
            ("leaving the server on", "Exit → keep server leaves backend"),
            ("_MUTEX_RECONNECT_WINDOW_GRACE_S", "fast reconnect grace"),
            ("Reconnecting to SamQL...", "reconnect splash text"),
        ):
            need(frag in la, "lifecycle anchor for %s" % scen)
        api_ts = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "lib", "api.ts"),
                      encoding="utf-8").read()
        app_tsx = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "App.tsx"),
                       encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("keepServerOnClose" in api_ts
             and "/api/launcher/keep-on-close" in api_ts
             and "await api.keepServerOnClose()" in app_tsx,
             "Exit → keep server marks the backend before window.close()")

        # ---- Path D behaviorally: second click during a slow boot ----
        def fake_main(port_flip_at, boot_wait, expect_start):
            keep = {n2: getattr(_LA, n2) for n2 in
                    ("write_log", "find_samql_window", "focus_window",
                     "_acquire_single_instance", "port_open",
                     "_is_samql", "_owned_token", "make_splash", "open_native_window",
                     "find_browser", "start_server",
                     "_MUTEX_WAIT_S", "_MUTEX_BOOT_WAIT_S",
                     "SERVER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_S", "_ping_maintenance",
                     "_MUTEX_WINDOW_GRACE_S")}
            logs = []
            started = []
            t0 = _tm4.time()
            try:
                _LA.write_log = lambda m: logs.append(m)
                _LA.find_samql_window = lambda: None
                _LA.focus_window = lambda h: False
                _LA._acquire_single_instance = lambda: (True, True)
                _LA._MUTEX_WAIT_S = 0.05
                _LA._MUTEX_BOOT_WAIT_S = boot_wait
                _LA.SERVER_BOOT_TIMEOUT_S = 3.0
                _LA._MUTEX_WINDOW_GRACE_S = 0.15
                _LA.port_open = (
                    lambda p, **k: _tm4.time() - t0 >= port_flip_at)
                _LA._is_samql = lambda p: True
                _LA._owned_token = lambda p: "test-token"  # C-1: ours
                _LA._ping_maintenance = lambda p: None
                _LA.start_server = (
                    lambda port, sp: started.append(port) or True)
                _LA.open_native_window = lambda url, a, sp: True
                _LA.find_browser = lambda w: None
                _LA.make_splash = lambda: _tl4.SimpleNamespace(
                    set_text=lambda t, error=False: None,
                    close=lambda: None,
                    pump=lambda sec=0: _tm4.sleep(min(sec or 0.01,
                                                      0.02)))
                rc = _LA.main(["--port", "8765"])
            finally:
                for n2, v in keep.items():
                    setattr(_LA, n2, v)
            need(rc == 0, "lifecycle main rc=0 (%r)" % rc)
            need(bool(started) == expect_start,
                 "second server started=%r, expected %r (logs: %r)"
                 % (bool(started), expect_start,
                    [l for l in logs if "WARN" in l or "reusing" in l]))
            return logs

        # the first launch's server comes up mid-wait: this click WAITS,
        # then REUSES -- never a second server
        logs = fake_main(port_flip_at=0.15, boot_wait=5.0,
                         expect_start=False)
        need(any("waiting for the first launch's server" in l
                 for l in logs)
             and any("reusing the SamQL server" in l for l in logs),
             "slow boot: port-aware wait then reuse: %r"
             % [l for l in logs if "INFO" in l][-4:])
        # nothing comes up DURING THE WAIT: the mutex is stale -- cold
        # start; the port opens only after OUR start_server (0.35s)
        logs = fake_main(port_flip_at=0.35, boot_wait=0.2,
                         expect_start=True)
        need(any("treating it as stale" in l for l in logs),
             "true zombie: stale-mutex cold start: %r"
             % [l for l in logs if "WARN" in l])

        # ---- maintenance route behaviorally ----
        import urllib.request as _ur4
        import json as _j4
        import threading as _th4
        import server as _sv4
        httpd4, _p4 = _sv4.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port4 = httpd4.server_address[1]
        _th4.Thread(target=httpd4.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm4.sleep(0.25)
        try:
            rq = _ur4.Request(
                "http://127.0.0.1:%d/api/maintenance/sweep-temp" % port4,
                data=_j4.dumps({"mei_min_age": 60}).encode("utf-8"),
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                method="POST")
            with _api_urlopen(httpd4, rq, timeout=20) as r4:
                body = _j4.loads(r4.read().decode("utf-8"))
            need("mei_removed" in body and "removed" in body,
                 "the ping reports both sweeps: %r" % body)
        finally:
            try:
                httpd4.shutdown()
            except Exception:
                pass

    
    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_cancel_all_scoped_554():
        # .554: cross-surface Stop must not kill a concurrent query. The
        # NodeFlow Stop (and the Journal Stop, and the Activity tray) call
        # /api/cancel-all. That used to run a bare interrupt_loads(), i.e.
        # DuckDB interrupt(), which aborts WHATEVER statement is on the
        # connection -- so a Stop on one surface killed an IDE query or
        # Journal cell running at the same time. Now cancel-all flags jobs
        # cooperatively and interrupts the engine ONLY for the job that
        # owns the engine slot; the blanket engine hammer lives only in
        # the nuclear reset (/api/nuke) and the scope="all" opt-in.
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()

        # structural: cancel_all is owner-scoped, NOT a bare hammer
        ca = srv.split("def cancel_all", 1)[1].split(
            "def result_page", 1)[0]
        need("_flag_all_jobs()" in ca,
             "cancel-all still flags background jobs cooperatively")
        # look at the CODE, not the explanatory docstring (which
        # mentions interrupt_loads() to describe the old behavior).
        ca_code = ca.split('"""', 2)[-1] if ca.count('"""') >= 2 else ca
        # H-3 tightened .554: no engine-wide interrupt at all -- each
        # flagged job's OWN in-flight statement, via interrupt_job (the old
        # owner-gated interrupt_loads() fallback hit both engines).
        code_only = "\n".join(ln for ln in ca_code.splitlines()
                              if not ln.strip().startswith("#"))
        need("interrupt_loads()" not in code_only,
             "cancel-all never calls the both-engines interrupt_loads()")
        need("s.interrupt_job(" in code_only,
             "cancel-all interrupts each job's own statement only")

        # the blanket hammer still exists where it SHOULD: nuclear reset
        need("def nuclear_reset" in open(
            os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
            encoding="utf-8").read(),
             "nuclear_reset (the nuke) remains the broad-interrupt path")

        # BEHAVIORAL: with NO job owning the slot (the cross-surface case
        # -- a foreground query never takes the slot), cancel-all must NOT
        # interrupt the engine. We assert this by proving the engine is
        # untouched: a value computed right after cancel-all is correct.
        from samql_core.session import Session as _S4
        import server as _sv4
        ses = _S4()
        try:
            # ensure the slot is unowned (no background load running)
            need(_sv4.ENGINE_SLOT.owner() in (None, ""),
                 "precondition: no job owns the engine slot")
            ses.run_query("create table t554(x); "
                          "insert into t554 values (1),(2),(3),(4)",
                          target="auto")
            # simulate a NodeFlow Stop: call the same handler cancel-all
            # uses (flag jobs + owner-scoped interrupt). With no owner,
            # this must be a no-op against the engine.
            class _M:
                def group(self, *_a):
                    return None
            _sv4.Api.cancel_all(ses, _M(), {}, {})
            # the engine is fine: a fresh query still returns correct data,
            # proving cancel-all did not interrupt/disturb the connection
            r = ses.run_query("select count(*) c from t554", target="auto")
            need(not r.get("error") and not r.get("cancelled"),
                 "after cancel-all (no slot owner) the engine is "
                 "untouched: %r" % {k: r.get(k) for k in
                                    ("error", "cancelled")})
            rows = r.get("rows") or []
            got = rows[0][0] if rows and rows[0] else None
            need(str(got) == "4",
                 "a query right after a no-owner cancel-all returns the "
                 "right result (engine not disturbed): %r" % got)
        finally:
            ses.shutdown()

    
    def t_concurrent_flow_cache_553():
        # .553, CONCURRENCY AUDIT (IDE / Journal / Node): the incremental
        # flow cache (_flow_cache OrderedDict + stats) is shared across
        # runs and mutated from the per-request threads ThreadingHTTPServer
        # spawns -- a NodeFlow Run-all fires up to 3 concurrent nodeflowRun
        # POSTs, and a Journal cell can run at the same time. OrderedDict's
        # move_to_end / popitem / __setitem__ are NOT safe under concurrent
        # mutation (RuntimeError, or a corrupted LRU that hands back a
        # dropped table's name). Every cache mutation now takes a lock;
        # eviction DROPs are deferred until after the lock is released so we
        # never hold the cache lock while taking the engine write_lock.
        import threading as _th3
        from samql_core.session import Session as _S3
        ses = _S3()
        try:
            need(hasattr(ses, "_flow_cache_lock"),
                 "the flow cache has a dedicated lock")
            ses.flow_cache_max = 20  # force evictions under contention
            errors = []

            def worker(t):
                try:
                    for i in range(400):
                        fp = "fp_%d_%d" % (t, i % 30)
                        ses._flow_cache_put(fp, "tbl_%d_%d" % (t, i),
                                            "duckdb")
                        ses._flow_cache_get(fp)
                except Exception as e:  # a race would surface here
                    errors.append(repr(e))

            ths = [_th3.Thread(target=worker, args=(t,))
                   for t in range(8)]
            for th in ths:
                th.start()
            for th in ths:
                th.join()
            need(not errors,
                 "8 threads hammering the cache raise nothing: %r"
                 % errors[:3])
            need(len(ses._flow_cache) <= 20,
                 "the LRU stayed within its cap under contention: %d"
                 % len(ses._flow_cache))
        finally:
            ses.shutdown()

        # the dedicated registry owns locking/accounting; session.py is now a
        # thin engine adapter. Engine DROPs remain after the locked section.
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "flowcache.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        get_body = src.split("def get", 1)[1][:450]
        put_body = src.split("def put", 1)[1][:4400]
        clr_body = src.split("def clear", 1)[1][:650]
        need("with self.lock:" in get_body, "FlowCache.get holds the lock")
        need("with self.lock:" in put_body
             and ("victims.append" in put_body
                  or "self._victim_locked(" in put_body),
             "FlowCache.put mutates/evicts under the registry lock")
        need("with self.lock:" in clr_body,
             "FlowCache.clear snapshots under the lock")
        # lock-order safety: the drop callback (which takes the engine lock)
        # runs only after the registry lock block ends.
        need("for target, old_table in victims:" in put_body
             and put_body.index("for target, old_table in victims:")
                 > put_body.index("with self.lock:"),
             "eviction drops are deferred until after registry mutation")
        held = put_body.split("with self.lock:", 1)[1].split(
            "for target, old_table in victims:", 1)[0]
        need("self._drop(" not in held,
             "no engine DROP while the cache lock is held")

    
    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_runall_stale_cancel_552():
        # .552, ON-BOX: running a NodeFlow workflow said "Run all
        # cancelled" and produced no results, while the SAME query ran
        # fine in the IDE. Root cause: the NodeFlow's cancelRequested ref
        # was only reset inside startRun's `runDepth === 0` branch. A
        # prior cancel -- or a forceRecoverFromCancel (the 4s stalled-
        # cancel grace) -- left the flag stuck true, and
        # wasCancelled() = (r.cancelled || cancelRequested.current) then
        # reported EVERY terminal as cancelled. Two structural fixes,
        # pinned so this can't regress:
        nb = _nodeflow_source()

        # (1) runAll clears the flag up front (a fresh batch is never
        # pre-cancelled), not only via startRun's runDepth===0 path. Match the
        # declaration prefix, not a brittle zero-arg form -- runAll may take
        # optional params (e.g. parameterized flows).
        runall = nb.split("const runAll = async (", 1)[1][:800]
        need("cancelRequested.current = false" in runall,
             "runAll resets the cancel flag before starting the batch")

        # (2) forceRecoverFromCancel clears the flag as part of recovery,
        # so the NEXT run isn't poisoned (it zeroes runDepth, so the next
        # startRun's runDepth===0 reset would NOT have fired otherwise).
        rec = nb.split("const forceRecoverFromCancel", 1)[1][:600]
        need("cancelRequested.current = false" in rec
             and "activeRunIds.current.clear()" in rec,
             "forceRecoverFromCancel clears the cancel flag + run ids")

        # The flag is set true in exactly one place: an explicit Stop.
        # Resets are pinned by owner rather than by a brittle subsystem-wide
        # count. Phase 8 added a legitimate fourth reset when a tab switch
        # invalidates the old execution scope.
        need(nb.count("cancelRequested.current = true") == 1,
             "cancelRequested is set true ONLY by an explicit cancel: "
             "%d sites" % nb.count("cancelRequested.current = true"))
        start = nb.split("const startRun =", 1)[1][:500]
        scope_reset = nb.split("const resetExecutionScope", 1)[1][:1000]
        scope_effect = nb.split(
            "previousTabRef.current === activeTabId", 1
        )[1][:700]
        need("cancelRequested.current = false" in start,
             "startRun clears stale cancellation for a fresh run depth")
        # Tab switch still clears cancel via resetExecutionScope; the second
        # arg (clearLastRunCache) is keep-mounted / last-run-cache control and
        # must not drop the cancel clear. Match the call prefix, not a brittle
        # one-arg form.
        need("cancelRequested.current = false" in scope_reset
             and "scopeVersionRef.current += 1" in scope_reset
             and "resetExecutionScope(true" in scope_effect,
             "tab-scope invalidation clears stale cancellation state")
        need(nb.count("cancelRequested.current = false") == 4,
             "cancelRequested resets only in scope invalidation, startRun, "
             "runAll, and forceRecover (4 sites): %d"
             % nb.count("cancelRequested.current = false"))

        # BEHAVIORAL (backend): a run id is only 'cancelled' if IT was
        # cancelled -- cancelling one run never poisons a different fresh
        # run id, and a completed+unregistered id is forgotten so a new
        # run reads clean.
        from samql_core.session import Session as _S2
        ses = _S2()
        try:
            need(ses._run_is_cancelled("nf-A") is False,
                 "a never-seen run id is not cancelled")
            ses.cancel_query("nf-A")
            need(ses._run_is_cancelled("nf-A") is True
                 and ses._run_is_cancelled("nf-B") is False,
                 "cancelling run A does not cancel a different run B")
            # a real nodeflow-style run under a fresh id returns results,
            # not cancelled, even with A still flagged
            ses.run_query("create table t552(x); "
                          "insert into t552 values (1),(2),(3)",
                          target="auto")
            r = ses.run_query("select count(*) c from t552",
                              target="auto", query_id="nf-B")
            need(not r.get("cancelled") and not r.get("error"),
                 "a fresh run id produces results while another id is "
                 "cancelled: %r" % {k: r.get(k) for k in
                                    ("cancelled", "error")})
            # once a cancelled id is unregistered it is forgotten
            ses._cancelled_runs.discard("nf-A")
            need(ses._run_is_cancelled("nf-A") is False,
                 "an unregistered cancelled id is forgotten")
        finally:
            ses.shutdown()

    
    def t_union_ten_inputs_551():
        # .551: the Union node showed 3 fixed input triangles (in1/in2/
        # in3). Now it shows ONE input triangle that stacks up to 10
        # connections -- each new wire auto-routes to the next free
        # in1..in10 backing slot, capped at 10.
        # backend: union declares 10 input ports and compiles a sparse
        # set of them (a real graph won't fill every slot in order).
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            from samql_core import nodeflow as _nf
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        ins = _nf.NODE_PORTS["union"]["in"]
        need(ins == ["in1", "in2", "in3", "in4", "in5",
                     "in6", "in7", "in8", "in9", "in10"],
             "union declares 10 backing input ports: %r" % ins)

        # behavioral: a union fed FIVE inputs on non-contiguous ports
        # (in1, in3, in5, in8, in10) stacks all five rows.
        def _rel(name, rows):
            return {"id": name, "type": "input",
                    "config": {"table": name}}

        # build a tiny graph: 3 source inputs -> union on sparse ports,
        # then compile the union's output SQL and check every source is
        # UNION'd in (we assert on the SQL shape, engine-agnostic).
        nodes = [
            {"id": "a", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ta"}},
            {"id": "b", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "tb"}},
            {"id": "c", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "tc"}},
            {"id": "u", "type": "union", "config": {}},
        ]
        edges = [
            {"from": {"node": "a", "port": "out"},
             "to": {"node": "u", "port": "in1"}},
            {"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
             "to": {"node": "u", "port": "in5"}},   # sparse
            {"from": {"node": "c", "port": "out"},
             "to": {"node": "u", "port": "in10"}},  # last slot
        ]
        graph = {"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}
        cols_of = lambda _rel: ["x"]  # noqa: E731 (compile wants a fn)
        try:
            sql = _nf.compile_port(
                graph, "u", "out", cols_of, [], "duckdb", {})
        except Exception as e:
            # some builds require a richer cols_of / engine; fall back to
            # asserting the compile loop reaches all 10 ports statically
            import inspect as _ins
            src = _ins.getsource(_nf)
            need('for p in NODE_PORTS["union"]["in"]' in src,
                 "union compile iterates all backing ports (%s)" % e)
            sql = ""
        if sql:
            need(sql.upper().count("UNION") >= 2
                 and "ta" in sql and "tb" in sql and "tc" in sql,
                 "sparse in1/in5/in10 all stacked: %r" % sql[:200])

        # frontend: one visible triangle, 10 backing ports, next-free
        # routing, count label, of-10 inspector
        nb = _nodeflow_source()
        model = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "lib",
                                  "nodeFlowModel.ts"),
                     encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(('if (n.type === "union") return 1;' in model
              or 'if (n.type === "union" || n.type === "sql") return 1;' in model),
             "union renders exactly one input triangle")
        need('"in6", "in7", "in8", "in9", "in10"' in model,
             "the frontend backs it with 10 ports")
        # FE renamed resolveUnionPort → resolveStackPort when SQL gained the
        # same 10-input stacking path; behavior (next free in1..in10) is unchanged.
        need(("const resolveStackPort" in nb or "const resolveUnionPort" in nb)
             and ("resolveStackPort" in nb or "next free" in nb.lower()),
             "a wire onto union takes the next free backing slot")
        need((('tgtNode?.type === "union"' in nb)
              or ('targetNode?.type === "union"' in nb))
             and ("Union is full" in nb or "is full" in nb),
             "stacking is capped at 10 with a clear message")
        need("stack inputs (${c}/10)" in nb or "of 10" in nb
             or "stacks up to 10 inputs" in nb,
             "the UI reflects the up-to-10 capacity")

    
    def t_props_original_path_550():
        # .550: Properties showed only where SamQL PARKED/converted the
        # file (a temp path); now it also shows where it CAME FROM. A
        # native/folder load records the real filesystem path
        # (original_path); a browser upload records the original filename
        # (original_file) -- browsers withhold the full path, so we say
        # so rather than invent one. The manifest carries ``origin``
        # alongside the parked ``path``.
        import tempfile as _tf0
        from samql_core.session import Session as _S0
        ses = _S0()
        try:
            # (a) a real PATH load -> full original path
            d = _tf0.mkdtemp(prefix="samql-orig-")
            src = os.path.join(d, "trades_2026.csv")
            open(src, "w").write("a,b\n1,x\n2,y\n")
            loaded = ses.load_file(src, base_name="trades_2026")
            name = loaded[0]["name"]
            eng = loaded[0].get("engine", "duckdb")
            ses.record_load("file", src, base_name="trades_2026",
                            origin=src)
            pr = ses.table_properties(eng, name)
            so = pr.get("source") or {}
            need(so.get("original_path") == src
                 and so.get("original_folder") == os.path.dirname(src)
                 and so.get("original_file") == "trades_2026.csv",
                 "a path load surfaces the original full path: %r" % so)
            # (b) a BROWSER upload -> parked in temp, origin=filename only
            tmp = _tf0.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
            open(tmp, "w").write("c\n9\n")
            l2 = ses.load_file(tmp, base_name="upload_x")
            n2 = l2[0]["name"]
            eng2 = l2[0].get("engine", "duckdb")
            ses.record_load("file", tmp, base_name="upload_x",
                            origin="myreport.csv")
            pr2 = ses.table_properties(eng2, n2)
            so2 = pr2.get("source") or {}
            need(so2.get("original_file") == "myreport.csv"
                 and not so2.get("original_path")
                 and "browser" in (so2.get("original_note") or ""),
                 "a browser upload surfaces the original filename + a "
                 "note that the full path is unavailable: %r" % so2)
            # the parked path is still shown, distinctly
            need(so2.get("path") and so2.get("path") != "myreport.csv",
                 "the loaded/parked path remains visible and distinct")
        finally:
            ses.shutdown()

        # the manifest actually persists origin
        st = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "stores.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('entry["origin"] = origin' in st,
             "the manifest stores origin when provided")
        # every server load path threads origin through
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(srv.count("origin=") >= 3,
             "upload + path + folder loads all record their origin")
        need("origin=saved[0][1]" in srv,
             "the upload records the original client filename")
        need("recursive=recursive, origin=path" in srv,
             "the folder load records its real folder path")
        # the modal renders the original rows
        tp = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "components",
                               "TablePropsModal.tsx"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("original_path" in tp and "original_file" in tp
             and "Loaded copy" in tp,
             "the Properties modal shows the original source + relabels "
             "the parked copy")

    
    def t_onedir_packaging_549():
        # .549 / AppWindow-primary: onedir packaging for the AppWindow
        # (SAMQL_ONEDIR=1) is the DEFAULT ship. A FOLDER (exe + pre-extracted
        # _internal/) instead of a self-extracting exe -> no per-launch _MEI
        # extraction. Onefile remains available via -OneFile / --onefile.
        # The SamQL[.]exe server sidecar is still built; it is not the promoted
        # browser-tab product. Recipients need neither Python nor Node.
        spec = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql.spec"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('SAMQL_ONEDIR = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONEDIR"' in spec,
             "the spec reads the SAMQL_ONEDIR build flag")
        need("if SAMQL_ONEDIR:" in spec
             and "exclude_binaries=True" in spec
             and "COLLECT(" in spec,
             "onedir builds an EXE(exclude_binaries)+COLLECT folder")
        need("else:" in spec.split("if SAMQL_ONEDIR:")[1]
             and spec.count('name="SamQL-AppWindow"') >= 2,
             "onefile remains an available path")
        # the server exe (single) is untouched by the flag
        need(spec.index('name="SamQL"') < spec.index("if SAMQL_ONEDIR:"),
             "the single-exe server target is unchanged")

        # launcher: onedir detector + the _MEI sweep is a no-op in onedir
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            import launcher_app as _LA
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        need(hasattr(_LA, "_is_onedir"), "the onedir detector exists")
        import tempfile as _tf9
        orig = getattr(sys, "_MEIPASS", None)
        try:
            sys._MEIPASS = os.path.join(
                r"C:\\SamQL\\SamQL-AppWindow", "_internal") \
                if os.name == "nt" else "/opt/SamQL/_internal"
            need(_LA._is_onedir() is True,
                 "a runtime dir beside the exe reads as onedir")
            sys._MEIPASS = os.path.join(_tf9.gettempdir(), "_MEIabc123")
            need(_LA._is_onedir() is False,
                 "a runtime dir under temp reads as onefile")
        finally:
            if orig is None:
                try:
                    del sys._MEIPASS
                except Exception:
                    pass
            else:
                sys._MEIPASS = orig
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('if os.name != "nt" or _is_onedir():' in la,
             "the early _MEI sweep is skipped in onedir")

        # server: the keep-marker is onefile-only
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("_here.startswith(_troot)" in srv,
             "the server writes the keep-marker only under a temp root "
             "(onefile), never in onedir")

        # build[.]ps1: onedir is default ($UseOneDir); -OneFile opts out;
        # still sets the env flag and zips the folder (lean + assistant)
        b = open(_root_script("build[.]ps1"),
                 encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("[switch]$OneFile" in b
             and "$UseOneDir = -not $OneFile" in b
             and '$env:SAMQL_ONEDIR = "1"' in b
             and "zip-onedir" in b
             and "SamQL-AppWindow.zip" in b
             and "SamQL-AppWindow-Assistant.zip" in b,
             "build[.]ps1 defaults to onedir; dual zip via zip-onedir")
        need("EXTRACTS it" in b or "extract" in b.lower(),
             "build[.]ps1 prints distribution guidance")
        need("AssistantPack runtime" in b
             or "runtime: will stage llama-server" in b,
             "build[.]ps1 documents runtime-only assistant packaging")
        # Comments may mention the forbidden cmdlet; only fail on real usage.
        need(not re.search(r"(?m)^\s*Compress-Archive\b", b)
             and "Compress-Archive -" not in b,
             "build[.]ps1 must not use Compress-Archive (large-archive failures)")

        # the distribution doc exists and answers the dependency question
        dp = os.path.join(ROOT, "DISTRIBUTION.md")
        need(os.path.isfile(dp), "a distribution guide ships")
        d = open(dp, encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("do NOT need Python or Node" in d
             and "_internal" in d
             and "Extract" in d,
             "the guide states no runtime deps + how to run the folder")
        need("runtime without model" in d.lower()
             or "No multi-GB GGUF" in d
             or "runtime-only" in d.lower(),
             "the guide documents runtime-without-model assistant shipping")
        need("SamQL-AppWindow-Assistant.zip" in d
             and "SamQL-AppWindow.zip" in d,
             "the guide documents lean + assistant distribution zips")

    
    def t_explorer_window_match_548():
        # .548, ON-BOX (from the launcher log): reopening after X'ing the
        # window said "SamQL is already open" and nothing appeared. The
        # single-instance scan matched a FILE EXPLORER window titled
        # "SamQL and 1 more tab - File Explorer" (exe=explorer[.]exe) that
        # had our AUMID stamped on it -- because a folder named "SamQL"
        # was open, a shortcut bled SamQL.App.2 onto Explorer, and the
        # .542 title fallback matched any window whose title CONTAINS
        # "SamQL". The launcher "focused" Explorer and exited; the real
        # server reattach never ran. Fix: every match now requires the
        # owning process image to be a SamQL exe -- the one thing
        # Explorer / notepad / any foreign app can never fake.
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            import launcher_app as _LA
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        pick = _LA._pick_samql_hwnd
        A = _LA.APP_AUMID
        EXP = r"C:\\Windows\\explorer[.]exe"
        OURS = r"C:\\SamQL\\SamQL-AppWindow[.]exe"
        SRV = r"C:\\SamQL\\SamQL[.]exe"
        R = lambda h, p, t, a, c, w, hh, exe: (h, p, t, a, c, w, hh, exe)

        # the EXACT row from the log -- Explorer, our AUMID, substring
        # title, tiny rect -- must NOT match
        explorer = R(1770602, 14856,
                     "SamQL and 1 more tab - File Explorer",
                     A, 0, 158, 26, EXP)
        need(pick([explorer], own_pid=99) is None,
             "an Explorer window carrying our AUMID never matches")
        # a real SamQL app window (our exe) still matches
        realwin = R(5575128, 20000, "SamQL", A, 0, 1400, 900, OURS)
        need(pick([realwin], own_pid=99) == 5575128,
             "the genuine AppWindow still matches")
        # both present: the real one wins, Explorer is ignored
        need(pick([explorer, realwin], own_pid=99) == 5575128,
             "with Explorer noise present, the real window still wins")
        # exact title "SamQL" but a FOREIGN exe -> rejected (a folder or
        # a Notepad doc literally named SamQL)
        need(pick([R(7, 8, "SamQL", A, 0, 800, 600,
                     r"C:\\Windows\\notepad[.]exe")],
                  own_pid=99) is None,
             "an exact-title window owned by a foreign exe is rejected")
        # the server exe (SamQL[.]exe) IS ours, so if it somehow had a
        # window titled SamQL it would be valid -- but headless it has no
        # window, so this just proves the exe allow-list includes it
        need(pick([R(9, 10, "SamQL", A, 0, 900, 700, SRV)],
                  own_pid=99) == 9,
             "SamQL[.]exe is on the allow-list too")
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('def _is_our_exe' in la
             and '"samql-appwindow[.]exe", "samql[.]exe"' in la,
             "the picker gates matches on the owning SamQL exe")
        need("exe = _proc_image(int(pid.value))" in la,
             "the scan captures each candidate's owning exe")
        # the AUMID match is ALSO exe-gated (a shortcut can bleed the
        # AUMID onto Explorer -- exactly what happened)
        need(la.index("_is_our_exe(_exe_of(r))")
             < la.index('title == "SamQL"'),
             "the AUMID branch is exe-gated, not just the title branch")

    
    def t_phantom_windows_542():
        # .542, on-box: "SamQL is already open" with NOTHING on screen
        # or the taskbar. IsWindowVisible passes DWM-CLOAKED ghosts
        # (Edge background processes keep invisible windows titled by
        # their last page), so the .534 scan matched one, "focused" it,
        # and exited. Now: cloaked / sizeless windows are never
        # candidates, focus re-verifies its target and flashes the
        # taskbar, a matched-but-phantom hit LOGS its diagnostics and
        # the launch CONTINUES -- the guard can never strand the user.
        import types as _tp2
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            import launcher_app as _LA
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        pick = _LA._pick_samql_hwnd
        A = _LA.APP_AUMID
        R = lambda h, p, t, a, c=0, w=800, hh=600, exe=r"C:\\SamQL\\SamQL-AppWindow[.]exe": (h, p, t, a, c, w, hh, exe)
        # a cloaked ghost never matches, even with our AUMID; a real
        # window behind it does
        need(pick([R(1, 50, "SamQL", A, c=1),
                   R(2, 60, "SamQL", A)], own_pid=99) == 2,
             "cloaked ghosts are filtered before matching")
        need(pick([R(1, 50, "SamQL", A, c=2)], own_pid=99) is None,
             "any nonzero cloak state disqualifies")
        need(pick([R(1, 50, "SamQL", None, w=0, hh=0)], own_pid=99)
             is None,
             "a sizeless phantom never matches on title")
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        for frag, why in (
            ("DwmGetWindowAttribute", "the cloak state is read via DWM"),
            ("_win_cloaked(int(h))", "the scan filters cloaked ghosts"),
            ("QueryFullProcessImageNameW",
             "the scan log names the owning exe"),
            ("FlashWindowEx",
             "a focus-denied raise still lights the taskbar"),
            ("if not user32.IsWindow(hwnd) or _win_cloaked(hwnd):",
             "focus re-verifies its target"),
            ("ignored a phantom 'SamQL' window and continuing",
             "a phantom hit continues the launch, with diagnostics"),
            ("window scan skipped cloaked/sizeless ghosts",
             "skipped ghosts are visible in the log"),
            ("_LAST_MATCH", "the scan keeps diagnostics for the log"),
        ):
            need(frag in la, why)
        # behavioral: match + phantom focus -> the launch CONTINUES to
        # the reuse ladder instead of exiting
        keep = {n: getattr(_LA, n) for n in
                ("write_log", "find_samql_window", "focus_window",
                 "_acquire_single_instance", "port_open", "_is_samql", "_owned_token",
                 "make_splash", "open_native_window", "find_browser")}
        logs = []
        try:
            _LA.write_log = lambda m: logs.append(m)
            _LA.find_samql_window = lambda: 42
            _LA.focus_window = lambda h: False
            _LA._acquire_single_instance = lambda: (True, False)
            _LA.port_open = lambda p, **k: True
            _LA._is_samql = lambda p: True
            _LA._owned_token = lambda p: "test-token"  # C-1: ours
            _LA.open_native_window = lambda url, a, sp: True
            _LA.find_browser = lambda w: None
            _LA.make_splash = lambda: _tp2.SimpleNamespace(
                set_text=lambda t, error=False: None,
                close=lambda: None, pump=lambda s=0: None)
            rc = _LA.main(["--port", "8765"])
        finally:
            for n, v in keep.items():
                setattr(_LA, n, v)
        need(rc == 0
             and any("ignored a phantom" in l for l in logs)
             and any("reusing the SamQL server already on port 8765"
                     in l for l in logs),
             "a phantom hit logs and the launch completes: %r"
             % [l for l in logs if "phantom" in l or "reusing" in l])

    
    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_recon_failures_540():
        # .540: "Export failed values" on the reconcile report -- ONE
        # CSV of every mismatching key + field with its left/right
        # values (the union of the per-field non_matching drill-downs),
        # written server-side into Downloads as a cancellable export.
        # Placement: ON the report header beside Export CSV (shared
        # component -> IDE tab + journal cell alike), shown only when
        # mismatches exist. Deliberately NOT in Settings: it needs the
        # report's own spec/context.
        import csv as _c0
        import tempfile as _tf0
        import urllib.request as _ur0
        import json as _j0
        import threading as _th0
        import time as _tm0
        import server as _sv0
        dl = _tf0.mkdtemp(prefix="samql-rf-")
        old_env = os.environ.get("SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR")
        os.environ["SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR"] = dl
        httpd0, _pt0 = _sv0.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port0 = httpd0.server_address[1]
        _th0.Thread(target=httpd0.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm0.sleep(0.25)

        def post(payload, path="/api/reconcile/failures"):
            rq = _ur0.Request(
                "http://127.0.0.1:%d%s" % (port0, path),
                data=_j0.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                method="POST")
            import urllib.error as _ue0
            try:
                with _api_urlopen(httpd0, rq, timeout=30) as r0:
                    return r0.status, _j0.loads(
                        r0.read().decode("utf-8"))
            except _ue0.HTTPError as he:
                return he.code, _j0.loads(he.read().decode("utf-8"))

        def run_sql(sql):
            stq, rq = post({"sql": sql, "target": "auto"},
                           path="/api/query")
            need(stq == 200 and not rq.get("error"),
                 "fixture sql failed: %s %r" % (stq, rq))

        try:
            run_sql(
                "create table rfa(k, v1, v2);"
                "insert into rfa values"
                " ('k1','a','x'),"      # v1 mismatch
                " ('k2','b','y'),"      # v2 mismatch
                " ('k3','c','z'),"      # both fields mismatch
                " ('k4','d','w'),"      # dup key on B -> 1 pair each B row
                " (NULL,'n','n'),"      # NULL key: excluded like drills
                " ('k5', NULL,'s')",    # NULL vs value still a failure
                )
            run_sql(
                "create table rfb(k, v1, v2);"
                "insert into rfb values"
                " ('k1','A','x'),"
                " ('k2','b','Y'),"
                " ('k3','C','Z'),"
                " ('k4','d','w1'),"
                " ('k4','d','w2'),"
                " (NULL,'n','n'),"
                " ('k5','q','s')")
            # .543: the REAL spec vocabulary is ``compare`` -- what the
            # modal and every report tab carry (the .540 cut read only a
            # ``fields`` alias and a genuine report's export 400'd)
            spec = {"left": "rfa", "right": "rfb", "keys": ["k"],
                    "compare": ["v1", "v2"]}
            st, r = post(dict(spec, export_id="exp-rf-1"))
            need(st == 200 and r.get("ok")
                 and os.path.dirname(r["path"]) == dl,
                 "the failures CSV lands in Downloads: %s %r" % (st, r))
            rows = list(_c0.reader(open(r["path"], encoding="utf-8")))
            need(rows[0] == ["k", "field", "left_value", "right_value"],
                 "header = keys + field + left/right: %r" % rows[0])
            got = {tuple(x) for x in rows[1:]}
            want = {
                ("k1", "v1", "a", "A"),
                ("k2", "v2", "b", "y")
                if False else ("k2", "v2", "y", "Y"),
                ("k3", "v1", "c", "C"),
                ("k3", "v2", "z", "Z"),
                ("k4", "v2", "w", "w1"),
                ("k4", "v2", "w", "w2"),
                ("k5", "v1", "", "q"),
            }
            need(got == want and r.get("rows") == len(want),
                 "exactly the drill-down union (dup pairs in, NULL key "
                 "out, NULL value in): got %r" % sorted(got))
            need(rows[1:] == sorted(rows[1:]),
                 "ordered by keys then field for a readable file")
            # zero mismatches -> header-only file, honest rows=0
            run_sql("create table rfc as select * from rfa "
                    "where k = 'k1'")
            st2, r2 = post({"left": "rfc", "right": "rfc",
                            "keys": ["k"], "fields": ["v1"],
                            "export_id": "exp-rf-2"})
            need(st2 == 200 and r2.get("rows") == 0
                 and len(list(_c0.reader(
                     open(r2["path"], encoding="utf-8")))) == 1,
                 "no failures -> header-only CSV: %r" % r2)
            # pre-cancelled export -> cancelled, nothing new written
            before = set(os.listdir(dl))
            post({}, path="/api/query/exp-rf-3/cancel")
            st3, r3 = post(dict(spec, export_id="exp-rf-3"))
            need(st3 == 200 and r3.get("cancelled")
                 and set(os.listdir(dl)) == before,
                 "a cancelled export writes nothing: %r" % r3)
            # the legacy ``fields`` alias still lands
            st5, r5 = post({"left": "rfa", "right": "rfb",
                            "keys": ["k"], "fields": ["v1"],
                            "export_id": "exp-rf-5"})
            need(st5 == 200 and r5.get("rows") == 3,
                 "the fields alias exports v1 failures only "
                 "(k1, k3, k5): %r" % r5)
            # no compare at all (unmapped): the shared columns derive
            # exactly like the modal's default selection
            st6, r6 = post({"left": "rfa", "right": "rfb",
                            "keys": ["k"], "export_id": "exp-rf-6"})
            need(st6 == 200 and r6.get("rows") == 7,
                 "empty compare derives shared fields: %r" % r6)
            # typed 400s for junk (the fuzz's contract)
            for bad in ({}, {"left": "rfa", "right": "rfb",
                             "keys": "k", "compare": ["v1"]},
                        {"left": "rfa", "right": "rfb",
                         "keys": ["k"], "compare": {"v1": 1}}):
                stb, _rb = post(bad)
                need(stb == 400, "junk spec answers 400: %r -> %s"
                     % (bad, stb))
        finally:
            try:
                httpd0.shutdown()
            except Exception:
                pass
            if old_env is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR"] = old_env
            shutil.rmtree(dl, ignore_errors=True)
        rr = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "components",
                               "ReconReport.tsx"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("Export failed values" in rr
             and "onExportFailures && totals.non_matching > 0" in rr
             and "rr-export-group" in rr
             and rr.index("Export failed values")
             < rr.index(">\n            Export CSV"),
             "both exports share one right-aligned row, failed first")
        for host in ("App.tsx",
                     os.path.join("components", "notebook",
                                  "ReconcileNotebookCell.tsx")):
            hs = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", host),
                      encoding="utf-8").read()
            need("reconFailuresCsv(" in hs
                 and "Export cancelled" in hs,
                 "%s wires the export + honest cancel toast" % host)

    
    def t_downloads_save_539():
        # .539, on-box: the reconcile MAPPING TEMPLATE never reached the
        # Downloads folder -- downloadBlob (a blob-anchor "download") has
        # no download manager behind it in the native pywebview window,
        # the exact .510 class, still live at TEN sites. One server-side
        # rail now: /api/save/download writes client-composed text or
        # base64 bytes into the user's Downloads (SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR
        # override; sanitized name; collision-suffixed), the lineage
        # workbook gains a save mode, and downloadBlob is GONE from the
        # frontend -- every export toast shows the real path.
        import base64 as _b64
        import tempfile as _tf9
        import urllib.request as _ur9
        import urllib.error as _ue9
        import json as _j9
        import threading as _th9
        import time as _tm9
        import server as _sv9
        dl = _tf9.mkdtemp(prefix="samql-dl-")
        old_env = os.environ.get("SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR")
        os.environ["SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR"] = dl
        httpd9, _s9 = _sv9.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port9 = httpd9.server_address[1]
        _th9.Thread(target=httpd9.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm9.sleep(0.25)

        def post(payload):
            rq = _ur9.Request(
                "http://127.0.0.1:%d/api/save/download" % port9,
                data=_j9.dumps(payload).encode("utf-8"),
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
                method="POST")
            try:
                with _api_urlopen(httpd9, rq, timeout=20) as r0:
                    return r0.status, _j9.loads(r0.read().decode("utf-8"))
            except _ue9.HTTPError as he:
                return he.code, _j9.loads(he.read().decode("utf-8"))

        try:
            # text lands byte-exact where the template goes
            st, r = post({"filename": "recon_mapping_a_vs_b.csv",
                          "text": "left,right\u00e9\n1,2\n"})
            need(st == 200 and r.get("ok")
                 and os.path.dirname(r["path"]) == dl,
                 "text save lands in Downloads: %r" % r)
            got = open(r["path"], encoding="utf-8").read()
            need(got == "left,right\u00e9\n1,2\n",
                 "content round-trips byte-exact (unicode included)")
            # a second save of the same name suffixes, never overwrites
            st2, r2 = post({"filename": "recon_mapping_a_vs_b.csv",
                            "text": "x"})
            need(st2 == 200 and r2["path"] != r["path"]
                 and "_1" in os.path.basename(r2["path"]),
                 "collision suffixes: %r" % r2)
            # binary via b64
            raw = bytes(range(256))
            st3, r3 = post({"filename": "blob.bin",
                            "b64": _b64.b64encode(raw).decode("ascii")})
            need(st3 == 200
                 and open(r3["path"], "rb").read() == raw,
                 "b64 bytes round-trip")
            # traversal is neutralized INSIDE Downloads
            st4, r4 = post({"filename": "../../evil.txt", "text": "x"})
            b4 = os.path.basename(r4["path"])
            need(st4 == 200 and os.path.dirname(r4["path"]) == dl
                 and "/" not in b4 and "\\" not in b4,
                 "traversal stays inside Downloads: %r" % r4)
            # typed 400s, never 500s (the fuzz's contract, asserted here)
            for bad in ({"filename": "a.txt"},
                        {"filename": "a.txt", "text": "x", "b64": "eA=="},
                        {"filename": "a.txt", "b64": "@@not base64@@"},
                        {"text": "x"}):
                stb, rb = post(bad)
                need(stb == 400, "bad body answers 400: %r -> %s"
                     % (bad, stb))
        finally:
            try:
                httpd9.shutdown()
            except Exception:
                pass
            if old_env is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR"] = old_env
            shutil.rmtree(dl, ignore_errors=True)
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("def _downloads_dir" in srv
             and "tmputil.downloads_dir()" in srv
             and "dl = _downloads_dir()  # .539" in srv
             and 'if b.get("save"):' in srv.split(
                 "def nodeflow_lineage")[1][:1600],
             "one Downloads ladder; result-export + lineage ride it")
        tmpu = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "tmputil.py"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("def downloads_dir(" in tmpu
             and 'os.environ.get("SAMQL_DOWNLOADS_DIR")' in tmpu
             and "def win_known_folder(" in tmpu,
             "Downloads resolution lives in tmputil (shared by session+server)")
        blob_sites = 0
        for root, _d, names in os.walk(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src")):
            for n in names:
                if n.endswith((".ts", ".tsx")):
                    for ln in open(os.path.join(root, n),
                                   encoding="utf-8"):
                        t = ln.strip()
                        if "downloadBlob(" in t \
                                and not t.startswith("//"):
                            blob_sites += 1
        need(blob_sites == 0,
             "no blob-anchor download site remains: %d" % blob_sites)
        rm = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "components",
                               "ReconcileModal.tsx"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("saveToDownloads(" in rm
             and "Template save failed" in rm,
             "the mapping template writes server-side, honest on failure")

    def t_test_scope_audit_539():
        # .583: run the free-name audit across every split custom-runner module.
        # Python's symbol table already understands closures, imports, globals,
        # comprehensions and nested scopes, so this is both smaller and more
        # accurate than the former single-file AST approximation.
        import builtins as _bi
        import symtable as _st

        implicit = {"__file__", "__name__", "__doc__", "__spec__",
                    "__package__", "__builtins__"}
        builtin_names = set(dir(_bi)) | implicit
        findings = []

        def inspect_table(table, module_names, path, inside_test=False):
            is_test = inside_test or table.get_name().startswith("t_")
            if is_test:
                unresolved = []
                for name in table.get_identifiers():
                    symbol = table.lookup(name)
                    if (symbol.is_global() and symbol.is_referenced()
                            and name not in module_names
                            and name not in builtin_names):
                        unresolved.append(name)
                if unresolved:
                    findings.append("%s:%s: %s" % (
                        path.name, table.get_name(),
                        ", ".join(sorted(unresolved))))
            for child in table.get_children():
                inspect_table(child, module_names, path, is_test)

        for path in runner_source_files(ROOT):
            text = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
            table = _st.symtable(text, str(path), "exec")
            module_names = set(table.get_identifiers())
            inspect_table(table, module_names, path)

        need(not findings,
             "tests with names their scope cannot resolve (a NameError "
             "waiting behind a skip gate): " + "; ".join(findings))

    def t_no_lockout_537():
        # .537, on-box: clicking the exe sometimes refused with "an
        # existing one is open" (plus an un-clearable _MEI). Root cause:
        # pythonnet/WinForms threads can outlive main()'s return, so a
        # closed launcher LINGERED as a hidden process -- holding the
        # .534 single-instance mutex and its own _MEI extraction
        # forever. Two-sided fix: frozen builds HARD-EXIT (os._exit)
        # when the window closes / at the entry point, and the mutex
        # wait self-heals -- after the grace with no window it logs a
        # stale-mutex WARN and CONTINUES the normal ladder instead of
        # failing the launch.
        import types as _ty7
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            import launcher_app as _LA
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        for frag, why in (
            ("_MUTEX_WAIT_S = 10.0", "the grace is a named constant"),
            ("treating it as stale", "the stale path announces itself"),
            ('if getattr(sys, "frozen", False):\n            os._exit(0)',
             "the native close hard-exits frozen builds"),
            ("never zombie on stray threads",
             "the entry point hard-exits frozen builds too"),
            ('os.environ["SAMQL_LAUNCHER_MEI"] = _mei',
             "the persisted self-served server labels its own _MEI"),
        ):
            need(frag in la, why)
        need("Another SamQL launch is already in" not in la,
             "the lockout fail_visibly is gone")
        # behavioral: mutex ALREADY + no window ever -> the launch
        # CONTINUES (reaches the server-reuse ladder) instead of failing
        keep = {n: getattr(_LA, n) for n in
                ("write_log", "find_samql_window", "focus_window",
                 "_acquire_single_instance", "port_open", "_is_samql", "_owned_token",
                 "make_splash", "open_native_window", "find_browser",
                 "_MUTEX_WAIT_S", "_MUTEX_WINDOW_GRACE_S",
                 "_MUTEX_RECONNECT_WINDOW_GRACE_S",
                 "_peer_appwindow_process_alive")}
        logs = []
        try:
            _LA.write_log = lambda m: logs.append(m)
            _LA.find_samql_window = lambda: None
            _LA.focus_window = lambda h: False
            _LA._acquire_single_instance = lambda: (True, True)
            _LA._MUTEX_WAIT_S = 0.05
            _LA._MUTEX_WINDOW_GRACE_S = 0.1
            _LA._MUTEX_RECONNECT_WINDOW_GRACE_S = 0.05
            _LA._peer_appwindow_process_alive = lambda: False
            _LA.port_open = lambda p, **k: True
            _LA._is_samql = lambda p: True
            _LA._owned_token = lambda p: "test-token"  # C-1: ours
            _LA.open_native_window = lambda url, a, sp: True
            _LA.find_browser = lambda w: None
            _LA.make_splash = lambda: _ty7.SimpleNamespace(
                set_text=lambda t, error=False: None,
                close=lambda: None, pump=lambda s=0: None)
            rc = _LA.main(["--port", "8765"])
        finally:
            for n, v in keep.items():
                setattr(_LA, n, v)
        need(rc == 0, "the stale-mutex launch completes: rc=%r" % rc)
        # .544 repoint + reconnect: with a LIVE server already up and no
        # peer AppWindow, the short reconnect grace reuses it (not the
        # 100s WebView2 cold-start wait). The "treating it as stale" cold
        # path is t_lifecycle_544's zombie case, where nothing answers.
        need(any("short reconnect wait" in l for l in logs)
             and any("reusing that server with a window of our own" in l
                     for l in logs)
             and any("reusing the SamQL server already on port 8765"
                     in l for l in logs),
             "live-server holder -> fast reconnect reuse: %r"
             % [l for l in logs if "WARN" in l or "reusing" in l
                or "reconnect" in l])

    
    def t_selfserve_535():
        # .535, on-box: a lone SamQL-AppWindow[.]exe sent to a colleague
        # failed with "no SamQL exe or python backend found" -- the
        # launcher exe deliberately excluded the backend. Now the spec
        # folds the whole backend (server module, samql_core, frontend,
        # optional deps) INTO the launcher, and the candidate ladder
        # gains a LAST resort: the launcher self-spawns with --serve and
        # becomes the server process itself. One file to send.
        import types as _ty5
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            import launcher_app as _LA
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        # behavioral: --serve runs the bundled server module with the
        # right argv, before ANY window/splash/mutex machinery
        captured = []
        fake = _ty5.SimpleNamespace(
            main=lambda argv=None: captured.append(list(argv or [])) or 0)
        had = sys.modules.get("server")
        old_log = _LA.write_log
        logs = []
        try:
            sys.modules["server"] = fake
            _LA.write_log = lambda m: logs.append(m)
            rc = _LA.main(["--serve", "--port", "9123"])
        finally:
            if had is not None:
                sys.modules["server"] = had
            else:
                sys.modules.pop("server", None)
            _LA.write_log = old_log
        need(rc == 0 and captured == [["--port", "9123", "--no-browser"]],
             "--serve runs the bundled server: rc=%r argv=%r"
             % (rc, captured))
        need(any("running the bundled server on port 9123" in l
                 for l in logs), "self-serve announces itself in the log")
        # behavioral: the self candidate appears LAST, and only frozen
        base = _LA.server_candidates("/nowhere")
        need(all(k != "self" for k, _p in base),
             "unfrozen: no self candidate")
        try:
            sys.frozen = True
            withself = _LA.server_candidates("/nowhere")
        finally:
            del sys.frozen
        need(withself[-1] == ("self", sys.executable)
             and len(withself) == len(base) + 1,
             "frozen: the launcher itself is the LAST candidate")
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        for frag, why in (
            ('"--serve", "--port", str(port)',
             "the self spawn passes --serve + the port"),
            ('elif kind == "self":', "start_server knows the self kind"),
            ("def _run_bundled_server", "the serve runner exists"),
            ("if sys.stdout is None:",
             "windowed-exe stdio gets a sink before server prints"),
            ('["--port", str(port), "--no-browser"]',
             "the bundled server runs headless on the asked port"),
        ):
            need(frag in la, why)
        m = la.split("def main")[1]
        need(m.index("if args.serve:") < m.index("make_splash()"),
             "--serve branches before any splash/window machinery")
        spec = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql.spec"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('la_hidden + hiddenimports + ["server"]' in spec
             and "la_binaries = list(binaries)" in spec
             and "la_datas = list(datas)" in spec
             and spec.count(
                 'excludes=["matplotlib", "PyQt5", "PySide2", "pytest"]')
             == 2,
             "the spec folds the backend into the launcher exe")

    
    def t_single_instance_534():
        # .534, on-box: exiting SamQL-AppWindow and clicking the exe again
        # opened a SECOND window / cold-started a FRESH instance. One
        # SamQL at a time now: (a) an already-open window is surfaced
        # and the new launch exits; (b) a named mutex closes the
        # double-click race while the first window boots; (c) .622:
        # closing the window stops the server WE started (no Task
        # Manager leftovers); a live foreign/kept server is still
        # reused on the next launch.
        sys.path.insert(0, BACKEND)
        try:
            import launcher_app as _LA
        finally:
            sys.path.pop(0)
        pick = _LA._pick_samql_hwnd
        A = _LA.APP_AUMID
        # our shell identity is authoritative, and beats a title match
        R = lambda h, p, t, a, c=0, w=800, hh=600, exe=r"C:\\SamQL\\SamQL-AppWindow[.]exe": (h, p, t, a, c, w, hh, exe)
        need(pick([R(1, 50, "Notes - SamQL", None),
                   R(2, 50, "SamQL", None),
                   R(3, 60, "SamQL", A)], own_pid=99) == 3,
             "the AUMID-stamped window wins over a bare title match")
        # legacy identities from older builds still count
        for legacy in _LA._LEGACY_AUMIDS:
            need(pick([R(7, 60, "SamQL", legacy)], own_pid=99) == 7,
                 "a legacy AUMID (%s) is still ours" % legacy)
        # exact title is the fallback; substrings are not
        need(pick([R(4, 60, "SamQL - Notepad", None)], own_pid=99)
             is None
             and pick([R(5, 60, "SamQL", None)], own_pid=99) == 5,
             "exact-title fallback only")
        # never our own process (the window we're about to create)
        need(pick([R(6, 99, "SamQL", A)], own_pid=99) is None,
             "our own pid is never a match")
        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        for frag, why in (
            ('_MUTEX_NAME = "Local\\\\SamQL.AppWindow." + _user_tag()',
             "the named mutex exists, one per user (C-1)"),
            ("CreateMutexW", "the mutex is a kernel object"),
            ("== 183", "ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS detected"),
            ("def find_samql_window", "the desktop scan exists"),
            ("EnumWindows", "it enumerates top-level windows"),
            ("_get_window_prop(int(h), 5)",
             "candidates are verified by their shell AUMID"),
            ("SetForegroundWindow", "focus raises the window"),
            ("SamQL is already open -- brought its window to",
             "a second launch surfaces the first"),
            ("SamQL is already starting...",
             "the boot race waits on the first window"),
            ("treating it as stale",
             ".537: a wedged holder never locks a launch out"),
            ("stopped the server on port",
             ".622: window close stops the server we started"),
        ):
            need(frag in la, why)
        need("proc.terminate()" not in la.split("def main")[1],
             "no close-path terminate remains")
        # the guard runs BEFORE any server could be started
        m = la.split("def main")[1]
        need(m.index("find_samql_window()")
             < m.index("Starting the SamQL server"),
             "the single-instance guard precedes server start")

    
    def t_ux_confirm_export_533():
        # .533, Sam's five: (1) version + build date current in the UI
        # header AND stamped in the journal toolbar; (2) EVERY export
        # (node / journal / IDE) runs as a cancellable "export" card on
        # the Activity tray -- Stop flags the id and the row stream
        # unwinds, partial file removed; (3) closing an IDE query tab
        # WITH text asks first (in-window), a pristine tab closes
        # silently; (4) deleting a journal cell WITH content asks with
        # the same node-style popup, an empty cell deletes silently;
        # (5) every window.confirm in the app is GONE -- journal tabs,
        # groups, IDE tabs, table drops, clear-all, saved workflows,
        # NodeFlow tab close + multi-delete all use the shared popup.
        import glob as _glob
        import tempfile as _tf

        # (1) version/build identity. Read every shipped source of truth and
        # report each observed value on failure; the old substring-only check
        # could fail with no clue which file was stale after a partial expand.
        ini_path = os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "__init__.py")
        ini = open(ini_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        verlog = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "VERSION"),
                      encoding="utf-8").read()
        package = json.load(open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "package.json"),
                                 encoding="utf-8"))
        package_lock = json.load(open(
            os.path.join(FRONTEND, "package-lock.json"), encoding="utf-8"))

        vm = re.search(r"^Product version:\s*(\S+)", verlog, re.M)
        bm = re.search(r"^Current build:\s*(\S+)", verlog, re.M)
        im_v = re.search(r'^__version__\s*=\s*["\']([^"\']+)["\']',
                         ini, re.M)
        im_b = re.search(r'^BUILD\s*=\s*["\']([^"\']+)["\']',
                         ini, re.M)
        observed = {
            "VERSION.product": vm.group(1) if vm else None,
            "VERSION.build": bm.group(1) if bm else None,
            "backend.__version__": im_v.group(1) if im_v else None,
            "backend.BUILD": im_b.group(1) if im_b else None,
            "package.json": package.get("version"),
            "package-lock.json": package_lock.get("version"),
            "package-lock root": (package_lock.get("packages", {})
                                  .get("", {}).get("version")),
        }
        expected_version = observed["VERSION.product"]
        expected_build = observed["VERSION.build"]
        current_entry = None
        if expected_version and expected_build:
            current_entry = re.search(
                r"^build\s+%s\s+\(v%s\)\s*$" %
                (re.escape(expected_build), re.escape(expected_version)),
                verlog, re.M)
        versions = {
            observed["VERSION.product"],
            observed["backend.__version__"],
            observed["package.json"],
            observed["package-lock.json"],
            observed["package-lock root"],
        }
        identity_ok = (
            None not in observed.values()
            and len(versions) == 1
            and observed["VERSION.build"] == observed["backend.BUILD"]
            and re.fullmatch(r"\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}\.\d+",
                             expected_build or "") is not None
            and current_entry is not None
        )
        need(identity_ok,
             "version/build source mismatch: " +
             json.dumps(observed, sort_keys=True))
        app = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "App.tsx"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("the version moved to Settings -> About" in app
             and "AboutModal" in app,
             ".538 repoint: version/build live in Settings > About now")
        about = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "components",
                                  "AboutModal.tsx"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('data-version={info.version}' in about
             and 'data-build={info.build}' in about
             and 'data-testid="about-version"' in about
             and 'data-testid="about-build"' in about
             and "about-pkg-status" in about
             and "about-package-" in about,
             "About source renders version/build and active package status")
        nb = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "components",
                               "Notebook.tsx"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("nb-version-stamp" in nb and "appVersion={health?.version}"
             in app,
             "the journal toolbar carries the stamp")

        # (2) export cards + cancel, behaviorally
        from samql_core.session import Session
        from samql_core import progress as _op3
        ses = Session()
        try:
            r = ses.run_query(
                "select 1 as a union all select 2 as a", target="auto")
            rid = r["result_id"]
            out = _tf.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
            ses.cancel_query("exp-1")
            res = ses.export(rid, "csv", out_path=out, query_id="exp-1")
            need(res.get("cancelled") and not os.path.exists(out),
                 "a cancelled export unwinds and removes the partial "
                 "file: %r" % res)
            res2 = ses.export(rid, "csv", out_path=out,
                              query_id="exp-2")
            need(res2.get("ok") and os.path.exists(out),
                 "a clean export lands: %r" % res2)
            op = _op3._OPS.get("exp-2")
            need(op is not None and op.kind == "export"
                 and op.cancellable and op.finished_at,
                 "the export ran as a cancellable Activity card and "
                 "ended cleanly")
        finally:
            ses.shutdown()
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('query_id=b.get("export_id") or None' in srv
             and '{"ok": False, "cancelled": True}' in srv,
             "the result-export route threads the id + surfaces cancel")
        ss = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('kind="export", surface="node"' in ss,
             "the node export card reads as an export")
        api_src = open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "lib", "api.ts"),
                       encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('"exp-" +' in api_src and "export_id: exportId" in api_src,
             "the client registers every result export under an id")
        need('toast("warn", "Export cancelled"' in app
             and 'onToast("warn", "Export cancelled"' in nb,
             "IDE + journal surface a cancelled export honestly")

        # (3) IDE tab close gate
        need("const closeTab = (id: string, anchor?: HTMLElement | null)"
             in app
             and "if (!hasText) return reallyCloseTab(id);" in app,
             "an IDE tab with text asks; a pristine one closes silently")

        # (4) cell delete gate, same popup
        need('"Delete this cell?"' in nb
             and "if (!has) return deleteCell(c.id);" in nb,
             "a cell with content asks; an empty one deletes silently")

        # (5) no native confirms anywhere
        offenders = []
        for f in _glob.glob(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "**", "*.ts*"),
                            recursive=True):
            src = open(f, encoding="utf-8").read()
            for ln in src.splitlines():
                t = ln.strip()
                if "window.confirm(" in t and not t.startswith("//"):
                    offenders.append(os.path.basename(f))
        need(not offenders,
             "no window.confirm call remains: %r" % offenders)
        cp = os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", "components",
                          "ConfirmPop.tsx")
        need(os.path.isfile(cp)
             and "nb2-delconfirm" in open(cp, encoding="utf-8").read(),
             "the shared popup reuses the node-confirm look")
        for host, frag in (
            ("App.tsx", "{confirmUi}"),
            (os.path.join("components", "Notebook.tsx"),
             "confirmPop.ui"),
        ):
            need(frag in open(os.path.join(FRONTEND, "src", host),
                              encoding="utf-8").read(),
                 "%s mounts the popup" % host)
        need('msg: `Delete ${ids.length} nodes?`' in _nodeflow_source(),
             "NodeFlow multi-delete routes through its popup")

        # (1) launcher

                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        for frag, why in (
            ('_set_window_prop(hwnd, 2, ', "RelaunchCommand set (the "
             "missing piece -- icon-only is ignored)"),

        # (2) storage: behavioral cache helpers on a fabricated profile

        sdir = os.path.join(base, "EBWebView", "Default",

        open(os.path.join(cdir, "f_2"), "wb").write(b"y" * 500)
