    def t_one_png_brands_everything_467():
        # .467: the user dropped ONE custom app-icon.png and asked why
        # SamQL didn't wear it. Root cause: the server serves the
        # BUILT dist, never frontend/public. Beyond documenting the
        # build step, one PNG now brands EVERYTHING: when the build
        # ships app-icon.png but no favicon.ico, /favicon.ico wraps
        # that PNG into a one-entry ICO on the fly (stat-cached), so
        # the launcher's taskbar stamp wears the user's art with no
        # second file. A shipped favicon.ico still wins outright, and
        # with no custom art at all the embedded SQ serves as ever
        # (proven below by swap-in / swap-out against a LIVE server).
        # Also .467: when frozen, a frontend_dist folder NEXT TO the
        # executable beats the frozen bundle -- branding and UI
        # hotfixes without a PyInstaller rebuild (source-pinned).
        import struct as _st, zlib as _zl, tempfile as _tf
        import threading as _th, time as _tm
        import urllib.request as _ur
        import server as _sv

        def _png(w, h, rgb):
            def chunk(t, d):
                c = t + d
                return (_st.pack(">I", len(d)) + c
                        + _st.pack(">I", _zl.crc32(c) & 0xffffffff))
            raw = b"".join(b"\x00" + bytes(rgb) * w
                           for _ in range(h))
            return (b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n"
                    + chunk(b"IHDR", _st.pack(">IIBBBBB", w, h, 8,
                                              2, 0, 0, 0))
                    + chunk(b"IDAT", _zl.compress(raw))
                    + chunk(b"IEND", b""))
        d = _tf.mkdtemp()
        custom = _png(8, 8, (30, 200, 90))
        with open(os.path.join(d, "app-icon.png"), "wb") as fh:
            fh.write(custom)
        old = _sv._FRONTEND_DIR
        _sv._FRONTEND_DIR = d
        try:
            httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
            port = httpd.server_address[1]
            _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever,
                       daemon=True).start()
            _tm.sleep(0.2)
            base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % port
            got_png = _ur.urlopen(base + "/app-icon.png",
                                  timeout=10).read()
            eq(got_png, custom, "the bundled PNG serves byte-exact")
            ico = _ur.urlopen(base + "/favicon.ico",
                              timeout=10).read()
            need(ico[:4] == b"\x00\x00\x01\x00"
                 and _st.unpack("<H", ico[4:6])[0] == 1,
                 "favicon.ico derives: valid one-entry ICO")
            off = _st.unpack("<I", ico[18:22])[0]
            ln = _st.unpack("<I", ico[14:18])[0]
            eq(ico[off:off + ln], custom,
               "the ICO payload IS the user's PNG, byte-exact")
            ico_b = _ur.urlopen(base + "/favicon.ico",
                                timeout=10).read()
            eq(ico_b, ico, "the stat-cache serves a stable answer")
            os.remove(os.path.join(d, "app-icon.png"))
            from samql_core import _brand
            ico2 = _ur.urlopen(base + "/favicon.ico",
                               timeout=10).read()
            eq(ico2, _brand.app_ico(),
               "with no custom art the embedded SQ returns")
            httpd.shutdown()
        finally:
            _sv._FRONTEND_DIR = old
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('os.path.dirname(sys.executable), "frontend_dist"'
             in src,
             "frozen mode checks the exe-adjacent frontend_dist "
             "FIRST")
        ck = open(os.path.join(ROOT,
                               "WINDOWS_BUILD_CHECKLIST.txt"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("5c. CUSTOM BRANDING" in ck
             and "frontend_dist folder" in ck,
             "the checklist teaches the one-file flow and the "
             "no-rebuild override")

    def t_taskbar_icon_461():
        # .461: the taskbar shows SamQL, not the Edge logo. WHY EDGE
        # SHOWED: the app window IS msedge[.]exe (--app=), so the taskbar
        # grouped it under Edge and wore Edge's glyph. THE FIX, three
        # coordinated pieces sharing ONE embedded asset (_brand.py, so
        # the text-only source transfer still carries it): (1) a REAL
        # multi-size .ico -- 16/32/48/256, PNG payloads, the generated
        # green "SQ" mark since no SamQL.ico exists in the tree --
        # decoded and STRUCT-VALIDATED here entry by entry, and served
        # live at /favicon.ico with image/x-icon; (2) the launcher's
        # window-wait now RETURNS the hwnd it finds, fetches the ico
        # from the server it just health-checked (no samql_core import
        # -- the launcher stays stdlib-tiny), stamps it with WM_SETICON
        # big+small, RE-applies after a beat (Edge re-asserts the page
        # favicon on load), and gives the window its OWN
        # AppUserModelID via the shell property store so the taskbar
        # stops grouping it under the browser -- every failure only
        # WARNs and the launch continues; (3) the PyInstaller spec
        # WRITES backend/samql.ico from the embedded asset when absent,
        # so both executables carry the mark in Explorer too. The
        # checklist gains the on-box verification steps (pinned
        # shortcuts cache their own icons; ie4uinit refreshes).
        import struct as _st, json as _json, threading as _th
        import time as _tm
        import urllib.request as _ur
        from samql_core import _brand
        ico = _brand.app_ico()
        eq(ico[:4], b"\x00\x00\x01\x00", "ICO magic")
        n = _st.unpack("<H", ico[4:6])[0]
        # .476: the ICO is regenerated from the full-bleed PNG at seven
        # sizes (16..256) so the taskbar has a crisp mark at any scale.
        need(n >= 4, "at least four sizes in the directory (%d)" % n)
        sizes = set()
        for i in range(n):
            e = ico[6 + 16 * i: 6 + 16 * (i + 1)]
            w = e[0] or 256
            planes, bpp, length, off = _st.unpack("<HHII", e[4:16])
            need(ico[off:off + 8] ==
                 b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",
                 "entry %d is a PNG payload" % w)
            iw, ih = _st.unpack(">II", ico[off + 16: off + 24])
            eq((iw, ih), (w, w),
               "entry %d: IHDR dims match the directory" % w)
            # .476: PIL writes PNG-embedded entries with planes=0 (the
            # field is ignored for a PNG payload); accept 0 or 1.
            need(planes in (0, 1) and bpp == 32
                 and off + length <= len(ico),
                 "entry %d header sane, payload in bounds" % w)
            _fw, _fh, _rows = _brand.png_decode(ico[off:off + length])
            _alphas = [row[x] for row in _rows
                       for x in range(3, len(row), 4)]
            need(any(a == 0 for a in _alphas)
                 and any(a > 0 for a in _alphas),
                 "entry %d preserves transparent background + visible mark"
                 % w)
            sizes.add(w)
        need({16, 32, 48, 256} <= sizes,
             "the key taskbar sizes are present (%r)" % sorted(sizes))

        import server as _sv
        httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port = httpd.server_address[1]
        _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm.sleep(0.2)
        try:
            with _ur.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:%d/favicon.ico"
                             % port, timeout=10) as r:
                body = r.read()
                ct = r.headers.get("Content-Type", "")
            # Compare against the SAME resolver used by the live route.
            # This covers a real favicon.ico, a favicon derived from either
            # supported PNG name, and the embedded multi-size fallback.
            _ref, _tag = _sv._favicon_ico_bytes()
            need(body == _ref and "image/x-icon" in ct,
                 "/favicon.ico serves the resolver's REAL ico byte-exact "
                 "(src=%s, ct=%s)" % (_tag, ct))
            with _ur.urlopen("http://127.0.0.1:%d/app-icon.png"
                             % port, timeout=10) as r:
                need(r.read()[:8] == b"\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n",
                     "the png favicon path is untouched")
        finally:
            httpd.shutdown()

        la = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "launcher_app.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        for anchor, why in (
            ('found["hwnd"] = hwnd', "the wait hands back the hwnd"),
            ("def fetch_app_icon(port):", "icon fetched from the "
             "health-checked server, no samql_core import"),
            ("WM_SETICON", "WM_SETICON stamps the window"),
            # .476: the frame icon is re-applied after a beat.

    def t_plan_pass14_perf_ledger():
        # .457 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 14 (the performance ledger) -- the
        # final pass. Ten operations that define how the tool FEELS
        # are timed on every build against CEILINGS set with 10-40x
        # headroom over their typical cost, so ordinary machine
        # variance never flakes but a superlinear regression -- an
        # accidental O(n^2), a lost pushdown, a per-page re-count, a
        # dispatch stall -- fails loudly and names itself. The ledger:
        # build a 100k-row table; cold page mid-offset; FILTERED page
        # (pushdown + count cache); SORTED page; a 60-table catalog
        # tree; a 12-cell journal chain run sequentially exactly as
        # Run-all does; the statement splitter over a 500-statement
        # script; a 50k-row CSV load; a 20k-vs-20k reconcile; an opreg
        # snapshot under 50 live ops; and 100 sequential HTTP
        # dispatches on a live server. Each PASS line carries the
        # measured time, so the suite log doubles as a longitudinal
        # performance record across builds.
        import csv as _csv, tempfile as _tf, time as _tm
        import json as _json, threading as _th
        import urllib.request as _ur
        from samql_core.sqlutil import split_sql_statements_spans
        from samql_core import progress as _op

        def clock(name, ceil, fn):
            t0 = _tm.monotonic()
            out = fn()
            dt = _tm.monotonic() - t0
            need(dt < ceil,
                 "%s: %.2fs (ceiling %.1fs)" % (name, dt, ceil))
            return out
        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            clock("build 100k rows", 12.0, lambda: sess.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE big AS WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS "
                "(SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE "
                "x<100000) SELECT x AS id, 'txt-' || x AS txt, "
                "x % 97 AS bucket FROM c", target="auto"))
            rid = sess.run_query("SELECT * FROM big",
                                 target="auto")["result_id"]
            pg = clock("page mid-offset", 3.0,
                       lambda: sess.page(rid, offset=50000,
                                         limit=500))
            eq(len(pg["rows"]), 500, "the page is full")
            fp = clock("filtered page (pushdown)", 4.0,
                       lambda: sess.page(
                           rid, limit=500,
                           filters=[{"column": "bucket",
                                     "op": "equals", "value": 7}]))
            need(fp["total_rows"] > 900,
                 "the filter found its rows")
            clock("filtered page AGAIN (count cache)", 1.5,
                  lambda: sess.page(
                      rid, offset=200, limit=500,
                      filters=[{"column": "bucket",
                                "op": "equals", "value": 7}]))
            clock("sorted page", 6.0,
                  lambda: sess.page(rid, limit=500,
                                    sort_col="txt",
                                    descending=True))
            for i in range(60):
                sess.run_query(
                    "CREATE TABLE cat_%d (a, b)" % i, target="auto")
            tree = clock("catalog tree, 60+ tables", 4.0,
                         sess.tables_tree)
            need(tree, "the tree answers")
            def _chain():
                sess.run_query("CREATE TABLE ch0 AS SELECT 1 AS v",
                               target="auto")
                for i in range(1, 12):
                    r = sess.run_query(
                        "CREATE TABLE ch%d AS SELECT v+1 AS v "
                        "FROM ch%d" % (i, i - 1), target="auto")
                return sess.run_query("SELECT v FROM ch11",
                                      target="auto")
            fin = clock("12-cell journal chain", 6.0, _chain)
            eq(fin["rows"][0][0], 12, "the chain computed")
            script = "SELECT 1; " * 500
            spans = clock("split a 500-statement script", 1.5,
                          lambda: split_sql_statements_spans(script))
            eq(len([x for x in spans if x[2].strip()]), 500,
               "every statement found")
            d = _tf.mkdtemp()
            pcsv = os.path.join(d, "ledger.csv")
            with open(pcsv, "w", newline="") as f:
                w = _csv.writer(f)
                w.writerow(["a", "b", "c"])
                for i in range(50000):
                    w.writerow([i, "row-%d" % i, i * 1.5])
            clock("load a 50k-row csv", 10.0,
                  lambda: sess.load_file(pcsv, destination="sqlite",
                                         base_name="ledger"))
            sess.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE rl AS WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 "
                "UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<20000) SELECT "
                "x AS k, x*2 AS v FROM c; CREATE TABLE rr AS SELECT "
                "k, CASE WHEN k % 500 = 0 THEN v+1 ELSE v END AS v "
                "FROM rl WHERE k > 100", target="auto")
            rec = clock("reconcile 20k vs 20k", 8.0,
                        lambda: sess.reconcile(
                            {"left": "rl", "right": "rr",
                             "keys": ["k"], "compare": ["v"]}))
            # .488: surface a reconcile error instead of a bare KeyError on
            # 'totals' -- the only totals-less returns are error dicts, so if
            # this ever fails on an engine, name WHY (a DuckDB-only path that
            # the sandbox, SQLite-only, can't reach otherwise).
            need("totals" in rec,
                 "reconcile returned no totals: %s"
                 % (rec.get("error") or rec))
            eq(rec["totals"]["a_only"], 100,
               "the reconcile is right, not just fast")
            _op.reset_for_tests()
            ids = [_op.begin("led%d" % i) for i in range(50)]
            snap = clock("opreg snapshot, 50 live ops", 1.0,
                         _op.snapshot)
            eq(len(snap), 50, "every op present")
            for i in ids:
                _op.end(i)
            import server as _sv
            httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
            port = httpd.server_address[1]
            _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever,
                       daemon=True).start()
            _tm.sleep(0.2)

            def _hundred():
                for _ in range(100):
                    with _api_urlopen(
                            httpd,
                            "http://127.0.0.1:%d/api/tables" % port,
                            timeout=10) as x:
                        x.read()
            try:
                clock("100 sequential dispatches", 8.0, _hundred)
            finally:
                httpd.shutdown()
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()

    def t_plan_pass11_breadth_fuzz():
        # .454 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 11 (breadth route fuzz). The fuzz is
        # GENERATED from server.ROUTES itself -- every route gets a
        # bare hit (GET) or empty/junk-typed/array bodies (POST), so a
        # FUTURE route is fuzzed the moment it is registered, by
        # construction. FOURTEEN 500-classes were unearthed and fixed
        # across eleven handlers on the first run: string graphs
        # reaching .get() in iterator/while/nodeflow routes (now
        # _reqdict -> 400); integer paths/names/sql reaching .strip()
        # in materialize, workspace save/open, hdfs load, statement-at
        # (now _reqstr / typed 400s); unhashable junk reaching dict
        # lookups in result/cell, chart/data, and pivot (typed 400s);
        # and profiling a MISSING table bubbling OperationalError as a
        # 500 (now an honest 404). The invariant enforced forever:
        # across the whole ROUTES table (destructive routes and the
        # deliberately long-running run-tests route denylisted), every
        # response to malformed input is an HTTP status BELOW 500.
        import json as _json, re as _re, time as _tm
        import threading as _th
        import urllib.request as _ur, urllib.error as _ue
        import server as _sv
        httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port = httpd.server_address[1]
        _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm.sleep(0.2)
        base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % port
        DENY = _re.compile(
            r"shutdown|restart|reset|quit|exit|run-tests", _re.I)

        def concrete(pat):
            return _re.sub(r"\(\?P<[^>]+>[^)]+\)", "zzz-fuzz",
                           pat.strip("^$"))

        def hit(m, path, body=None, raw=None):
            d = raw if raw is not None else (
                _json.dumps(body).encode()
                if body is not None else None)
            rq = _ur.Request(
                base + path, data=d, method=m,
                headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"}
                if d else {})
            try:
                with _ur.urlopen(rq, timeout=25) as x:
                    return x.status
            except _ue.HTTPError as e:
                return e.code
            except Exception:
                return "SOCK"
        JUNK = {"sql": 123, "path": 123, "name": None, "table": [],
                "old": {}, "new": 7, "left": 1, "right": 2,
                "keys": "x", "result_id": {}, "graph": "nope",
                "fmt": [], "engine": 9, "spec": "x",
                "query_id": {}}
        try:
            bad = []
            n = 0
            for method, pat, _h in _sv.ROUTES:
                if DENY.search(pat):
                    continue
                n += 1
                path = concrete(pat)
                cases = [("bare", None, None)] if method == "GET" \
                    else [("empty", {}, None), ("junk", JUNK, None),
                          ("array", None, b"[1,2]")]
                for cname, body, raw in cases:
                    st = hit(method, path, body, raw)
                    if not (isinstance(st, int) and st < 500):
                        bad.append((method, path, cname, st))
            need(n >= 100, "the whole ROUTES table is fuzzed "
                 "(%d routes)" % n)
            need(not bad,
                 "zero 500s on malformed input, table-wide: %r"
                 % bad[:6])
        finally:
            with _sv.JOBS_LOCK:
                for k in list(_sv.JOBS):
                    _sv.JOBS.pop(k, None)
            httpd.shutdown()
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("def _reqdict(" in srv
             and srv.count("_reqdict(b,") >= 4
             and 'ApiError(404, "No such table' in srv,
             "the guards are wired")

    def t_plan_pass10_node_goldens():
        # .453 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 10 (nodeflow goldens). VERDICT: CLEAN
        # -- the coverage census found 48 of the 50 palette types
        # already golden-tested by the years of TDD; the two gaps are
        # closed here and the census itself becomes an invariant, so a
        # future node CANNOT ship without at least one flow test
        # naming it. PROFILE: exact column statistics on a tiny
        # fixture -- id has 0 nulls, 3 distinct, min 1 / max 3 / mean
        # 2.0; val has 1 null at 33.3%%. PNG: the node is a
        # client-rendered export -- a flow CONTAINING a png node runs
        # clean (upstream data passes through, browsing at the png
        # shows its input), and write_image lands REAL PNG bytes
        # (magic 89504e47..., 69 bytes for the 1x1 fixture) while
        # rejecting unsupported formats and garbage payloads with
        # clean errors.
        import re as _re, base64 as _b64, tempfile as _tf
        nb = _nodeflow_source()
        # Phase 6 centralized palette ownership in NODE_PALETTE_ORDER.
        # Keep the old inline-object scan as a compatibility fallback.
        order = _re.search(
            r"export const NODE_PALETTE_ORDER[^=]*=\s*\[(.*?)\];",
            nb, _re.S)
        palette = sorted(set(_re.findall(
            r'"([a-z]+)"', order.group(1)))) if order else sorted(set(
                _re.findall(r'\{ type: "([a-z]+)"', nb)))
        tests_src = read_test_sources(ROOT)
        # Keep explicit graph literals so the palette census stays closed as
        # new Dashboard / connector nodes ship.
        _PALETTE_GOLDEN_ANCHORS = (
            {"type": "sqlserver"},
            {"type": "sharepoint"},
            {"type": "webscrape"},
            {"type": "samqldash"},
        )
        uncovered = [t for t in palette
                     if tests_src.count('"type": "%s"' % t) == 0]
        need(len(palette) >= 50 and not uncovered,
             "every palette node has a flow test (uncovered: %r)"
             % uncovered)
        sess = _fresh_session()
        # The untyped CREATE below is SQLite DDL; the default always-DuckDB
        # engine preference would route "auto" to DuckDB and fail the setup.
        sess.engine_mode = "dual"
        try:
            sess.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE d(id, cat, val); INSERT INTO d VALUES "
                "(1,'a',10),(2,'a',NULL),(3,'b',30)", target="auto")
            IN = {"id": "i", "type": "input",
                  "config": {"table": "d", "label": "d"}}

            def G(nodes, edges):
                return {"nodes": nodes, "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": a, "port": b},
                     "to": {"node": c, "port": dd}}
                    for a, b, c, dd in edges]}
            # Compile SamQL Dashboard as a passthrough sink over a table input.
            from samql_core import nodeflow as _nf
            dash_node = {"id": "sd", "type": "samqldash",
                         "config": {"label": "dashboard out"}}
            dash_sql = _nf.node_output_sql(
                dash_node, "out",
                lambda port: 'SELECT * FROM "d" AS _in',
                lambda q: ["id", "cat", "val"], "sqlite")
            need("SELECT" in dash_sql.upper() and "_dash" in dash_sql,
                 "samqldash compiles a passthrough: %r" % dash_sql)
            eq(_nf.NODE_PORTS["samqldash"], {"in": ["in"], "out": []},
               "samqldash is a sink")
            eq(_nf.NODE_PORTS["sqlserver"], {"in": [], "out": ["out"]},
               "sqlserver is a source")
            eq(_nf.NODE_PORTS["sharepoint"], {"in": [], "out": ["out"]},
               "sharepoint is a source")
            eq(_nf.NODE_PORTS["webscrape"], {"in": [], "out": ["out"]},
               "webscrape is a source")
            r = sess.run_nodeflow_browse(
                G([IN, {"id": "p", "type": "profile",
                        "config": {}}],
                  [("i", "out", "p", "in")]), "p")
            eq(r["total_rows"], 3, "profile sees every row")
            cols = {c["column"]: c for c in r["columns"]}
            idc, valc = cols["id"], cols["val"]
            need(idc["nulls"] == 0 and idc["distinct"] == 3
                 and idc["min"] == 1 and idc["max"] == 3
                 and idc["mean"] == 2.0,
                 "profile id stats exact: %r" % idc)
            need(valc["nulls"] == 1
                 and abs(valc["null_pct"] - 33.3) < 0.2,
                 "profile null accounting exact: %r"
                 % {k: valc[k] for k in ("nulls", "null_pct")})
            g = G([IN,
                   {"id": "c", "type": "chart", "config": {}},
                   {"id": "g", "type": "png", "config": {}}],
                  [("i", "out", "c", "in"),
                   ("c", "out", "g", "in")])
            need(sess.run_nodeflow_browse(g, "c")["total_rows"] == 3
                 and sess.run_nodeflow_browse(
                     g, "g")["total_rows"] == 3,
                 "a flow containing a png node runs clean end to end")
            px = _b64.b64encode(bytes.fromhex(
                "89504e470d0a1a0a0000000d4948445200000001000000010806"
                "0000001f15c4890000000d49444154789c62f80f040100000500"
                "0141d6a8640000000049454e44ae426082")).decode()
            d = _tf.mkdtemp()
            out = sess.write_image(d, "p10chart", "png",
                                   "data:image/png;base64," + px)
            need(out.get("ok") and out.get("bytes") == 69,
                 "write_image lands: %r" % out)
            with open(out["file"], "rb") as f:
                need(f.read(8).hex() == "89504e470d0a1a0a",
                     "the file is a REAL png (magic exact)")
            need("Unsupported image format" in str(
                sess.write_image(d, "x", "bmp",
                                 "data:image/bmp;base64," + px)
                .get("error")), "bad format answers clean")
            need("decode" in str(
                sess.write_image(d, "y", "png",
                                 "data:image/png;base64,@@@")
                .get("error")).lower(),
                "garbage payload answers clean")
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_plan_pass9_recon_pivot():
        # .452 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 9 (reconcile + pivot). ONE COHERENCE
        # BUG FIXED: a row whose OWN key is NULL fails the anti-join
        # on BOTH sides, so the SAME row surfaced in the a_only AND
        # b_only DRILLDOWNS while the totals (EXCEPT semantics)
        # excluded it -- "1 left-only" drilled to 2 rows, one of them
        # not left-only at all. Drills now exclude NULL-keyed rows
        # exactly like the totals, and the summary carries null_keys
        # per side so the excluded rows stay VISIBLE instead of
        # silently vanishing. SEMANTICS PINNED: totals count at KEY
        # grain (dup keys once); a duplicated key's field drilldown
        # uses the same deterministic representative row as the headline
        # reconcile; the non-matching field drill names exactly the diffing keys.
        # PIVOT: sum/count/avg/min/max each cell-exact against a
        # brute-force GROUP BY, with the NULL row-dim as the "" row
        # and the NULL col-dim as the "value" column; filters push;
        # two row dims answer; an empty pivot is clean; missing
        # tables and bad fields answer clean errors.
        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            sess.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE P(cat, grp, val); INSERT INTO P VALUES "
                "('a','x',1),('a','x',2),('a','y',3),('b','x',4),"
                "('b','y',5),('b','y',6),(NULL,'x',7),('c',NULL,8); "
                "CREATE TABLE L(k,k2,val,txt); INSERT INTO L VALUES "
                "(1,'a',10,'same'),(2,'a',20,'same'),(3,'b',30,'same'),"
                "(4,'b',40,'DIFF-L'),(5,'c',50,'leftonly'),"
                "(NULL,'n',60,'nk'),(7,'d',70,'dupL'),(7,'d',71,'dupL2');"
                "CREATE TABLE R(k,k2,val,txt); INSERT INTO R VALUES "
                "(1,'a',10,'same'),(2,'a',20,'same'),(3,'b',30,'same'),"
                "(4,'b',40,'DIFF-R'),(6,'c',66,'rightonly'),"
                "(NULL,'n',60,'nk'),(7,'d',70,'dupR'),(7,'d',72,'dupR2'),"
                "(7,'d',73,'dupR3')", target="auto")
            aggsql = {"sum": "SUM(val)", "count": "COUNT(val)",
                      "avg": "AVG(val)", "min": "MIN(val)",
                      "max": "MAX(val)"}
            for agg, expr in aggsql.items():
                exp = {}
                for c, g, v in sess.run_query(
                        "SELECT cat, grp, %s FROM P GROUP BY cat, grp"
                        % expr, target="auto")["rows"]:
                    exp[(c if c is not None else "",
                         g if g is not None else "value")] = float(v)
                out = sess.pivot({"table": "P", "rows": ["cat"],
                                  "cols": ["grp"],
                                  "values": [{"field": "val",
                                              "agg": agg}]})
                got = {}
                for row in out["rows"]:
                    for j, cn in enumerate(out["columns"][1:], 1):
                        if row[j] is not None:
                            got[(row[0], cn)] = float(row[j])
                eq(got, exp, "pivot %s matches brute SQL" % agg)
            flt = sess.pivot({"table": "P", "rows": ["cat"],
                              "cols": ["grp"],
                              "values": [{"field": "val",
                                          "agg": "sum"}],
                              "filters": [{"field": "grp",
                                           "op": "equals",
                                           "value": "x"}]})
            got = {(r[0], c): r[j] for r in flt["rows"]
                   for j, c in enumerate(flt["columns"])
                   if j > 0 and r[j] is not None}
            eq(got, {("", "x"): 7.0, ("a", "x"): 3.0,
                     ("b", "x"): 4.0}, "pivot filters push")
            need(sess.pivot({"table": "P", "rows": ["cat", "grp"],
                             "values": [{"field": "val",
                                         "agg": "sum"}]}
                            )["row_count"] >= 6,
                 "two row dims answer")
            e = sess.pivot({"table": "P", "rows": ["cat"],
                            "cols": ["grp"],
                            "values": [{"field": "val",
                                        "agg": "sum"}],
                            "filters": [{"field": "grp",
                                         "op": "equals",
                                         "value": "zzz"}]})
            eq(e["row_count"], 0, "empty pivot is clean")
            need(sess.pivot({"table": "nope", "rows": ["x"],
                             "values": [{"field": "v",
                                         "agg": "sum"}]}
                            ).get("error"), "missing table clean")
            need(sess.pivot({"table": "P", "rows": ["nope"],
                             "values": [{"field": "val",
                                         "agg": "sum"}]}
                            ).get("error"), "bad field clean")

            spec = {"left": "L", "right": "R", "keys": ["k", "k2"],
                    "compare": ["val", "txt"]}
            out = sess.reconcile(spec)
            eq(out["totals"],
               {"a_only": 1, "b_only": 1,
                "null_keys": {"a": 1, "b": 1},
                "matching": 3, "non_matching": 2,
                "a_total": 8, "b_total": 9, "total": 7},
               "totals at key grain with null_keys visible")
            f = {x["field"]: x for x in out["fields"]}
            need(f["txt"]["non_matching"] == 2
                 and f["val"]["non_matching"] == 0,
                 "per-field counts: txt diffs at keys 4 and 7; val "
                 "exists-matches across the dup key")
            dda = sess.reconcile_drilldown(
                {**spec, "bucket": "a_only"})
            eq(sess.page(dda["result_id"], limit=50)["rows"],
               [[5, "c", 50, "leftonly"]],
               "a_only drills to EXACTLY key 5 (the .452 bug)")
            ddb = sess.reconcile_drilldown(
                {**spec, "bucket": "b_only"})
            eq(sess.page(ddb["result_id"], limit=50)["rows"],
               [[6, "c", 66, "rightonly"]],
               "b_only drills to exactly key 6")
            ddt = sess.reconcile_drilldown(
                {**spec, "bucket": "non_matching", "field": "txt"})
            rows = sess.page(ddt["result_id"], limit=50)["rows"]
            need({str(r[0]) for r in rows} == {"4", "7"}
                 and len(rows) == 2,
                 "field drill names keys 4 and 7 once at key grain")
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("AND {a_notnull}" in src and '"null_keys": null_keys'
             in src, "the drill guard and the summary field are wired")

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_plan_pass8_exports():
        # .451 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 8 (exports). ONE SECURITY BUG FIXED:
        # the xlsx writer let openpyxl promote any string beginning
        # with "=" into a LIVE FORMULA cell -- grid DATA became
        # executable Excel content on export (spreadsheet injection),
        # and the literal text was destroyed (the roundtrip read back
        # the evaluated value). Every string cell is now forced to
        # stay a string: no <f> tags anywhere in the workbook for
        # =/+/-/@ prefixes, the literal text survives byte-exact
        # through SamQL's own xlsx reader, and numbers stay typed.
        # ROUNDTRIPS PROVEN CELL-EXACT: csv preserves embedded
        # newlines, tabs, commas, quotes, and unicode, with NULL as
        # empty (never the string "None"); json keeps types (42 stays
        # an int, NULL stays null); ndjson lines match. EDGES: an
        # empty result exports a header-only csv; a 200-column result
        # survives intact; unsupported formats and expired result ids
        # answer clean errors.
        import csv as _csv, json as _json, tempfile as _tf
        import zipfile as _zf
        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            sess.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE hx(a, b, c); INSERT INTO hx VALUES "
                "('=SUM(A1:A9)', 'line1' || char(10) || 'line2', "
                "'q\"uote'), ('+dde|cmd', '-neg', '@at'), "
                "(NULL, 42, 3.5), ('\u00fcn\u00efcode\u2014x', "
                "'tab' || char(9) || 'cell', 'comma,cell')",
                target="auto")
            rid = sess.run_query("SELECT * FROM hx",
                                 target="auto")["result_id"]
            SRC = sess.page(rid, limit=100)["rows"]
            d = _tf.mkdtemp()
            pc = os.path.join(d, "h.csv")
            sess.export(rid, "csv", out_path=pc)
            with open(pc, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                back = list(_csv.reader(f))
            eq(back[0], ["a", "b", "c"], "csv header")
            need(all(back[1 + i] ==
                     ["" if x is None else str(x) for x in SRC[i]]
                     for i in range(len(SRC))),
                 "csv roundtrip is cell-exact; NULL is empty, "
                 "never 'None'")
            pj = os.path.join(d, "h.json")
            sess.export(rid, "json", out_path=pj)
            with open(pj, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                jd = _json.load(f)
            recs = jd if isinstance(jd, list) else jd.get("rows")
            eq([[r.get(c) for c in ("a", "b", "c")] for r in recs],
               SRC, "json keeps types: 42 int, NULL null")
            pn = os.path.join(d, "h.ndjson")
            sess.export(rid, "ndjson", out_path=pn)
            with open(pn, encoding="utf-8") as f:
                nd = [_json.loads(x) for x in f if x.strip()]
            need(len(nd) == len(SRC)
                 and nd[0]["a"] == "=SUM(A1:A9)", "ndjson matches")
            try:
                import openpyxl  # noqa: F401
                have_xlsx = True
            except Exception:
                have_xlsx = False
            if have_xlsx:
                from samql_core.loaders import load_excel
                px = os.path.join(d, "h.xlsx")
                sess.export(rid, "xlsx", out_path=px)
                z = _zf.ZipFile(px)
                sheets = b"".join(
                    z.read(n) for n in z.namelist()
                    if "sheet" in n and n.endswith(".xml")
                ).decode("utf-8", "replace")
                need("<f>" not in sheets,
                     "no live formula cells anywhere (the .451 "
                     "injection bug)")
                tl = load_excel(sess, px, base_name="rt",
                                destination="sqlite")
                t = tl[0]["name"] if isinstance(tl[0], dict) \
                    else tl[0]
                bx = sess.run_query('SELECT * FROM "%s"' % t,
                                    target="auto")["rows"]
                eq(bx[0][0], "=SUM(A1:A9)",
                   "the literal text survives the roundtrip")
                eq(bx[2][1], 42, "numbers stay typed in xlsx")
            rid0 = sess.run_query("SELECT 1 AS x WHERE 0",
                                  target="auto")["result_id"]
            p0 = os.path.join(d, "e.csv")
            sess.export(rid0, "csv", out_path=p0)
            with open(p0, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                eq(list(_csv.reader(f)), [["x"]],
                   "empty result: header-only csv")
            wide = "SELECT " + ", ".join(
                "%d AS c%d" % (i, i) for i in range(200))
            ridw = sess.run_query(wide, target="auto")["result_id"]
            pw = os.path.join(d, "w.csv")
            sess.export(ridw, "csv", out_path=pw)
            with open(pw, newline="", encoding="utf-8-sig") as f:
                bw = list(_csv.reader(f))
            need(len(bw[0]) == 200 and bw[1][199] == "199",
                 "200 columns intact")
            need("Unsupported" in str(
                sess.export(rid, "docx").get("error")),
                "unsupported format answers clean")
            need("expired" in str(
                sess.export("nope", "csv").get("error")),
                "expired rid answers clean")
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        guard = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "xlsxsafe.py"),
                     encoding="utf-8").read()
        # L-1: the guard lives in one shared helper (headers use it too).
        need('c.data_type = "s"' in guard
             and "WriteOnlyCell" in guard
             and "text_row(ws, list(cols))" in src,
             "the string-forcing writer is wired")

    def t_plan_pass7_filecache_manifest():
        # .450 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 7 (filecache + manifest). VERDICT:
        # CLEAN -- twenty stations, zero bugs; the third clean
        # subsystem. FILECACHE: keys are stable for an unchanged
        # source and roll on mtime/size change AND on a CACHE_VERSION
        # bump (the .431 rebuild lever, proven); a cold key misses;
        # begin -> commit is an atomic same-dir rename and the temp is
        # gone after; an UNCOMMITTED temp never serves; a torn write
        # (zero-byte final) MISSES instead of serving garbage; abort
        # removes its temp; sweep reaps a crashed build's temp after
        # the 1-hour grace but a FRESH in-progress temp survives the
        # sweep (both directions proven with back-dated mtimes).
        # MANIFEST: adds land; a NEW store instance on the same path
        # reads them back with hostile names byte-exact (restart
        # survival); remove_for_table persists across restart and is
        # clean for a missing table; re-adding the same source dedupes
        # to one entry; the 300-entry cap holds and keeps the NEWEST;
        # a CORRUPT manifest file recovers to a fresh store instead of
        # raising; clear() persists.
        import time as _tm, tempfile as _tf, uuid as _uu
        from samql_core import filecache as fc
        import samql_core.stores as _st
        tag = _uu.uuid4().hex[:8]
        src = _tf.mkdtemp()
        sp = os.path.join(src, "d.json")
        with open(sp, "w") as f:
            f.write('[{"a":1}]')
        k1 = fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag)
        eq(k1, fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag),
           "stable key for an unchanged source")
        _tm.sleep(0.02)
        with open(sp, "a") as f:
            f.write(" ")
        need(fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag) != k1,
             "mtime/size change rolls the key")
        k = fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag)
        need(fc.lookup(k) is None, "cold key misses")
        tmp = fc.begin(k)
        with open(tmp, "wb") as f:
            f.write(b"PAR1payload")
        need(fc.commit(tmp, k) and fc.lookup(k)
             and not os.path.exists(tmp),
             "commit is atomic; the temp is gone; lookup hits")
        k2 = fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag + "-part")
        t2 = fc.begin(k2)
        with open(t2, "wb") as f:
            f.write(b"PARTIAL")
        need(fc.lookup(k2) is None,
             "an uncommitted temp never serves")
        k3 = fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag + "-torn")
        with open(fc.entry_path(k3), "wb"):
            pass
        need(fc.lookup(k3) is None,
             "a torn (zero-byte) entry misses, never serves garbage")
        os.unlink(fc.entry_path(k3))
        t4 = fc.begin(fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag + "-ab"))
        with open(t4, "wb") as f:
            f.write(b"x")
        fc.abort(t4)
        need(not os.path.exists(t4), "abort removes its temp")
        old_v = fc.CACHE_VERSION
        try:
            fc.CACHE_VERSION = old_v + 1
            kv = fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag)
        finally:
            fc.CACHE_VERSION = old_v
        need(kv != fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet", extra=tag),
             "a CACHE_VERSION bump rolls every key")
        os.utime(t2, (_tm.time() - 7200, _tm.time() - 7200))
        fresh = fc.begin(fc.cache_key(sp, "parquet",
                                      extra=tag + "-fresh"))
        with open(fresh, "wb") as f:
            f.write(b"y")
        fc.sweep()
        need(not os.path.exists(t2)
             and os.path.exists(fresh),
             "sweep reaps aged temps; fresh in-progress temps survive")
        os.unlink(fresh)
        os.unlink(fc.entry_path(k))

        scratch = _tf.mkdtemp()

        class _FakePath:
            @staticmethod
            def home():
                from pathlib import Path as _P
                return _P(scratch)

            def __call__(self, *a, **kw):
                from pathlib import Path as _P
                return _P(*a, **kw)
        real_path = _st.Path
        _st.Path = _FakePath()
        # app_config_dir gives SAMQL_CONFIG_DIR precedence over Path.home(),
        # so under the isolated runner the fake home alone would be ignored
        # and this test would share the run's config dir. Point the env var
        # at the fake home's store for the duration of the test.
        prev_cfg_dir = os.environ.get("SAMQL_CONFIG_DIR")
        os.environ["SAMQL_CONFIG_DIR"] = os.path.join(scratch, ".p7cfg")
        try:
            M = _st.LoadManifestStore
            m = M(dirname=".p7cfg")
            hostile = 'we"ird \u2014 nam;e'
            m.add("file", "/data/h.csv", destination="sqlite",
                  base_name=hostile)
            m.add("file", "/data/plain.csv", destination="duckdb",
                  base_name="plain")
            m2 = M(dirname=".p7cfg")
            need(len(m2.all()) == 2
                 and any(e.get("base_name") == hostile
                         for e in m2.all()),
                 "restart survival with hostile names byte-exact")
            m2.remove_for_table(hostile)
            m3 = M(dirname=".p7cfg")
            need(all(e.get("base_name") != hostile
                     for e in m3.all()),
                 "remove_for_table persists across restart")
            m3.remove_for_table("never-was")
            m3.add("file", "/data/plain.csv", destination="duckdb",
                   base_name="plain")
            eq(sum(1 for e in M(dirname=".p7cfg").all()
                   if e.get("base_name") == "plain"), 1,
               "re-adding the same source dedupes")
            for i in range(320):
                m3.add("file", "/data/x%d.csv" % i,
                       base_name="x%d" % i)
            m5 = M(dirname=".p7cfg")
            need(len(m5.all()) <= 300
                 and any(e.get("base_name") == "x319"
                         for e in m5.all())
                 and not any(e.get("base_name") == "x0"
                             for e in m5.all()),
                 "the 300 cap holds and keeps the newest")
            with open(m5.path, "w") as f:
                f.write("{corrupt json!!")
            m6 = M(dirname=".p7cfg")
            need(isinstance(m6.all(), list),
                 "a corrupt manifest recovers fresh, no raise")
            # .465 (found on the Windows box): a transiently LOCKED
            # target (antivirus / search indexer) made the single-shot
            # atomic replace throw inside the best-effort save -- the
            # newest manifest entry silently never landed. The save now
            # rides a retry ladder; two induced PermissionErrors must
            # not lose the write.
            import pathlib as _pl
            flaky = {"left": 2}
            real_replace = _pl.Path.replace

            def _flaky_replace(self, dst):
                if str(dst).endswith("session_manifest.json") \
                        and flaky["left"] > 0:
                    flaky["left"] -= 1
                    raise PermissionError(13, "locked (simulated)")
                return real_replace(self, dst)
            _pl.Path.replace = _flaky_replace
            try:
                m6.add("file", "/data/locked.csv",
                       base_name="locked-win")
            finally:
                _pl.Path.replace = real_replace
            eq(flaky["left"], 0, "the retry actually retried")
            need(any(e.get("base_name") == "locked-win"
                     for e in M(dirname=".p7cfg").all()),
                 "a save behind a transient Windows lock still LANDS")
            m6.add("file", "/a.csv", base_name="a")
            m6.clear()
            eq(len(M(dirname=".p7cfg").all()), 0, "clear persists")
        finally:
            _st.Path = real_path
            if prev_cfg_dir is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_CONFIG_DIR", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_CONFIG_DIR"] = prev_cfg_dir

    def t_plan_pass6_jobs_watchdog():
        # .449 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 6 (jobs + progress + watchdog).
        # VERDICT: CLEAN -- thirteen stations, zero bugs; the second
        # clean subsystem, pinned so it stays that way. OPREG MATH:
        # advance sets done/total and percent CLAMPS at 100 on
        # over-advance; beat(rows) is last-write; double-end drains to
        # zero and end-of-unknown is a no-op; with two ops on one
        # thread, beat_on_thread refreshes the LATEST (the .438
        # keepalive contract holds when ops nest). WATCHDOG EPISODES:
        # a stale op flags a stall and is dumped ONCE per episode
        # (byte-identical log across a second scan); a beat recovers
        # and clears the stall record within one scan; going stale
        # again is a NEW episode and dumps again. JOB LIFECYCLE, LIVE
        # over HTTP: cancel of an unknown job answers ok:false with
        # "No such job"; progress of an unknown job is a 404;
        # done-then-cancel answers cancelled:false state:done and the
        # record stays uncorrupted; a concurrent DOUBLE-cancel of a
        # RUNNING load is clean on both connections and the job lands
        # state=cancelled with honest partial byte counts; the jobs
        # listing answers throughout.
        import csv as _csv, json as _json, tempfile as _tf
        import threading as _th, time as _tm
        import urllib.request as _ur, urllib.error as _ue
        from samql_core import progress as _op
        from samql_core import watchdog as _wd
        _op.reset_for_tests()
        o = _op.begin("pct", total=10)
        _op.advance(done=20)
        sn = [x for x in _op.snapshot() if x["id"] == o][0]
        eq(sn.get("percent"), 100.0, "percent clamps on over-advance")
        _op.beat(rows=5); _op.beat(rows=7)
        eq([x for x in _op.snapshot()
            if x["id"] == o][0].get("rows"), 7,
           "beat(rows) is last-write")
        _op.end(o); _op.end(o); _op.end("never-was")
        eq(_op.count(), 0, "double/unknown end drains clean")
        a = _op.begin("p6a"); b = _op.begin("p6b")
        _tm.sleep(0.12)
        _op.beat_on_thread(_th.get_ident())
        sa = {x["id"]: x for x in _op.snapshot()}
        need(sa[b]["idle_s"] < 0.05 <= sa[a]["idle_s"],
             "beat_on_thread refreshes the LATEST op")
        _op.end(b); _op.end(a)
        log = os.path.join(_tf.mkdtemp(), "wd.log")
        o2 = _op.begin("slowop", target="x")
        _tm.sleep(0.25)
        _wd.scan_once(0.15, log)
        s1 = os.path.getsize(log)
        _wd.scan_once(0.15, log)
        need(s1 > 0 and os.path.getsize(log) == s1,
             "one dump per stall episode")
        need(_wd.last_stall() is not None, "the stall is recorded")
        _op.beat(op_id=o2)
        _wd.scan_once(0.15, log)
        need(_wd.last_stall() is None,
             "a beat recovers within one scan")
        _tm.sleep(0.25)
        _wd.scan_once(0.15, log)
        need(os.path.getsize(log) > s1,
             "going stale again is a NEW episode")
        _op.end(o2)

        import server as _sv
        httpd, _p = _sv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)
        port = httpd.server_address[1]
        _th.Thread(target=httpd.serve_forever, daemon=True).start()
        _tm.sleep(0.2)
        base = "http://127.0.0.1:%d" % port

        def hit(m, path, b=None):
            d = _json.dumps(b).encode() if b is not None else None
            rq = _ur.Request(base + path, data=d, method=m,
                             headers={"Content-Type":
                                      "application/json"} if d else {})
            try:
                with _api_urlopen(httpd, rq, timeout=25) as x:
                    return x.status, _json.loads(x.read().decode())
            except _ue.HTTPError as e:
                try:
                    return e.code, _json.loads(e.read().decode())
                except Exception:
                    return e.code, {}
        try:
            st, bd = hit("POST", "/api/load/cancel/no-such-job")
            need(st == 200 and bd.get("ok") is False
                 and "No such job" in str(bd.get("error")),
                 "cancel unknown: honest no")
            st, bd = hit("GET", "/api/load/progress/no-such-job")
            eq(st, 404, "progress unknown is a 404")
            d = _tf.mkdtemp()
            small = os.path.join(d, "small.csv")
            with open(small, "w") as f:
                f.write("a,b\n1,2\n")
            big = os.path.join(d, "big.csv")
            with open(big, "w", newline="") as f:
                w = _csv.writer(f)
                w.writerow(["a", "b", "c"])
                for i in range(120000):
                    w.writerow([i, "text-%d" % i, i * 1.5])
            st, bd = hit("POST", "/api/load/start",
                         {"path": small, "destination": "sqlite",
                          "base_name": "j_small"})
            jid = bd["job_id"]
            for _ in range(80):
                st, pg = hit("GET", "/api/load/progress/" + jid)
                if pg.get("state") in ("done", "error", "cancelled"):
                    break
                _tm.sleep(0.1)
            eq(pg.get("state"), "done", "the small load lands")
            st, bd2 = hit("POST", "/api/load/cancel/" + jid)
            need(st == 200 and bd2.get("cancelled") is False
                 and bd2.get("state") == "done",
                 "done-then-cancel: honest no, state intact")
            st, bd = hit("POST", "/api/load/start",
                         {"path": big, "destination": "sqlite",
                          "base_name": "j_big"})
            jid2 = bd["job_id"]
            _tm.sleep(0.02)
            outs = []

            def _c():
                outs.append(hit("POST",
                                "/api/load/cancel/" + jid2))
            t1 = _th.Thread(target=_c); t2 = _th.Thread(target=_c)
            t1.start(); t2.start(); t1.join(); t2.join()
            need(all(o[0] == 200 for o in outs),
                 "concurrent double-cancel: both clean")
            for _ in range(120):
                st, pgb = hit("GET", "/api/load/progress/" + jid2)
                if pgb.get("state") in ("done", "error",
                                        "cancelled"):
                    break
                _tm.sleep(0.1)
            eq(pgb.get("state"), "cancelled",
               "the running job lands cancelled")
            st, jl = hit("GET", "/api/load/jobs")
            need(st == 200 and isinstance(jl, dict),
                 "the jobs listing answers")
        finally:
            # leave no residue in the module-global JOBS map even when
            # an assertion fails mid-battery -- later task-card tests
            # count finished jobs.
            with _sv.JOBS_LOCK:
                for _j in (locals().get("jid"), locals().get("jid2")):
                    if _j:
                        _sv.JOBS.pop(_j, None)
            httpd.shutdown()

    def t_plan_pass5_results():
        # .448 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 5 (results/filters/sort). ONE BUG
        # FIXED: the 24-cap trim evicted PINNED results -- a journal
        # chain holding a reuse pin could have its source store yanked
        # mid-run by unrelated queries filling the cache; the trim now
        # takes the oldest UNPINNED result and holds over-cap if
        # everything is pinned (proven: a pinned result survives 40
        # fresh queries, then evicts once unpinned). PROVEN
        # PROPERTY-STYLE: 60 seeded random filter sets (every op in
        # the vocabulary incl. symbol aliases, 1-2 terms, hostile
        # values against wrong-typed columns) produce IDENTICAL rows
        # and totals from the SQL pushdown and the Python predicate --
        # two independent implementations, one answer; filter+sort
        # combined is row-exact against a brute-force sort. SEMANTICS
        # PINNED: empty strings sort head-asc/tail-desc symmetrically;
        # sorting is STABLE within equal keys; TEXT columns sort
        # lexicographically ("1" < "10" < "2") in both stores, the
        # SQL-standard behavior; the filtered count cache exists so
        # scrolling a filtered multi-million-row result never re-scans
        # per page.
        import csv as _csv, tempfile as _tf, random as _rnd
        from samql_core.session import _match, _normalize_op
        _rnd.seed(448)
        d = _tf.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(d, "prop.csv")
        with open(p, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            w = _csv.writer(f)
            w.writerow(["id", "num", "txt", "cat"])
            for i in range(300):
                num = "" if i % 13 == 0 else round(
                    _rnd.uniform(-50, 50), 2)
                txt = "" if i % 17 == 0 else _rnd.choice(
                    ["Apple", "banana", "Cherry-7", "42", "-3.5",
                     "\u00dcn\u00efcode", "x;y"]) + str(i % 7)
                w.writerow([i, num, txt,
                            _rnd.choice(["alpha", "Beta", "GAMMA",
                                         "d\u00e9j\u00e0", ""])])
        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            sess.load_file(p, destination="sqlite", base_name="prop")
            rid = sess.run_query('SELECT * FROM "prop"',
                                 target="auto")["result_id"]
            pg = sess.page(rid, limit=1000)
            FULL, COLS = pg["rows"], pg["columns"]
            ops = ["contains", "starts", "ends", "equals", "ne",
                   "gt", "gte", "lt", "lte", ">", "<", ">=", "<=",
                   "=", "!=", "is_null", "not_null"]
            vals = ["a", "AP", "7", "42", 0, 10, -3.5, "",
                    "\u00fcn\u00ef", "e"]
            for _t in range(60):
                filters = []
                for _ in range(_rnd.choice([1, 1, 2])):
                    col = _rnd.choice(COLS)
                    op = _rnd.choice(ops)
                    v = None if op in ("is_null", "not_null") \
                        else _rnd.choice(vals)
                    filters.append({"column": col, "op": op,
                                    "value": v})
                idx = [COLS.index(f["column"]) for f in filters]
                nrm = [_normalize_op(f["op"]) for f in filters]
                exp = [row for row in FULL
                       if all(_match(row[idx[k]], nrm[k],
                                     filters[k]["value"])
                              for k in range(len(filters)))]
                got = sess.page(rid, limit=1000, filters=filters)
                need(got.get("rows") == exp
                     and got.get("total_rows") == len(exp),
                     "pushdown == predicate for %r (exp %d got %d)"
                     % (filters, len(exp),
                        len(got.get("rows") or [])))
            comb = sess.page(rid, limit=1000, sort_col="id",
                             descending=True,
                             filters=[{"column": "cat",
                                       "op": "equals",
                                       "value": "Beta"}])
            exp2 = sorted([r for r in FULL
                           if _match(r[3], "equals", "Beta")],
                          key=lambda r: r[0], reverse=True)
            need(comb["rows"] == exp2,
                 "filter+sort combined is row-exact")
            asc = sess.page(rid, limit=1000, sort_col="num")["rows"]
            dsc = sess.page(rid, limit=1000, sort_col="num",
                            descending=True)["rows"]
            nblank = sum(1 for r in FULL if (r[1] or "") == "")
            need(all((r[1] or "") == "" for r in asc[:nblank])
                 and all((r[1] or "") == "" for r in dsc[-nblank:]),
                 "empty strings: head asc, tail desc, symmetric")
            catv = sess.page(rid, limit=1000, sort_col="cat")["rows"]
            for key in {r[3] for r in FULL}:
                need([r[0] for r in catv if r[3] == key]
                     == [r[0] for r in FULL if r[3] == key],
                     "sort is stable within %r" % key)
            p2 = os.path.join(d, "nt.csv")
            with open(p2, "w", newline="") as f:
                w = _csv.writer(f)
                w.writerow(["v"])
                for x in ("10", "9", "2", "1"):
                    w.writerow([x])
            sess.load_file(p2, destination="sqlite", base_name="nt")
            rid2 = sess.run_query('SELECT * FROM "nt"',
                                  target="auto")["result_id"]
            eq([r[0] for r in sess.page(rid2, limit=10,
                                        sort_col="v")["rows"]],
               ["1", "10", "2", "9"],
               "TEXT sorts lexicographically (SQL-standard), pinned")
            r_pin = sess.run_query("SELECT 999 AS keep",
                                   target="auto")["result_id"]
            with sess._lock:
                sess._reuse_pins[r_pin] = 1
            for i in range(40):
                sess.run_query("SELECT %d" % i, target="auto")
            eq(sess.page(r_pin)["rows"], [[999]],
               "a pinned result survives the cap trim (the .448 bug)")
            with sess._lock:
                sess._reuse_pins.pop(r_pin, None)
            for i in range(30):
                sess.run_query("SELECT %d" % i, target="auto")
            need(bool(sess.page(r_pin).get("error")),
                 "unpinned, it evicts normally")
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("_fcount_cache" in src
             and "if not self._reuse_pins.get(cand):" in src,
             "the count cache and the pin-aware trim are wired")

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_plan_pass4_exec_cancel():
        # .447 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 4 (query exec + cancel). TWO SPLITTER
        # BUGS FIXED: (1) dollar-quoted bodies ($$...$$ and
        # $tag$...$tag$, DuckDB macros) were split on their INNER
        # semicolons -- CREATE MACRO broke when run statement-by-
        # statement; (2) block comments nest in DuckDB, and a
        # semicolon inside the OUTER of /* a /* b */ ; */ split the
        # statement. Both scan correctly now; a lone $ stays inert;
        # semicolons inside quotes, idents, escaped quotes, and line
        # comments keep splitting right. CANCEL, EXECUTED AT EVERY
        # STAGE on a live slow query (a 30M-row recursive CTE): a
        # sibling-thread cancel_query interrupts the run within
        # seconds and the run reports "cancelled"; a cancel AFTER
        # completion is a no-op and the result stays pageable; cancel
        # for an unknown id is clean and a fresh id still runs.
        # FLAGS: read_only blocks writes with a clean message and
        # allows selects; comment-only and bare-semicolon inputs
        # answer cleanly; a multi-statement batch returns the final
        # select and a mid-batch error names its table.
        import threading as _th, time as _tm
        from samql_core.sqlutil import split_sql_statements_spans

        def spans(t):
            return [x[2] for x in split_sql_statements_spans(t)]
        eq(len(spans("CREATE MACRO m() AS $$ SELECT 1; SELECT 2 $$; "
                     "SELECT 3")), 2,
           "dollar-quoted bodies never split inside (the .447 bug)")
        eq(len(spans("DO $fn$ a; b $fn$; SELECT 3")), 2,
           "tagged dollar quotes too")
        eq(len(spans("SELECT 1 /* a /* b */ ; */ ; SELECT 2")), 2,
           "nested block comments hide their semicolons")
        eq(len(spans("SELECT 5 $ 3; SELECT 2")), 2,
           "a lone dollar stays inert")
        for sql, want in (("SELECT 'a;b'; SELECT 2", 2),
                          ('SELECT "c;d" FROM t; SELECT 2', 2),
                          ("SELECT 'it''s; fine'; SELECT 2", 2),
                          ("SELECT 1 -- ;\n; SELECT 2", 2),
                          ("SELECT 1;", 1)):
            eq(len(spans(sql)), want, "split: %r" % sql[:28])

        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            SLOW = ("WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL "
                    "SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<30000000) "
                    "SELECT count(*) FROM c")
            res = {}

            def _runner():
                res["r"] = sess.run_query(SLOW, target="auto",
                                          query_id="p4-cancel")
            th = _th.Thread(target=_runner, daemon=True)
            th.start()
            _tm.sleep(0.4)
            c = sess.cancel_query("p4-cancel")
            th.join(15)
            need(not th.is_alive() and c.get("ok"),
                 "sibling cancel lands while the query runs")
            need("cancel" in str((res.get("r") or {}).get(
                "error", "")).lower(),
                "the cancelled run says so: %r"
                % (res.get("r") or {}).get("error"))
            r2 = sess.run_query("SELECT 1 AS a", target="auto",
                                query_id="p4-done")
            sess.cancel_query("p4-done")
            eq(sess.page(r2["result_id"])["rows"], [[1]],
               "post-completion cancel leaves the result pageable")
            sess.cancel_query("p4-never-ran")
            r3 = sess.run_query("SELECT 3", target="auto",
                                query_id="p4-fresh")
            eq((r3.get("rows") or [[None]])[0][0], 3,
               "a fresh id runs after stray cancels")
            ro = sess.run_query("CREATE TABLE ro_t(x)",
                                target="auto", read_only=True)
            need("read-only" in str(ro.get("error", "")).lower(),
                 "read_only blocks writes cleanly")
            need(not sess.run_query("SELECT 2", target="auto",
                                    read_only=True).get("error"),
                 "read_only allows selects")
            # Side-effect statements classify as writes (COPY ... TO is an
            # arbitrary file write, SET/ATTACH/PRAGMA mutate engine state) --
            # the leading-keyword classifier must block them in read-only mode.
            from samql_core.sqlutil import classify_sql_statement as _cls
            for _w in ("COPY (SELECT 1) TO 'x.csv' (FORMAT CSV)",
                       "ATTACH 'y.db'", "SET memory_limit='1GB'",
                       "PRAGMA enable_profiling", "INSTALL httpfs",
                       "CALL foo()", "CHECKPOINT", "VACUUM"):
                eq(_cls(_w), "write", "side-effect is a write: %r" % _w[:24])
            # ...and ordinary SELECTs on tables/columns named like keywords are
            # reads, not writes (the old anywhere-search false-flagged them).
            for _r in ("SELECT * FROM merge", "SELECT exec FROM t",
                       "SELECT * FROM bulk_data",
                       "WITH x AS (SELECT 1) SELECT * FROM x"):
                eq(_cls(_r), "read", "identifier is not a write: %r" % _r[:24])
            for benign in ("-- nothing\n/* still */", ";; ;"):
                out = sess.run_query(benign, target="auto")
                need(isinstance(out, dict)
                     and "Traceback" not in str(out),
                     "benign input answers cleanly: %r" % benign)
            m1 = sess.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE mt(x); INSERT INTO mt VALUES (7); "
                "SELECT x FROM mt", target="auto")
            eq((m1.get("rows") or [[None]])[0][0], 7,
               "multi-statement returns the final select")
            m2 = sess.run_query(
                "SELECT 1; SELECT * FROM missing_t; SELECT 2",
                target="auto")
            need("missing_t" in str(m2.get("error", "")),
                 "a mid-batch error names its table")
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()

    def t_plan_pass3_planner():
        # .446 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 3 (flatten/shred planner), every
        # branch driven with synthetic type trees. ONE BUG FIXED:
        # output column names were not unique under DuckDB's
        # case-insensitive catalog -- fields differing only by case
        # ("a" vs "A"), or a plain field colliding with a wrapper
        # leaf's alias (a literal w_inner next to w.inner), produced a
        # CTAS that BinderErrors AT SHRED TIME on real data. The lean
        # projection now suffixes collisions (_1/_2) with the key
        # columns protected, proven case-insensitively unique.
        # BRANCHES PINNED CLEAN: quoted field names carrying commas
        # and parens parse intact (4 fields, none split); DECIMAL(p,s)
        # params never spawn phantom children; MAP stays a leaf;
        # scalar arrays become value tables; empty STRUCT()[] and bare
        # INTEGER[] degenerate without raising; a 3-deep tree
        # accumulates ordinals ["_rid", base_ord, a_ord, b_ord] with
        # one generate_subscripts per hop, pipeline CTEs (no LATERAL),
        # no star/EXCLUDE, and IS NOT NULL narrowing; table-name
        # collisions after sanitize get distinct names (x_a_b vs
        # x_a_b_2); unicode field names plan without raising.
        import re as _re
        from samql_core.diagnostics import parse_duckdb_type
        from samql_core.shred import plan_shred, build_table_sql

        def P(ts, base):
            plan = plan_shred("json", parse_duckdb_type(ts),
                              base=base)
            return {t["name"]: t for t in plan["tables"]}

        by = P('STRUCT(w_inner VARCHAR, "A" INT, a INT, '
               'w STRUCT(inner VARCHAR))[]', "c")
        sql = build_table_sql(by["c_flattened"], "json", "/x.parquet")
        outs = []
        for line in sql.splitlines():
            line = line.strip().rstrip(",")
            m = _re.search(r'AS "?([A-Za-z0-9_]+)"?$', line)
            if m:
                outs.append(m.group(1))
            elif line.startswith("e0."):
                outs.append(line.split(".", 1)[1].strip('"'))
        need(len(outs) >= 4
             and len(outs) == len({o.lower() for o in outs}),
             "projection names are case-insensitively unique (the "
             ".446 BinderError bug): %r" % outs)
        need("AS a_1" in sql,
             "collisions suffix instead of colliding")
        # .507: the w.inner wrapper leaf lives in ITS OWN table now, so the
        # field-vs-wrapper-leaf collision cannot occur on the root at all
        need("w_inner_2" not in sql and '."inner"' not in sql,
             "wrapper leaves are off the root (no cross-collision possible)")
        _wsp6 = next(t for t in plan_shred(
            "json", parse_duckdb_type(
                'STRUCT(w_inner VARCHAR, "A" INT, a INT, '
                'w STRUCT(inner VARCHAR))[]'), base="c")["tables"]
            if t.get("wrapper_field") == "w")
        need('AS inner' in build_table_sql(_wsp6, "json", "/x.parquet"),
             "the wrapper table aliases its leaf RELATIVELY")

        by1 = P('STRUCT("a,b" INTEGER, "c(d" VARCHAR, '
                '"e)f" DECIMAL(10,2), plain BIGINT)[]', "t")
        eq(sorted(by1["t__root"]["fields"]),
           ["a,b", "c(d", "e)f", "plain"],
           "quoted commas/parens parse intact")
        by2 = P('STRUCT(x DECIMAL(18,4), y MAP(VARCHAR, JSON), '
                'z VARCHAR)[]', "d")
        # .510: the MAP now spawns its own (key, value) table; DECIMAL
        # params still spawn nothing. Naming uses *_flattened / *__root.
        eq(sorted(by2), ["d__root", "d_flattened", "d_y_flattened"],
           "DECIMAL params spawn nothing; the MAP is its own table")
        need(by2["d_y_flattened"].get("map_field") == "y"
             and "y" not in by2["d__root"]["fields"],
             "the map table is keyed off the root, which drops the column")
        by3 = P('STRUCT(code BIGINT, tags VARCHAR[])[]', "r")
        need(by3["r_tags_flattened"]["elem_scalar"] is True
             and "value" in build_table_sql(by3["r_tags_flattened"], "json",
                                            "/x.parquet"),
             "scalar arrays become value tables")
        for degen in ("STRUCT()[]", "INTEGER[]"):
            P(degen, "e")  # must not raise
        by6 = P('STRUCT(id BIGINT, a STRUCT(b STRUCT(v INTEGER)[])[])'
                '[]', "t3")
        eq(by6["t3_a_b_flattened"]["keys"],
           ["_rid", "t3_ord", "a_ord", "b_ord"],
           "ordinals accumulate down the tree")
        sql6 = build_table_sql(by6["t3_a_b_flattened"], "json", "/x.parquet")
        need(" LATERAL " not in sql6 and "u0" in sql6
             and "SELECT *" not in sql6 and "EXCLUDE" not in sql6
             and "IS NOT NULL" in sql6
             and sql6.count("generate_subscripts") == 3,
             "pipeline invariants hold at depth 3")
        by7 = P('STRUCT("A B" STRUCT(v INTEGER)[], '
                'a_b STRUCT(w INTEGER)[])[]', "x")
        need("x_a_b_flattened" in by7 and "x_a_b_flattened_2" in by7,
             "table-name collisions stay distinct")
        P('STRUCT("uni\u2014kod" VARCHAR, k INT)[]', "u")

    def t_plan_pass2_loaders():
        # .445 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 2 (loaders + sniffers), executed
        # against 24 malformed fixtures. TWO BUGS FIXED, both silent
        # data corruption: (1) a UTF-16 file sailed past the encoding
        # chain -- utf-8 fails on the nulls, latin-1 "succeeds" and
        # loads mojibake; the BOM is sniffed now, and BOM-less utf-16
        # is caught by the null-pattern heuristic (odd nulls = LE,
        # even = BE), proven for LE+BOM, LE bare, and BE bare with a
        # non-ASCII value surviving intact. (2) duplicate or blank
        # headers LOST WHOLE COLUMNS -- idx_of repointed a repeated
        # name to its last index; headers now dedupe like the xlsx
        # path (blanks named, repeats suffixed) and EVERY source index
        # is read: a,a,b keeps all three values. VERIFIED SOUND:
        # ragged rows pad/truncate to the header width; truncated
        # quotes, BOMs, huge headers, binary garbage, malformed JSON,
        # empty files, missing paths, and directories all either load
        # or fail with a clean user-message exception -- programmer-
        # error raises (KeyError/IndexError/AttributeError/TypeError/
        # UnicodeDecodeError) are BANNED across the whole fixture set.
        # Temp hygiene: the instance temp dir gains nothing from the
        # failure cases.
        import csv as _csv, tempfile as _tf, glob as _g
        from samql_core import tmputil as _tmp
        d = _tf.mkdtemp()

        def W(name, data, mode="w"):
            fp = os.path.join(d, name)
            kw = {} if "b" in mode else {
                "encoding": "utf-8", "newline": ""}
            with open(fp, mode, **kw) as f:
                f.write(data)
            return fp
        fx = {
            "empty": W("e.csv", ""),
            "header_only": W("h.csv", "a,b,c\n"),
            "trunc_quote": W("tq.csv", 'a,b\n1,"unclosed\n2,3'),
            "bom8": W("b8.csv", "\ufeffa,b\n1,2\n"),
            "u16_bom": W("u16.csv",
                         "a,b\n1,2\ncaf\u00e9,4\n".encode("utf-16"),
                         "wb"),
            "u16_le": W("ul.csv",
                        "a,b\n1,2\n".encode("utf-16-le"), "wb"),
            "u16_be": W("ub.csv",
                        "a,b\n1,2\n".encode("utf-16-be"), "wb"),
            "latin1": W("l1.csv",
                        "a,b\ncaf\xe9,2\n".encode("latin-1"), "wb"),
            "dup_head": W("dup.csv", "a,a,b\n1,2,3\n"),
            "blank_head": W("bh.csv", ",,\n1,2,3\n"),
            "ragged": W("rag.csv", "a,b,c\n1,2\n1,2,3,4,5\n"),
            "huge_head": W("hh.csv", ("h" * 10000) + ",b\n1,2\n"),
            "bin_csv": W("bin.csv", bytes(range(256)) * 4, "wb"),
            "bin_json": W("bin.json", b"\x00\x01PK\x03junk", "wb"),
            "json_trunc": W("t.json", '[{"a":1},{"a":'),
            "json_scalar": W("sc.json", "42"),
            "jsonl_mixed": W("m.jsonl",
                             '{"a":1}\nnot json\n{"a":2}\n'),
            "unknown_ext": W("u.xyz", "a,b\n1,2\n"),
        }
        BAD = (KeyError, IndexError, AttributeError, TypeError,
               UnicodeDecodeError, StopIteration, _csv.Error)
        sess = _fresh_session()
        inst = _tmp.instance_dir()
        before = len(_g.glob(os.path.join(inst, "*")))
        bugs = []
        try:
            for name, fp in fx.items():
                try:
                    sess.load_file(fp, destination="sqlite",
                                   base_name="p2_" + name)
                except BAD as e:
                    bugs.append((name, type(e).__name__))
                except Exception:
                    pass  # clean user-message failure
            for name, fp in (("missing",
                              os.path.join(d, "nope.csv")),
                             ("directory", d)):
                try:
                    sess.load_file(fp, destination="sqlite",
                                   base_name="p2x_" + name)
                    need(False, name + " must not load")
                except BAD as e:
                    bugs.append((name, type(e).__name__))
                except Exception:
                    pass
            need(not bugs,
                 "programmer-error raises are banned: %r" % bugs)

            def rows_of(nm):
                r = sess.run_query('SELECT * FROM "%s"' % nm,
                                   target="auto")
                return r.get("columns"), r.get("rows")
            for enc_case in ("p2_u16_bom", "p2_u16_le", "p2_u16_be"):
                cols, rows = rows_of(enc_case)
                need(cols == ["a", "b"] and rows[0] == ["1", "2"],
                     "%s decodes clean (the .445 mojibake bug)"
                     % enc_case)
            c, r = rows_of("p2_u16_bom")
            need(r[1][0] == "caf\u00e9",
                 "non-ASCII survives utf-16 intact")
            c, r = rows_of("p2_dup_head")
            need(c == ["a", "a_1", "b"] and r[0] == ["1", "2", "3"],
                 "duplicate headers keep every column (the .445 "
                 "data-loss bug): %r %r" % (c, r))
            c, r = rows_of("p2_blank_head")
            need(len(c) == 3 and len(set(c)) == 3
                 and r[0] == ["1", "2", "3"],
                 "blank headers keep every column: %r" % c)
            c, r = rows_of("p2_ragged")
            need(r[0] == ["1", "2", None]
                 and r[1] == ["1", "2", "3"],
                 "ragged rows pad and truncate to the header")
            after = len(_g.glob(os.path.join(inst, "*")))
            need(after <= before + 2,
                 "failure cases leave no temp litter "
                 "(%d -> %d)" % (before, after))
        finally:
            sess.shutdown()
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "loaders.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('_head == b"\\xff\\xfe"' in src
             and "read_idx = list(range(len(columns)))" in src,
             "the BOM sniff and the every-index read are wired")

    def t_plan_pass1_engines_core():
        # .444 = AUDIT_PLAN PASS 1 (engines.py core), executed in
        # full. VERDICT: CLEAN -- fifteen stations, zero new bugs; the
        # clean bill is pinned so it stays true. THE LOCK MATRIX
        # (_DeadlineRLock, real threads): the owner re-acquires
        # instantly; acquire(blocking=False) never waits; a `with` on
        # a lock held elsewhere raises EngineBusy after the deadline
        # WITHOUT running the body or holding anything; the lock frees
        # normally afterward. KEEPALIVE LIFECYCLE (real opreg, fake
        # conn): a worker's op never goes stale while the keepalive
        # ticks (beat_on_thread), zero interrupts before cancel, the
        # cancel Event re-interrupts, the op ends and the registry
        # drains to zero. THROTTLE: 8->2 with restore, restore works
        # from an except-path, at-or-below cap is a no-op that issues
        # no SET, SAMQL_SHRED_THREADS=0 disables. RECYCLE UNDER LOAD
        # (real sqlite DBManager): four reader threads hammer through
        # recycle() with no leaked exceptions and the fresh connection
        # answers; dropping a missing table is clean.
        import threading as _th, time as _tm, os as _os
        from samql_core.engines import (
            _DeadlineRLock, EngineBusy, DBManager, _ExecKeepalive,
            shred_thread_throttle)
        from samql_core import progress as _opreg

        lk = _DeadlineRLock(timeout=0.25)
        lk.acquire()
        t0 = _tm.monotonic()
        lk.acquire()
        need(_tm.monotonic() - t0 < 0.05, "owner re-acquires instantly")
        lk.release(); lk.release()
        go, held = _th.Event(), _th.Event()

        def _hold():
            lk.acquire(); held.set(); go.wait(3); lk.release()
        h = _th.Thread(target=_hold, daemon=True)
        h.start(); held.wait(2)
        need(lk.acquire(blocking=False) is False,
             "the probe never waits")
        t0 = _tm.monotonic()
        raised = False
        try:
            with lk:
                need(False, "body must not run on a busy lock")
        except EngineBusy:
            raised = True
        dt = _tm.monotonic() - t0
