    def t_name_reservation():
        # .406 loader/flattener audit: _unique_name is a lock-free READ,
        # so two concurrent own-cursor ops (.402 loads, .404 flatten)
        # could pick the SAME table name. reserve_table_name() picks and
        # reserves atomically under the write lock, reservations
        # self-prune once the table exists, and failed ops release.
        import types as _t
        import threading as _th
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager
        m = DuckDBManager.__new__(DuckDBManager)
        m.table_columns = {"t": ["a"]}
        m._reserved_names = set()
        m.write_lock = _th.RLock()
        a = DuckDBManager.reserve_table_name(m, "t")
        b = DuckDBManager.reserve_table_name(m, "t")
        need(a == "t_2" and b == "t_3" and a != b,
             "two concurrent picks of the same base never collide")
        DuckDBManager.release_table_name(m, b)
        need(DuckDBManager.reserve_table_name(m, "t") == "t_3",
             "a released (failed-op) name is reusable")
        m.table_columns[a] = ["x"]   # the op CREATEd it
        DuckDBManager.reserve_table_name(m, "zz")
        need(a not in m._reserved_names,
             "reservations self-prune once the table exists")
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "engines.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        body = src[src.index("def create_table_from_file"):]
        body = body[:body.index("\n    def ", 10)]
        need("final = self.reserve_table_name(name)" in body
             and "self.release_table_name(final)" in body
             and body.index("reserve_table_name")
             < body.index("with lock_ctx:"),
             "loads reserve BEFORE the (possibly null) lock and always "
             "release")
        sess = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        eq(sess.count("mgr.reserve_table_name("), 3,
           "all three flatten name picks reserve")

    def t_result_file_ownership():
        # .405 runtime audit, the critical find: ParquetResultStore.close()
        # unlinked its path UNCONDITIONALLY -- but a .399 zero-copy result
        # BORROWS the table's source cache parquet as its path, so any
        # eviction / tab release / shutdown of that result deleted the
        # loaded table's backing ("No files found that match the
        # pattern"). Stores now carry ownership: borrowed files are never
        # unlinked and never count toward the qr disk budget; owned
        # result files delete exactly as before.
        import types as _t
        from samql_core.rows import ParquetResultStore
        import samql_core.session as S
        import tempfile
        eng = _t.SimpleNamespace(conn=None)
        tdir = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="samql_own_")
        keep = os.path.join(tdir, "fc_keep_own.parquet")
        gone = os.path.join(tdir, "qr_gone_own.parquet")
        for f in (keep, gone):
            with open(f, "wb") as fh:
                fh.write(b"x")
        try:
            borrowed = ParquetResultStore(eng, keep, ["a"],
                                          owns_path=False)
            owned = ParquetResultStore(eng, gone, ["a"])
            borrowed.close()
            owned.close()
            need(os.path.exists(keep) and not os.path.exists(gone),
                 "borrowed survives close; owned is deleted")
            need(borrowed._owns_path is False and owned._owns_path is True,
                 "ownership recorded")
        finally:
            for f in (keep, gone):
                try:
                    os.unlink(f)
                except OSError:
                    pass
            try:
                os.rmdir(tdir)
            except OSError:
                pass
        # the zero-copy constructor marks the borrow
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("owns_path=False" in src
             and src.index("def _zero_copy_source")
             < src.index("owns_path=False"),
             "the zero-copy store borrows its source")
        need('if not getattr(st, "_owns_path", True):' in src,
             "borrowed files don't count toward the qr disk budget")

    def t_native_op_cursor():
        # .404 audit: LONG catalog-writers (shred CREATEs, flatten
        # CREATEs, dump COPY, count probe) moved off the global write
        # lock onto native_op_cursor -- own cursor, registered for
        # interrupt, always deregistered + closed, locked fallback on
        # cursor failure. Brief DDL stays locked by design.
        import types as _t
        import threading as _th
        import inspect
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager

        class _Cur:
            def __init__(self, log):
                self.log = log

            def close(self):
                self.log.append("close")

        m = DuckDBManager.__new__(DuckDBManager)
        log = []
        m.concurrent_reads = True
        m._conn = _t.SimpleNamespace(cursor=lambda: _Cur(log))
        DuckDBManager.conn = DuckDBManager.conn  # property stays
        m._native_ops = {}
        m._native_ops_lock = _th.Lock()
        m.write_lock = _th.RLock()
        with DuckDBManager.native_op_cursor(m) as (xc, lk):
            need(isinstance(xc, _Cur)
                 and m._native_ops.get(_th.get_ident()) is xc,
                 "own cursor, registered while the op runs")
            with lk:
                pass   # _NullCtx
        need(not m._native_ops and log == ["close"],
             "deregistered and closed on exit")
        # locked fallback when cursors are off / fail
        m2 = DuckDBManager.__new__(DuckDBManager)
        m2.concurrent_reads = False
        m2._conn = _t.SimpleNamespace()
        m2._native_ops = {}
        m2._native_ops_lock = _th.Lock()
        m2.write_lock = _th.RLock()
        with DuckDBManager.native_op_cursor(m2) as (xc2, lk2):
            need(xc2 is m2._conn and lk2 is m2.write_lock,
                 "concurrency off -> main conn under the write lock")
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        # .474: table-level flatten's cache COPY is a seventh own-cursor
        # site (keepalive-guarded, so a long flatten heartbeats).
        eq(src.count("native_op_cursor() as (xc, lk)"), 7,
           ".474 repoint: shred + flatten + probe + dump + rowcount + "
           "the docs function list + the flatten cache COPY")

    def t_selection_and_statement_pick():
        # .403, on-box: highlighting the FIRST query and hitting Run ran
        # both statements (the grid shows the LAST result), and Statement
        # hardcoded end-of-document. Now: (a) the toolbar's Run and
        # Statement act on the SELECTION first; (b) Statement uses the
        # REAL cursor; (c) a cursor in the gap after a semicolon picks
        # the PRECEDING statement -- backend and client agree.
        from samql_core.sqlutil import find_statement_at
        spans = [(0, 10, "one"), (20, 30, "two")]
        eq(find_statement_at(spans, 5)[2], "one", "inside the first")
        eq(find_statement_at(spans, 15)[2], "one",
           "the gap after ; belongs to the statement just finished")
        eq(find_statement_at(spans, 25)[2], "two", "inside the second")
        eq(find_statement_at(spans, 99)[2], "two", "past the end: last")
        eq(find_statement_at([(5, 9, "a")], 1)[2], "a",
           "before the first statement: the first")
        need(find_statement_at([], 3) is None, "no statements -> None")
        app = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "App.tsx"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        ed = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "components",
                               "SqlEditor.tsx"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        lib = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "lib",
                                "sql.ts"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        checks = [
            ("the editor publishes the live caret/selection",
             "caretRef" in ed and "onSelect={(e)" in ed
             and "caretRef={editorCaret}" in app),
            ("Run: selection wins",
             "const sel = selectedSql();" in app
             and "runAll(sel.trim() ? sel : activeTab.sql);" in app),
            ("Statement: selection first, else the REAL cursor",
             "runStatementAt(editorCaret.current.start);" in app
             and "runStatementAt(activeTab.sql.length);" not in app),
            ("client gap rule matches the backend",
             "if (s.end <= pos) prev = s;" in lib
             and "spans[spans.length - 1]" not in lib),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "pick wiring: " + "; ".join(missing))

    def t_concurrent_native_loads():
        # .402: a native load ran under the GLOBAL write_lock for its
        # whole duration, so a second load (the Load modal) queued behind
        # a running conversion. Loads now run on their OWN cursor when
        # concurrent reads are on (DuckDB MVCC, different tables
        # guaranteed by _unique_name), the cursor is registered in
        # _native_ops, and interrupt() sweeps those handles so Stop /
        # reset still reaches an own-cursor load.
        import inspect
        import types as _t
        import threading as _th
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager
        body = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager.create_table_from_file)
        checks = [
            ("own cursor when concurrent",
             "self.conn.cursor()" in body
             and 'getattr(self, "concurrent_reads", False)' in body
             and "_NullCtx()" in body),
            ("registered for interrupt, always deregistered + closed",
             "self._native_ops[threading.get_ident()] = handle" in body
             and "self._native_ops.pop(threading.get_ident(), None)"
             in body and "handle.close()" in body),
            ("all statements go through the chosen connection",
             "exec_conn.execute" in body
             and "self.conn.execute" not in body),
            ("cursor failure falls back to the locked path",
             "lock_ctx = self.write_lock" in body),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "concurrent-load wiring: " + "; ".join(missing))
        isrc = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager.interrupt)
        need("_native_ops" in isrc and "h.interrupt()" in isrc,
             "interrupt sweeps own-cursor loads")
        # behavioral: the sweep actually fires on registered handles
        m = DuckDBManager.__new__(DuckDBManager)
        hits = []
        m._cancel = _t.SimpleNamespace(set=lambda: hits.append("flag"))
        m._conn = _t.SimpleNamespace(
            interrupt=lambda: hits.append("main"))
        m._native_ops_lock = _th.Lock()
        m._native_ops = {1: _t.SimpleNamespace(
            interrupt=lambda: hits.append("cursor"))}
        DuckDBManager.interrupt(m)
        eq(sorted(hits), ["cursor", "flag", "main"],
           "flag + main + every load cursor are all interrupted")

    def t_flatten_unnest_first():
        # .401, from the on-box ConversionException ('' -> INT64): the
        # vectorized in-engine UNNEST flatten existed with a documented
        # caller contract (None -> fall back) but had NO caller --
        # flatten_json always took the dump + typed-re-parse road, where a
        # blank in an INT64-sampled field kills the whole task. The
        # DuckDB flatten now tries the in-engine path FIRST (typed data,
        # no re-parse, conversion-proof) and only falls back when it
        # reports nothing to do.
        from samql_core import session as S
        import inspect
        body = inspect.getsource(S.Session.flatten_json)
        need("fast = self._duckdb_unnest_flatten(" in body,
             "flatten_json actually calls the in-engine flatten")
        need(body.index("fast = self._duckdb_unnest_flatten(")
             < body.index("loaders.load_json(mgr, path"),
             "...and tries it BEFORE the dump + re-parse path")
        need("if fast is not None:" in body
             and "return fast" in body
             and body.index("return fast")
             < body.index("path = mgr.table_sources.get(table)"),
             "a fast result returns before any dump/path resolution")
        # behavioral: a session whose unnest returns a result never
        # touches the JSON path
        sess = _fresh_session()
        try:
            calls = []
            sess.duckdb = type("M", (), {"table_sources": {},
                                         "table_columns": {}})()
            sess._duckdb_unnest_flatten = (
                lambda *a, **k: calls.append("fast") or
                {"ok": True, "tables": ["t", "t_legs"], "method": "sql"})
            sess._register_run = lambda *a, **k: calls.append("reg")
            sess._unregister_run = lambda *a, **k: calls.append("unreg")
            sess._run_is_cancelled = lambda *a: False
            sess.snapshot_table_names = lambda: set()
            sess._table_source_path = getattr(
                sess, "_table_source_path", lambda t: None)
            r = S.Session.flatten_json.__get__(sess, S.Session)(
                "t", engine="duckdb", query_id="q1")
            need(r.get("ok") and r["tables"] == ["t", "t_legs"]
                 and "fast" in calls,
                 "the in-engine result is returned as-is: %r" % (r,))
        finally:
            sess.duckdb = None
            sess.shutdown()

    def t_reset_unclogs_and_stall_heals():
        # .400: (a) "stalled" reflects the PRESENT -- when nothing is
        # stale any more (finished, interrupted, or reset) the flag
        # clears on the next scan, and clear_stall() forces the fresh
        # check; (b) Reset engines actually UNCLOGS: it interrupts every
        # registered query handle (concurrent-read cursors the main
        # interrupt can't reach), abandons the orphaned op records, and
        # clears the stall so the watchdog re-flags only if NEW work
        # stalls.
        from samql_core import watchdog as W
        from samql_core import progress as P
        P.reset_for_tests()
        W._state["last_stall"] = {"id": "zz", "at": 1.0}
        with W._dumped_lock:
            W._dumped = {"zz"}
        W.clear_stall()
        need(W.last_stall() is None and not W._dumped,
             "clear_stall forgets the record and the dumped ids")
        # a clean scan self-heals a lingering record
        W._state["last_stall"] = {"id": "zz", "at": 1.0}
        W.scan_once(9999, None)   # nothing stale -> heals
        need(W.last_stall() is None, "no stale ops -> not stalled")
        # ...and a genuinely-stale op re-flags on the next scan
        op = P.begin("query", target="t", engine="duckdb")
        try:
            with P._LOCK:
                P._OPS[op].last_beat = 0.0   # ancient -> stale
            W.scan_once(1, None)
            need(W.last_stall() is not None
                 and W.last_stall()["id"] == op,
                 "a persisting stall is re-flagged after the check")
        finally:
            P.end(op_id=op)
            W.clear_stall()
        # (b) the reset wiring, in order: sweep -> orphan -> abandon ->
        # clear
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        body = src[src.index("def reset_engines"):]
        body = body[:body.index("def optional_features")]
        need("for qid in list(self._running):" in body
             and "self.cancel_query(qid)" in body
             and body.index("self.cancel_query(qid)")
             < body.index("old_duck = self.duckdb"),
             "registered handles are interrupted BEFORE orphaning")
        need("opreg.end(op_id=o.get(\"id\"))" in body
             and "watchdog.clear_stall()" in body
             and body.index("opreg.end") < body.index("clear_stall"),
             "orphaned op records are abandoned, then the stall re-checks")

    def t_zero_copy_and_headroom():
        # .399, from two on-box dumps: a bare SELECT * over a
        # parquet-backed view re-materialized gigabytes of nested structs
        # (saturating DuckDB's internal pool so hard that Thread.start()
        # stalled and every poll timed out). (a) That query now serves the
        # SOURCE parquet as the result store directly -- zero copy,
        # instant, pruned paging; (b) DuckDB leaves two cores of
        # interpreter headroom (env-overridable).
        import samql_core.session as S

        class _Cur:
            def execute(self, q, *a):
                pass

            def fetchone(self):
                return (925,)

            def fetchall(self):
                return [("json", "STRUCT"), ("code", "BIGINT")]

            def close(self):
                pass

        class _Eng:
            table_sources = {"sophis_Trade": "C:/t/fc_a.parquet",
                             "plain": "C:/t/x.csv"}
            conn = type("C", (), {"cursor":
                                  staticmethod(lambda: _Cur())})()

        class _O:
            _BARE_SELECT = S.Session._BARE_SELECT
            _SIMPLE_SELECT = S.Session._SIMPLE_SELECT
            _parse_simple_select_cols = staticmethod(
                S.Session._parse_simple_select_cols)
            _parquet_table_source = S.Session._parquet_table_source
        zc = S.Session._zero_copy_source
        o = _O()
        r = zc(o, _Eng(), "SELECT * FROM sophis_trade")
        need(r is not None and r[2] == 925
             and r[1]._path == "C:/t/fc_a.parquet"
             and r[1].capped is False and r[0] == ["json", "code"],
             "the bare full-table select serves the source parquet, "
             "uncapped, case-insensitively")
        need(zc(o, _Eng(), 'select * from "sophis_Trade" ;') is not None,
             "quoted + trailing semicolon still matches")
        # Simple projections zero-copy too (column list pushed at read time).
        r2 = zc(o, _Eng(), "SELECT code FROM sophis_trade")
        need(r2 is not None and r2[0] == ["code"]
             and r2[1]._path == "C:/t/fc_a.parquet",
             "simple projection borrows the source parquet: %r" % (r2,))
        need(zc(o, _Eng(), "SELECT * FROM sophis_trade LIMIT 10") is None,
             "LIMIT must not zero-copy (export would escape the row cap)")
        need(zc(o, _Eng(), "SELECT code FROM sophis_trade LIMIT 3") is None,
             "projected LIMIT must not zero-copy either")
        for bad in ("SELECT * FROM sophis_trade WHERE 1=1",
                    "SELECT code AS c FROM sophis_trade",
                    "SELECT f(code) FROM sophis_trade",
                    "SELECT * FROM plain",
                    "SELECT * FROM missing"):
            need(zc(o, _Eng(), bad) is None,
                 "anything non-trivial takes the normal path: " + bad)
        sess = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                    encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("fast = self._zero_copy_source(engine, sql)" in sess,
             "the materializer short-circuits through the fast path")
        # (b) headroom
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager
        tc = DuckDBManager._thread_count
        real = os.environ.pop("SAMQL_DUCKDB_THREADS", None)
        try:
            import unittest.mock as _mock
            with _mock.patch("os.cpu_count", return_value=8):
                eq(tc(), 6, "two cores stay free for the interpreter")
                eq(tc(low_memory=True), 2, "low-memory stays small")
            os.environ["SAMQL_DUCKDB_THREADS"] = "3"
            eq(tc(), 3, "the env override wins")
        finally:
            os.environ.pop("SAMQL_DUCKDB_THREADS", None)
            if real is not None:
                os.environ["SAMQL_DUCKDB_THREADS"] = real

    def t_tab_naming_and_rename():
        # .396: a NEW tab's number comes from the MAX existing "Query N"
        # (closing a tab can't make the next new one collide), and titles
        # rename inline via double-click with Enter/blur commit and Esc
        # cancel -- the title labels the tab's runs in the stat window.
        app = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "App.tsx"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        ide = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "controllers",
                                "useIdeController.ts"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        checks = [
            ("collision-proof numbering",
             "Math.max(" in ide
             and "/^Query (\\d+)$/.exec(tab.title" in ide
             and "`Query ${edTabs.length + 1}`" not in ide),
            ("double-click rename with commit + cancel",
             "onDoubleClick" in app
             and 'className="tab-rename"' in app
             and "commitRename" in app
             and 'e.key === "Escape"' in app),
            ("a blank rename keeps the old title",
             "const name = r.draft.trim();" in app
             and "if (name)" in app),
            ("the produced RESULT tabs follow the rename",
             'x.originTabId === r.id' in app
             and app.index("setEdTabs((tabs) =>\n"
                           "            tabs.map((x) => (x.id === r.id")
             < app.index('x.originTabId === r.id')),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "tab UX broken: " + "; ".join(missing))

    def t_shred_joinkeys_and_cache_guard():
        # .394: (a) every shred plan carries a slim JOIN HUB -- _rid + a
        # few scalar identifiers -- named <base>_flattened with a
        # self-explaining path, built from explicit columns (never .*);
        # (b) clearing the conversion cache SKIPS files live tables still
        # point at and says so; (c) the journal export carries the group.
        from samql_core.diagnostics import parse_duckdb_type
        from samql_core.shred import plan_shred, build_table_sql
        t = ("STRUCT(code BIGINT, currency VARCHAR, note JSON, "
             "legs STRUCT(r DOUBLE)[])[]")
        plan = plan_shred("json", parse_duckdb_type(t), base="trade")
        jk = [x for x in plan["tables"] if x.get("join_helper")]
        need(len(jk) == 1 and jk[0]["name"] == "trade_flattened",
             "one helper, named <base>_flattened")
        jk = jk[0]
        eq(jk["fields"], ["code", "currency", "note"],
           ".520: the hub IS the records table -- it carries EVERY "
           "depth-1 scalar (JSON included); nothing is silently dropped")
        need("join" in jk["path"] and "_rid" in jk["path"],
             "the path TELLS the user what to join on: %r" % jk["path"])
        eq(jk["parent"], plan["tables"][0]["name"],
           "parented to the root it slims down")
        sql = build_table_sql(jk, "json", "C:/x.parquet")
        need("e0.code" in sql and "e0.currency" in sql
             and ".*" not in sql and "trade_flattened" in sql,
             "explicit slim columns, never star: %s" % sql[:160])
        # (b) in-use cache guard, executed against the real handler
        import server as _srv
        from samql_core import filecache
        s2 = _fresh_session()
        os.makedirs(filecache._DIR, exist_ok=True)
        keepf = os.path.join(filecache._DIR, "fc_inuse_test.parquet")
        dropf = os.path.join(filecache._DIR, "fc_orphan_test.parquet")
        try:
            for f in (keepf, dropf):
                with open(f, "wb") as fh:
                    fh.write(b"x" * 32)

            class _Mgr:
                table_sources = {"t": keepf}
            s2.duckdb = _Mgr()
            r = _srv.Api.storage_clean(s2, None, {"filecache": True},
                                       {"query": {}})
            need(os.path.exists(keepf) and not os.path.exists(dropf),
                 "the in-use file survives; the orphan is removed")
            need("kept" in (r.get("note") or ""),
                 "the response SAYS a file was kept: %r" % r.get("note"))
        finally:
            s2.duckdb = None
            s2.shutdown()
            for f in (keepf, dropf):
                try:
                    os.unlink(f)
                except OSError:
                    pass
        # (c) journal export group wiring
        nb = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "components",
                               "Notebook.tsx"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        lib = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "lib",
                                "notebook.ts"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("group: groupNameOf(c)" in nb
             and '"Cell", "Group", "SQL"' in lib
             and "r.group || \"\"" in lib,
             "the export carries each cell's group")

    def t_shred_deep_arrays():
        # .393 (on-box preflight read "arrays": 2 on a 6-array type): the
        # planner now descends through PLAIN STRUCT WRAPPERS, so an array
        # like fixedFlowsList.fixedFlows gets its own table with a dotted
        # hop the SQL builder derefs; wrapper scalars are kept. Quoted
        # field names parse; the preflight names the planned tables and
        # flags a truncated type string.
        from samql_core.diagnostics import parse_duckdb_type
        from samql_core.shred import plan_shred, build_table_sql
        t = ("STRUCT(code BIGINT, identifier MAP(VARCHAR, JSON), "
             "\"name\" VARCHAR, "
             "floatingFlowsList STRUCT(isForced VARCHAR)[], "
             "fixedFlowsList STRUCT(fixedFlows STRUCT(fixedRate "
             "DOUBLE)[], percentage BIGINT), "
             "futureCashFlows STRUCT(receivingLeg STRUCT(fixingDate "
             "DATE)[], payingLeg STRUCT(startDate DATE)[])[])[]")
        plan = plan_shred("json", parse_duckdb_type(t), base="trade")
        names = [x["name"] for x in plan["tables"]]
        # .507: +1 -- the fixedFlowsList wrapper's scalar (percentage) now
        # lives in its OWN wrapper table instead of a dotted root column.
        # .510: +1 more -- the identifier MAP becomes a (key, value) table.
        eq(len(names), 9,
           "six array levels + wrapper + map + the join hub plan: %s"
           % names)
        need(any(t.get("map_field") == "identifier"
                 for t in plan["tables"]),
             "the element-root MAP is its own (key, value) table (.510)")
        need("trade_fixedflowslist_fixedflows_flattened" in names,
             "the wrapper-hidden array gets its own table")
        root = plan["tables"][0]
        need("fixedFlowsList" not in root["fields"]
             and isinstance(root.get("leaves"), list),
             ".428 repoint: the wrapper is no longer a kept blob "
             "(that duplication blew the 13 GiB ceiling); its scalar "
             "siblings survive as dotted LEAVES instead")
        ff = [x for x in plan["tables"]
              if x["name"].endswith("_fixedflows_flattened")][0]
        sql = build_table_sql(ff, "json", "C:/x.parquet")
        need('"fixedFlowsList"."fixedFlows"' in sql,
             "the dotted hop derefs through the wrapper: %s" % sql[:200])
        # preflight surfaces the plan + truncation
        s2 = _fresh_session()
        try:
            class _Mgr:
                table_sources = {"t": "C:/x/fc.parquet"}

                def _column_types_raw(self, table):
                    return {"json": t,
                            "cut": "STRUCT(a STRUCT(b INT"}
            s2.duckdb = _Mgr()
            r = s2.shred_preflight("duckdb", "t")
            cols = {c["name"]: c for c in r["columns"]}
            eq(cols["json"]["arrays"], 9,
           "preflight counts six levels + wrapper + map + the join hub")
            need("trade" not in cols["json"]["tables"]
                 and cols["json"]["tables"][0] == "t__root"
                 and "t_flattened" in cols["json"]["tables"]
                 and "t_fixedflowslist_fixedflows_flattened"
                 in cols["json"]["tables"]
                 and len(cols["json"]["tables"]) == 9,
                 "the planned table NAMES are visible: %r"
                 % cols["json"]["tables"])
            need("TRUNCATED" in cols["cut"]["reason"],
                 "an unbalanced type string is flagged")
        finally:
            s2.duckdb = None
            s2.shutdown()

    def t_shred_preflight():
        # .388: a shred decline EXPLAINS itself. Every gate + per-column
        # reason, and the picker's empty state consumes the verdict.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            class _Mgr:
                table_sources = {"t_copy": None,
                                 "t_pq": "C:/x/fc_a.parquet"}

                def _column_types_raw(self, table):
                    if table == "t_pq":
                        return {"json": "STRUCT(a BIGINT, "
                                        "legs STRUCT(r DOUBLE)[])[]",
                                "identifier": "MAP(VARCHAR, VARCHAR)",
                                "ghost": ""}
                    return {}
            s.duckdb = _Mgr()
            r = s.shred_preflight("duckdb", "t_copy")
            g = {x["name"]: x for x in r["gates"]}
            need(not g["parquet source"]["ok"]
                 and "Copy into a table" in g["parquet source"]["detail"]
                 and "Blocked by the Parquet-source gate"
                 in r["verdict"],
                 "a copy-mode table names the gate AND the fix: %r"
                 % r["verdict"])
            r = s.shred_preflight("duckdb", "t_pq")
            g = {x["name"]: x for x in r["gates"]}
            need(g["parquet source"]["ok"]
                 and g["nested array columns"]["ok"]
                 and r["candidates"] == ["json"]
                 and "Ready: json ->" in r["verdict"],
                 "a shreddable table reads Ready with its columns")
            cols = {c["name"]: c for c in r["columns"]}
            need(cols["json"]["arrays"] >= 2,
                 "the LIST-of-STRUCT chain plans multiple tables")
            need("MAP" in cols["identifier"]["reason"]
                 and "map_extract" in cols["identifier"]["reason"],
                 "a MAP column explains itself with the alternative")
            need("unreadable" in cols["ghost"]["reason"],
                 "a blank type explains the DESCRIBE/typeof gap")
            r = s.shred_preflight("sqlite", "t_pq")
            need(not r["gates"][0]["ok"] and "DuckDB" in r["verdict"]
                 or "Load the file into DuckDB" in r["verdict"],
                 "the engine gate speaks first")
        finally:
            s.duckdb = None
            s.shutdown()
        # wiring: registry entry + endpoint + the picker consumes it
        di = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "diagnostics.py"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        need('"shred_preflight"' in di and "why won't this table flatten"
             in di, "the diagnostic is registered for the modal")
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("/api/shred/preflight" in srv, "the endpoint is routed")
        fx = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "components",
                               "FieldExplorer.tsx"),
                  encoding="utf-8").read()
        # .607: preflight endpoint stays for the modal, but the field explorer
        # drives shred through the lighter plan/run pair (shredPlan/shredRun),
        # not preflight -- so the FE still never calls shredPreflight.
        need("shredPreflight(" not in fx,
             "the field explorer drives shred via plan/run, not preflight")

    def t_store_page_pruning():
        # The stall's true root (.387): unsorted store pages ran
        # ORDER BY "__rn" (a synthesized expression -> no pruning -> TopN
        # over EVERY row group of a giant nested file). Unsorted paging and
        # exports now predicate/order on the RAW prunable file_row_number;
        # a user sort keeps the legacy TopN (genuinely unavoidable).
        from samql_core.rows import ParquetResultStore
        ran = []

        class _Cur:
            def execute(self, sql, *a):
                ran.append(sql)

            def fetchall(self):
                return [(1, 2)]

            def fetchmany(self, n):
                return []

            def fetchone(self):
                return (0,)

            def close(self):
                pass

        class _Eng:
            conn = type("C", (), {"cursor":
                                  staticmethod(lambda: _Cur())})()
        store = ParquetResultStore(_Eng(), "C:\\t\\qr_x.parquet",
                                   ["a", "b"])
        store._n = 1000
        _ = store[0:200]
        need("WHERE file_row_number >= 0" in ran[-1]
             and "AND file_row_number < 200" in ran[-1]
             and "ORDER BY file_row_number" in ran[-1]
             and '"__rn"' not in ran[-1],
             "an unsorted page prunes by file_row_number: %s" % ran[-1])
        _ = store[500]
        need("file_row_number >= 500" in ran[-1]
             and "file_row_number < 501" in ran[-1],
             "an integer index prunes to one row's group")
        it = iter(store)
        next(it, None)
        need("ORDER BY file_row_number" in ran[-1]
             and '"__rn"' not in ran[-1]
             and "WHERE" not in ran[-1],
             "an export streams in raw file order (no synthesized sort)")
        # Sorted pages: first page is TopN (no write_lock COPY); a background
        # snapshot then enables file_row_number range pages. CODE was wrong to
        # block the first page on a full COPY — test updated to the deferred
        # contract (exact totals unchanged).
        mat_calls = []

        def _fake_mat(order, where="", params=None):
            mat_calls.append(order)
            snap = ParquetResultStore(_Eng(), "C:\\t\\qv_sorted.parquet",
                                      ["a", "b"])
            snap._n = 1000
            return snap

        store._materialize_snapshot = _fake_mat
        sv = store.sorted_view(0, descending=True)
        need(not mat_calls,
             "sorted_view must not COPY before the first page")
        _ = sv[0:50]
        need(any("LIMIT 50" in s and "OFFSET 0" in s and 'ORDER BY "a" DESC' in s
                 for s in ran),
             "first sorted page uses TopN LIMIT/OFFSET: %s" % ran[-1])
        # Kickoff starts background mat; wait briefly for fake_mat to land.
        import time as _time
        deadline = _time.monotonic() + 2.0
        while not mat_calls and _time.monotonic() < deadline:
            _time.sleep(0.01)
        need(mat_calls and 'ORDER BY "a" DESC' in mat_calls[0],
             "background snapshot materializes with the user ORDER BY")
        # Once snap is in cache, pages use file_row_number ranges.
        deadline = _time.monotonic() + 2.0
        while store._snap_cache.get(("sort", 0, True)) is None \
                and _time.monotonic() < deadline:
            _time.sleep(0.01)
        snap = store._snap_cache.get(("sort", 0, True))
        need(snap is not None, "snapshot landed in cache")
        ran.clear()
        _ = snap[0:50]
        need("WHERE file_row_number >= 0" in ran[-1]
             and "file_row_number < 50" in ran[-1],
             "after materialize, sorted pages use file_row_number ranges")

    def t_audit_fix_high_snap_ready_and_filtered_total():
        # Post-651 audit: failed snap must not leave _ready sticky; filtered
        # DiskBackedRows views must honor total= (no per-page COUNT).
        import threading as _th
        from samql_core.rows import DiskBackedRows, _LazySnapView

        store = DiskBackedRows(block=100)
        store.extend([(i, "v%s" % i) for i in range(40)])
        store._flush()
        counts = {"n": 0}
        real = store._count_where

        def _counting(where, params):
            counts["n"] += 1
            return real(where, params)

        store._count_where = _counting
        terms = [(0, "equals", 7)]
        view = store.filtered_view(terms, total=1)
        eq(len(view), 1, "filtered view uses provided total")
        _ = view[0:1]
        eq(counts["n"], 0,
           "slice with total= must not re-COUNT: %s" % counts["n"])

        class _BoomStore:
            _closed = False
            _snap_cache = {}
            _pending_snaps = {}

            def _materialize_snapshot(self, order, where="", params=None):
                raise RuntimeError("snap fail")

        boom = _BoomStore()
        view2 = _LazySnapView(
            boom, ("sort", 0, False), 'ORDER BY "a"', total=10)
        view2._kickoff()
        need(view2._ready.wait(2.0), "failed build still signals ready")
        need(view2._started is False, "failed build clears _started")
        need(view2._snap is None, "failed build leaves no snap")
        # Retry must clear ready so awaiters wait for the new generation.
        cleared = []

        class _Gate(_th.Event):
            def clear(self):
                cleared.append(1)
                return super().clear()

        view2._ready = _Gate()
        view2._ready.set()  # poison like a prior failure
        view2._kickoff()
        need(cleared, "retry kickoff clears sticky _ready")
        view2._ready.wait(2.0)

    def t_stall_escalation():
        # On-box 2026-07-02: a cancelled query stayed wedged in a native
        # fetch (the watchdog dump showed rows._fetch under page). The
        # watchdog now RE-FIRES the engine interrupt on every pass for a
        # stalled op the user already cancelled -- idempotent, logged.
        from samql_core import watchdog as W
        from samql_core import progress as P
        import tempfile as _tf
        fired = []
        real = W._state.get("reinterrupt")
        try:
            W.set_reinterrupt(lambda qid: fired.append(qid) or True)
            P.begin("query", op_id="stuck1", engine="duckdb",
                    surface="ide", label="monster")
            log = _tf.NamedTemporaryFile(suffix=".log", delete=False).name
            W.scan_once(0.0, log)      # everything is "stale" at 0s
            need("stuck1" in fired,
                 "the escalation hook fires for a stalled op")
            need("re-interrupt fired" in open(log, encoding="utf-8").read(),
                 "the escalation is logged next to the dump")
        finally:
            W._state["reinterrupt"] = real
            P.end(op_id="stuck1")
            try:
                os.unlink(log)
            except OSError:
                pass
        # the session-side hook: only cancel-requested runs re-fire, and the
        # registered handle's interrupt is what gets called
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            hits = []

            class _H:
                def interrupt(self):
                    hits.append(1)
            with s._running_lock:
                s._running["qq"] = _H()
            eq(s.reinterrupt_if_cancelled("qq"), False,
               "a run the user never cancelled is left alone")
            s._cancelled_runs.add("qq")
            eq(s.reinterrupt_if_cancelled("qq"), True,
               "a cancelled stalled run re-fires")
            eq(hits, [1], "the interrupt handle was invoked")
            with s._running_lock:
                s._running.pop("qq", None)
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("set_reinterrupt(" in srv and "timeout = 60" in srv,
             "startup installs the hook; request sockets can't wedge "
             "threads forever")

    def t_journal_dependency_gate():
        # Journal scheduling now uses one tested id-keyed dependency graph for
        # direct names, group aliases, chart/pivot sources and reconcile inputs.
        # A run registers synchronously before awaiting anything; same-cell
        # reruns queue, dependents await active prerequisites, and optimized
        # Run all executes stale cells in dependency waves.
        nb = open(os.path.join(ROOT, "frontend", "src", "components",
                               "Notebook.tsx"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        checks = [
            ("a registry of in-flight runs keyed by cell id",
             "inflightRef" in nb
             and "useRef<Map<string, Promise<void>>>" in nb
             and "inflightRef.current.set(id, gate)" in nb),
            ("registration happens before any await",
             nb.index("inflightRef.current.set(id, gate)")
             < nb.index("if (hadGate) await hadGate;")),
            ("the shared dependency graph supplies direct prerequisites",
             "buildJournalDependencyGraph(" in nb
             and ").depIds[id] || []" in nb),
            ("dependents WAIT for their in-flight inputs",
             "if (dep && dep !== gate) await dep;" in nb),
            ("a re-run of the same cell queues behind its prior run",
             "if (hadGate) await hadGate;" in nb),
            ("the gate always releases (even on error/early return)",
             "release();" in nb and "} finally {" in nb),
            ("Run all executes stale dependency waves to completion",
             "for (const wave of plan.waves)" in nb
             and "await Promise.allSettled(" in nb
             and "planJournalRunAll(" in nb),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "dependency gate broken: " + "; ".join(missing))

    def t_field_checkbox_not_stretched():

                   "FileLoadTab.tsx")

        need('width: "auto"' in window and "flex: \"0 0 auto\"" in window,
             "field checkbox opts out of the full-width form-row rule")

    def t_result_row_cap():
        # A runaway explode must terminate at a safety ceiling instead of
        # materializing forever (which pins the engine lock and wedges the app).
        # Verify the cap helper, that the COPY carries the LIMIT, and that an
        # over-cap result is flagged + reported at the ceiling.
        import types as _t
        import threading as _th
        import os as _os
        from samql_core import session as S

        class C:
            _result_row_cap = S.Session._result_row_cap
            low_memory = False

            def _zero_copy_source(self, e, q):
                return None
        c = C()
        _os.environ.pop("SAMQL_MAX_RESULT_ROWS", None)
        need(c._result_row_cap() == 10_000_000, "default safety cap is 10M rows")
        _os.environ["SAMQL_MAX_RESULT_ROWS"] = "0"
        need(c._result_row_cap() is None, "cap disabled with 0")
        _os.environ["SAMQL_MAX_RESULT_ROWS"] = "5"
        # NOTE: everything below runs under try/finally so a failure can't
        # leak a 5-row cap into later tests.

        try:
            seen = []

            class FakeCur:
                def __init__(self, desc=None, one=None):
                    self.description = desc
                    self._one = one

                def fetchone(self):
                    return self._one

            class FakeConn:
                def __init__(self, cnt):
                    self.cnt = cnt

                def execute(self, sql):
                    seen.append(sql)
                    if sql.startswith("COPY"):
                        return FakeCur()
                    if "LIMIT 0" in sql:
                        return FakeCur(desc=[("a",), ("b",)])
                    if "count(*)" in sql:
                        return FakeCur(one=(self.cnt,))
                    return FakeCur()

            exec_pq = S.Session._exec_duckdb_parquet.__get__(c, S.Session)
            # over the cap: 6 > 5
            eng = _t.SimpleNamespace(conn=FakeConn(6), write_lock=_th.Lock())
            cols, store, total, kind = exec_pq(eng, "SELECT * FROM big")
            copy_sql = next(s for s in seen if s.startswith("COPY"))
            need("LIMIT 6" in copy_sql,
                 "COPY carries the safety LIMIT (cap+1): " + copy_sql)
            need("row_number()" not in copy_sql,
                 "the COPY pays NO global window; __rn is synthesized at read "
                 "time: " + copy_sql)
            need(cols == ["a", "b"],
                 "store columns are the data columns (no __rn to strip)")
            from samql_core.rows import ParquetResultStore
            src = ParquetResultStore(eng, "/tmp/x.parquet", ["a"])._src()
            need("file_row_number = true" in src and '"__rn"' in src
                 and "EXCLUDE (file_row_number)" in src,
                 "the store synthesizes a 1-based __rn from file_row_number: "
                 + src)
            need(total == 5 and getattr(store, "capped", False) is True
                 and store.cap == 5,
                 "over-cap result is flagged capped and total reports the ceiling")
            # under the cap: 3 < 5 -> not capped, real total
            seen.clear()
            eng2 = _t.SimpleNamespace(conn=FakeConn(3), write_lock=_th.Lock())
            _cols, store2, total2, _k = exec_pq(eng2, "SELECT * FROM small")
            need(total2 == 3 and getattr(store2, "capped", False) is False,
                 "under-cap result is not flagged and keeps its real total")
        finally:
            _os.environ.pop("SAMQL_MAX_RESULT_ROWS", None)
        # the cached result carries the flag, and page() surfaces it
        cr = S._CachedResult("rid", ["a"], _t.SimpleNamespace(capped=True, cap=5),
                             5, "sql", "t", "duckdb")
        need(cr.capped is True and cr.cap == 5,
             "_CachedResult inherits capped/cap from the store")
        # a REAL page() call proves the flag flows to the wire (was a grep)
        class _CR2:
            cols = ["a"]
            total = 1
            sql = "SELECT 1"
            engine = "duckdb"
            capped = True
            cap = 5
            data_epoch = 0

            def view(self, sort_col, descending):
                return [(1,)]
        sess2 = _t.SimpleNamespace(
            _results={"rid2": _CR2()}, _data_epoch=0,
            _running_lock=_th.Lock(), _running={})
        sess2._live_cached_result = \
            S.Session._live_cached_result.__get__(sess2, S.Session)
        sess2._clear_stale_engine_cancel = \
            S.Session._clear_stale_engine_cancel.__get__(sess2, S.Session)
        sess2._register_run = lambda *a, **k: None
        sess2._unregister_run = lambda *a, **k: None
        sess2._end_run_keep_cancel = lambda *a, **k: None
        sess2._run_is_cancelled = lambda q: False
        pg = S.Session.page.__get__(sess2, S.Session)("rid2")
        need(pg.get("result_capped") is True and pg.get("result_cap") == 5,
             "page() surfaces result_capped/result_cap on the wire: "
             + repr({k: pg.get(k) for k in ("result_capped", "result_cap")}))

    def t_capped_is_a_toast():

             "IDE run toasts on a capped result")

    def t_temp_cleanup_on_restart():
        # Every session's temp data must be gone on exit AND on the next start.
        # reset_instance() (startup) wipes our dir to a clean slate even if a
        # dead same-PID instance left junk; cleanup_instance() (exit) removes it.
        #
        # Isolate onto a THROWAWAY dir instead of the real shared instance dir:
        # when DuckDB is installed the suite's live engine holds open handles to
        # its db file + spill dir inside the real instance dir, and Windows
        # refuses to rmtree a directory that still has open handles -- so testing
        # cleanup against the live dir mid-suite is not a valid check. (At real
        # shutdown the engines are recycled first, releasing those handles.)
        import tempfile as _tf
        from samql_core import tmputil as T
        saved_inst, saved_made = T._INSTANCE, T._made
        tmp = _tf.mkdtemp(prefix="samql_cleanup_test_")
        try:
            T._INSTANCE, T._made = tmp, True
            # reset_instance() wipes leftovers and recreates the dir empty.
            stale = os.path.join(tmp, "stale_qr_test.parquet")
            with open(stale, "w") as fh:
                fh.write("x")
            T.reset_instance()
            need(not os.path.exists(stale) and os.path.isdir(T._INSTANCE),
                 "reset_instance wipes leftovers and recreates the dir empty")
            # cleanup_instance() removes the whole dir. Files are written via a
            # closed context manager so no handle lingers to defeat rmtree.
            with open(os.path.join(T._INSTANCE, "live.tmp"), "w") as fh:
                fh.write("y")
            T.cleanup_instance()
            need(not os.path.exists(T._INSTANCE),
                 "cleanup_instance removes the whole instance dir on shutdown")
        finally:
            T._INSTANCE, T._made = saved_inst, saved_made
            try:
                import shutil as _sh
                _sh.rmtree(tmp, ignore_errors=True)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def t_temp_cleanup_wiring():
        # Structural: startup wipes+sweeps, exit cleans, and every temp artifact
        # lives under the per-instance dir so those two hooks actually catch it.
        def rd(*p):
            return open(os.path.join(ROOT, *p), encoding="utf-8").read()
        srv = rd("backend", "server.py")
        tmp = rd("backend", "samql_core", "tmputil.py")
        eng = rd("backend", "samql_core", "engines.py")
        sess = rd("backend", "samql_core", "session.py")
        checks = [
            ("startup wipes our instance dir, then sweeps dead ones",
             "tmputil.reset_instance()" in srv
             and "tmputil.sweep_stale()" in srv),
            ("clean exit removes this instance's temp dir",
             "tmputil.cleanup_instance()" in srv),
            ("exit handlers cover atexit + termination signals",
             "atexit.register(_graceful_shutdown)" in srv
             and "SIGTERM" in srv and "SIGINT" in srv),
            ("reset_instance wipes then recreates the dir",
             "def reset_instance" in tmp
             and "_rmtree(_INSTANCE" in tmp),
            ("cleanup is hardened against Windows read-only leftovers",
             "def _rmtree" in tmp and "S_IWRITE" in tmp),
            ("DuckDB spill + db file live under the instance dir",
             'instance_path("duckdb_spill")' in eng
             and "tmputil.instance_path(" in eng
             and '/duckdb_spill")' not in eng
             and '+ "/duckdb_spill"' not in eng),
            ("parquet result store + large-file cache use instance temp",
             'new_tempfile("qr_"' in sess and 'new_tempfile("cache_"' in eng),
            ("the on-disk SQLite db lives under the instance dir",
             "dir=tmputil.instance_dir()" in eng),
            ("session shutdown closes remote connections then recycles engines",
             "interrupt_loads()" in sess
             and "for name, conn in list((self.connections" in sess
             and "sync_restore_manifest()" in sess
             and "self.clear_all(clear_manifest=False)" in sess
             and sess.index("interrupt_loads()")
             < sess.index("self.clear_all(clear_manifest=False)")
             and sess.index("self.connections.clear()")
             < sess.index("self.clear_all(clear_manifest=False)")),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "temp-cleanup wiring broken: " + "; ".join(missing))

    def t_session_shutdown_closes_connections():
        # A clean Exit→stop / Ctrl+C must close ODBC/SQL Server connections
        # before engines recycle, so the next start never inherits hung
        # driver sessions or locked spill files from a half-closed exit.
        s = _fresh_session()
        closed = []

        class _Conn:
            def close(self):
                closed.append(True)

        try:
            s.connections["mssql_prod"] = _Conn()
            s.shutdown()
            need(closed == [True], "remote connection.close() ran on shutdown")
            need(not s.connections, "connections map cleared on shutdown")
            need(getattr(s, "_closed", False), "session marked closed")
        finally:
            try:
                s.shutdown()
            except Exception:
                pass

    def t_json_streaming_parser():
        from samql_core.flatten import stream_json_records
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

        def w(name, text):
            p = os.path.join(dd, name)
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(text)
            return p

        eq(len(list(stream_json_records(
            w("a.json", '[{"x":1},{"x":2},{"x":3}]')))), 3, "array of objects")
        eq(len(list(stream_json_records(
            w("p.json", '[\n {"x":1},\n {"x":2}\n]\n')))), 2, "pretty array")
        eq(len(list(stream_json_records(
            w("n.jsonl", '{"x":1}\n{"x":2}\n\n{"x":3}\n')))), 3, "ndjson")
        eq(list(stream_json_records(w("o.json", '{"only":true}'))),
           [{"only": True}], "single object")
        eq(len(list(stream_json_records(
            w("c.json", '{"x":1} {"x":2}\n{"x":3}')))), 3, "concatenated")
        eq(list(stream_json_records(w("e.json", "[]"))), [], "empty array")
        # a value larger than one read chunk must still parse as one record
        big = '[{"id":1,"blob":"' + ("z" * 200000) + '"},{"id":2}]'
        recs = list(stream_json_records(w("big.json", big)))
        eq(len(recs), 2, "chunk-straddling element")
        eq(len(recs[0]["blob"]), 200000, "big value intact")

    def t_json_stream_spill_equiv():
        # streamed + spilled flatten must equal the whole-file flatten
        from samql_core.flatten import (stream_json_records, JSONFlattener,
                                        read_json_any_format)
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "equiv.json")
        data = [{"id": i, "user": {"name": f"n{i}"},
                 "tags": ["a", "b"][: 1 + (i % 2)]} for i in range(1500)]
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(data, f)
        fa = JSONFlattener(root_name="data")
        fa.flatten(read_json_any_format(p))
        fb = JSONFlattener(root_name="data", spill_threshold=100)
        try:
            for rec in stream_json_records(p):
                fb.add_record(rec)
            ta = {t: fa.row_count(t) for t in fa.table_names()}
            tb = {t: fb.row_count(t) for t in fb.table_names()}
            eq(tb, ta, "streamed+spill row counts differ from whole-file")
            eq(fb.columns("data"), fa.columns("data"), "column order differs")
        finally:
            fa.close()
            fb.close()

    def t_json_load_ndjson():
        # end-to-end NDJSON load through a Session, with spill forced low
        import samql_core.loaders as L
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "people.jsonl")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for i in range(300):
                f.write(json.dumps({"id": i, "tags": ["a", "b"]}) + "\n")
        try:
            out = L.load_json(s.db, p, base_name="ppl", spill_threshold=50)
            counts = {o["name"]: o["rows"] for o in out}
            eq(counts.get("ppl"), 300, "ndjson root rows")
            eq(counts.get("ppl_tags"), 600, "ndjson child rows")
            n = s.run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ppl_tags",
                            target="__local__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(n, 600, "child table not queryable")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_duckdb_json_readers():
        # The DuckDB JSON reader list is NDJSON-aware. For .ndjson/.jsonl the
        # first reader pins format='newline_delimited' so DuckDB skips the
        # format-sniffing scan on huge files; for plain .json it auto-detects.
        # Both keep a tolerant retry and cap the per-object size. Pure string
        # builder, so this runs even without duckdb installed.
        from samql_core import engines as E
        fwd = "C:/data/huge.ndjson"
        eq(E._is_ndjson_path("a/b.ndjson"), True, ".ndjson is ndjson")
        eq(E._is_ndjson_path("a/b.JSONL"), True, ".jsonl is ndjson (any case)")
        eq(E._is_ndjson_path("a/b.json"), False, "plain .json is not ndjson")

        nd = E._json_readers(fwd, ndjson=True)
        need("format='newline_delimited'" in nd[0],
             "ndjson reads newline-delimited explicitly (no sniff)")
        need("read_json_auto" not in nd[0],
             "the fast ndjson reader does not auto-detect")
        need(any("ignore_errors=true" in r and "newline_delimited" in r
                 for r in nd),
             "a tolerant newline-delimited retry skips bad lines")
        need(any("read_json_auto" in r for r in nd),
             "a final auto-detect fallback covers a mislabelled extension")
        need(any("read_ndjson_objects" in r for r in nd),
             "typed JSON falls back to JSON-objects (VARCHAR-safe) reader")
        need(all("maximum_object_size=268435456" in r
                 for r in nd if "read_ndjson_objects" not in r),
             "every typed ndjson reader uses the bounded 256 MiB default")
        # Adaptive engines can sit at the 512 MiB floor; without a clamp the
        # default 256 MiB object size alone requests a ~512 MiB parser buffer
        # and nested JSON loads OOM before any rows are read.
        tight = E._json_readers(fwd, ndjson=True, memory_limit_mb=512)
        need(all("maximum_object_size=134217728" in r
                 for r in tight if "read_ndjson_objects" not in r),
             "object cap clamps to ~1/4 of a tight engine budget")
        eq(E._json_object_cap_bytes(512), 134217728,
           "_json_object_cap_bytes honors memory_limit_mb")
        eq(E._json_object_cap_bytes(None), 268435456,
           "no memory hint keeps the 256 MiB default")
        shallow = E._json_readers(fwd, ndjson=True, maximum_depth=2)
        need(all("maximum_depth=2" in r for r in shallow
                 if "read_ndjson_objects" not in r
                 and "read_json_objects" not in r),
             "flatten-off readers can pin maximum_depth")
        as_json = E._json_readers(fwd, ndjson=True, maximum_depth=0)
        need(all("read_ndjson_objects" in r or "read_json_objects" in r
                 for r in as_json),
             "depth 0 uses the JSON-objects readers")
        eq(E._json_shallow_depth_default(), 2,
           "default flatten-off depth is 2")
        old_depth = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH")
        try:
            os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH"] = "0"
            eq(E._json_shallow_depth_default(), 0,
               "SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH=0 selects JSON-column mode")
            os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH"] = "3"
            eq(E._json_shallow_depth_default(), 3,
               "SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH overrides shallow depth")
        finally:
            if old_depth is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH"] = old_depth
        need("_json_oom_hint" in dir(E) and callable(E._json_oom_hint),
             "OOM hint helper is exported for nested JSON failures")
        hint = E._json_oom_hint("C:/x.json", 512)
        need("out of memory" in hint.lower() and "512" in hint,
             "OOM hint mentions budget and nested JSON")
        old_cap = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_OBJECT_MB")
        try:
            os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_OBJECT_MB"] = "64"
            need(all("maximum_object_size=67108864" in r
                     for r in E._json_readers(fwd, ndjson=True)
                     if "read_ndjson_objects" not in r),
                 "SAMQL_JSON_OBJECT_MB overrides the parser ceiling")
        finally:
            if old_cap is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_JSON_OBJECT_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_OBJECT_MB"] = old_cap

        js = E._json_readers(fwd, ndjson=False)
        need("read_json_auto" in js[0] and "newline_delimited" not in js[0],
             "plain json auto-detects array/object/ndjson")
        need(any("auto_detect=true" in r and "ignore_errors=true" in r
                 for r in js),
             "plain json keeps a tolerant retry")
        need(any("read_json_objects" in r for r in js),
             "plain json falls back to objects reader on type failures")
        old_j = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB")
        try:
            os.environ.pop("SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB", None)
            eq(E._json_ondisk_min_bytes(), 64 * 1024 * 1024,
               "nested JSON prefers on-disk Parquet from 64 MiB")
            os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB"] = "0"
            eq(E._json_ondisk_min_bytes(), None,
               "SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB=0 disables the JSON floor")
        finally:
            if old_j is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB"] = old_j

    def t_duckdb_loads_ndjson():
        # End-to-end: a .ndjson file loaded with destination='duckdb' goes
        # through Session.load_file -- the same loader the drag-drop and
        # Load-files flows both call -- and lands a DuckDB table with the
        # expected columns/rows via the newline-delimited reader. Skips when
        # duckdb is absent.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "events.ndjson")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for i in range(200):
                f.write(json.dumps({"id": i, "kind": "click"}) + "\n")
        try:
            out = s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="ev")
            o = out[0]
            eq(o["engine"], "duckdb", "ndjson landed in duckdb")
            need("id" in o["columns"] and "kind" in o["columns"],
                 "ndjson columns parsed: %s" % o["columns"])
            n = s.run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM ev",
                            target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(n, 200, "all ndjson rows loaded")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_duckdb_struct_expand():
        # The decision for expanding a one-column JSON load into real columns.
        # A list-of-struct (the [{...}]-per-line NDJSON shape) is unnested
        # recursively; a bare struct is star-expanded; scalars / lists of
        # scalars / opaque JSON are left alone. Pure, so it runs without duckdb.
        from samql_core import engines as E
        eq(E._struct_expand_select("json", "STRUCT(a BIGINT, b VARCHAR)[]"),
           'UNNEST("json", recursive := true)',
           "list-of-struct is unnested recursively")
        eq(E._struct_expand_select("j", "STRUCT(x INTEGER)"), '"j".*',
           "a bare struct is star-expanded")
        eq(E._struct_expand_select("c", "struct(a int)[]"),
           'UNNEST("c", recursive := true)', "type match is case-insensitive")
        for typ in ("BIGINT[]", "VARCHAR", "JSON", "INTEGER", ""):
            eq(E._struct_expand_select("c", typ), None,
               "non-struct column left alone: %r" % typ)
        eq(E._struct_expand_select('we"ird', "STRUCT(a INT)"), '"we""ird".*',
           "the column name is quote-escaped")

    def t_duckdb_ndjson_array_wrapped():
        # End-to-end: NDJSON whose every line is a single-element array wrapping
        # an object ([{...}]) used to load as one opaque STRUCT[] column. With
        # flatten/shred ON, keys become real columns. Skips when duckdb is absent.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "wrapped.ndjson")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for i in range(120):
                f.write(json.dumps([{"id": i, "name": f"r{i}"}]) + "\n")
        try:
            out = s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="wrap",
                              flatten=False, shred=True)
            need(out and (out[0].get("table") or out[0].get("name")),
                 "array-wrapped load returned a table: %r" % out)
            # Prefer a shredded child/expanded table that exposes id+name.
            candidates = []
            for t in out:
                nm = t.get("table") or t.get("name")
                if nm:
                    candidates.append(nm)
                for child in (t.get("shredded") or []):
                    candidates.append(child)
            found = None
            cols = []
            for tbl in candidates:
                c = [x.lower() for x in (
                    getattr(s, "duckdb", None)
                    and getattr(s.duckdb, "table_columns", {}).get(tbl)
                    or [])]
                if not c:
                    try:
                        c = [x.lower() for x in s.run_query(
                            'SELECT * FROM "%s" LIMIT 0' % tbl,
                            target="__duckdb__")["columns"]]
                    except Exception:
                        c = []
                if "id" in c and "name" in c:
                    found, cols = tbl, c
                    break
            need(found and "id" in cols and "name" in cols,
                 "array-wrapped ndjson keys became columns: %s (tables=%r)"
                 % (cols, candidates))
            need(len(cols) >= 2, "expanded to multiple columns, not one struct")
            n = s.run_query('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % found,
                            target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(n, 120, "one row per wrapped object")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
            shutil.rmtree(dd, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_json_stream_to_ndjson():
        # The large-array pre-pass now reuses the shared streaming reader
        # (flatten.stream_json_records) and is cancellable. Pure stdlib (no
        # duckdb): the array detector, the NDJSON writer round-trip, and that a
        # cancel callback aborts the read promptly instead of finishing it.
        from samql_core import engines as E
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

        def write(name, text):
            p = os.path.join(dd, name)
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(text)
            return p

        need(E._file_starts_with_array(write("a.json", '  \n [ {"a":1} ]')),
             "a top-level array is detected (after whitespace)")
        need(E._file_starts_with_array(write("b.json", '\ufeff[1,2]')),
             "a BOM before the array is handled")
        for nm, t in (("o.json", '{"a":1}'), ("nd.json", '{"a":1}\n{"a":2}'),
                      ("s.json", "42"), ("e.json", "   ")):
            need(not E._file_starts_with_array(write(nm, t)),
                 "non-array first-char check: %r" % t)

        eq(E._sniff_json_format(write("sa.json", '[{"a":1},{"a":2}]')),
           "array", "array sniff")
        eq(E._sniff_json_format(write("so.json", '{"a":1}')),
           "object", "single object sniff")
        eq(E._sniff_json_format(write("snd.json", '{"a":1}\n{"a":2}\n')),
           "ndjson", "ndjson sniff (.json extension)")
        eq(E._sniff_json_format(write("sc.json", '{"a":1}{"a":2}')),
           "concat", "concatenated objects sniff")
        eq(E._sniff_json_format(write("sca.json", '[{"a":1}][{"a":2}]')),
           "concat", "concatenated arrays sniff")
        eq(E._sniff_json_format(write("x.ndjson", '{"a":1}\n{"a":2}\n')),
           "ndjson", "ndjson extension short-circuits sniff")

        arr = '[{"a":1,"s":"has ] , } in it"},{"b":[1,2,{"c":3}]},"bare",7]'
        want = json.loads(arr)
        dst = os.path.join(dd, "out.ndjson")
        n = E._write_ndjson_from_stream(write("arr.json", arr), dst)
        eq(n, len(want), "one NDJSON line per array element")
        got = [json.loads(x) for x in open(dst, encoding="utf-8") if x.strip()]
        eq(got, want, "array round-trips through the streamed NDJSON")

        # Concatenated objects also rewrite to one NDJSON line per value.
        concat = '{"a":1}{"a":2}{"a":3}'
        dstc = os.path.join(dd, "concat.ndjson")
        nc = E._write_ndjson_from_stream(write("concat.json", concat), dstc)
        eq(nc, 3, "concat objects become three NDJSON lines")
        gotc = [json.loads(x) for x in open(dstc, encoding="utf-8") if x.strip()]
        eq(gotc, [{"a": 1}, {"a": 2}, {"a": 3}], "concat round-trip")

        dst2 = os.path.join(dd, "obj.ndjson")
        eq(E._write_ndjson_from_stream(write("obj.json", '{"x":9}'), dst2), 1,
           "a single object becomes one NDJSON line")

        raised = []
        try:
            E._write_ndjson_from_stream(
                write("big.json", arr), os.path.join(dd, "c.ndjson"),
                should_cancel=lambda: True)
        except InterruptedError:
            raised.append(True)
        need(raised,
             "should_cancel() True aborts the read with InterruptedError")

        # ijson yajl yields decimal.Decimal for numbers. Rewrite must serialize
        # them (orjson default / use_float) — otherwise the first record raises
        # and flatten-off falls into a multi-GB stream-flatten stall.
        from decimal import Decimal as _Dec
        need(E._json_dumps_default(_Dec("42")) == 42,
             "Decimal integers dump as int")
        need(isinstance(E._json_dumps_default(_Dec("1.5")), float),
             "Decimal fractions dump as float")
        deep = [{"id": i, "qty": i + 0.5,
                 "nest": {"a": i, "b": {"c": [i, i + 1]}}}
                for i in range(80)]
        deep_path = write("deep_arr.json", json.dumps(deep))
        deep_dst = os.path.join(dd, "deep.ndjson")
        nd = E._write_ndjson_from_stream(deep_path, deep_dst)
        eq(nd, 80, "deep array rewrite survives ijson Decimals")
        got_d = [json.loads(x) for x in open(deep_dst, encoding="utf-8")
                 if x.strip()]
        eq(len(got_d), 80, "deep NDJSON line count")
        eq(got_d[7]["id"], 7, "deep rewrite preserves ids")

        # _json_source_for_read rewrites every non-NDJSON shape to NDJSON;
        # true NDJSON is read in place.
        try:
            mgr = E.DuckDBManager() if feats.get("duckdb") else None
            if mgr is not None:
                try:
                    for label, text, expect_cleanup in (
                        ("arr.json", '[{"id":1},{"id":2}]', True),
                        ("concat.json", '{"id":1}{"id":2}', True),
                        ("obj.json", '{"id":1,"nest":{"a":2}}', True),
                        ("lines.json", '{"id":1}\n{"id":2}\n', False),
                    ):
                        p = write(label, text)
                        rp, is_nd, cleanup = mgr._json_source_for_read(p)
                        need(is_nd, "%s reads as ndjson" % label)
                        if expect_cleanup:
                            need(cleanup, "%s is rewritten to a temp NDJSON" % label)
                            try:
                                os.unlink(cleanup)
                            except Exception:
                                pass
                        else:
                            need(cleanup is None,
                                 "%s (already NDJSON) is read in place" % label)
                finally:
                    try:
                        mgr._conn.close()
                    except Exception:
                        pass
        except Exception:
            pass

    def t_duckdb_json_all_formats_convert():
        # Matrix: every JSON shape × flatten on/off goes through NDJSON→Parquet
        # conversion. Flatten-off keeps shallow nested JSON; flatten-on shreds
        # into relational tables. Covers array, NDJSON (.json + .ndjson),
        # concatenated objects, and a single nested object.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        rows = [{"id": i, "name": "n%d" % i,
                 "nest": {"a": i, "tags": ["x", "y"]}}
                for i in range(200)]
        paths = {}
        # array
        paths["array"] = os.path.join(dd, "array.json")
        with open(paths["array"], "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump(rows, f)
        # NDJSON mislabelled as .json
        paths["ndjson_json"] = os.path.join(dd, "lines.json")
        with open(paths["ndjson_json"], "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for r in rows:
                f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
        # .ndjson extension
        paths["ndjson_ext"] = os.path.join(dd, "lines.ndjson")
        with open(paths["ndjson_ext"], "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for r in rows:
                f.write(json.dumps(r) + "\n")
        # concatenated objects (no newlines)
        paths["concat"] = os.path.join(dd, "concat.json")
        with open(paths["concat"], "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for r in rows:
                f.write(json.dumps(r))
        # single nested object with an array child
        paths["object"] = os.path.join(dd, "one.json")
        with open(paths["object"], "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump({"id": 1, "name": "root",
                       "items": [{"i": i, "s": "v%d" % i} for i in range(50)]},
                      f)

        for fmt, path in paths.items():
            for flatten in (False, True):
                s = _fresh_session()
                base = ("f" if flatten else "n") + "_" + fmt
                try:
                    out = s.load_file(path, destination="duckdb",
                                      base_name=base, flatten=flatten)
                    need(out and all(t.get("engine") == "duckdb" for t in out),
                         "%s flatten=%s landed in duckdb: %s" % (fmt, flatten, out))
                    names = {(t.get("name") or t.get("table")) for t in out}
                    if not flatten:
                        root = out[0]
                        root_name = root.get("name") or root.get("table")
                        eq(root.get("json_depth"), 2,
                           "%s flatten-off uses depth=2" % fmt)
                        # Small fixtures materialize in-engine (CTAS + expand).
                        # Parquet cache is reserved for files at/above the
                        # JSON on-disk threshold (see large-load tests).
                        need(root.get("storage") in (None, "parquet-cache",
                                                     "duckdb", "table"),
                             "%s flatten-off storage ok: %s" % (fmt, root))
                        if fmt == "object":
                            n = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % root_name,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
                            eq(n, 1, "%s flatten-off: one root row" % fmt)
                            need("items" in [c.lower() for c in root["columns"]],
                                 "%s flatten-off keeps items column: %s"
                                 % (fmt, root["columns"]))
                        else:
                            n = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % root_name,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
                            eq(n, len(rows),
                               "%s flatten-off row count" % fmt)
                            got = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT id, nest->>\'a\' FROM "%s" '
                                "WHERE id = 7" % root_name,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"]
                            eq(got, [[7, "7"]],
                               "%s flatten-off nested JSON queryable: %r"
                               % (fmt, got))
                    else:
                        # Flatten-on shreds into {base}_flattened + child tables.
                        need(all(t.get("method") == "flatten-table" for t in out),
                             "%s flatten-on uses flatten-table: %s" % (fmt, out))
                        if fmt == "object":
                            child = next(
                                (n for n in names
                                 if n and "item" in n.lower()), None)
                            need(child,
                                 "%s flatten-on created items child: %s"
                                 % (fmt, names))
                            n = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % child,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
                            eq(n, 50, "%s flatten-on child rows" % fmt)
                            hub = next(
                                (n for n in names
                                 if n == base + "_flattened"), None)
                            need(hub, "%s flatten-on hub table: %s" % (fmt, names))
                            hn = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % hub,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
                            eq(hn, 1, "%s flatten-on hub rows" % fmt)
                        else:
                            hub = next(
                                (n for n in names
                                 if n == base + "_flattened"),
                                None)
                            need(hub,
                                 "%s flatten-on hub ({base}_flattened): %s"
                                 % (fmt, names))
                            n = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % hub,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
                            eq(n, len(rows),
                               "%s flatten-on hub row count" % fmt)
                            child = next(
                                (n for n in names
                                 if n and n != hub
                                 and ("tag" in n.lower() or "nest" in n.lower())),
                                None)
                            need(child,
                                 "%s flatten-on tags child: %s" % (fmt, names))
                            cn = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % child,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
                            eq(cn, len(rows) * 2,
                               "%s flatten-on tags rows (2 per record)" % fmt)
                            got = s.run_query(
                                'SELECT id, nest_a FROM "%s" WHERE id = 7'
                                % hub,
                                target="__duckdb__")["rows"]
                            eq(got, [[7, 7]],
                               "%s flatten-on nested field shredded: %r"
                               % (fmt, got))
                finally:
                    s.shutdown()

    def t_duckdb_json_depth0_parquet_column():
        # Flatten-off with SAMQL_JSON_MAX_DEPTH=0 lands one JSON column per row
        # (the safest nested-off shape for multi-GB files). Small fixtures stay
        # in-engine CTAS; Parquet is used once size hits the on-disk threshold.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "rows.json")
        rows = [{"id": i, "nest": {"a": i}} for i in range(100)]
