        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        duck = s.get_duckdb()
        need(duck is not None, "DuckDB manager available")
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        try:
            # Streaming insert: ints in sample, blank later (the reported bug).
            name, n = duck.add_table_streaming(
                "blank_int", ["id", "qty"],
                iter([(1, 10), (2, 20), (3, ""), (4, 40), (5, "x")]),
                chunk=2)
            eq(n, 5, "every row survived blank/mixed qty: %s" % n)
            rows = s.run_query(
                'SELECT id, qty FROM "%s" ORDER BY id' % name,
                target="__duckdb__")["rows"]
            eq(len(rows), 5, "all five rows queryable")
            # Blank became NULL (or '', after varchar widen); 'x' must exist.
            need(any(r[0] == 5 for r in rows), "mixed non-numeric row kept")

            # CSV with blank numeric cells.
            csv_path = os.path.join(dd, "blank.csv")
            with open(csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("id,qty,note\n")
                for i in range(200):
                    f.write("%d,%s,n%d\n" % (i, i if i % 17 else "", i))
            out = s.load_file(csv_path, destination="duckdb",
                              base_name="blank_csv")
            need(out and out[0].get("name"), "csv load returned a table")
            cnt = s.run_query(
                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % out[0]["name"],
                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(cnt, 200, "csv blank cells did not abort the load")

            # Nested JSON array with blank numeric fields → stream/Parquet path.
            js_path = os.path.join(dd, "blank.json")
            payload = [{"id": i, "qty": (i if i % 11 else ""),
                        "meta": {"code": (i if i % 13 else "")}}
                       for i in range(500)]
            with open(js_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(payload, f)
            jout = s.load_file(js_path, destination="duckdb",
                               base_name="blank_json", flatten=False)
            need(jout and jout[0].get("name"), "json load returned a table")
            jcnt = s.run_query(
                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % jout[0]["name"],
                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(jcnt, 500, "json blank cells did not abort the load")

            # Stream-flatten path (Python insert) with blanks.
            old = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB")
            os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB"] = "0"
            try:
                # Force streamer via giant-object gate: single object + low floor.
                one = os.path.join(dd, "one_blank.json")
                blob = {"code": 1,
                        "items": [{"i": i, "n": ("" if i % 9 == 0 else i)}
                                  for i in range(800)]}
                with open(one, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    json.dump(blob, f)
                os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB"] = "1"
                fout = s.load_file(one, destination="duckdb",
                                   base_name="one_blank", flatten=True)
                need(fout, "stream-flatten load returned tables")
                need(all(t.get("engine") == "duckdb" for t in fout),
                     "streamer tables in duckdb despite blank numerics")
            finally:
                if old is None:
                    os.environ.pop("SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB", None)
                else:
                    os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB"] = old
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
            shutil.rmtree(dd, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_large_csv_json_ondisk_loads_fast():
        # Multi-MB CSV / JSON must take the on-disk Parquet path (bounded RAM)
        # and finish quickly -- no full-file type scan, no in-engine materialize.
        # Size here is large enough to cross soft on-disk floors when lowered.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        from samql_core import engines as E
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        old_od = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB")
        old_jod = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB")
        old_hard = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB")
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "1"
        os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB"] = "1"
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = "1"
        try:
            # ~2.5 MB CSV
            csv_path = os.path.join(dd, "big.csv")
            with open(csv_path, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
                f.write("id,name,score,tag\n")
                for i in range(80000):
                    f.write("%d,name_%d,%.2f,t%d\n"
                            % (i, i, i * 0.5, i % 9))
            t0 = time.time()
            cout = s.load_file(csv_path, destination="duckdb",
                               base_name="bigcsv")
            csv_s = time.time() - t0
            need(cout and cout[0].get("storage") == "parquet-cache",
                 "large csv uses parquet-cache: %r" % cout)
            ccnt = s.run_query(
                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % cout[0]["name"],
                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(ccnt, 80000, "large csv row count")
            need(csv_s < 45.0,
                 "large csv load finished quickly (%.1fs)" % csv_s)

            # ~2 MB nested JSON array (NDJSON rewrite + Parquet)
            js_path = os.path.join(dd, "big.json")
            rows = [{"id": i, "sym": "S%d" % (i % 11),
                     "qty": i, "nested": {"a": i % 5, "b": "x"}}
                    for i in range(25000)]
            with open(js_path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump(rows, f)
            t1 = time.time()
            jout = s.load_file(js_path, destination="duckdb",
                               base_name="bigjson", flatten=False)
            js_s = time.time() - t1
            need(jout and jout[0].get("storage") == "parquet-cache",
                 "large json uses parquet-cache: %r" % jout)
            jcnt = s.run_query(
                'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % jout[0]["name"],
                target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(jcnt, 25000, "large json row count")
            need(js_s < 60.0,
                 "large json load finished quickly (%.1fs)" % js_s)

            # NDJSON rewrite prefers orjson when available (speed contract).
            import inspect
            src = inspect.getsource(E._write_ndjson_from_stream)
            need("orjson" in src,
                 "NDJSON rewrite uses orjson when installed")
        finally:
            for key, old in (("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB", old_od),
                             ("SAMQL_JSON_ONDISK_MB", old_jod),
                             ("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB", old_hard)):
                if old is None:
                    os.environ.pop(key, None)
                else:
                    os.environ[key] = old
            s.shutdown()
            shutil.rmtree(dd, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_json_reader_large_records_linear():
        # Regression: the streaming readers decode by advancing an INDEX and grow
        # their reads to complete a large value, rather than re-slicing the
        # buffer and re-scanning from zero after every value. The old readers did
        # the latter, which is quadratic in record size -- a file of ~MB records
        # crawled (throughput fell from ~47 MB/s at 77 KB records to ~3 MB/s at
        # 4 MB records). Assert (a) large concatenated records read back intact
        # and in order (exercises the grow-to-complete path), and (b) the readers
        # use the index + growing read so the quadratic pattern can't silently
        # return. Pure -> runs everywhere.
        import inspect
        import tempfile
        from samql_core import flatten as F
        # ~2.5 MB per record, concatenated with no separators, so each value
        # spans well past the base read and must be completed by growing reads.
        recs = [{"i": k, "blob": ("v%d " % k) * 500000} for k in range(6)]
        p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            for r in recs:
                f.write(json.dumps(r))
        try:
            got = list(F.stream_json_records(p))
        finally:
            os.unlink(p)
        need(len(got) == len(recs),
             "all large concatenated records are read (%d of %d)"
             % (len(got), len(recs)))
        need([g.get("i") for g in got] == list(range(len(recs))),
             "large records come back in order")
        need(got[3]["blob"] == recs[3]["blob"],
             "a large record's value survives the growing-read reassembly")
        for fn in (F._iter_concat_values, F._iter_stream_records):
            src = inspect.getsource(fn)
            need("_READ_CAP" in src and "<<= 1" in src,
                 "%s grows its read to complete a large value" % fn.__name__)
            need("scan(" in src,
                 "%s decodes by index (raw_decode at a position)" % fn.__name__)

    def t_deep_flatten_sophis_shape():
        # A real Sophis instrument shape (option on an equity, from the field):
        # deeply nested single objects -- identifier, underlyer, and a 3-level
        # strike -> strikeValue -> strikePrice -- that must FLATTEN INTO the
        # parent row as underscore-joined columns, plus one array (links) that
        # must become a keyed child table. Loads N copies through the real
        # load_json into a real in-memory SQLite engine and checks the tables,
        # the flattened nested columns (including 3-level depth), the row counts,
        # and that every parent joins to exactly its child rows. Runs everywhere.
        import tempfile
        from samql_core.engines import DBManager
        from samql_core import loaders
        rec = {
            "code": 899881807,
            "identifier": {"sophis": 899881807, "optionSymbol": "OPT_CA_BIP",
                           "ticker": "BIP.UN CA 09/18/26 C50 Equity"},
            "currency": "CAD", "name": "OPT_CA_BIP.UN260918C50",
            "underlyer": {"sophis": 136424980, "bbglobalID": "BBG000VC6X81",
                          "longCompName": "Brookfield Infrastructure Partners LP",
                          "netAsset": 31335.47, "dynamicSector": "Utilities"},
            "settlementType": "PhysicalDelivery",
            "strike": {"strikeValue": {"strikePrice": {"currency": "CAD",
                                                       "amount": 50}},
                       "fixingType": "Last"},
            "links": [
                {"rel": "instrumentPosition",
                 "href": "http://echo.tdbfg.com/v1.2/echo/query/globalPositional"
                         "?instrumentCode=899881807"},
                {"rel": "insPositionInstrumentPrice",
                 "href": "http://echo.tdbfg.com/v1.2/echo/query/price"
                         "?instrumentCode=899881807"},
                {"rel": "insUnderlyingInstrumentPrice",
                 "href": "http://echo.tdbfg.com/v1.2/echo/query/price"
                         "?instrumentCode=899881807"},
                {"rel": "basketSettings",
                 "href": "http://echo.tdbfg.com/v1.2/echo/basketSettings/"
                         "899881807"}],
        }
        n = 200
        recs = []
        for i in range(n):
            r = json.loads(json.dumps(rec))
            r["code"] = 899881807 + i
            r["identifier"]["sophis"] = 899881807 + i
            recs.append(r)
        p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8").write(json.dumps(recs))  # top-level array
        db = DBManager(disk_backed=False)
        try:
            out = loaders.load_json(db, p, base_name="sophis", engine="sqlite")
        finally:
            os.unlink(p)
        tabs = {o["name"]: o for o in out}
        need(set(tabs) == {"sophis", "sophis_links"},
             "deep flatten yields root + one keyed child (links): %r"
             % list(tabs))
        eq(tabs["sophis"]["rows"], n, "one root row per instrument")
        eq(tabs["sophis_links"]["rows"], n * 4, "four link rows per instrument")
        conn = db._conn
        cols = set(r[1] for r in conn.execute('PRAGMA table_info("sophis")'))
        for c in ("identifier_sophis", "underlyer_longCompName",
                  "strike_strikeValue_strikePrice_amount", "strike_fixingType"):
            need(c in cols, "nested object flattened into column %r" % c)
        lcols = set(r[1] for r in
                    conn.execute('PRAGMA table_info("sophis_links")'))
        need({"rel", "href", "sophis_id"} <= lcols,
             "child links table has rel/href + a parent FK: %r" % lcols)
        per = conn.execute('SELECT sophis_id, COUNT(*) FROM "sophis_links" '
                           'GROUP BY sophis_id').fetchall()
        need(len(per) == n and all(c == 4 for _, c in per),
             "every parent joins to exactly its 4 links")
        amt = conn.execute('SELECT strike_strikeValue_strikePrice_amount '
                           'FROM "sophis" LIMIT 1').fetchone()[0]
        eq(amt, 50, "a 3-level-deep value (strike amount) flattened intact")

    def t_json_reader_stdlib_override_and_diag():
        # (1) SAMQL_JSON_READER=stdlib forces the stdlib raw_decode reader even
        # for a '[' file -- the lever for boxes where ijson's per-object event
        # building is the slow part. (2) the CLI tool (tools/diag_load.py) is a
        # thin wrapper over the shared samql_core.diagnostics core, so the CLI
        # and the Error log -> Diagnostics tab never drift. Pure -> everywhere.
        import tempfile
        from samql_core import flatten as F
        p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(p, "w").write('[{"a":1,"b":{"c":2}},{"a":3,"b":{"c":4}}]')
        prev = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_READER")
        try:
            os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_READER"] = "stdlib"
            recs = list(F.stream_json_records(p))
            need(len(recs) == 2 and recs[0]["a"] == 1,
                 "SAMQL_JSON_READER=stdlib still streams every record")
        finally:
            if prev is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_JSON_READER", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_READER"] = prev
            os.unlink(p)
        # the CLI delegates to the shared core (imports profile_json_load)
        root = os.path.dirname(BACKEND)
        diag_path = os.path.join(root, "tools", "diag_load.py")
        need(os.path.exists(diag_path), "tools/diag_load.py is present")
        src = open(diag_path, encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("from samql_core.diagnostics import" in src
             and "profile_json_load" in src,
             "diag_load CLI uses the shared samql_core.diagnostics core")

    def t_stream_concatenated_records():
        # The streaming reader must handle a *stream of concatenated* top-level        # values -- one or more arrays and/or bare objects back to back -- not
        # just a single array. Before the fix, a file starting with '[' had
        # everything after the first array's ']' silently dropped. Pure -> runs
        # everywhere (exercises the stdlib concat reader; the ijson path uses
        # multiple_values for the same effect).
        from samql_core import flatten as F
        import tempfile as _tf
        import os as _os

        def _count(text):
            p = _tf.mktemp(suffix=".json")
            open(p, "w").write(text)
            try:
                return list(F.stream_json_records(p))
            finally:
                _os.unlink(p)

        eq(len(_count('[{"id":1},{"id":2},{"id":3}]')), 3, "single array")
        eq(len(_count('[{"id":1},{"id":2}][{"id":3},{"id":4}]')), 4,
           "concatenated arrays yield every element (not just the first array)")
        eq(len(_count('[{"id":1}][{"id":2},{"id":3}]{"id":4}')), 4,
           "mixed concatenated arrays + trailing object")
        eq(len(_count('{"id":1}{"id":2}{"id":3}')), 3, "concatenated objects")
        eq(len(_count('{"a":1}\n{"a":2}\n')), 2, "NDJSON still works")
        eq(len(_count('{"only":1}')), 1, "single object still works")
        # Object-first stream with an EMBEDDED top-level array: the array must be
        # unwrapped element-by-element (streamed), not yielded/buffered as one
        # whole list. This is the fallback path (first char != '['); it now uses
        # the same array-aware reader so an embedded array gets bounded-memory
        # streaming and the fast index + growing-read decode too.
        obj_first = _count('{"id":1}[{"id":2},{"id":3}]{"id":4}')
        eq(len(obj_first), 4,
           "object-first stream with an embedded array yields every record")
        need(all(isinstance(r, dict) for r in obj_first),
             "an embedded top-level array is unwrapped element-by-element, "
             "not buffered/yielded as one whole list")
        # end-to-end: concatenated arrays of trades with nested legs flatten to
        # every trade and every leg, across all arrays.
        p = _tf.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(p, "w").write(
            '[{"tradeId":"A","legs":[{"n":1}]}]'
            '[{"tradeId":"B","legs":[{"n":2},{"n":3}]}]')
        fl = F.JSONFlattener(root_name="trades")
        try:
            for rec in F.stream_json_records(p):
                fl.add_record(rec)
        finally:
            _os.unlink(p)
        eq(fl.row_count("trades"), 2, "both concatenated trades flattened")
        eq(fl.row_count("trades_legs"), 3, "all legs across both trades")

    def t_flatten_json_setting():
        # The 'flatten JSON on load' setting defaults OFF (nested Parquet is
        # the fast path), toggles, and persists to the config store. Restores
        # the real config file EXACTLY afterward (removing the key if it was
        # absent) so running the suite never flips the user's default.
        s = _fresh_session()
        had = "flatten_json" in s.config.data
        orig_val = s.config.data.get("flatten_json")
        orig_attr = getattr(s, "flatten_on_load", False)
        try:
            s.config.data.pop("flatten_json", None)
            need(bool(s.config.get("flatten_json", False)) is False,
                 "flatten defaults off when the key is unset")
            # Session attribute follows the same default when re-read from config
            s.flatten_on_load = bool(s.config.get("flatten_json", False))
            need(s.flatten_json_enabled() is False,
                 "session reports flatten off by default")
            need(s.set_flatten_json(True) is True, "set returns new state")
            need(s.flatten_json_enabled() is True, "reads back on")
            need(s.config.get("flatten_json") is True, "persisted to config")
            need(s.set_flatten_json(False) is False and not s.flatten_json_enabled(),
                 "toggled back off")
        finally:
            s.flatten_on_load = orig_attr
            if had:
                s.config.set("flatten_json", orig_val)
            else:
                s.config.data.pop("flatten_json", None)
                s.config.save()

    def t_fresh_load_setting():
        # Fresh load (skip filecache) defaults OFF, toggles via
        # set_fresh_load / fresh_load_enabled, and persists. Restores the
        # user's config key exactly afterward.
        s = _fresh_session()
        had = "fresh_load" in s.config.data
        orig_val = s.config.data.get("fresh_load")
        orig_attr = getattr(s, "fresh_load", False)
        try:
            s.config.data.pop("fresh_load", None)
            s.fresh_load = bool(s.config.get("fresh_load", False))
            need(s.fresh_load_enabled() is False,
                 "fresh_load defaults off")
            need(s.set_fresh_load(True) is True, "set returns new state")
            need(s.fresh_load_enabled() is True, "reads back on")
            need(s.config.get("fresh_load") is True, "persisted to config")
            need(s.set_fresh_load(False) is False
                 and not s.fresh_load_enabled(),
                 "toggled back off")
        finally:
            s.fresh_load = orig_attr
            if had:
                s.config.set("fresh_load", orig_val)
            else:
                s.config.data.pop("fresh_load", None)
                s.config.save()

    def t_json_load_shred_only_when_toggled():
        # Relational shred runs only when shred=True / flatten-on-load is on.
        # Default flatten is off so a plain DuckDB JSON load stays one nested
        # table (the fast path for multi-GB files).
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        # Force the session default off regardless of the user's config file.
        s.flatten_on_load = False
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        try:
            p = os.path.join(dd, "nested.json")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                json.dump([{"id": i, "legs": [{"n": i}, {"n": i + 1}]}
                           for i in range(20)], f)
            out = s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="nest",
                              flatten=False, shred=False)
            names = {t.get("name") for t in out}
            eq(names, {"nest"},
               "no shred without toggle: single table %r" % names)
            need(not any(t.get("shredded") for t in out),
                 "shredded list absent when shred off")

            out2 = s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="nest2",
                               flatten=False, shred=True)
            need(any(t.get("shredded") for t in out2),
                 "shred=True produces relational child tables: %r" % out2)
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
            shutil.rmtree(dd, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_flatten_json_load_routing():
        # .423 routing: a JSON load routes by the flatten setting and
        # engine, with the strategy INVERTED from the Python-streamer
        # era:
        #   DuckDB + flatten ON  -> native nested load FIRST (fast, the
        #                           path that always works), THEN the
        #                           in-engine recursive UNNEST flatten
        #                           (session.flatten_json) replacing it.
        #   DuckDB + flatten OFF -> the single nested table, untouched.
        #   SQLite               -> always the Python flattener.
        #   A flatten failure is LOUD and the nested load STANDS.
        from samql_core import loaders as L
        import tempfile as _tf
        calls = []

        class _FD:
            table_columns = {}

        _fd = _FD()

        class _Sess:
            db = object()
            low_memory = False

            def __init__(self, flatten, flat_result="ok"):
                self.flatten_on_load = flatten
                self._flat_result = flat_result

            def get_duckdb(self):
                return _fd

            def default_destination(self):
                return "duckdb"

            def flatten_table(self, table, base=None, **kw):
                # .501 audit: the load path runs the ONE hardened engine
                calls.append(("flatten_table", table, base))
                if self._flat_result == "boom":
                    raise ValueError("bind fail")
                if self._flat_result == "none":
                    return {"ok": True, "created": [], "base": None,
                            "note": "no nested columns to flatten"}
                return {"ok": True, "base": table,
                        "created": [
                            {"name": table, "rows": 925, "kind": "base"},
                            {"name": "json", "rows": 5000, "kind": "list"},
                            {"name": table + "_flattened", "rows": 925,
                             "kind": "joinkeys"},
                        ]}

        def _fake_lj(db, path, base_name=None, **kw):
            calls.append(("load_json", "duckdb" if db is _fd else "sqlite",
                          kw.get("engine")))
            return [{"name": "t", "rows": 1, "columns": [], "engine": "x"}]

        def _fake_nested(session, path, base_name, kind, **kw):
            calls.append(("nested", kind))
            return [{"table": base_name or "nb", "rows": 1, "columns": [],
                     "engine": "duckdb"}]

        o_lj, o_n = L.load_json, L._load_into_duckdb
        L.load_json, L._load_into_duckdb = _fake_lj, _fake_nested
        p = _tf.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(p, "w").write('[{"a":1}]')
        try:
            calls.clear()
            out = L.load_file(_Sess(True), p, destination="duckdb")
            need(calls[0] == ("nested", "json")
                 and calls[1][0] == "flatten_table",
                 "flatten-on: nested load FIRST, then flatten_table "
                 "replacing it in place: %r" % calls)
            need(isinstance(out, list)
                 and any(t.get("table", "").endswith("_flattened")
                         for t in out)
                 and all("table" in t for t in out),
                 "the load result reports the flattened tree "
                 "(hub included): %r" % out)
            calls.clear()
            L.load_file(_Sess(False), p, destination="duckdb")
            need(calls[:1] == [("nested", "json")]
                 and not any(c[0] == "flatten_table" for c in calls),
                 "flatten-off: nested table only: %r" % calls)
            calls.clear()
            L.load_file(_Sess(False), p, destination="sqlite")
            need(calls[:1] == [("load_json", "sqlite", None)],
                 "SQLite always flattens regardless of the toggle: "
                 "%r" % calls)
            # a flatten FAILURE is loud and the nested load stands
            calls.clear()
            out = L.load_file(_Sess(True, "boom"), p,
                              destination="duckdb")
            need(calls[0] == ("nested", "json")
                 and isinstance(out, list)
                 and out and out[0].get("table"),
                 "flatten failure: the nested load STANDS: %r" % out)
            # nothing-to-do keeps the nested load too
            calls.clear()
            out = L.load_file(_Sess(True, "none"), p,
                              destination="duckdb")
            need(isinstance(out, list) and out
                 and out[0].get("table"),
                 "flatten nothing-to-do keeps the nested load")
        finally:
            L.load_json, L._load_into_duckdb = o_lj, o_n
            os.unlink(p)

    def t_ram_detection_one_source():
        # RAM detection is now one function; the DuckDB memory cap (GiB) and the
        # session's low-memory heuristic (bytes) both delegate to it, so they
        # can't disagree. Pure -> runs anywhere, and on any real machine it
        # returns a positive byte count.
        from samql_core import engines as E
        from samql_core import Session
        b = E.total_physical_ram_bytes()
        need(isinstance(b, int) and b > 0, "detects some RAM: %r" % b)
        need(abs(E.DuckDBManager._total_ram_gb() - b / (1024 ** 3)) < 1e-6,
             "DuckDB GiB cap reads the same source")
        eq(Session._system_total_bytes(), b,
           "session low-memory heuristic reads the same source")

    def t_ondisk_threshold():
        # The size threshold that routes a load to an on-disk Parquet cache
        # (view) instead of an in-memory table. Pure -> runs everywhere.
        from samql_core import engines as E
        from samql_core import load_thresholds as LT
        old = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB")
        old_h = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB")
        LT.clear_overrides()
        try:
            os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB", None)
            eq(E._ondisk_min_bytes(), 512 * 1024 * 1024, "default is 512 MB")
            os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "128"
            eq(E._ondisk_min_bytes(), 128 * 1024 * 1024, "override honored")
            os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "0"
            need(E._ondisk_min_bytes() is None,
                 "0 disables soft threshold")
            os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "junk"
            eq(E._ondisk_min_bytes(), 512 * 1024 * 1024, "bad value -> default")
            os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB", None)
            eq(E._ondisk_hard_floor_bytes(), 256 * 1024 * 1024,
               "hard floor default 256 MB")
            os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = "0"
            need(E._ondisk_hard_floor_bytes() is None,
                 "hard floor can be disabled for tests")
            # UI overrides beat env
            LT.apply_overrides({"ondisk_mb": 64})
            eq(E._ondisk_min_bytes(), 64 * 1024 * 1024,
               "UI override wins over env")
        finally:
            LT.clear_overrides()
            if old is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = old
            if old_h is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = old_h

    def t_load_thresholds_configure():
        # Session configure_load_thresholds persists and applies live.
        from samql_core import load_thresholds as LT
        from samql_core import engines as E
        LT.clear_overrides()
        s = _fresh_session()
        prev = dict(s.config.get("load_thresholds") or {})
        try:
            info = s.configure_load_thresholds(
                updates={"ondisk_mb": 100, "upload_mb": 2048})
            need(info.get("ok"), "info ok")
            eq(info["thresholds"]["ondisk_mb"]["value"], 100,
               "ondisk applied")
            eq(info["thresholds"]["ondisk_mb"]["source"], "override",
               "marked as override")
            eq(E._ondisk_min_bytes(), 100 * 1024 * 1024,
               "engines see live override")
            snap = s.config.get("load_thresholds") or {}
            eq(snap.get("ondisk_mb"), 100, "persisted in config")
            s.configure_load_thresholds(reset=True)
            need(E._ondisk_min_bytes() == 512 * 1024 * 1024
                 or isinstance(E._ondisk_min_bytes(), (int, type(None))),
                 "reset restores env/default path")
            need(not (s.config.get("load_thresholds") or {}),
                 "config key cleared on reset")
        finally:
            try:
                if prev:
                    s.configure_load_thresholds(updates=prev)
                else:
                    s.configure_load_thresholds(reset=True)
            except Exception:
                LT.clear_overrides()
            s.shutdown()

    def t_load_preflight():
        # Advise before large loads: missing file, Excel guidance, DuckDB gate.
        s = _fresh_session()
        td = tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="samql_preflight_")
        try:
            miss = s.load_preflight("")
            need(not miss.get("ok") and miss.get("blockers"),
                 "empty path is a blocker")
            miss2 = s.load_preflight(os.path.join(td, "no-such-file-xyz.csv"))
            need(not miss2.get("ok")
                 and any("not found" in b.lower()
                         for b in (miss2.get("blockers") or [])),
                 "missing file blocks: %r" % miss2)
            xlsx = os.path.join(td, "preflight_tiny.xlsx")
            # Touch a fake workbook path (size/ext only — no real Excel bytes).
            with open(xlsx, "wb") as f:
                f.write(b"PK" + b"\0" * 200)
            xl = s.load_preflight(xlsx)
            need(xl.get("exists") and xl.get("ok"),
                 "tiny fake workbook is not a hard block")
            need(any("Excel" in w for w in (xl.get("warnings") or [])),
                 "Excel guidance warning present: %r" % xl)
            # Large CSV without DuckDB -> blocker. Force HAS_DUCKDB off.
            from samql_core import engines as E
            big = os.path.join(td, "preflight_big.csv")
            with open(big, "wb") as f:
                f.write(b"a,b\n" + b"1,2\n" * (70 * 1024))  # ~few hundred KB
            # Inflate reported size via patched getsize for the gate.
            real_getsize = os.path.getsize
            try:
                os.path.getsize = lambda p: (
                    600 * 1024 * 1024 if os.path.abspath(p) == os.path.abspath(big)
                    else real_getsize(p))
                old = E.HAS_DUCKDB
                E.HAS_DUCKDB = False
                try:
                    blocked = s.load_preflight(big)
                    need(not blocked.get("ok"),
                         "large CSV without DuckDB blocks")
                    need(any("DuckDB" in b
                             for b in (blocked.get("blockers") or [])),
                         "DuckDB required message: %r" % blocked)
                finally:
                    E.HAS_DUCKDB = old
            finally:
                os.path.getsize = real_getsize
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
            shutil.rmtree(td, ignore_errors=True)

    def t_copy_parquet_midflight_abort():
        # Mid-flight COPY monitor: byte ceiling and cancel interrupt early.
        from samql_core import engines as E
        import tempfile
        import time

        dest = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".parquet")
        fwd = dest.replace("\\", "/")

        class _Cur:
            def __init__(self):
                self.interrupted = False
                self.calls = 0

            def execute(self, sql):
                self.calls += 1
                # Simulate a long COPY that grows the dest file.
                with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(b"x" * (256 * 1024))
                t0 = time.time()
                while time.time() - t0 < 6.0:
                    if self.interrupted:
                        raise RuntimeError("INTERRUPT")
                    try:
                        with open(dest, "ab") as f:
                            f.write(b"y" * (512 * 1024))
                    except OSError:
                        pass
                    time.sleep(0.2)
                raise RuntimeError("COPY finished without interrupt")

            def interrupt(self):
                self.interrupted = True

        try:
            c = _Cur()
            try:
                E.exec_copy_parquet(
                    c, "SELECT 1", fwd, max_bytes=1024 * 1024)
                need(False, "byte ceiling must abort COPY")
            except RuntimeError as e:
                msg = str(e).lower()
                need("ceiling" in msg or "exceeded" in msg or "gib" in msg,
                     "ceiling error surfaces: %r" % e)
            need(c.interrupted, "interrupt was called")

            c2 = _Cur()
            try:
                E.exec_copy_parquet(
                    c2, "SELECT 1", fwd,
                    should_cancel=lambda: True)
                need(False, "cancel must abort COPY")
            except RuntimeError as e:
                need("cancel" in str(e).lower(),
                     "cancel error surfaces: %r" % e)
        finally:
            try:
                os.unlink(dest)
            except OSError:
                pass

    def t_ondisk_parquet_fail_no_ctas_fallthrough():
        # Large JSON: Parquet-route failure must NOT fall through to in-engine
        # CREATE TABLE AS (OOM risk). It raises a recoverable error so the
        # JSON loader can stream-flatten instead.
        from samql_core import loaders as L

        class _FakeDuck:
            def __init__(self):
                self.table_columns = {}
                self.ctas = 0

            def load_file_to_parquet_view(self, *a, **k):
                raise RuntimeError("simulated parquet COPY failure")

            def create_view_from_file(self, *a, **k):
                raise RuntimeError("simulated view failure")

            def create_table_from_file(self, *a, **k):
                self.ctas += 1
                raise AssertionError("CTAS must not run for large JSON")

            def apply_resource_memory_mb(self, *_a, **_k):
                return False

            def execute(self, _sql):
                return (None, [[0]])

        class _Sess:
            def get_duckdb(self):
                return duck

        duck = _FakeDuck()
        try:
            L._load_into_duckdb(_Sess(), "/tmp/big.json", "big", "json",
                                force_ondisk=True)
            need(False, "expected RuntimeError (no CTAS for large JSON)")
        except RuntimeError as e:
            need("Streaming flatten will be tried" in str(e)
                 or "On-disk Parquet load failed" in str(e),
                 "error signals stream recovery: %s" % e)
            need("simulated parquet" in str(e).lower()
                 or "COPY failure" in str(e),
                 "original failure preserved: %s" % e)
        eq(duck.ctas, 0, "create_table_from_file must not be called")

    def t_json_parquet_fail_stream_flatten_fallback():
        # Flatten-on: any Parquet conversion failure (not only OOM) must
        # stream-flatten so the load succeeds instead of hard-failing.
        from samql_core import loaders as L

        calls = {"stream": 0}

        def _fake_stream(*_a, **_k):
            calls["stream"] += 1
            return [{"name": "t", "rows": 1, "columns": ["a"],
                     "engine": "duckdb", "method": "stream-flatten"}]

        def _fake_native(*_a, **_k):
            raise RuntimeError(
                "On-disk Parquet load failed for large JSON x "
                "(simulated). Streaming flatten will be tried next.")

        o_sf, o_n = L._stream_flatten_into_duckdb, L._load_into_duckdb
        L._stream_flatten_into_duckdb = _fake_stream
        L._load_into_duckdb = _fake_native
        old_mb = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB")
        # Keep giant-object short-circuit off so we exercise the Parquet path.
        os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB"] = "0"
        try:
            class _Sess:
                def get_duckdb(self):
                    raise AssertionError("should not open duckdb here")

            dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
            p = os.path.join(dd, "arr.json")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write('[{"a":1},{"a":2}]')
            out = L._load_json_duckdb(_Sess(), p, "arr", flatten=True)
            eq(calls["stream"], 1, "stream flatten invoked once")
            eq(out[0]["method"], "stream-flatten", "stream result returned")
        finally:
            L._stream_flatten_into_duckdb = o_sf
            L._load_into_duckdb = o_n
            if old_mb is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_FLATTEN_MB"] = old_mb

    def t_large_csv_sqlite_upgrades_to_duckdb():
        # Multi-hundred-MiB CSV with destination=sqlite must auto-upgrade to
        # DuckDB on-disk Parquet when DuckDB is available (never fail the load).
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        from samql_core import loaders as L
        old = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB")
        old_h = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB")
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "wide.csv")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("a,b\n")
            for i in range(500):
                f.write("%d,%d\n" % (i, i * 2))
        # Pretend the file is huge via a tiny soft threshold.
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "0.000001"  # ~1 byte
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = "0"    # don't also trip floor
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            out = L.load_file(s, p, destination="sqlite", base_name="wide")
            eq(out[0].get("engine"), "duckdb",
               "large CSV upgraded off SQLite: %s" % out)
            eq(out[0].get("storage"), "parquet-cache",
               "lands as on-disk Parquet: %s" % out)
            n = s.run_query('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % out[0]["name"],
                            target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(n, 500, "every row queryable after upgrade")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
            if old is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = old
            if old_h is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = old_h

    def t_large_csv_sqlite_fail_without_duckdb():
        # Without DuckDB, a large CSV→SQLite still fails loud (no silent thrash).
        from samql_core import loaders as L
        from samql_core import engines as E
        old = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB")
        old_h = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB")
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "wide.csv")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("a,b\n1,2\n")
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "0.000001"
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = "0"
        prev = E.HAS_DUCKDB
        E.HAS_DUCKDB = False
        try:
            class _Sess:
                db = object()

                def default_destination(self):
                    return "sqlite"

                def get_duckdb(self):
                    raise AssertionError("must not open DuckDB")

            try:
                L.load_file(_Sess(), p, destination="sqlite", base_name="sq")
                need(False, "expected RuntimeError without DuckDB")
            except RuntimeError as e:
                need("too large for SQLite" in str(e),
                     "fail-loud message: %s" % e)
                need("duckdb" in str(e).lower(),
                     "mentions install duckdb: %s" % e)
        finally:
            E.HAS_DUCKDB = prev
            if old is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = old
            if old_h is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = old_h

    def t_duckdb_large_csv_parquet_view():
        # Large CSV loads as a Parquet cache (not in-memory CTAS), queryable.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "big.csv")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8", newline="") as f:
            f.write("id,sym,qty\n")
            for i in range(20000):
                f.write("%d,X%d,%d\n" % (i, i % 7, i * 3))
        old = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB")
        old_h = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB")
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "0.1"  # ~100 KB -> force on-disk
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB"] = "0"
        try:
            out = s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="bigcsv")
            eq(out[0].get("storage"), "parquet-cache",
               "large CSV stored as Parquet cache: %s" % out)
            n = s.run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM bigcsv",
                            target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(n, 20000, "every CSV row queryable through Parquet view")
            src = s.duckdb.table_sources.get(out[0]["name"], "")
            need(str(src).lower().endswith(".parquet"),
                 "backed by Parquet file, not in-memory: %s" % src)
        finally:
            for k, v in (("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB", old),
                         ("SAMQL_ONDISK_HARD_MB", old_h)):
                if v is None:
                    os.environ.pop(k, None)
                else:
                    os.environ[k] = v
            s.shutdown()

    def t_csv_parquet_fail_promotes_via_ctas():
        # When direct COPY→Parquet fails for CSV, CTAS then promote-to-Parquet
        # so the load still ends as an efficient cache (never a hard fail).
        from samql_core import loaders as L

        class _FakeDuck:
            def __init__(self):
                self.table_columns = {"t": ["a", "b"]}
                self.promoted = False
                self.ctas = 0

            def load_file_to_parquet_view(self, *a, **k):
                raise RuntimeError("simulated csv parquet COPY failure")

            def create_table_from_file(self, name, *a, **k):
                self.ctas += 1
                self.table_columns[name] = ["a", "b"]
                return name

            def view_to_parquet(self, table_name, cache, cancel=None):
                with open(cache, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(b"PAR1")  # stub bytes; view path mocked below
                self.promoted = True

            def drop_table(self, _name):
                pass

            def create_view_from_file(self, name, path, kind, delimiter=None):
                self.table_columns[name] = ["a", "b"]
                return name

            def apply_resource_memory_mb(self, *_a, **_k):
                return False

            def execute(self, _sql):
                return (None, [[2]])

        class _Sess:
            def get_duckdb(self):
                return duck

        duck = _FakeDuck()
        out = L._load_into_duckdb(_Sess(), "/tmp/big.csv", "big", "csv",
                                  force_ondisk=True)
        eq(duck.ctas, 1, "CTAS ran as Parquet recovery")
        need(duck.promoted, "table promoted to Parquet")
        eq(out[0].get("storage"), "parquet-cache",
           "final storage is parquet-cache: %s" % out)

    def t_duckdb_large_load_parquet_view():
        # End-to-end: a load at/above the on-disk threshold lands as a Parquet
        # cache exposed as a query-in-place view (bounded memory), not an
        # in-memory table -- and it's queryable with the right rows/columns.
        # Threshold dropped so a small fixture exercises it. Skips without duckdb.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        # The Parquet cache view is the NESTED large-file route; with flattening
        # on (the default) a JSON load normalizes instead, so take the nested
        # path here. Set the attribute DIRECTLY (not set_flatten_json, which
        # would persist to the real config and flip the user's default off).
        s.flatten_on_load = False
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "trades.json")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump([{"id": i, "sym": "X%d" % (i % 5)}
                       for i in range(30000)], f)      # ~0.6 MB single array
        old = os.environ.get("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB")
        old_j = os.environ.get("SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_MB")
        os.environ["SAMQL_ONDISK_MB"] = "0.1"          # ~100 KB -> force on-disk
        os.environ["SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_MB"] = "0.1"
        try:
            out = s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="trades")
            eq(out[0].get("storage"), "parquet-cache",
               "a large load is stored as a Parquet cache view")
            cols = [c.lower() for c in out[0]["columns"]]
            need("id" in cols and "sym" in cols,
                 "the array keys became columns: %s" % cols)
            n = s.run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM trades",
                            target="__duckdb__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(n, 30000, "every row is queryable through the Parquet view")
            # the source points at a .parquet cache, confirming it's not in-memory
            src = s.duckdb.table_sources.get(out[0]["name"], "")
            need(str(src).lower().endswith(".parquet"),
                 "the table is backed by a Parquet file, not an in-memory copy")
        finally:
            for k, v in (("SAMQL_ONDISK_MB", old),
                         ("SAMQL_JSON_STREAM_MB", old_j)):
                if v is None:
                    os.environ.pop(k, None)
                else:
                    os.environ[k] = v
            s.shutdown()

    def t_flatten_no_source_dumps():
        # Flatten a DuckDB table that has NO file on disk (e.g. loaded from
        # the API connector, whose spooled temp file was deleted): flatten_json
        # must dump the table to JSON and flatten that instead of erroring
        # "No source file on disk". We inject a fake DuckDB whose COPY (...) TO
        # writes NDJSON, so the dump+flatten path runs without a real DuckDB.
        import re as _re
        import threading as _th
        s = _fresh_session()

        class _FakeConn:
            def execute(self, sql):
                # emulate DuckDB: COPY (...) TO 'path' (FORMAT JSON) -> NDJSON
                m = _re.search(r"TO '([^']+)'", sql)
                if not m:
                    raise RuntimeError("fake COPY: no path in " + sql)
                with open(m.group(1), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    for i in range(4):
                        f.write(json.dumps(
                            {"id": i, "name": f"r{i}",
                             "tags": [{"t": "x"}, {"t": "y"}]}) + "\n")
                return self

        class _FakeDuck:
            def native_op_cursor(self):
                import contextlib as _cl

                @_cl.contextmanager
                def _inner():
                    yield self.conn, self.write_lock
                return _inner()

            def __init__(self):
                self.table_sources = {}          # no source -> triggers dump
                self.table_columns = {}
                self.write_lock = _th.RLock()
                self.conn = _FakeConn()
                self._rows = {}                  # tables the flatten writes here

            # the flatten now lands the relational tables back in DuckDB (this
            # engine), so a fake add_table_streaming records what it receives.
            def add_table_streaming(self, raw_name, columns, row_iter,
                                    source="", chunk=50000):
                rows = list(row_iter)
                name, k = raw_name, 2
                while name in self.table_columns:
                    name = "%s_%d" % (raw_name, k)
                    k += 1
                self.table_columns[name] = list(columns)
                self._rows[name] = rows
                return name, len(rows)

            # tables_tree() asks the engine for column types when it lists the
            # newly-created DuckDB tables; return a dict so it doesn't choke.
            def column_types(self, name):
                return {c: "" for c in self.table_columns.get(name, [])}

            # no-op the lifecycle/catalog calls the session makes
            # (sync_catalog, recycle, drop_all, close, checkpoint, ...)
            def __getattr__(self, _name):
                return lambda *a, **k: None

        try:
            # sanity: a non-duckdb engine with no file still reports clearly
            r0 = s.flatten_json("api_data", engine="sqlite")
            need("error" in r0 and "No source file" in r0["error"],
                 "sqlite/no-file flatten should still report no source file")
            # the duckdb dump path -> the flattened tables now land in
            # DuckDB (this engine), NOT SQLite.
            s.duckdb = _FakeDuck()
            res = s.flatten_json("api_data", engine="duckdb")
            need(res.get("ok"),
                 "flatten from dump failed: " + str(res.get("error")))
            tables = res.get("tables") or []
            names = {t["name"] for t in tables}
            need("api_data" in names, "root table missing from dump-flatten")
            child = next((t for t in tables
                          if t["name"].startswith("api_data_tags")), None)
            need(child is not None,
                 "nested child table missing from dump-flatten")
            eq(child["rows"], 8, "flattened child rows (4 rows x 2 tags)")
            need(all(t.get("engine") == "duckdb" for t in tables),
                 "a DuckDB table's flatten must land in DuckDB, not SQLite")
            need(s.duckdb._rows.get(child["name"]) is not None,
                 "the flattened child rows were written to the DuckDB engine")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_flatten_source_predicate():
        # _source_is_json_file gates ONLY the read-the-file-directly shortcut:
        # true for a JSON/NDJSON file on disk, false for anything else -- so a
        # DuckDB table with a non-JSON source still routes to the dump path
        # rather than being rejected. Pure -> runs everywhere.
        from samql_core.session import _source_is_json_file
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        j = os.path.join(dd, "a.json")
        open(j, "w").write("[]")
        nd = os.path.join(dd, "a.ndjson")
        open(nd, "w").write("{}\n")
        t = os.path.join(dd, "a.txt")
        open(t, "w").write("x")
        need(_source_is_json_file(j), "a .json file reads directly")
        need(_source_is_json_file(nd), "a .ndjson file reads directly")
        need(not _source_is_json_file(t), ".txt is not read directly (dump)")
        need(not _source_is_json_file(os.path.join(dd, "nope.json")),
             "a missing file is not read directly")
        need(not _source_is_json_file(None), "no source -> dump path")
        need(not _source_is_json_file(""), "empty source -> dump path")

    def t_flatten_duckdb_nonjson_source_dumps():
        # A DuckDB table whose SOURCE FILE is not JSON (its JSON arrived as a
        # .txt bundle, or it's backed by a Parquet cache from a large load) must
        # still flatten -- by dumping the table to JSON -- instead of erroring
        # "not a JSON-backed table". Uses the same FakeDuck dump path, so it
        # runs without a real DuckDB.
        import re as _re
        import threading as _th
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        src = os.path.join(dd, "sophis_derivs.txt")     # non-JSON extension
        with open(src, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("(placeholder; flatten must dump the table, not read this)\n")

        class _FakeConn:
            def execute(self, sql):
                m = _re.search(r"TO '([^']+)'", sql)
                if not m:
                    raise RuntimeError("fake COPY: no path in " + sql)
                with open(m.group(1), "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    for i in range(3):
                        f.write(json.dumps(
                            {"id": i, "legs": [{"k": "a"}, {"k": "b"}]}) + "\n")
                return self

        class _FakeDuck:
            def native_op_cursor(self):
                import contextlib as _cl

                @_cl.contextmanager
                def _inner():
                    yield self.conn, self.write_lock
                return _inner()

            def __init__(self):
                self.table_sources = {"derivs": src}    # non-JSON file on disk
                self.table_columns = {}                 # empty: no name collision
                self.write_lock = _th.RLock()
                self.conn = _FakeConn()
                self._rows = {}

            def add_table_streaming(self, raw_name, columns, row_iter,
                                    source="", chunk=50000):
                rows = list(row_iter)
                name, k = raw_name, 2
                while name in self.table_columns:
                    name = "%s_%d" % (raw_name, k)
                    k += 1
                self.table_columns[name] = list(columns)
                self._rows[name] = rows
                return name, len(rows)

            def column_types(self, name):
                return {c: "" for c in self.table_columns.get(name, [])}

            def __getattr__(self, _name):
                return lambda *a, **k: None

        try:
            s.duckdb = _FakeDuck()
            res = s.flatten_json("derivs", engine="duckdb")
            need(res.get("ok"),
                 "non-JSON-source flatten should dump+flatten, got: "
                 + str(res.get("error")))
            names = {t["name"] for t in (res.get("tables") or [])}
            need("derivs" in names, "root table present after dump-flatten")
            need(any(n.startswith("derivs_legs") for n in names),
                 "nested child table produced from the dumped JSON")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_load_view_mode():
        # "Query the file in place" load mode: a DuckDB view over read_*,
        # not a materialized copy. Two live checks (the DuckDB view SQL itself
        # needs a real DuckDB, so that part is asserted structurally):
        #   A) with no DuckDB available, view mode safely FALLS BACK to a
        #      normal materialized load (so it never hard-fails);
        #   B) with DuckDB present (faked here), it routes to a view and
        #      returns a view descriptor instead of copying.
        import samql_core.loaders as L
        import threading as _th
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        csv = os.path.join(dd, "rows.csv")
        with open(csv, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write("id,name\n1,a\n2,b\n3,c\n")
        try:
            # A) no DuckDB -> fall back to materialize. Force DuckDB "off" for
            #    this case so the check is hermetic: on a host that actually
            #    has DuckDB installed, get_duckdb() lazily builds a real engine
            #    and view mode would (correctly) return a view, not a fallback.
            _orig_gd = s.get_duckdb
            s.get_duckdb = lambda: None
            try:
                out = L.load_file(s, csv, destination="sqlite",
                                  base_name="fallback", mode="view")
                need(out and not out[0].get("view"),
                     "view mode without DuckDB should fall back to materialize")
                n = s.run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM fallback",
                                target="__local__")["rows"][0][0]
                eq(n, 3, "fallback materialized rows")
            finally:
                s.get_duckdb = _orig_gd

            # B) DuckDB present (faked) -> a view, not a copy
            class _FakeDuck:
                def __init__(self):
                    self.table_columns = {}
                    self.table_sources = {}
                    self.write_lock = _th.RLock()

                def create_view_from_file(self, name, path, kind,
                                          delimiter=None):
                    self.view_call = (name, kind)
                    self.table_columns[name] = ["id", "name"]
                    self.table_sources[name] = path
                    return name

                def __getattr__(self, _n):
                    return lambda *a, **k: None

            s.duckdb = _FakeDuck()
            out2 = L.load_file(s, csv, destination="auto",
                               base_name="inplace", mode="view")
            need(out2 and out2[0].get("view") is True,
                 "view mode with DuckDB should return a view descriptor")
            eq(out2[0]["engine"], "duckdb", "view lives in DuckDB")
            eq(out2[0]["rows"], None, "a view has no eager row count")
            eq(s.duckdb.view_call, ("inplace", "csv"), "view kind = csv")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_parquet_materializes_by_default():
        # A .parquet load now reads the file once into a real DuckDB table
        # (fast repeated queries / node re-runs) instead of a zero-copy view
        # that re-parses on every query. Query-in-place is still available via
        # mode="view" (the escape hatch for files too big to copy). DuckDB is
        # faked here so the routing is checked without a real engine.
        import samql_core.loaders as L
        import threading as _th

        class _FakeDuck:
            def __init__(self):
                self.table_columns = {}
                self.table_sources = {}
                self.write_lock = _th.RLock()
                self.table_call = None
                self.view_call = None

            def create_table_from_file(self, name, path, kind, delimiter=None,
                                       **_kw):
                self.table_call = (name, kind)
                self.table_columns[name] = ["a", "b"]
                self.table_sources[name] = path
                return name

            def create_view_from_file(self, name, path, kind, delimiter=None,
                                      **_kw):
                self.view_call = (name, kind)
                self.table_columns[name] = ["a", "b"]
                self.table_sources[name] = path
                return name

            def execute(self, _sql):
                return (None, [[0]])

            def __getattr__(self, _n):
                return lambda *a, **k: None

        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            # default load -> materialized table, NOT a view
            s.duckdb = _FakeDuck()
            out = L.load_file(s, "/tmp/data.parquet", destination="auto",
                              base_name="pq_mat", mode="materialize")
            need(out and not out[0].get("view"),
                 "default parquet load should materialize, not view")
            eq(out[0]["engine"], "duckdb", "materialized parquet lives in DuckDB")
            eq(s.duckdb.table_call, ("pq_mat", "parquet"),
               "parquet routed to create_table_from_file")
            need(s.duckdb.view_call is None,
                 "default parquet load must not create a view")
            # explicit query-in-place -> a view (escape hatch for huge files)
            s.duckdb = _FakeDuck()
            out2 = L.load_file(s, "/tmp/data.parquet", destination="auto",
                               base_name="pq_view", mode="view")
            need(out2 and out2[0].get("view") is True,
                 "mode=view should still create a parquet view")
            eq(s.duckdb.view_call, ("pq_view", "parquet"),
               "view mode routed to create_view_from_file")
            need(s.duckdb.table_call is None,
                 "view mode must not materialize")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_container_backend():
        # Backend pieces for the container iterator: (a) the iterator's new
        # "out" port reads from its accumulator table by name so downstream
        # nodes can build on it; (b) the driver row -> ${var} binding honors the
        # column->name rename. Both are pure (no engine needed).
        from samql_core import nodeflow as NF
        from samql_core.session import _rename_row_vars
        gi = lambda _p: None
        co = lambda _t: []
        # (a) out compiles to a read of the (sanitized) accumulator table
        sql = NF.node_output_sql(
            {"type": "iterator", "id": "it", "config": {"table": "my acc!"}},
            "out", gi, co, None)
        need('SELECT * FROM "my_acc" AS _iter' in sql,
             "iterator out should read its accumulator table")
        raised = False
        try:
            NF.node_output_sql({"type": "iterator", "id": "it2",
                                "config": {}}, "out", gi, co, None)
        except NF.NodeflowError:
            raised = True
        need(raised, "iterator out without an accumulator name should raise")
        # (b) rename: renamed col -> new var name (original dropped); others kept
        r = _rename_row_vars({"date": "2026-01", "amt": 5, "n": None},
                             {"date": "as_of"})
        eq(r.get("as_of"), "2026-01", "renamed driver column becomes the var")
        need("date" not in r, "original column name dropped once renamed")
        eq(r.get("amt"), "5", "unrenamed column keeps its name (stringified)")
        eq(r.get("n"), "", "None binds as empty string")

    def t_opreg_progress_percent():
        # The op registry computes a true completion percentage when a total is
        # known, and reports None (indeterminate) when it is not.
        from samql_core import progress as opreg
        opreg.reset_for_tests()
        try:
            opreg.begin("query", op_id="p1")
            opreg.advance(3, 12, unit="pass", op_id="p1")
            snap = [o for o in opreg.snapshot() if o["id"] == "p1"][0]
            eq(snap["percent"], 25.0, "3/12 -> 25%")
            eq(snap["unit"], "pass", "unit is recorded")
            eq(snap["done"], 3, "done recorded")
            eq(snap["total"], 12, "total recorded")
            opreg.advance(12, 12, op_id="p1")
            snap = [o for o in opreg.snapshot() if o["id"] == "p1"][0]
            eq(snap["percent"], 100.0, "12/12 -> 100%")
            opreg.begin("query", op_id="p2")
            snap = [o for o in opreg.snapshot() if o["id"] == "p2"][0]
            need(snap["percent"] is None,
                 "no total -> percent None (indeterminate bar)")
            opreg.advance(99, 10, op_id="p2")
            snap = [o for o in opreg.snapshot() if o["id"] == "p2"][0]
            eq(snap["percent"], 100.0, "over-100 clamps to 100")
        finally:
            opreg.reset_for_tests()

    def t_iterator_reports_progress():
        # End to end: a 2-pass container iterator must report determinate
        # progress (pass idx of the known pass count) to the op registry, keyed
        # by its query id, so the Run bar shows a true percentage.
        from samql_core import progress as opreg
        calls = []
        orig = opreg.advance

        def spy(done=None, total=None, unit=None, op_id=None):
            calls.append((done, total, unit, op_id))
            return orig(done=done, total=total, unit=unit, op_id=op_id)

        opreg.advance = spy
        s = Session()
        try:
            vals = {"id": "v", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "v", "columns": ["col1"],
                "rows": [["a"], ["b"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            body = {"id": "b", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "b", "columns": ["x"],
                "rows": [["z"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            it = {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                "table": "res", "accumulate": "append", "reset_first": False,
                "children": [{"id": "fx", "type": "formula", "config": {
                    "label": "formula",
                    "formulas": [{"name": "x2", "expr": "{{col1}}"}]}}]}}
            g = {"nodes": [vals, body, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it", query_id="QID")
            need(not r.get("error"),
                 "iterator ran: %s" % (r.get("error") or r.get("errors")))
            mine = [c for c in calls if c[3] == "QID"]
            need(mine, "iterator reported progress for its query id")
            dones = sorted(set(c[0] for c in mine))
            need(1 in dones and 2 in dones,
                 "reported pass 1 and pass 2: %r" % dones)
            need(all(c[1] == 2 for c in mine),
                 "total is the 2-row pass count: %r" % mine)
            need(all(c[2] == "pass" for c in mine), "unit is 'pass'")
        finally:
            opreg.advance = orig
            s.shutdown()

    def t_run_loops_report_progress_wiring():
        # Guard the determinate-progress reporting in all three loop bodies
        # (cheaper than building a converging while graph): each reports
        # done/total to opreg so the Run bar can show a real percentage.
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(re.search(r'opreg\.advance\(idx, len\(var_rows\), unit="pass"',
                       src),
             "container iterator must report opreg.advance(idx, len(var_rows))")
        need(re.search(r'opreg\.advance\(idx, len\(values\), unit="pass"', src),
             "classic iterator must report opreg.advance(idx, len(values))")
        need(re.search(r'opreg\.advance\(i, max_iters, unit="iteration"', src),
             "while loop must report opreg.advance(i, max_iters)")

    def t_retry_loops_unified():
        import samql_core.apiload as A
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "apiload.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        eq(len(re.findall(r"for attempt in range\(", src)), 1,
           "exactly one retry loop should remain (was two)")
        need("_retry_call(" in src, "_retry_call must exist")
        # both tuple shapes give up with an error set after a stuck status
        seen = []
        fr = A._fetch_with_retries(lambda: (503, "j", None, "b", None),
                                   {"retries": 1},
                                   sleep=lambda s: seen.append(s))
        eq(fr[0], 503, "fetch give-up keeps status")
        need(fr[4] and "gave up" in fr[4], "fetch give-up sets error field")
        eq(len(seen), 1, "one backoff sleep between two attempts")
        sr = A._spool_with_retries(lambda: (502, "c", None, 7),
                                   {"retries": 1}, sleep=lambda s: None)
        eq(sr[0], 502, "spool give-up keeps status")
        need(sr[2] and "gave up" in sr[2], "spool give-up sets error msg")
        eq(sr[3], 7, "spool give-up keeps nbytes")
        fr2 = A._fetch_with_retries(lambda: (200, "j", {"x": 1}, "", None),
                                    {"retries": 3}, sleep=lambda s: None)
        eq(fr2[2], {"x": 1}, "non-transient success returns data untouched")

    def t_col_names_shared():
        from samql_core.session import Session

        class _Eng:
            def __init__(self):
                self.q = []

            def execute(self, sql):
                self.q.append(sql)
                return (["a", "b"], [])

        sess = Session.__new__(Session)  # _col_names uses only the engine
        e = _Eng()
        eq(sess._col_names(e, table="my tbl"), ["a", "b"], "table columns")
        need('FROM "my tbl" LIMIT 0' in e.q[-1], "table probe query shape")
        eq(sess._col_names(e, sql="SELECT 1"), ["a", "b"], "subquery columns")
        need("(SELECT 1) AS _z LIMIT 0" in e.q[-1], "subquery probe shape")

        class _Empty:
            def execute(self, sql):
                return (None, [])

        eq(sess._col_names(_Empty(), table="x"), [], "None cols -> []")
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need(src.count("_col_names(") >= 8,
             "the LIMIT-0 introspection sites should use the shared helper")

    def t_sanitize_ident_shared():
        # Table-name sanitisation lives in one helper now, not inlined at 7
        # call sites. Verify behaviour + that the inline copies are gone.

        eq(sanitize_ident("my acc!"), "my_acc", "non-word runs -> _")
        eq(sanitize_ident("  a-b  c "), "a_b_c", "trim + collapse")
        eq(sanitize_ident("123t"), "t_123t", "leading digit -> t_")
        eq(sanitize_ident(""), "", "empty -> '' by default")
        eq(sanitize_ident("", "flow_result"), "flow_result", "empty -> fallback")
        eq(sanitize_ident(None, "table"), "table", "None -> fallback")

             "session must import the shared sanitize_ident")

             "no inline table-name sanitization should remain in session.py")

    def t_load_header_spaces_to_underscore():
        # On load, whitespace in field headers becomes ``_`` so NodeFlow /
        # Journal never see spaced identifiers. DuckDB native reads used to
        # preserve ``Order Date`` while the SQLite CSV path already sanitized.
        from samql_core.sqlutil import sanitize_column_header
        eq(sanitize_column_header("Order Date"), "Order_Date", "space -> _")
        eq(sanitize_column_header("  foo   bar  "), "foo_bar",
           "trim + collapse whitespace runs")
        eq(sanitize_column_header("a__b"), "a__b",
           "existing underscores are not collapsed")
        eq(sanitize_column_header('a"b'), 'a"b',
           "punctuation is left alone (whitespace-only sanitizer)")
        eq(sanitize_column_header("   "), "", "all-whitespace -> empty")

        import tempfile
        path = None
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            fd, path = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".csv")
            os.close(fd)
            with open(path, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("Order Date,foo  bar,Amount\n2020-01-01,x,10\n")
            loaded_sql = s.load_file(path, destination="sqlite",
                                     base_name="hdr_sql")
            cols_sql = loaded_sql[0]["columns"]
            need("Order_Date" in cols_sql, "sqlite spaced header: %r" % cols_sql)
            need("foo_bar" in cols_sql, "sqlite multi-space header: %r" % cols_sql)
            need("Order Date" not in cols_sql, "sqlite kept spaced name: %r" % cols_sql)

            from samql_core.engines import HAS_DUCKDB
            if not HAS_DUCKDB:
                return
            loaded = s.load_file(path, destination="duckdb",
                                 base_name="hdr_duck")
            cols = loaded[0]["columns"]
            need("Order_Date" in cols, "duckdb spaced header: %r" % cols)
            need("foo_bar" in cols, "duckdb multi-space header: %r" % cols)
            need("Order Date" not in cols, "duckdb kept spaced name: %r" % cols)
            r = s.run_query(
                'SELECT a."Order_Date", b."Amount" FROM "hdr_duck" a '
                'JOIN "hdr_duck" b ON a."Order_Date" = b."Order_Date"',
                target="__duckdb__")
            need(not r.get("error"), "join on sanitized headers failed: %r" % r)
            eq(len(r.get("rows") or []), 1, "join row count")
        finally:
            if path:
                try:
                    os.unlink(path)
                except Exception:
                    pass
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_unquoted_var_and_missing_accum():
        # Build .205 — two iterator-ergonomics fixes from a real screenshot:
        # (1) a formula using a BARE ${col1} substitutes the row's *text* value
        #     as an identifier ('no such column: dog'); the per-pass error now
        #     appends a hint to quote it as '${col1}'. The quoted form runs.
        # (2) reading the iterator's out port before it has run fails with a
        #     bare 'no such table: res'; it now says to run the iterator first.
        s = Session()
        try:
            vals = {"id": "v", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "v", "columns": ["col1", "col2"],
                "rows": [["dog", "dog"], ["cat", "cat"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            body = {"id": "b", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "b", "columns": ["dog1", "dog2"],
                "rows": [["cow", "cow"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}

            def graph(expr):
                it = {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "table": "res", "accumulate": "append",
                    "reset_first": False,
                    "var_rename": {"col1": "col1", "col2": "col2"},
                    "children": [{"id": "fx", "type": "formula", "config": {
                        "label": "formula",
                        "formulas": [{"name": "dog1", "expr": expr}]}}]}}
                return {"nodes": [vals, body, it], "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}

            # (1) bare ${col1} -> the pass fails, error recommends {{col1}}
            g = graph("${col1}")
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            msg = (r.get("errors") or [{}])[0].get("error", "")
            need("{{col1}}" in msg and "quotes automatically" in msg,
                 "bare ${var} pass error recommends {{col1}}: %r" % msg)
            eq(r.get("passes"), 0, "the bare-variable pass fails")

            # (2) read res before it exists -> 'run the iterator first'
            ro = s.run_nodeflow(g, "it", "out")
            em = ro.get("error", "")
            need("res" in em and "run the iterator" in em.lower()
                 and "no such table" not in em.lower(),
                 "missing-accumulator error tells the user to run first: %r"
                 % em)

            # (3) the quoted form runs and builds res
            g2 = graph("'${col1}'")
            r2 = s.run_iterator(g2, "it")
            need(not r2.get("error") and r2.get("passes") == 2,
                 "the quoted ${var} runs 2 passes: %s"
                 % (r2.get("error") or r2.get("errors")))
            ro2 = s.run_nodeflow(g2, "it", "out")
            eq(len(ro2.get("rows") or []), 2,
               "the out port reads the 2 accumulated rows")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_quoted_variable_braces():
        # Build .206 — {{name}} substitutes a variable as a quoted SQL string
        # literal (auto-escaped), so a formula can use {{col}} for a text value
        # instead of '${col}'. ${name} stays the raw form; the SQL node's
        # {{in}} / {{input}} splice keywords are never auto-quoted.
        from samql_core import applyvars as A
        ctx = {"col": "dog", "q": "O'Brien", "n": "42"}
        eq(A.substitute_text("x = {{col}}", ctx), "x = 'dog'",
           "{{name}} -> quoted string literal")
        eq(A.substitute_text("x = ${col}", ctx), "x = dog",
           "${name} stays raw")
        eq(A.substitute_text("n = {{q}}", ctx), "n = 'O''Brien'",
           "{{name}} escapes embedded quotes")
        eq(A.substitute_text("FROM {{input}}", ctx), "FROM {{input}}",
           "{{input}} SQL-splice keyword is left for the SQL node")
        eq(A.substitute_text("x = {{missing}}", ctx), "x = {{missing}}",
           "unbound {{name}} is left untouched")
        eq(A.unresolved_tokens({"e": "{{missing}} ${other} {{input}}"}),
           ["missing", "other"],
           "unresolved_tokens reports {{}} and ${} but not the splice keyword")
        # end to end: an iterator formula using {{col1}} runs (no manual quotes)
        s = Session()
        try:
            vals = {"id": "v", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "v", "columns": ["col1", "col2"],
                "rows": [["dog", "dog"], ["cat", "cat"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            body = {"id": "b", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "b", "columns": ["dog1", "dog2"],
                "rows": [["cow", "cow"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            it = {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                "table": "res", "accumulate": "append", "reset_first": False,
                "var_rename": {"col1": "col1", "col2": "col2"},
                "children": [{"id": "fx", "type": "formula", "config": {
                    "label": "formula",
                    "formulas": [{"name": "dog1", "expr": "{{col1}}"}]}}]}}
            g = {"nodes": [vals, body, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
