            need(not r.get("error") and r.get("passes") == 2,
                 "a formula using {{col1}} runs without manual quotes: %s"
                 % (r.get("error") or r.get("errors")))
            ro = s.run_nodeflow(g, "it", "out")
            eq(sorted(row[ro["columns"].index("dog1")]
                      for row in (ro.get("rows") or [])),
               ["cat", "dog"], "{{col1}} wrote the text values into dog1")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_brace_misuse_guardrail():
        # Build .207 -- {{name}} inserts a quoted SQL string, so it is rejected
        # up front for the two misuses it can't express: a numeric value (wants
        # the bare number via ${name}); and a raw-value node -- an API URL or a
        # file-browser path -- (wants ${name}, no SQL quotes). ${name} and a
        # text {{name}} stay fine; the SQL {{input}} splice is never flagged.
        from samql_core import applyvars as A
        fx = lambda e: {"nodes": [{"id": "fx", "type": "formula",
                        "config": {"formulas": [{"name": "o", "expr": e}]}}]}
        m = A.brace_misuse(fx("x = {{n}}"), {"n": "42"})
        need(m and "${n}" in m, "numeric {{n}} is flagged, points to ${n}: %r" % m)
        eq(A.brace_misuse(fx("x = {{n}}"), {"n": "dog"}), None, "text {{n}} ok")
        eq(A.brace_misuse(fx("x = ${n}"), {"n": "42"}), None, "raw ${n} ok")
        api = {"nodes": [{"id": "a", "type": "apinode",
               "config": {"url": "http://x/{{id}}"}}]}
        m = A.brace_misuse(api, {})
        need(m and "${id}" in m, "{{id}} in an API URL is flagged: %r" % m)
        fb = {"nodes": [{"id": "f", "type": "filebrowser",
              "config": {"pattern": "/d/*_{{as_of}}.csv"}}]}
        m = A.brace_misuse(fb, {})
        need(m and "file browser" in m, "{{}} in a file path is flagged: %r" % m)
        eq(A.brace_misuse({"nodes": [{"id": "s", "type": "sql", "config": {
            "sql": "SELECT * FROM {{input}} WHERE x={{v}}"}}]}, {"v": "dog"}),
            None, "{{input}} splice + a text {{v}} are both fine")
        # integration: the guardrail surfaces through the real run paths
        s = Session()
        try:
            var = {"id": "vn", "type": "variable", "config": {"vars": [
                {"name": "n", "value": "42"}, {"name": "w", "value": "dog"}]}}
            data = {"id": "d", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "d", "columns": ["a"], "rows": [["1"]],
                "dest": "sqlite"}}
            flt = {"id": "flt", "type": "filter",
                   "config": {"condition": "CAST(a AS INT) >= {{n}}"}}
            g = {"nodes": [var, data, flt], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "d", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "flt", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_nodeflow(g, "flt", "true")
            need(r.get("error") and "${n}" in r["error"],
                 "preview of a filter with numeric {{n}} errors to ${n}: %r"
                 % r.get("error"))
            flt["config"]["condition"] = "a = {{w}}"
            r = s.run_nodeflow(g, "flt", "true")
            eq(r.get("error"), None, "a text {{w}} filter previews fine")
            # the guardrail also fires on save-to-table, not just preview
            flt["config"]["condition"] = "CAST(a AS INT) >= {{n}}"
            r = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(g, "flt", "saved_t")
            need(r.get("error") and "${n}" in r["error"],
                 "save-to-table with numeric {{n}} also errors to ${n}: %r"
                 % r.get("error"))
            flt["config"]["condition"] = "a = {{w}}"
            r = s.fetch_api_node("a", {"url": "https://x.test/{{id}}",
                                 "params": [], "headers": []}, {"nodes": []})
            need(r.get("error") and "${id}" in r["error"],
                 "fetch_api_node rejects {{id}} in the URL: %r" % r.get("error"))
            # iterator: a numeric per-pass {{col1}} is caught before the loop
            iv = {"id": "v", "type": "createtable", "config": {"label": "v",
                  "columns": ["col1"], "rows": [["42"], ["7"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            ib = {"id": "b", "type": "createtable", "config": {"label": "b",
                  "columns": ["z"], "rows": [["x"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            it = {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {"table": "res",
                  "accumulate": "append", "reset_first": False,
                  "var_rename": {"col1": "col1"},
                  "children": [{"id": "fx", "type": "formula", "config": {
                      "formulas": [{"name": "o", "expr": "y = {{col1}}"}]}}]}}
            g = {"nodes": [iv, ib, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            need(r.get("error") and "${col1}" in r["error"],
                 "iterator with a numeric {{col1}} errors to ${col1}: %r"
                 % r.get("error"))
            # a numeric *variable-node* value used as {{thr}} inside the loop is
            # caught the same way (the loop sees variable-node values too)
            vthr = {"id": "vt", "type": "variable",
                    "config": {"vars": [{"name": "thr", "value": "5"}]}}
            it["config"]["children"] = [{"id": "fx", "type": "formula",
                "config": {"formulas": [{"name": "o", "expr": "n >= {{thr}}"}]}}]
            g = {"nodes": [vthr, iv, ib, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            iv["config"]["rows"] = [["dog"]]   # non-numeric binding this time
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            need(r.get("error") and "${thr}" in r["error"],
                 "numeric variable-node {{thr}} inside a loop errors to ${thr}:"
                 " %r" % r.get("error"))
            # a stray, half-built node elsewhere must not block a scoped preview
            bad = {"id": "bad", "type": "formula", "config": {
                "formulas": [{"name": "q", "expr": "{{n}}"}]}}
            g2 = {"nodes": [var, data, bad], "edges": []}
            r = s.run_nodeflow(g2, "d", "out")
            eq(r.get("error"), None,
               "a stray {{n}} elsewhere doesn't block an unrelated preview")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_variables_in_all_nodes():
        # Build .207 -- {{name}} (auto-quoted text) and ${name} (raw) resolve in
        # every node's string config, not just formulas, so no manual '' is ever
        # needed. Exercise a filter and a SQL node (whose {{input}} splice still
        # works alongside a {{var}}), plus a filter inside an iterator.
        s = Session()
        def ct(nid, cols, rows):
            return {"id": nid, "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": nid, "columns": cols, "rows": rows, "dest": "sqlite"}}
        try:
            var = {"id": "vn", "type": "variable", "config": {"vars": [
                {"name": "v", "value": "dog"}, {"name": "min", "value": "2"}]}}
            data = ct("d", ["name", "n"],
                      [["dog", "1"], ["cat", "2"], ["dog", "3"]])
            flt = {"id": "flt", "type": "filter",
                   "config": {"condition": "name = {{v}}"}}
            g = {"nodes": [var, data, flt], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "d", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "flt", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_nodeflow(g, "flt", "true")
            eq(len(r.get("rows") or []), 2,
               "filter {{v}} (auto-quoted) matched the 2 dog rows")
            flt["config"]["condition"] = "CAST(n AS INT) >= ${min}"
            r = s.run_nodeflow(g, "flt", "true")
            eq(len(r.get("rows") or []), 2,
               "filter ${min} (raw number) kept the 2 rows n>=2")
            sql = {"id": "sq", "type": "sql", "config": {
                "sql": "SELECT * FROM {{input}} WHERE name = {{v}}"}}
            g = {"nodes": [var, data, sql], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "d", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "sq", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_nodeflow(g, "sq", "out")
            eq(len(r.get("rows") or []), 2,
               "SQL node resolved {{v}} and spliced {{input}} together")
            # a filter (not formula) inside an iterator, using a per-pass {{col1}}
            vals = ct("v", ["col1"], [["dog"], ["cat"]])
            it = {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {"table": "res",
                  "accumulate": "append", "reset_first": False,
                  "var_rename": {"col1": "col1"},
                  "children": [{"id": "flt2", "type": "filter",
                      "config": {"condition": "name = {{col1}}"}}]}}
            g = {"nodes": [vals, data, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "d", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            eq(r.get("error"), None,
               "an iterator filter body with {{col1}} runs: %s"
               % (r.get("error") or ""))
            # a text *variable-node* value works the same way inside a loop --
            # {{tag}} auto-quotes, no manual '' and no spurious guardrail error
            vtag = {"id": "vg", "type": "variable",
                    "config": {"vars": [{"name": "tag", "value": "dog"}]}}
            it["config"]["children"] = [{"id": "flt3", "type": "filter",
                "config": {"condition": "name = {{col1}} OR name = {{tag}}"}}]
            g = {"nodes": [vtag, vals, data, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "d", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            eq(r.get("error"), None,
               "a text variable-node {{tag}} inside a loop runs: %s"
               % (r.get("error") or ""))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_unbound_var_message():
        # An iterator body that references a ${name} the values row doesn't
        # provide used to fail every pass with the engine's cryptic
        # 'unrecognized token: "$"' (the ${name} survived substitution and a
        # lone $ reached SQL). It now returns ONE clear error naming the bad
        # variable and listing the fields the values row actually provides --
        # so a typo or a column-name mismatch is obvious instead of looking
        # like the columns "aren't syncing".
        from samql_core import applyvars
        eq(applyvars.unresolved_tokens(
            {"a": "x ${foo} y", "b": ["${bar}", "plain"],
             "c": {"d": "${foo}"}}),
            ["bar", "foo"], "unresolved_tokens lists unique names, sorted")
        eq(applyvars.unresolved_tokens({"a": "no tokens"}), [],
           "fully-resolved config has no unresolved tokens")
        s = Session()
        try:
            vals = {"id": "v", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "vals", "columns": ["col1", "col2"],
                "rows": [["dog", "dog"], ["cat", "cat"]], "dest": "sqlite"}}
            side = {"id": "sd", "type": "sql", "config": {
                "sql": "SELECT 1 AS id", "label": "sd"}}
            it = {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                "table": "acc", "accumulate": "append", "reset_first": True,
                "children": [{"id": "fx", "type": "formula", "config": {
                    "formulas": [{"name": "bad", "expr": "${nope}"}]}}]}}
            g = {"nodes": [vals, side, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "sd", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            msg = r.get("error") or ""
            need("${nope}" in msg and "col1" in msg and "col2" in msg,
                 "iterator names the unbound var AND the available fields: %r"
                 % msg)
            need("unrecognized token" not in msg,
                 "the cryptic engine token error is replaced: %r" % msg)
            # a ${var} that matches a values column still runs fine
            it["config"]["children"][0]["config"]["formulas"] = [
                {"name": "tag", "expr": "'${col1}'"}]
            r2 = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            need(not r2.get("error") and r2.get("passes") == 2,
                 "a ${var} matching a values column still works: %s"
                 % (r2.get("error") or r2.get("errors")))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_container_no_loopvar():
        # A container iterator (children present) driven by a wired "values"
        # table runs WITHOUT a loop-variable name: each values row is one pass
        # with its columns bound as ${vars}, and the body processes the wired
        # "in" data each pass. Guards the UI path (the frontend no longer
        # pre-requires config.var for a container) end to end.
        s = Session()
        try:
            vsrc = {"id": "v", "type": "sql",
                    "config": {"sql": "SELECT 'a' AS k UNION ALL SELECT 'b'",
                               "label": "v"}}
            dsrc = {"id": "d", "type": "sql",
                    "config": {"sql": "SELECT 1 AS id UNION ALL SELECT 2",
                               "label": "d"}}
            it = {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                "table": "acc", "accumulate": "append", "reset_first": True,
                # no "var" / driver -- the passes come from the wired vars port
                "children": [
                    {"id": "body", "type": "sql",
                     "config": {"sql": "SELECT id, '${k}' AS tag FROM input",
                                "label": "body"}}]}}
            g = {"nodes": [vsrc, dsrc, it], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "v", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                {"from": {"node": "d", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            need(not r.get("error") and not (r.get("errors") or []),
                 "container iterator runs off a wired values table without a "
                 "loop variable: %s" % (r.get("error") or r.get("errors")))
            eq(r.get("passes"), 2, "one pass per values row")
            out = s.run_query("SELECT tag, COUNT(*) AS n FROM acc "
                              "GROUP BY tag ORDER BY tag",
                              target="__local__")["rows"]
            eq([(row[0], row[1]) for row in out], [("a", 2), ("b", 2)],
               "each pass's ${k} binding tagged the 2 'in' rows")
            # the iterator's out port reads that accumulator like any table
            ro = s.run_nodeflow(g, "it", "out")
            need(not ro.get("error"),
                 "the out port reads the accumulator: %s" % ro.get("error"))
            eq(len(ro["rows"]), 4, "out port returns all accumulated rows")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_load_view_mode_wiring():
        # Structural: the view SQL + the mode plumbing through every layer.
        def rd(*p):
            return open(os.path.join(ROOT, *p), encoding="utf-8").read()
        eng = rd("backend", "samql_core", "engines.py")
        ld = rd("backend", "samql_core", "loaders.py")
        srv = rd("backend", "server.py")
        api = rd("frontend", "src", "lib", "api.ts")
        modal = rd("frontend", "src", "components", "load",
                   "FileLoadTab.tsx")
        checks = [
            ("engine creates a view (not a table) over the native readers",
             "def create_view_from_file" in eng
             and 'CREATE VIEW "{final}" AS SELECT * FROM {rdr}' in eng
             and "read_parquet('{fwd}')" in eng
             and "read_csv_auto('{fwd}', sample_size=204800" in eng),
            ("the view registers a persistent source path",
             "self.table_sources[final] = path" in eng),
            ("loader routes view mode to the view (with materialize fallback)",
             'mode == "view"' in ld
             and "create_view_from_file" in ld
             and '"view": True' in ld),
            ("server load_start + load_path thread mode",
             'b.get("mode") or "materialize"' in srv
             and "mode=mode" in srv),
            ("api sends mode for the load",
             "mode = \"materialize\"" in api and "delimiter, mode, sheet" in api),
            ("the load dialog offers a query-in-place option",
             "How to load" in modal
             and 'value="view"' in modal
             and "loadMode" in modal),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "load view-mode wiring broken: " + "; ".join(missing))

    def t_journal_persists_across_tabs():
        import re as _re
        # A running Journal (Notebook) query must survive switching the top view
        # tab. That requires the Notebook to stay MOUNTED (hidden with display)
        # rather than being conditionally rendered -- a conditional render
        # unmounts it, destroying the in-flight query's state and its result, so
        # it looks cancelled when you come back. IDE / NodeFlow / Dashboard use
        # the same keep-mounted pattern so their in-flight work survives too.
        def rd(*p):
            return open(os.path.join(ROOT, *p), encoding="utf-8").read()
        app = rd("frontend", "src", "App.tsx")
        checks = [
            ("Journal is kept mounted, hidden via display when inactive",
             'display: view === "notebook" ? "contents" : "none"' in app),
            ("the Notebook mount itself is never behind a conditional "
             "(the display-style ternary is the ALLOWED form)",
             not _re.search(r'view === "notebook"\s*\?\s*\(', app)
             and not _re.search(
                 r'view === "notebook"\s*&&\s*\(?\s*<Notebook', app)),
            ("IDE is keep-mounted via display (not unmounted on tab switch)",
             'display: view === "ide" ? "contents" : "none"' in app
             and 'data-testid="ide-surface"' in app),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing,
             "journal-persist wiring broken: " + "; ".join(missing))

    def t_client_abort_is_quiet():
        # The browser aborts in-flight requests constantly and harmlessly
        # (navigating, superseding a running query, dropping a progress poll
        # mid-reply). The server must swallow those ConnectionError writes with
        # no console noise -- but still print genuine errors. Drives the real
        # server's handle_error.
        import io
        import server as _srv
        httpd = _srv.make_server("127.0.0.1", 0)[0]
        try:
            buf = io.StringIO()
            saved, sys.stderr = sys.stderr, buf
            try:
                try:
                    raise ConnectionResetError(10053, "aborted by host")
                except ConnectionError:
                    httpd.handle_error(None, ("127.0.0.1", 0))
                quiet = buf.getvalue()
                try:
                    raise ValueError("a genuine bug")
                except ValueError:
                    httpd.handle_error(None, ("127.0.0.1", 0))
                noisy = buf.getvalue()
            finally:
                sys.stderr = saved
        finally:
            httpd.server_close()
        eq(quiet, "", "a client-abort is swallowed with no console noise")
        need("a genuine bug" in noisy,
             "a real error still prints a traceback to the console")

    def t_perf_config():
        # Final-pass guard: the performance + memory wiring stays in place so a
        # later edit can't quietly regress it.
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        eng = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "engines.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        ses = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "session.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        checks = [
            ("HTTP handler disables Nagle (TCP_NODELAY) for low latency",
             "disable_nagle_algorithm = True" in srv),
            ("HTTP/1.1 keep-alive is on",
             'protocol_version = "HTTP/1.1"' in srv),
            ("large responses are gzipped",
             "_gz.compress(data, 1)" in srv),
            ("DuckDB runs multi-threaded", "SET threads TO" in eng),
            ("DuckDB has a memory cap (spills past it)",
             "SET memory_limit" in eng),
            ("DuckDB object cache is on", "enable_object_cache = true" in eng),
            ("DuckDB skips insertion-order bookkeeping",
             "preserve_insertion_order = false" in eng),
            ("results are parquet-backed (compact, spillable)",
             "use_parquet_results" in ses),
            ("startup note is clear (no ambiguous 'slower')",
             "first start takes a few seconds" in srv),
        ]
        missing = [n for n, ok in checks if not ok]
        need(not missing, "perf config regressed: " + "; ".join(missing))

    def t_json_big_integers():
        # JSON ints beyond 64-bit used to crash the SQLite load with
        # OverflowError. They must now load and be preserved (as text).
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "bi.json")
        big = 12345678901234567890  # > 2**63 - 1
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            json.dump([{"id": 1, "acct": big}, {"id": 2, "acct": 7}], f)
        try:
            s.load_file(p, destination="sqlite", base_name="bi")
            rows = s.run_query("SELECT acct FROM bi ORDER BY id",
                               target="__local__")["rows"]
            eq(str(rows[0][0]), str(big), "big int not preserved")
            # the bind-safe net: raw big ints fed straight to a typed insert
            name, _n = s.db.add_table_streaming(
                "raw", ["id", "big"],
                iter([(1, 99), (2, 10 ** 30), (3, -10 ** 25)]), source="t")
            vs = [str(r[0]) for r in s.run_query(
                f"SELECT big FROM {name} ORDER BY id",
                target="__local__")["rows"]]
            eq(vs, ["99", str(10 ** 30), str(-10 ** 25)],
               "bind-safe revert-to-text failed")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_json_number_edge_cases():
        # floats, scientific notation, and the non-standard NaN/Infinity
        # literals must all stream in without crashing.
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
        p = os.path.join(dd, "n.json")
        with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
            f.write('[{"v":0.1},{"v":3.14159265358979},{"v":-2.5e-3},'
                    '{"v":1000000.01},{"v":NaN},{"v":Infinity},'
                    '{"v":-Infinity}]')
        try:
            s.load_file(p, destination="sqlite", base_name="num")
            n = s.run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM num",
                            target="__local__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(n, 7, "number edge cases dropped or crashed")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_json_robust_shapes():
        from samql_core.flatten import stream_json_records
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

        def w(name, text):
            p = os.path.join(dd, name)
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(text)
            return p
        try:
            # BOM + single object + duplicate keys (last wins)
            recs = list(stream_json_records(
                w("bom.json", "\ufeff" + '{"id":1,"id":2,"name":"z"}')))
            eq(recs, [{"id": 2, "name": "z"}], "BOM/single/dup-keys")
            # deep nesting + unicode + null + empty array, end to end
            doc = [{"id": 1, "meta": {"a": {"b": {"c": 1}}}, "tags": [],
                    "note": None, "emoji": "\u2728\U0001F680"},
                   {"id": 2, "meta": {}, "tags": [{"k": "v"}], "note": "x"}]
            p = w("nest.json", json.dumps(doc, ensure_ascii=False))
            out = s.load_file(p, destination="sqlite", base_name="nst")
            em = s.run_query("SELECT emoji FROM nst WHERE id=1",
                             target="__local__")["rows"][0][0]
            eq(em, "\u2728\U0001F680", "unicode mangled on load")
            need(any(o["name"] == "nst_tags" for o in out),
                 "child table for array of objects missing")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_keyset_paging():
        # Deep paging over a spilled result must use the keyset index range
        # scan and still return the right rows.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            res = s.run_query(
                "WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT x+1 "
                "FROM c WHERE x<60000) SELECT x FROM c", target="__local__")
            rid = res["result_id"]
            need(type(s._results[rid].store).__name__ == "DiskBackedRows",
                 "expected a spilled DiskBackedRows store")
            eq(res["total_rows"], 60000, "expected 60k rows")
            deep = s.page(rid, offset=59995, limit=5)
            eq([r[0] for r in deep["rows"]],
               [59996, 59997, 59998, 59999, 60000], "deep keyset page")
            mid = s.page(rid, offset=30000, limit=3)
            eq([r[0] for r in mid["rows"]], [30001, 30002, 30003], "mid page")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_deep_sorted_paging():
        # Deep paging over a sorted/filtered spilled result uses the deferred
        # index-only OFFSET scan (past _DEFER_OFFSET) and must return exactly
        # the rows the plain plan would -- including the deterministic `i`
        # tiebreaker so tied sort values page consistently.
        from samql_core.rows import _DEFER_OFFSET
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            n = _DEFER_OFFSET + 4000
            s.db.add_table_streaming(
                "ds", ["id", "grp"], ((i, i % 50) for i in range(n)))
            s.db.sync_catalog()
            rid = s.run_query("SELECT * FROM ds",
                              target="__local__")["result_id"]
            ci = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(s._results[rid].cols)}
            rows = [(i, i % 50) for i in range(n)]

            def ref(col, desc, off, lim):
                j = ci[col]
                srt = sorted(rows, key=lambda r: r[0])          # i asc
                srt = sorted(srt, key=lambda r: r[j], reverse=desc)  # stable
                return [list(x) for x in srt[off:off + lim]]

            for col, desc, off in [("grp", True, _DEFER_OFFSET + 100),
                                   ("id", False, _DEFER_OFFSET + 2000)]:
                pg = s.page(rid, offset=off, limit=25,
                            sort_col=col, descending=desc)
                got = [[r[ci["id"]], r[ci["grp"]]] for r in pg["rows"]]
                eq(got, ref(col, desc, off, 25),
                   "deep sorted page (%s desc=%s off=%d)" % (col, desc, off))
            fpg = s.page(rid, offset=_DEFER_OFFSET + 50, limit=10,
                         sort_col="id", descending=False,
                         filters=[{"column": "grp", "op": "gte", "value": 0}])
            ids = [r[ci["id"]] for r in fpg["rows"]]
            eq(ids, list(range(_DEFER_OFFSET + 50, _DEFER_OFFSET + 60)),
               "deep filtered page rows")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_column_projection():
        s = _loaded_session()
        try:
            res = s.run_query("SELECT * FROM data", target="__local__")
            rid = res["result_id"]
            full = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=2)
            proj = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=2, columns=["score", "id"])
            eq(proj["columns"], ["score", "id"], "projection columns/order")
            i_id = full["columns"].index("id")
            i_sc = full["columns"].index("score")
            eq(proj["rows"][0],
               [full["rows"][0][i_sc], full["rows"][0][i_id]],
               "projected values")
            allc = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=1, columns=["nope"])
            eq(allc["columns"], full["columns"],
               "all-invalid projection should return all columns")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def _recon_fixtures(s, dest):
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

        def w(n, t):
            p = os.path.join(dd, n)
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(t)
            return p
        # left ids 0..699, right ids 100..799 -> only-left 0..99 (100),
        # only-right 700..799 (100); shared 100..699 all differ -> 600.
        left = "id,val\n" + "\n".join(f"{i},{i}" for i in range(700))
        right = "id,val\n" + "\n".join(f"{i},{i+1}" for i in range(100, 800))
        s.load_file(w("L.csv", left), destination=dest, base_name="L")
        s.load_file(w("R.csv", right), destination=dest, base_name="R")

    def t_reconcile_dupe_keys_counts():
        # Real-world data often has duplicate keys. Reconcile is key-based, so
        # counts + balance must NOT fan out on the join. Duplicate rows here
        # carry identical values so the 1-row-per-key collapse is deterministic.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

            def w(n, t):
                pth = os.path.join(dd, n)
                with open(pth, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    f.write(t)
                return pth
            # A keys {1,1,2,3}; B keys {1,2,2,4}. Distinct: A={1,2,3} B={1,2,4}
            # -> a_only={3}=1, b_only={4}=1, matched={1,2}=2, total=4.
            left = ("id,val,bal\n1,a,10\n1,a,10\n2,x,20\n3,y,30\n")
            right = ("id,val,bal\n1,a,10\n2,x,20\n2,x,20\n4,w,40\n")
            s.load_file(w("DL.csv", left), destination="sqlite", base_name="DL")
            s.load_file(w("DR.csv", right), destination="sqlite",
                        base_name="DR")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "DL", "right": "DR", "keys": ["id"],
                               "compare": ["val"], "balance": "bal"})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"reconcile error: {rec.get('error')}")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq(t["a_only"], 1, "dupe a_only (distinct keys)")
            eq(t["b_only"], 1, "dupe b_only (distinct keys)")
            eq(t["matching"], 2, "dupe matched not fanned out (keys 1,2)")
            eq(t["non_matching"], 0, "dupe rows all agree")
            eq(t["total"], 4, "dupe total = distinct union of keys")
            fv = rec["fields"][0]
            eq(fv["matching"], 2, "per-field matching not fanned out")
            eq(fv["non_matching"], 0, "per-field non-matching")
            # balance summed once per matched key: 10 (key1) + 20 (key2) = 30
            eq(round(fv["sum_matching_balance"], 2), 30.0,
               "balance summed once per key (no fan-out)")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_balance_currency():
        # Balances stored as text with thousands separators / currency signs
        # must still sum numerically.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

            def w(n, t):
                pth = os.path.join(dd, n)
                with open(pth, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                    f.write(t)
                return pth
            left = ('id,val,bal\n1,a,"1,000.50"\n2,b,"$2,000.25"\n')
            right = ('id,val,bal\n1,a,"1,000.50"\n2,b,"$2,000.25"\n')
            s.load_file(w("CL.csv", left), destination="sqlite",
                        base_name="CL")
            s.load_file(w("CR.csv", right), destination="sqlite",
                        base_name="CR")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "CL", "right": "CR", "keys": ["id"],
                               "compare": ["val"], "balance": "bal"})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"reconcile error: {rec.get('error')}")
            fv = rec["fields"][0]
            eq(round(fv["sum_matching_balance"], 2), 3000.75,
               "currency-formatted balance parsed + summed")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_after_drilldown_close():
        # Repro of the reported bug: reconcile -> drill-down -> close the
        # result -> reconcile again used to fail, because closing the result
        # scheduled a background checkpoint/optimize that raced the next query
        # on the same engine connection. execute() now holds the engine lock,
        # so foreground queries and background maintenance can't collide.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            _recon_fixtures(s, "sqlite")
            spec = {"left": "L", "right": "R", "keys": ["id"],
                    "compare": ["val"]}
            r1 = s.reconcile(spec)
            need(not r1.get("error"), f"1st reconcile: {r1.get('error')}")
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({**spec, "bucket": "a_only"})
            need(d.get("result_id"), "drilldown produced no result")
            s.discard_result(d["result_id"])         # schedules bg cleanup
            s._reclaim(full=True)                      # run that cleanup now
            r2 = s.reconcile(spec)
            need(not r2.get("error"), f"2nd reconcile: {r2.get('error')}")
            eq(r2["totals"]["a_only"], 100, "2nd reconcile totals intact")
            # background maintenance concurrent with foreground reconciles
            import threading as _t
            stop = _t.Event()
            errs = []

            def churn():
                while not stop.is_set():
                    try:
                        s._reclaim(full=True)
                    except Exception as e:  # pragma: no cover
                        errs.append(("reclaim", str(e)))

            th = _t.Thread(target=churn, daemon=True)
            th.start()
            try:
                for _ in range(8):
                    rr = s.reconcile(spec)
                    if rr.get("error"):
                        errs.append(("reconcile", rr["error"]))
            finally:
                stop.set()
                th.join(timeout=2)
            need(not errs, f"concurrent maintenance broke queries: {errs[:3]}")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_pivot_values_and_filters():
        # Single-source pivot: row/col dims, multiple summarize values, and a
        # filter pushed into the WHERE clause.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
            p = os.path.join(dd, "P.csv")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("cat,reg,amt\nA,East,10\nA,West,20\n"
                        "B,East,30\nB,East,40\n")
            s.load_file(p, destination="sqlite", base_name="P")
            # rows=cat, cols=reg, one value (sum amt) -> col-key headers
            r = s.pivot({"table": "P", "engine": "sqlite", "rows": ["cat"],
                         "cols": ["reg"], "values": [{"field": "amt",
                                                      "agg": "sum"}]})
            need(not r.get("error"), f"pivot error: {r.get('error')}")
            eq(r["columns"], ["cat", "East", "West"], "col-key headers")
            rowmap = {row[0]: row for row in r["rows"]}
            eq(rowmap["A"][1], 10.0, "A/East sum")
            eq(rowmap["A"][2], 20.0, "A/West sum")
            eq(rowmap["B"][1], 70.0, "B/East sum (30+40)")
            need(rowmap["B"][2] is None, "B/West empty cell")
            # multiple summarize values, no col dims -> one column per value
            r2 = s.pivot({"table": "P", "engine": "sqlite", "rows": ["cat"],
                          "cols": [], "values": [{"field": "amt", "agg": "sum"},
                                                 {"field": "amt",
                                                  "agg": "avg"}]})
            eq(r2["columns"], ["cat", "sum(amt)", "avg(amt)"], "value headers")
            m2 = {row[0]: row for row in r2["rows"]}
            eq(m2["A"][1], 30.0, "A sum")
            eq(m2["A"][2], 15.0, "A avg")
            eq(m2["B"][1], 70.0, "B sum")
            eq(m2["B"][2], 35.0, "B avg")
            # filter: only cat A rows
            r3 = s.pivot({"table": "P", "engine": "sqlite", "rows": ["reg"],
                          "values": [{"field": "amt", "agg": "sum"}],
                          "filters": [{"field": "cat", "op": "equals",
                                       "value": "A"}]})
            regs = {row[0] for row in r3["rows"]}
            eq(regs, {"East", "West"}, "filtered to cat A regions")
            tot = sum(row[1] for row in r3["rows"])
            eq(tot, 30.0, "filtered sum = 10+20")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_pivot_python_sql_parity():
        # The SQL pivot path (table source) and the Python pivot path (small
        # "current result" source) must agree. Locks the fixes for: count/
        # count_distinct/min/max over a TEXT column (Python used to drop
        # non-numeric cells -> 0/blank), and case-insensitive contains.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
            p = os.path.join(dd, "P.csv")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("cat,sub,amt,d\n"
                        "A,North,10,2026-01-05\n"
                        "A,South,20,2026-03-01\n"
                        "B,north,5,2026-02-02\n"
                        "B,South,,2026-01-01\n")
            s.load_file(p, destination="sqlite", base_name="P")
            rid = s.run_query("SELECT * FROM P",
                              target="__local__")["result_id"]

            def bycat(res):
                return {row[0]: row[1] for row in res["rows"]}

            def both(values, filters=None):
                spec = {"rows": ["cat"], "values": values}
                if filters:
                    spec["filters"] = filters
                sql = s.pivot({**spec, "table": "P", "engine": "sqlite"})
                py = s.pivot({**spec, "result_id": rid})
                need(not sql.get("error"), "sql pivot: %s" % sql.get("error"))
                need(not py.get("error"), "py pivot: %s" % py.get("error"))
                return bycat(sql), bycat(py)

            # count of a TEXT column: non-zero and equal across paths
            sql, py = both([{"field": "sub", "agg": "count"}])
            eq(py, {"A": 2, "B": 2}, "python count(text) per group")
            eq(sql, py, "count(text) SQL == Python")
            # count_distinct of a text column
            sql, py = both([{"field": "sub", "agg": "count_distinct"}])
            eq(py, {"A": 2, "B": 2}, "python count_distinct(text)")
            eq(sql, py, "count_distinct(text) SQL == Python")
            # max of a date-ish text column: latest value, not blank
            sql, py = both([{"field": "d", "agg": "max"}])
            eq(py, {"A": "2026-03-01", "B": "2026-02-02"},
               "python max(date text) not blank")
            eq(sql, py, "max(date text) SQL == Python")
            # case-insensitive contains: "NORTH" matches North and north
            sql, py = both([{"field": "sub", "agg": "count"}],
                           filters=[{"field": "sub", "op": "contains",
                                     "value": "NORTH"}])
            eq(py, {"A": 1, "B": 1}, "python contains is case-insensitive")
            eq(sql, py, "contains SQL == Python (case-insensitive)")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_pivot_date_equals_filter():
        # DATE-typed DuckDB columns: equals (plain + SQL-quoted paste) and
        # range ops must not CAST the ISO string through DOUBLE / re-quote it
        # into an invalid DATE literal.
        if not feats.get("duckdb"):
            return
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
            p = os.path.join(dd, "dates.csv")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("d,amt,cat\n2026-01-26,10,A\n2026-01-27,20,B\n"
                        "2026-01-26,5,B\n")
            s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="PD")
            kind = s.get_duckdb().execute(
                "SELECT typeof(d) FROM PD LIMIT 1")[1][0][0]
            eq(str(kind).upper(), "DATE", "fixture column is DATE-typed")

            def _sum_by_cat(filters):
                out = s.pivot({
                    "table": "PD", "engine": "duckdb", "rows": ["cat"],
                    "values": [{"field": "amt", "agg": "sum"}],
                    "filters": filters,
                })
                need(not out.get("error"),
                     "pivot date filter error: %s" % out.get("error"))
                return {row[0]: float(row[1]) for row in out["rows"]}

            eq(_sum_by_cat([{"field": "d", "op": "equals",
                             "value": "2026-01-26"}]),
               {"A": 10.0, "B": 5.0}, "date equals YYYY-MM-DD")
            eq(_sum_by_cat([{"field": "d", "op": "equals",
                             "value": "'2026-01-26'"}]),
               {"A": 10.0, "B": 5.0},
               "date equals tolerates SQL-quoted paste")
            # Generated WHERE must not re-quote a pasted SQL date literal.
            where_q = Session._pivot_where(
                [{"field": "d", "op": "equals", "value": "'2026-01-26'"}],
                {"d": 0}, lambda i: '"d"',
                lambda c: "TRY_CAST(%s AS DOUBLE)" % c)
            need("'''2026-01-26'''" not in where_q,
                 "pivot WHERE must not emit '''2026-01-26'''")
            need("'2026-01-26'" in where_q,
                 "pivot WHERE keeps a single-quoted ISO date")
            eq(_sum_by_cat([{"field": "d", "op": "gte",
                             "value": "2026-01-26"}]),
               {"A": 10.0, "B": 25.0}, "date gte (not DOUBLE cast)")
            eq(_sum_by_cat([{"field": "d", "op": "between",
                             "value": "2026-01-26",
                             "value2": "2026-01-26"}]),
               {"A": 10.0, "B": 5.0}, "date between same day")
            # Numeric filters still use the castnum path.
            eq(_sum_by_cat([{"field": "amt", "op": "gt", "value": "10"}]),
               {"B": 20.0}, "numeric gt unchanged")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_pivot_malformed_data():
        # The pivot modal must never crash on malformed / hostile result data:
        # non-numeric / NaN / Inf strings under sum, mixed-type value columns,
        # NULLs in row/col/value, quote+unicode column-header values, a
        # high-cardinality column dimension (truncated, not exploded), an empty
        # result, and an injection-attempt filter value. Every case returns a
        # clean grid or a clean validation error -- never an exception.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            def rid_for(sql):
                r = s.run_query(sql, target="auto")
                need(not r.get("error"), "setup query: %s" % r.get("error"))
                return r["result_id"]

            def ok(label, res):
                need(isinstance(res, dict), "%s: non-dict %r" % (label, res))
                need(not res.get("error"),
                     "%s: unexpected error %r" % (label, res.get("error")))
                return res

            mal = rid_for(
                "SELECT 'east' AS region, 'q1' AS quarter, '10' AS amount, "
                "'A' AS grp "
                "UNION ALL SELECT 'east','q1','oops','a' "   # non-numeric; A/a
                "UNION ALL SELECT 'west','q2','20','B' "
                "UNION ALL SELECT 'west',NULL,NULL,NULL "    # nulls everywhere
                "UNION ALL SELECT 'east','q2','nan','C' "    # 'nan' string
                "UNION ALL SELECT 'west','q1','inf','C' "    # 'inf' string
                "UNION ALL SELECT NULL,'q1','5','D'")        # null row dim
            base = {"result_id": mal}

            ok("sum over text/nan/inf", s.pivot({
                **base, "rows": ["region"], "cols": ["quarter"],
                "values": [{"field": "amount", "agg": "sum"}]}))
            ok("avg over text/nan/inf", s.pivot({
                **base, "rows": ["region"],
                "values": [{"field": "amount", "agg": "avg"}]}))
            ok("max mixed-type", s.pivot({
                **base, "rows": ["region"],
                "values": [{"field": "amount", "agg": "max"}]}))
            ok("count_distinct text", s.pivot({
                **base, "rows": ["region"],
                "values": [{"field": "grp", "agg": "count_distinct"}]}))
            # Case-only-distinct header values (A/a) and a NULL header must not
            # collide or crash -- the crosstab is assembled in Python, so both
            # survive as distinct output columns.
            cad = ok("case-dup + null headers", s.pivot({
                **base, "rows": ["region"], "cols": ["grp"],
                "values": [{"field": "amount", "agg": "sum"}]}))
            need(len(cad.get("columns") or []) >= 4,
                 "case-differing headers stay distinct: %r" % cad.get("columns"))
            # A filter value with a quote must be escaped, not injected.
            ok("quote-in-filter (no injection)", s.pivot({
                **base, "rows": ["region"],
                "values": [{"field": "amount", "agg": "sum"}],
                "filters": [{"field": "grp", "op": "equals",
                             "value": "O'Brien"}]}))
            # Validation errors are clean, not exceptions.
            need(s.pivot({**base, "rows": ["nope"],
                          "values": [{"field": "amount", "agg": "sum"}]}
                         ).get("error"),
                 "unknown column is a clean error")
            need(s.pivot({**base, "values": [{"field": "amount",
                                              "agg": "sum"}]}).get("error"),
                 "no row/col dims is a clean error")

            # High-cardinality column dimension -> MAXCOLS truncation, not blow-up.
            big = rid_for(
                "WITH RECURSIVE c(i) AS (SELECT 0 UNION ALL "
                "SELECT i+1 FROM c WHERE i < 4999) "
                "SELECT (i % 7) AS k, i AS col, 1 AS v FROM c")
            hc = ok("high-cardinality col truncates", s.pivot({
                "result_id": big, "rows": ["k"], "cols": ["col"],
                "values": [{"field": "v", "agg": "sum"}]}))
            need(hc.get("truncated") and len(hc.get("columns") or []) <= 402,
                 "high-cardinality pivot is capped: cols=%d truncated=%r"
                 % (len(hc.get("columns") or []), hc.get("truncated")))

            # Empty result set.
            emp = ok("empty result", s.pivot({
                "result_id": rid_for("SELECT 1 AS a, 2 AS b WHERE 1=0"),
                "rows": ["a"], "values": [{"field": "b", "agg": "sum"}]}))
            eq(emp.get("row_count"), 0, "empty pivot has zero rows")

            # Quote / unicode values used as column headers.
            uni = rid_for(
                "SELECT 'r' AS r, 'He said \"hi\"' AS grp, 1 AS v "
                "UNION ALL SELECT 'r','a''b',2 "
                "UNION ALL SELECT 'r','éé',3")
            ok("quote/unicode headers", s.pivot({
                "result_id": uni, "rows": ["r"], "cols": ["grp"],
                "values": [{"field": "v", "agg": "sum"}]}))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_sql_str_literal_no_double_quote():
        # Shared quoting helper: bare ISO and already-SQL-quoted ISO must both
        # become a single-quoted literal -- never '''2026-01-26'''. Covers the
        # Pivot / Filter / {{var}} / nodeflow._strlit paths that share it.
        from samql_core import Session, applyvars as A, nodeflow, sqlutil
        for raw in ("2026-01-26", "'2026-01-26'", '"2026-01-26"'):
            lit = sqlutil.sql_str_literal(raw)
            eq(lit, "'2026-01-26'", "sql_str_literal(%r)" % (raw,))
            need("'''" not in lit,
                 "sql_str_literal(%r) must not triple-quote" % (raw,))
        eq(sqlutil.unwrap_sql_quoted_temporal("'hello'"), "'hello'",
           "non-temporal quoted text is left alone")
        eq(A.substitute_text("d = {{as_of}}", {"as_of": "2026-01-26"}),
           "d = '2026-01-26'", "{{as_of}} bare ISO")
        eq(A.substitute_text("d = {{as_of}}", {"as_of": "'2026-01-26'"}),
           "d = '2026-01-26'", "{{as_of}} already-quoted ISO")
        need("'''2026-01-26'''" not in A.substitute_text(
            "d = {{as_of}}", {"as_of": "'2026-01-26'"}),
             "{{as_of}} must not emit '''2026-01-26'''")
        eq(nodeflow._strlit("'2026-01-26'"), "'2026-01-26'",
           "nodeflow._strlit unwraps quoted ISO")
        eq(nodeflow._strlit("O'Brien"), "'O''Brien'",
           "nodeflow._strlit still escapes embedded quotes")
        where = Session._pivot_where(
            [{"field": "d", "op": "equals", "value": "'2026-01-26'"}],
            {"d": 0}, lambda i: '"d"',
            lambda c: "TRY_CAST(%s AS DOUBLE)" % c)
        need("'''2026-01-26'''" not in where,
             "pivot WHERE from shared helper has no triple quote")

    def t_filter_date_equals_no_double_quote():
        # NodeFlow Filter: equals on a DATE column with bare ISO and with a
        # SQL-quoted paste (as the Filter UI / {{var}} path can emit).
        if not feats.get("duckdb"):
            return
        from samql_core import applyvars as A, nodeflow
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()
            p = os.path.join(dd, "nf_dates.csv")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write("d,name\n2026-01-26,a\n2026-01-27,b\n2026-01-26,c\n")
            s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb", base_name="NFD")
            kind = s.get_duckdb().execute(
                "SELECT typeof(d) FROM NFD LIMIT 1")[1][0][0]
            eq(str(kind).upper(), "DATE", "fixture column is DATE-typed")
            src = {"id": "src", "type": "input",
                   "config": {"table": "NFD"}}
            edges = [{"from": {"node": "src", "port": "out"},
                      "to": {"node": "F", "port": "in"}}]

            def _true_names(cond):
                g = {"nodes": [src, {"id": "F", "type": "filter",
                                     "config": {"condition": cond}}],
                     "edges": edges}
                sql = nodeflow.compile_port(
                    g, "F", "true", s.relation_columns, None,
                    engine="duckdb")
                need("'''2026-01-26'''" not in sql,
                     "filter SQL must not contain '''2026-01-26''': %s" % sql)
                need("'2026-01-26'" in sql,
                     "filter SQL keeps a single-quoted ISO date")
                rt = s.run_nodeflow(g, "F", "true")
                need(not rt.get("error"),
                     "filter date equals error: %s" % rt.get("error"))
                return sorted(r[1] for r in rt["rows"])

            eq(_true_names("[d] = '2026-01-26'"), ["a", "c"],
               "filter equals ISO date literal")
            g_var = {
                "nodes": [
                    {"id": "v", "type": "variable",
                     "config": {"vars": [
                         {"name": "as_of", "value": "'2026-01-26'"}]}},
                    src,
                    {"id": "F", "type": "filter",
                     "config": {"condition": "[d] = {{as_of}}"}},
                ],
                "edges": edges,
            }
            rg = A.resolve_graph(g_var)
            fcfg = next(n["config"] for n in rg["nodes"] if n["id"] == "F")
            eq(fcfg["condition"], "[d] = '2026-01-26'",
               "resolve_graph unwraps quoted ISO in {{as_of}}")
            need("'''2026-01-26'''" not in fcfg["condition"],
                 "resolved filter condition must not triple-quote")
            rt = s.run_nodeflow(rg, "F", "true")
            need(not rt.get("error"),
                 "filter {{as_of}} date equals error: %s" % rt.get("error"))
            eq(sorted(r[1] for r in rt["rows"]), ["a", "c"],
               "filter equals via {{as_of}} quoted ISO paste")
            # Bare ISO in the variable (UI default) also works.
            g_bare = {
                "nodes": [
                    {"id": "v", "type": "variable",
                     "config": {"vars": [
                         {"name": "as_of", "value": "2026-01-26"}]}},
                    src,
                    {"id": "F", "type": "filter",
                     "config": {"condition": "[d] = {{as_of}}"}},
                ],
                "edges": edges,
            }
            rg2 = A.resolve_graph(g_bare)
            eq(next(n["config"] for n in rg2["nodes"]
                    if n["id"] == "F")["condition"],
               "[d] = '2026-01-26'", "{{as_of}} bare ISO")
            rt2 = s.run_nodeflow(rg2, "F", "true")
            need(not rt2.get("error"),
                 "filter bare {{as_of}} error: %s" % rt2.get("error"))
            eq(sorted(r[1] for r in rt2["rows"]), ["a", "c"],
               "filter equals via {{as_of}} bare ISO")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_filter_numeric_equals_order_id():
        # Regression: demo_orders-shaped Create Table + Filter
        # ``[order_id] = 101`` (FE simple UI emits bare numeric) must return
        # the matching row on True — not empty from type/quote mismatch.
        from samql_core import nodeflow
        s = Session()
        try:
            cols = ["order_id", "customer_id", "region", "amount", "qty"]
            rows = [
                ["101", "C1", "East", "120", "2"],
                ["102", "C2", "West", "45", "1"],
                ["103", "C1", "East", "80", "3"],
            ]
            g = {
                "nodes": [
                    {"id": "orders", "type": "createtable",
                     "config": {"label": "demo_orders", "columns": cols,
                                "rows": rows, "dest": "sqlite"}},
                    {"id": "F", "type": "filter",
                     "config": {"condition": "[order_id] = 101"}},
                ],
                "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": "orders", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "F", "port": "in"}},
                ],
            }
            sql = nodeflow.compile_port(
                g, "F", "true", s.relation_columns, None, engine="sqlite")
            need('"order_id" = 101' in sql,
                 "filter SQL keeps bare numeric equals: %s" % sql)
            where = sql.split("WHERE", 1)[-1]
            need("'101'" not in where,
                 "filter WHERE must not quote 101 as text: %s" % sql)
            rt = s.run_nodeflow(g, "F", "true")
            need(not rt.get("error"),
                 "filter order_id=101 error: %s" % rt.get("error"))
            eq(rt.get("total_rows"), 1, "filter true: one matching order")
            eq([r[0] for r in rt["rows"]], [101],
               "filter true: order_id 101 row")
            rf = s.run_nodeflow(g, "F", "false")
            need(not rf.get("error"),
                 "filter false error: %s" % rf.get("error"))
            eq(sorted(r[0] for r in rf["rows"]), [102, 103],
               "filter false: non-matching order_ids")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_true_counts():
        # SQLite: the report carries headline totals + a per-field row;
        # the underlying rows are fetched on demand (drilldown / profile),
        # not inlined.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            _recon_fixtures(s, "sqlite")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "L", "right": "R", "keys": ["id"],
                               "compare": ["val"]})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"reconcile error: {rec.get('error')}")
            eq(rec["engine"], "sqlite", "engine field")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq(t["a_only"], 100, "true only-left count")
            eq(t["b_only"], 100, "true only-right count")
            eq(t["non_matching"], 600, "row-level non-matching (val differs)")
            eq(t["matching"], 0, "row-level matching (none clean)")
            eq(t["total"], 800, "total = a_only + b_only + matched(600)")
            need("rows" not in rec, "reconcile must not carry rows inline")
            fields = rec["fields"]
            eq(len(fields), 1, "one field row (val)")
            fv = fields[0]
            eq(fv["field"], "val", "field name")
            eq(fv["non_matching"], 600, "per-field val non-matching")
            eq(fv["matching"], 0, "per-field val matching")
            eq(fv["a_only"], 100, "per-field carries table-level a_only")
            # drill-down: a_only -> 100 pageable rows
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "L", "right": "R",
                                       "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "a_only"})
            need(not d.get("error"), f"drilldown error: {d.get('error')}")
            eq(d["count"], 100, "a_only drilldown count")
            need(d["result_id"], "a_only drilldown should be pageable")
            pg = s.page(d["result_id"], offset=0, limit=5)
            eq(pg["total_rows"], 100, "drilldown pages to true count")
            eq(len(pg["rows"]), 5, "drilldown is pageable")
            # matching bucket is empty here -> null result_id
            dm = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "L", "right": "R",
                                        "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "matching",
                                        "field": "val"})
            eq(dm["count"], 0, "matching drilldown empty")
            need(dm["result_id"] is None, "empty bucket -> null result_id")
            # profile the underlying a_only rows (subquery profiling)
            pr = s.reconcile_profile({"left": "L", "right": "R",
                                      "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "a_only"})
            need("error" not in pr, f"profile error: {pr.get('error')}")
            eq(pr["total_rows"], 100, "profile a_only row count")
            need(any(c["column"] == "id" for c in pr["columns"]),
                 "profile exposes underlying columns")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    @_pinned_engine_mode("dual")
    def t_reconcile_drilldown_spills():
        # A big drill-down must spill to a temp store (DiskBackedRows), not
        # the Python heap, and still page correctly at a deep offset.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE BL AS WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 0 "
                "UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<109999) "
                "SELECT x AS id, x AS val FROM c", target="__local__")
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE BR AS WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 60000 "
                "UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<169999) "
                "SELECT x AS id, x+1 AS val FROM c", target="__local__")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "BL", "right": "BR",
                               "keys": ["id"], "compare": ["val"]})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"reconcile error: {rec.get('error')}")
            eq(rec["totals"]["a_only"], 60000, "large only-left count")
            eq(rec["totals"]["non_matching"], 50000, "large non-matching")
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "BL", "right": "BR",
                                       "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "a_only"})
            eq(d["count"], 60000, "drilldown a_only count")
            store = type(s._results[d["result_id"]].store).__name__
            eq(store, "DiskBackedRows",
               f"large drilldown should spill, got {store}")
            deep = s.page(d["result_id"], offset=59995, limit=5)
            eq(len(deep["rows"]), 5, "deep paging of a spilled drilldown")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_report_balance():
        # Per-field matching / non-matching counts and summed balances, plus
        # row-level tiles, and matching / non-matching drill-downs.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            for tbl, rows in [
                ("A", "(1,'Al','open',100.0),(2,'Bo','open',50.0),"
                      "(3,'Cy','closed',25.0),(4,'Di','open',10.0)"),
                ("B", "(1,'Al','open',100.0),(2,'Bo','closed',50.0),"
                      "(3,'Cy','closed',999.0),(5,'Ed','open',7.0)")]:
                s.run_query(
                    f"CREATE TABLE {tbl} "
                    "(id INTEGER, name TEXT, status TEXT, amt REAL)",
                    target="__local__")
                s.run_query(f"INSERT INTO {tbl} VALUES {rows}",
                            target="__local__")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "A", "right": "B", "keys": ["id"],
                               "compare": ["name", "status"],
                               "balance": "amt"})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"reconcile error: {rec.get('error')}")
            eq(rec["balance_field"], "amt", "balance field echoed")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq((t["a_only"], t["b_only"], t["total"]), (1, 1, 5),
               "totals a_only/b_only/total")
            # only id2 differs (on status) -> row-level non-matching 1
            eq((t["matching"], t["non_matching"]), (2, 1), "row-level tiles")
            byf = {f["field"]: f for f in rec["fields"]}
            eq((byf["name"]["matching"], byf["name"]["non_matching"]), (3, 0),
               "name matches on all shared rows")
            eq((byf["status"]["matching"], byf["status"]["non_matching"]),
               (2, 1), "status differs on id2")
            # balance: status matching = 100+25 = 125 ; non-matching = 50
            need(abs(byf["status"]["sum_matching_balance"] - 125.0) < 1e-9,
                 "status matching balance")
            need(abs(byf["status"]["sum_non_matching_balance"] - 50.0) < 1e-9,
                 "status non-matching balance")
            # drill into the status break -> id2, with A_/B_ columns
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "A", "right": "B",
                                       "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "non_matching",
                                       "field": "status", "balance": "amt"})
            eq(d["count"], 1, "status non-matching drilldown count")
            need(any(c.startswith("A_") for c in d["columns"])
                 and any(c.startswith("B_") for c in d["columns"]),
                 "drilldown exposes A_/B_ columns")
            dm = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "A", "right": "B",
                                        "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "matching",
                                        "field": "status"})
            eq(dm["count"], 2, "status matching drilldown count")
            # error path: a missing table
            err = s.reconcile({"left": "A", "right": "nope", "keys": ["id"]})
            need("error" in err and "not found" in err["error"].lower(),
                 "missing-table error path")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_field_mapping():
        # A field mapping lines up differently-named columns under a canonical
        # name (colmap_a / colmap_b). The report uses canonical names, labels
        # show both originals, and -- the part that broke before -- drill-down
        # and profile resolve through the same per-side columns.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE A "
                        "(acct INTEGER, nm TEXT, stat TEXT, amount REAL)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO A VALUES (1,'Al','open',100.0),"
                        "(2,'Bo','open',50.0),(3,'Cy','closed',25.0),"
                        "(4,'Di','open',10.0)", target="__local__")
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE B "
                        "(account INTEGER, name TEXT, state TEXT, bal REAL)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO B VALUES (1,'Al','open',100.0),"
                        "(2,'Bo','closed',50.0),(3,'Cy','closed',999.0),"
                        "(5,'Ed','open',7.0)", target="__local__")
            cma = {"id": "acct", "name": "nm", "status": "stat",
                   "amount": "amount"}
            cmb = {"id": "account", "name": "name", "status": "state",
                   "amount": "bal"}
            spec = {"left": "A", "right": "B", "keys": ["id"],
                    "compare": ["name", "status"], "balance": "amount",
                    "colmap_a": cma, "colmap_b": cmb}
            rec = s.reconcile(spec)
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"mapped reconcile error: {rec}")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq((t["a_only"], t["b_only"], t["total"]), (1, 1, 5),
               "mapped totals")
            eq((t["matching"], t["non_matching"]), (2, 1),
               "mapped row-level tiles")
            byf = {f["field"]: f for f in rec["fields"]}
            eq(byf["name"]["label"], "name (A: nm / B: name)", "name label")
            eq(byf["status"]["label"], "status (A: stat / B: state)",
               "status label")
            eq((byf["status"]["matching"], byf["status"]["non_matching"]),
               (2, 1), "mapped status per-field counts")
            need(abs(byf["status"]["sum_non_matching_balance"] - 50.0) < 1e-9,
                 "mapped status non-matching balance")
            # drill-down through the mapping (full A row for a_only; canonical
            # key + A_/B_ cols for the field buckets)
            da = s.reconcile_drilldown({**spec, "bucket": "a_only"})
            eq(da["count"], 1, "mapped a_only drilldown count")
            eq(da["columns"], ["acct", "nm", "stat", "amount"],
               "a_only drilldown exposes A's real columns")
            need(s.page(da["result_id"], offset=0, limit=5)["total_rows"] == 1,
                 "mapped a_only drilldown pages")
            dn = s.reconcile_drilldown({**spec, "bucket": "non_matching",
                                        "field": "status"})
            eq(dn["count"], 1, "mapped status non-matching drilldown count")
            eq(dn["columns"],
               ["id", "A_status", "B_status", "A_amount", "B_amount"],
               "mapped field drilldown columns")
            # profile through the mapping
            pr = s.reconcile_profile({**spec, "bucket": "non_matching",
                                      "field": "status"})
            need("error" not in pr and pr["total_rows"] == 1,
                 f"mapped profile: {pr}")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_no_compare_no_materialize():
        # Keys only (no compare fields) -> the report still returns headline
        # totals with an empty field list, and -- the core optimization --
        # reconcile() materializes NO rows (the result cache is untouched;
        # only a later drill-down spills rows).
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE A (id INTEGER, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO A VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b'),(3,'c')",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE B (id INTEGER, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO B VALUES (2,'b'),(3,'X'),(4,'d')",
                        target="__local__")
            before = len(s._results)
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "A", "right": "B", "keys": ["id"]})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"no-compare reconcile: {rec}")
            eq(rec["fields"], [], "no-compare -> empty field list")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq((t["a_only"], t["b_only"], t["total"]), (1, 1, 4),
               "no-compare totals")
            eq(len(s._results), before,
               "reconcile must not materialize any rows into the cache")
            # a compare run also materializes nothing
            before2 = len(s._results)
            s.reconcile({"left": "A", "right": "B", "keys": ["id"],
                         "compare": ["v"]})
            eq(len(s._results), before2,
               "field-level reconcile must not materialize rows either")
            # but a (non-empty) drill-down DOES add exactly one cached result
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "A", "right": "B",
                                       "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "a_only"})
            need(d.get("result_id"), f"a_only drilldown should have rows: {d}")
            eq(len(s._results), before2 + 1,
               "a non-empty drill-down caches exactly one result")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_multikey_and_nulls():
        # Composite key + NULL handling: compares are text via
        # COALESCE(CAST(.. AS VARCHAR),''), so NULL==NULL counts as matching
        # and NULL vs a value counts as non-matching.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE A (k1 INTEGER, k2 TEXT, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO A VALUES (1,'x',NULL),(2,'y','a'),"
                        "(3,'z','m')", target="__local__")
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE B (k1 INTEGER, k2 TEXT, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO B VALUES (1,'x',NULL),(2,'y',NULL),"
                        "(3,'z','m')", target="__local__")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "A", "right": "B",
                               "keys": ["k1", "k2"], "compare": ["v"]})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"multikey reconcile: {rec}")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq((t["a_only"], t["b_only"], t["total"]), (0, 0, 3),
               "multikey totals (all keys match)")
            vf = {f["field"]: f for f in rec["fields"]}["v"]
            # row1 NULL==NULL -> match; row2 'a' vs NULL -> differ; row3 match
            eq((vf["matching"], vf["non_matching"]), (2, 1),
               "NULL==NULL matches, NULL vs value differs")
            # drill the one break on the composite key
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "A", "right": "B",
                                       "keys": ["k1", "k2"],
                                       "bucket": "non_matching", "field": "v"})
            eq(d["count"], 1, "multikey non-matching drilldown count")
            eq(d["columns"], ["k1", "k2", "A_v", "B_v"],
               "multikey drilldown carries both key columns")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_empty_bucket_and_errors():
        # Empty buckets free immediately (result_id None, count 0) and profile
        # cleanly; bad specs return an error rather than raising.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE A (id INTEGER, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO A VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b')",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE B (id INTEGER, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO B VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b')",
                        target="__local__")
            base = {"left": "A", "right": "B", "keys": ["id"]}
            # identical key sets -> a_only / b_only empty
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({**base, "bucket": "a_only"})
            need(d.get("result_id") is None and d["count"] == 0,
                 f"empty a_only drilldown should free at once: {d}")
            p = s.reconcile_profile({**base, "bucket": "b_only"})
            need("error" not in p and p["total_rows"] == 0,
                 f"empty b_only profile should be clean: {p}")
            # error paths (no exception, structured error)
            need(s.reconcile({"left": "A", "right": "B",
                              "keys": []}).get("error"),
                 "missing keys should error")
            need(s.reconcile({"left": "A", "right": "nope",
                              "keys": ["id"]}).get("error"),
                 "missing table should error")
            need(s.reconcile_drilldown({**base, "bucket": "bogus"}).get(
                "error"), "invalid bucket should error")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_profile_buckets():
        # Profile resolves for every bucket (each builds a different label /
        # SQL shape): a_only (full A row), matching (key + A_/B_ values).
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE A (id INTEGER, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO A VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b'),(3,'c')",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE B (id INTEGER, v TEXT)",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO B VALUES (2,'b'),(3,'X'),(4,'d')",
                        target="__local__")
            base = {"left": "A", "right": "B", "keys": ["id"],
                    "compare": ["v"]}
            pa = s.reconcile_profile({**base, "bucket": "a_only"})
            need("error" not in pa and pa["total_rows"] == 1,
                 f"a_only profile: {pa}")
            need("id" in [c["column"] for c in pa["columns"]],
                 "a_only profile exposes the row columns")
            pm = s.reconcile_profile({**base, "bucket": "matching",
                                      "field": "v"})
            need("error" not in pm and pm["total_rows"] == 1,
                 f"matching profile (id 2): {pm}")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_json():
        # JSON files flatten into tables that reconcile like any other.
        s = _fresh_session()
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

        def w(n, t):
            p = os.path.join(dd, n)
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(t)
            return p
        try:
            s.load_file(w("jl.json", json.dumps(
                [{"id": 1, "v": "a"}, {"id": 2, "v": "b"},
                 {"id": 3, "v": "c"}])), destination="sqlite", base_name="jl")
            s.load_file(w("jr.json", json.dumps(
                [{"id": 2, "v": "b"}, {"id": 3, "v": "X"},
                 {"id": 4, "v": "d"}])), destination="sqlite", base_name="jr")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "jl", "right": "jr",
                               "keys": ["id"], "compare": ["v"]})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"reconcile error: {rec.get('error')}")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq(t["a_only"], 1, "json only-left")
            eq(t["b_only"], 1, "json only-right")
            eq(t["non_matching"], 1, "json row non-matching (id3 v differs)")
            eq(t["matching"], 1, "json row matching (id2)")
            byf = {f["field"]: f for f in rec["fields"]}
            eq((byf["v"]["matching"], byf["v"]["non_matching"]), (1, 1),
               "json per-field v counts")
            # an identical self-compare: no breaks, all matched
            same = s.reconcile({"left": "jl", "right": "jl",
                                "keys": ["id"], "compare": ["v"]})
            eq(same["totals"]["a_only"], 0, "self only-left == 0")
            eq(same["totals"]["non_matching"], 0, "self non-matching == 0")
            eq(same["totals"]["matching"], 3, "self matching == all rows")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_duckdb():
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            _recon_fixtures(s, "duckdb")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "L", "right": "R", "keys": ["id"],
                               "compare": ["val"]})
            need(not rec.get("error"), f"reconcile error: {rec.get('error')}")
            eq(rec["engine"], "duckdb", "engine should be duckdb")
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq(t["a_only"], 100, "duckdb only-left count")
            eq(t["b_only"], 100, "duckdb only-right count")
            eq(t["non_matching"], 600, "duckdb non-matching count")
            eq(t["total"], 800, "duckdb total")
            d = s.reconcile_drilldown({"left": "L", "right": "R",
                                       "keys": ["id"], "bucket": "a_only"})
            need(d["result_id"], "duckdb drilldown should be pageable")
            eq(s.page(d["result_id"], offset=0, limit=5)["total_rows"], 100,
               "duckdb drilldown pages to true count")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_local_temp_store_on_disk():
        # Heavy ops (EXCEPT / ORDER BY / hash joins -- e.g. a large
        # reconcile) build temporary b-trees; the local engine must keep
        # them on disk (temp_store=FILE, 1) so RAM stays bounded.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            v = s.db._conn.execute("PRAGMA temp_store").fetchone()[0]
            eq(v, 1, "local engine temp_store should be FILE(1), not MEMORY")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_chart_pivot_pushdown():
        # Charts/pivots over a spilled result must aggregate in SQL (bounded
        # memory) and match the Python reference exactly. This test is about
        # the SQLITE spill store (DiskBackedRows) + pushdown parity, so route
        # by table location (dual) -- the default always-DuckDB preference
        # would send the unpinned __local__ CREATE to DuckDB and swap the
        # store type out from under the assertions.
        s = _fresh_session()
        s.engine_mode = "dual"
        try:
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE big AS WITH RECURSIVE c(x) AS (SELECT 1 "
                "UNION ALL SELECT x+1 FROM c WHERE x<120000) "
                "SELECT x AS id, (x%50) AS cat, (x%7) AS grp, (x*1.0) AS amt "
                "FROM c", target="__local__")
            rid = s.run_query("SELECT * FROM big",
                              target="__local__")["result_id"]
            store = s._results[rid].store
            cols = s._results[rid].cols
            eq(type(store).__name__, "DiskBackedRows",
               "result should spill (exercises the SQL pushdown path)")
            out = s.chart_data({"result_id": rid, "chart_type": "bar",
                                "x": "cat", "y": "amt", "agg": "sum"})
            eq(len(out["series"][0]["values"]), 50, "bar: 50 groups")
            eq(out["labels"][:3], ["0", "1", "2"], "bar labels ordered by x")
            h = s.chart_data({"result_id": rid, "chart_type": "histogram",
                              "x": "amt", "bins": 10})
            eq(len(h["series"][0]["values"]), 10, "histogram: 10 bins")
            eq(sum(h["series"][0]["values"]), 120000,
               "histogram counts every row")
            pv = s.pivot({"result_id": rid, "rows": ["cat"], "cols": ["grp"],
                          "value": "amt", "agg": "sum"})
            eq(pv["row_count"], 50, "pivot: 50 rows")
            eq(len(pv["columns"]), 1 + 7, "pivot: key + 7 column groups")
            # table source pushes down too, identically
            ot = s.chart_data({"table": "big", "engine": "sqlite",
                               "chart_type": "bar", "x": "cat", "y": "amt",
                               "agg": "sum"})
