        eq(A.expand_var_functions("today()"), "current_date",
           "TODAY() maps to current_date (case-insensitive)")
        eq(A.expand_var_functions("UPPER(x)"), "UPPER(x)",
           "a call WITH arguments is never rewritten")
        eq(A.expand_var_functions("my_fn()"), "my_fn()",
           "an unknown zero-arg call is left for the engine")

        # scalars render as clean, dialect-portable literals
        eq(A.render_scalar(_dtv.datetime(2026, 7, 22, 19, 55, 41, 123456)),
           "2026-07-22 19:55:41",
           "a timestamp drops microseconds/'+00' so it drops into a literal")
        eq(A.render_scalar(_dtv.date(2026, 7, 22)), "2026-07-22",
           "a date renders ISO")
        eq(A.render_scalar(None), "", "NULL renders as empty text")

        # a row with no kind stays literal text (saved workflows keep meaning)
        legacy = {"nodes": [{"id": "v", "type": "variable", "config": {
            "vars": [{"name": "a", "value": "TODAY()"}]}}]}
        s = Session()
        try:
            ev = s._variable_expr_evaluator()
            eq(A.collect_vars(legacy, evaluate=ev), {"a": "TODAY()"},
               "a row without kind='expr' is NOT evaluated (back-compat)")

            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "v", "type": "variable", "config": {"vars": [
                    {"name": "today", "value": "TODAY()", "kind": "expr"},
                    {"name": "n", "value": "40 + 2", "kind": "expr"},
                    {"name": "plain", "value": "literal", "kind": "text"}]}},
                {"id": "q", "type": "sql", "config": {
                    "sql": "SELECT '${today}' AS d, ${n} AS n, "
                           "'${plain}' AS p"}},
            ], "edges": []}
            ctx = A.collect_vars(g, evaluate=ev)
            eq(ctx["n"], "42", "an arithmetic expression evaluates to a scalar")
            eq(ctx["plain"], "literal", "a text row is not evaluated")
            eq(ctx["today"], _dtv.date.today().isoformat(),
               "TODAY() evaluates to the current date")

            r = s.run_nodeflow(g, "q", "out")
            need(not r.get("error"),
                 "expression-variable flow runs: %s" % r.get("error"))
            row = list(r["rows"][0])
            eq(row[0], _dtv.date.today().isoformat(),
               "the evaluated date landed in the SQL result")
            eq(int(row[1]), 42, "the evaluated number landed as a bare number")
            eq(row[2], "literal", "the text row is unchanged")

            # a broken expression names the offending variable
            bad = {"nodes": [{"id": "v", "type": "variable", "config": {
                "vars": [{"name": "oops", "value": "NOT_A_FUNC(",
                          "kind": "expr"}]}}]}
            try:
                A.collect_vars(bad, evaluate=ev)
                need(False, "a broken expression must raise")
            except Exception as e:
                need("oops" in str(e),
                     "the error names the offending variable: %s" % e)
            # the lenient (schema-probe) evaluator never raises while typing
            lax = A.collect_vars(
                bad, evaluate=s._variable_expr_evaluator(lenient=True))
            eq(lax, {"oops": "NOT_A_FUNC("},
               "a probe keeps the raw text instead of raising")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_sqlserver_node_resolves_variables():
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb is not installed [QUARANTINE]")
        # The SQL Server node's interactive Fetch must resolve ${name} the same
        # way a full run does -- fetch_source_node used to drop `graph` for
        # sqlserver (only apinode got it), so a WHERE clause kept a literal
        # "${as_of}" and the remote query filtered on nonsense.
        import inspect as _insp
        from samql_core.session import Session as _S
        src = _insp.getsource(_S.fetch_source_node)
        need("graph=graph" in src.split('"sqlserver"')[1].split("if ")[0],
             "fetch_source_node passes the graph to the SQL Server fetch")
        sig = _insp.signature(_S.fetch_sqlserver_node)
        need("graph" in sig.parameters,
             "fetch_sqlserver_node accepts a graph for variable resolution")

        # the query template resolves against a variable node, expression rows
        # included, and lands as a plain literal the remote dialect can parse
        from samql_core import applyvars as A
        s = Session()
        try:
            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "v", "type": "variable", "config": {"vars": [
                    {"name": "as_of", "value": "TODAY()", "kind": "expr"},
                    {"name": "region", "value": "EMEA"}]}},
                {"id": "ss", "type": "sqlserver", "config": {
                    "query": "SELECT * FROM Orders WHERE OrderDate >= "
                             "'${as_of}' AND Region = {{region}}"}},
            ], "edges": []}
            rg = A.resolve_graph(g, evaluate=s._variable_expr_evaluator())
            q = rg["nodes"][1]["config"]["query"]
            import datetime as _d
            need(_d.date.today().isoformat() in q,
                 "the expression variable resolved into the query: %s" % q)
            need("'EMEA'" in q,
                 "{{name}} auto-quoted the text value: %s" % q)
            need("${" not in q and "{{" not in q,
                 "no unresolved tokens remain: %s" % q)
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_flow_write_append():
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb is not installed [QUARANTINE]")
        # the write node's overwrite (default) / append modes, and an idempotent
        # append (delete-by-key then insert) so re-running doesn't duplicate.
        # Unpinned SQL source materialises on the write destination (DuckDB).
        from samql_core.session import DUCKDB_TARGET
        vals = "(VALUES (1, 'a'), (2, 'a'), (3, 'b'), (4, 'b'), (5, 'c'))"

        def graph(cat, mode, keys=None, dest=None):
            cfg = {"name": "acc_t", "mode": mode}
            if keys is not None:
                cfg["replace_keys"] = keys
            if dest is not None:
                cfg["dest"] = dest
            sql = ("WITH t(id, cat) AS %s "
                   "SELECT id, cat FROM t WHERE cat = '%s'" % (vals, cat))
            return {"nodes": [
                {"id": "src", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql": sql}},
                {"id": "w", "type": "write", "config": cfg}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "src", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}

        s = Session()
        try:
            r = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(graph("a", "overwrite"), "w", "acc_t")
            need(r.get("ok"), "overwrite ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("engine"), "duckdb", "unpinned write defaults to DuckDB")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 2, "overwrite wrote the two 'a' rows")
            eq(r.get("mode"), "overwrite", "mode echoed back")
            eq(s.run_query("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM acc_t",
                           target=DUCKDB_TARGET)["rows"][0][0], 2,
               "rows land in DuckDB")
            r = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(graph("b", "append"), "w", "acc_t")
            need(r.get("ok"), "append ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 4, "append added the two 'b' rows -> 4")
            # re-append the same 'b' rows keyed on id -> delete-then-insert, no dup
            r = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(
                graph("b", "append", keys=["id"]), "w", "acc_t")
            need(r.get("ok"), "idempotent append ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 4, "idempotent re-append by id did not duplicate")
            # plain append (no keys) of the 'c' row grows the table
            r = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(graph("c", "append"), "w", "acc_t")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 5, "plain append added the 'c' row -> 5")
            # bad replace key is reported, not silently ignored
            r = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(
                graph("b", "append", keys=["nope"]), "w", "acc_t")
            need(r.get("error") and "nope" in r["error"],
                 "unknown replace-key column is reported")
            # overwrite resets the table
            r = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(graph("a", "overwrite"), "w", "acc_t")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 2, "overwrite reset the table to the two 'a' rows")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_flow_write_overwrite_input_change():
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb is not installed [QUARANTINE]")
        # Write overwrite must replace destination contents when the Input
        # table (or upstream shape) changes — not keep the first-run rows,
        # and not leave a file-origin watch that can restore the old CSV.
        from samql_core.session import DUCKDB_TARGET
        import tempfile, os, csv, time

        def graph(table, dest="dest_w", mode="overwrite"):
            return {"nodes": [
                {"id": "i", "type": "input", "config": {"table": table}},
                {"id": "w", "type": "write",
                 "config": {"name": dest, "mode": mode}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "i", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}

        s = Session()
        try:
            s.set_fresh_run(False)
            s.flow_cache = True
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE src_a AS "
                "SELECT 1 AS id, 'a' AS v", target=DUCKDB_TARGET)
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE src_b AS "
                "SELECT 2 AS id, 'b' AS v UNION ALL SELECT 3, 'c'",
                target=DUCKDB_TARGET)
            r1 = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(graph("src_a"), "w", "dest_w")
            need(r1.get("ok"), "first overwrite: %s" % r1.get("error"))
            eq(r1.get("engine"), "duckdb",
               "DuckDB-input write stores on DuckDB")
            eq(r1.get("rows"), 1, "first write one row")
            rows1 = s.run_query(
                "SELECT * FROM dest_w ORDER BY id", target=DUCKDB_TARGET)
            eq(rows1.get("rows"), [[1, "a"]], "dest starts as src_a")

            r2 = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(graph("src_b"), "w", "dest_w")
            need(r2.get("ok"), "overwrite after input change: %s"
                 % r2.get("error"))
            eq(r2.get("mode"), "overwrite", "mode still overwrite")
            eq(r2.get("engine"), "duckdb", "overwrite stays on DuckDB")
            eq(r2.get("rows"), 2, "dest row count follows new upstream")
            rows2 = s.run_query(
                "SELECT * FROM dest_w ORDER BY id", target=DUCKDB_TARGET)
            eq(rows2.get("rows"), [[2, "b"], [3, "c"]],
               "overwrite replaced dest with src_b rows "
               "(_clear_write_destination on DuckDB)")

            # Schema change on overwrite (not append-aligned NULLs).
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE src_c AS "
                "SELECT 9 AS id, 'z' AS v, 1.5 AS amt",
                target=DUCKDB_TARGET)
            r3 = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(graph("src_c"), "w", "dest_w")
            need(r3.get("ok"), "overwrite schema change: %s" % r3.get("error"))
            cols = s.run_query(
                "SELECT * FROM dest_w", target=DUCKDB_TARGET).get("columns")
            need(cols and "amt" in cols,
                 "overwrite replaced schema with new upstream columns")

            # File-backed destination: overwrite must detach origin watch so
            # a later file edit cannot restore the pre-write CSV.
            td = tempfile.mkdtemp()
            p = os.path.join(td, "sales.csv")
            with open(p, "w", newline="") as fh:
                w = csv.writer(fh)
                w.writerow(["id", "v"])
                w.writerow([1, "from_file"])
            sales = s.load_file(
                p, destination="duckdb", base_name="sales")[0]["name"]
            r4 = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(
                graph("src_b", dest=sales), "w", sales)
            need(r4.get("ok"), "overwrite file-backed: %s" % r4.get("error"))
            eq(s.duckdb.table_sources.get(sales), "nodeflow",
               "write marks destination as nodeflow")
            ow = getattr(s, "_origin_watch", None)
            need(ow is not None, "origin watch present")
            need(ow.path_for("duckdb", sales) is None,
                 "overwrite unregisters file-origin watch")
            with open(p, "w", newline="") as fh:
                fh.write("id,v\n1,REVERTED\n2,X\n")
            time.sleep(0.05)
            os.utime(p, None)
            s.tables_tree()
            got = s.run_query(
                'SELECT * FROM "%s" ORDER BY id' % sales,
                target=DUCKDB_TARGET).get("rows")
            eq(got, [[2, "b"], [3, "c"]],
               "watcher must not restore CSV over nodeflow overwrite")

            # Append still grows / fills missing columns (not a full replace).
            # dest_w currently has the single src_c row (id,v,amt); append
            # adds src_d (id,v) with amt=NULL → 2 rows, schema kept.
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE src_d AS "
                "SELECT 4 AS id, 'd' AS v", target=DUCKDB_TARGET)
            r5 = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(
                graph("src_d", dest="dest_w", mode="append"), "w", "dest_w")
            need(r5.get("ok"), "append preserved: %s" % r5.get("error"))
            eq(r5.get("rows"), 2,
               "append added a row without wiping the prior overwrite")
            rows5 = s.run_query(
                "SELECT id, v FROM dest_w ORDER BY id",
                target=DUCKDB_TARGET).get("rows")
            eq(rows5, [[4, "d"], [9, "z"]],
               "append kept prior overwrite row and added the new one")

            # Temp-name shadow + VIEW destination: overwrite must still land.
            s.duckdb.execute(
                "CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE shadow_t AS "
                "SELECT 1 AS id, 'old' AS v")
            s.duckdb.execute(
                "CREATE TEMP TABLE shadow_t AS "
                "SELECT 99 AS id, 'temp' AS v")
            r6 = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(
                graph("src_a", dest="shadow_t"), "w", "shadow_t")
            need(r6.get("ok"), "overwrite through temp shadow: %s"
                 % r6.get("error"))
            eq(s.run_query(
                "SELECT * FROM shadow_t", target=DUCKDB_TARGET).get("rows"),
               [[1, "a"]], "overwrite replaced main table despite temp shadow")

            s.duckdb.execute("DROP TABLE IF EXISTS view_dest")
            s.duckdb.execute(
                "CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW view_dest AS "
                "SELECT 1 AS id, 'view' AS v")
            r7 = s.run_nodeflow_to_table(
                graph("src_b", dest="view_dest"), "w", "view_dest")
            need(r7.get("ok"), "overwrite view destination: %s"
                 % r7.get("error"))
            eq(s.run_query(
                "SELECT * FROM view_dest ORDER BY id",
                target=DUCKDB_TARGET).get("rows"),
               [[2, "b"], [3, "c"]],
               "overwrite replaced a VIEW with a real table from upstream")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_flow_filebrowser():
        # the dynamic file browser compiles to a DuckDB glob reader: the path
        # pattern (with ${vars} already resolved) is read directly, with a
        # filename column for provenance. SQLite can't read files -> clear error.
        from samql_core import nodeflow, applyvars

        def fb_sql(pattern, engine, source_col=None):
            cfg = {"pattern": pattern}
            if source_col is not None:
                cfg["source_column"] = source_col
            g = {"nodes": [{"id": "fb", "type": "filebrowser", "config": cfg}],
                 "edges": []}
            return nodeflow.compile_port(g, "fb", "out", lambda s: [], None,
                                         engine)

        # CSV glob -> read_csv_auto with filename + union_by_name; filename hidden
        sql = fb_sql("/data/*.csv", "duckdb")
        need("read_csv_auto('/data/*.csv'" in sql, "csv glob -> read_csv_auto")
        need("filename=true" in sql, "filename column requested (provenance)")
        need("union_by_name=true" in sql, "union_by_name for schema drift")
        need("EXCLUDE (filename)" in sql, "filename hidden when no source column")
        # extension routing
        need("read_parquet(" in fb_sql("/d/*.parquet", "duckdb"),
             "parquet -> read_parquet")
        need("read_json_auto(" in fb_sql("/d/data.json", "duckdb"),
             "json -> read_json_auto")
        # a source column surfaces DuckDB's filename under that name
        psql = fb_sql("/d/*.csv", "duckdb", source_col="src")
        need('RENAME (filename AS "src")' in psql,
             "source column renames filename: %s" % psql)
        # a single quote in the path is doubled (kept inside the SQL string)
        qsql = fb_sql("/d/o'brien/*.csv", "duckdb")
        need("/d/o''brien/*.csv" in qsql, "single quote in path is escaped")
        # ${var} resolves into the glob via the normal substitution pass
        g = {"nodes": [
            {"id": "v", "type": "variable", "config": {"vars": [
                {"name": "as_of", "value": "2026-06-01"}]}},
            {"id": "fb", "type": "filebrowser",
             "config": {"pattern": "/d/tx_${as_of}.csv"}}], "edges": []}
        rg = applyvars.resolve_graph(g)
        sql = nodeflow.compile_port(rg, "fb", "out", lambda s: [], None,
                                    "duckdb")
        need("tx_2026-06-01.csv" in sql, "var resolved into the glob: %s" % sql)
        # SQLite can't read files from SQL -> a clear, DuckDB-pointing error
        try:
            fb_sql("/d/*.csv", "sqlite")
            need(False, "sqlite filebrowser should raise")
        except nodeflow.NodeflowError as e:
            need("DuckDB" in str(e), "sqlite error names DuckDB: %s" % e)
        # an empty pattern is reported, not compiled into a broken read
        try:
            fb_sql("", "duckdb")
            need(False, "empty pattern should raise")
        except nodeflow.NodeflowError:
            pass

    def t_flow_apinode():
        # the API node fetches JSON (here via an injected fetcher -- no network),
        # loads it into a hidden table, and reads it like an input. ${vars} in
        # the URL and params resolve from the graph before the call.
        g = {"nodes": [
            {"id": "v", "type": "variable", "config": {"vars": [
                {"name": "region", "value": "us"}]}},
            {"id": "api", "type": "apinode", "config": {
                "url": "https://x.test/${region}/items",
                "params": [{"key": "limit", "value": "${region}"}],
                "json_path": ""}},
            {"id": "f", "type": "select", "config": {}},
        ], "edges": [{"from": {"node": "api", "port": "out"},
                      "to": {"node": "f", "port": "in"}}]}
        s = Session()
        try:
            captured = {}

            def fake(url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw):
                captured["url"] = url
                captured["auth_user"] = auth_user
                return (200, "application/json",
                        [{"id": 1, "name": "a"}, {"id": 2, "name": "b"}],
                        "", None)

            s._api_fetcher = fake
            r = s.fetch_api_node("api", g["nodes"][1]["config"], graph=g)
            need(r.get("ok"), "api fetch ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 2, "two records loaded")
            need("name" in (r.get("columns") or []), "columns include 'name'")
            need(captured["url"] == "https://x.test/us/items?limit=us",
                 "URL + param resolved the ${region} var: %s" % captured["url"])
            # the node now references its hidden table -> the flow reads it
            g["nodes"][1]["config"]["table"] = r["table"]
            rr = s.run_nodeflow(g, "api", "out")
            need(not rr.get("error"), "apinode flow runs: %s" % rr.get("error"))
            eq(rr.get("total_rows"), 2, "apinode flow returns the two rows")
            # a missing URL is a clear error, not a crash
            bad = s.fetch_api_node("api2", {"url": ""}, graph=g)
            need(bad.get("error"), "empty URL reported")
            # a fetcher error is surfaced
            s._api_fetcher = lambda *a, **k: (None, "", None, "", "boom")
            er = s.fetch_api_node("api3", {"url": "https://x.test/d"}, graph=g)
            need(er.get("error") and "boom" in er["error"],
                 "fetch error surfaced: %s" % er.get("error"))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_apinode_secret():
        # the basic-auth password comes from the secret store by key and is
        # never read from the saved config when a key is set.
        from samql_core.secretstore import SecretStore
        prot = (lambda txt: ("enc:" + txt).encode("utf-8"),
                lambda blob: bytes(blob).decode("utf-8")[4:])
        store = SecretStore(protector=prot)
        need(store.available, "test secret store is available")
        store.set("apinode:api1", "s3cret")
        eq(store.get("apinode:api1"), "s3cret", "secret round-trips")
        s = Session()
        try:
            s._secrets = store
            captured = {}

            def fake(url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw):
                captured["auth_pass"] = auth_pass
                captured["auth_user"] = auth_user
                return (200, "application/json", [{"x": 1}], "", None)

            s._api_fetcher = fake
            cfg = {"url": "https://x.test/d", "auth_user": "u",
                   "secret_key": "apinode:api1",
                   "auth_pass": "WRONG-inline"}
            r = s.fetch_api_node("api1", cfg)
            need(r.get("ok"), "fetch ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(captured["auth_user"], "u", "username passed through")
            eq(captured["auth_pass"], "s3cret",
               "password resolved from the store, not the inline config")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_flow_iterator():
        # the iterator loops a driver's values, runs the body each pass with the
        # loop var set, and appends into one accumulator table.
        s = Session()
        try:
            def iter_graph(values, table, **extra):
                cfg = {"var": "i", "table": table,
                       "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": values}}
                cfg.update(extra)
                return {"nodes": [
                    {"id": "body", "type": "sql",
                     "config": {"sql": "SELECT ${i} AS n"}},
                    {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": cfg}],
                    "edges": [{"from": {"node": "body", "port": "out"},
                               "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}

            # list driver -> three rows accumulated
            r = s.run_iterator(iter_graph(["1", "2", "3"], "acc_it"), "it")
            need(r.get("ok"), "iterator (list) ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("passes"), 3, "three passes")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 3, "accumulator has three rows")
            # the accumulator is a real, queryable table
            rr = s.run_nodeflow({"nodes": [
                {"id": "in", "type": "input",
                 "config": {"table": r["table"]}}], "edges": []}, "in", "out")
            eq(rr.get("total_rows"), 3, "accumulator readable via an Input node")
            # re-running with reset_first (default) rebuilds rather than doubling
            r2 = s.run_iterator(iter_graph(["1", "2", "3"], "acc_it"), "it")
            eq(r2.get("rows"), 3, "re-run with reset stays at three rows")
            # with reset off, a re-run accumulates across runs -- the opt-in
            # "keep adding" mode behind the inspector checkbox
            s.run_iterator(
                iter_graph(["1", "2", "3"], "acc_keep", reset_first=False),
                "it")
            rk = s.run_iterator(
                iter_graph(["1", "2", "3"], "acc_keep", reset_first=False),
                "it")
            eq(rk.get("rows"), 6, "re-run with reset off doubles (accumulates)")

            # continue-on-error skips the one bad value, keeps the rest
            re = s.run_iterator(
                iter_graph(["1", "2", "oops", "4"], "acc_err",
                           continue_on_error=True), "it")
            eq(re.get("passes"), 3, "three good passes (bad value skipped)")
            eq(len(re.get("errors") or []), 1, "one error recorded")
            eq(re.get("rows"), 3, "accumulator has the three good rows")
            need(re.get("ok"), "continue-on-error run is ok overall")
            # without it, the same flow stops at the bad value
            rs = s.run_iterator(
                iter_graph(["1", "2", "oops", "4"], "acc_stop",
                           continue_on_error=False), "it")
            eq(rs.get("passes"), 2, "stops after the two good passes")
            need(not rs.get("ok"), "stop-on-error run is not ok")

            # column driver: distinct values of a loaded table's column
            s.run_nodeflow_to_table({"nodes": [
                {"id": "s", "type": "sql", "config": {
                    "sql": "WITH t(c) AS (VALUES ('a'),('a'),('b')) "
                           "SELECT c FROM t"}},
                {"id": "w", "type": "write", "config": {
                    "name": "cats", "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "s", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}, "w", "cats")
            rc = s.run_iterator({"nodes": [
                {"id": "body", "type": "sql",
                 "config": {"sql": "SELECT '${c}' AS cat"}},
                {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "var": "c", "table": "acc_col",
                    "driver": {"kind": "column", "table": "cats",
                               "column": "c"}}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "body", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}, "it")
            need(rc.get("ok"), "iterator (column) ok: %s" % rc.get("error"))
            eq(rc.get("rows"), 2, "two distinct categories accumulated")

            # date-range driver values (helper), with day + month steps
            vals, _ = s._iterator_values(
                {"kind": "daterange", "start": "2026-01-01",
                 "end": "2026-01-03", "step": "day"}, 1000)
            eq(vals, ["2026-01-01", "2026-01-02", "2026-01-03"],
               "daterange day step")
            mvals, _ = s._iterator_values(
                {"kind": "daterange", "start": "2026-01-31",
                 "end": "2026-03-31", "step": "month"}, 1000)
            eq(mvals, ["2026-01-31", "2026-02-28", "2026-03-28"],
               "daterange month step clamps the day")
            # cap + note
            capped, note = s._iterator_values(
                {"kind": "list", "values": ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5"]}, 2)
            eq(len(capped), 2, "list capped to max_passes")
            need(note, "cap note is set when truncated")
            # no body wired -> a clear error, not a crash
            nb = s.run_iterator({"nodes": [
                {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "var": "i", "table": "x",
                    "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": ["1"]}}}],
                "edges": []}, "it")
            # wired "vars" input (the top connector) drives the loop: one pass
            # per row of the wired table, its columns bound as scalar ${vars}.
            s.run_nodeflow_to_table({"nodes": [
                {"id": "s", "type": "sql", "config": {
                    "sql": "SELECT 10 AS amt UNION ALL SELECT 20 "
                           "UNION ALL SELECT 30"}},
                {"id": "w", "type": "write", "config": {
                    "name": "drv", "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "s", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}, "w", "drv")
            rv = s.run_iterator({"nodes": [
                {"id": "src", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "drv"}},
                {"id": "body", "type": "sql",
                 "config": {"sql": "SELECT ${amt} AS got"}},
                {"id": "it", "type": "iterator",
                 "config": {"table": "acc_vars"}}],
                "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": "src", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "it", "port": "vars"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "body", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}, "it")
            need(rv.get("ok"),
                 "iterator (wired vars) ok: %s" % rv.get("error"))
            eq(rv.get("passes"), 3, "wired vars drove three passes")
            eq(rv.get("rows"), 3, "accumulator has three rows from wired vars")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_api_spool_response():
        # the chunked spool copies a readable to disk with a hard byte cap so a
        # huge response never lands in memory all at once.
        import io
        import tempfile
        import os as _os
        from samql_core import apiload
        fd, dst = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".bin")
        _os.close(fd)
        try:
            n, over = apiload.spool_response(
                io.BytesIO(b"hello world"), dst, max_bytes=1000)
            eq(n, 11, "spooled all 11 bytes")
            need(not over, "no overrun under the cap")
            eq(open(dst, "rb").read(), b"hello world", "bytes written verbatim")
            n2, over2 = apiload.spool_response(
                io.BytesIO(b"y" * 5000), dst, max_bytes=1000, chunk=256)
            eq(n2, 1000, "stopped writing at the cap")
            need(over2, "overrun flagged past the cap")
            eq(_os.path.getsize(dst), 1000, "file truncated to max_bytes")
        finally:
            try:
                _os.unlink(dst)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def t_api_records_from_file():
        # records stream out of a spooled file: a top-level array, a nested
        # array via json_path, and a lone object all normalize correctly.
        import json as _json
        import tempfile
        import os as _os
        from samql_core import apiload
        fd, p = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".json")
        _os.close(fd)
        try:
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(_json.dumps([{"a": 1}, {"a": 2}, {"a": 3}]))
            eq(len(list(apiload._records_from_file(p, None))), 3,
               "top-level array streamed")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(_json.dumps({"data": {"items": [{"b": 1}, {"b": 2}]}}))
            recs = list(apiload._records_from_file(p, "data.items"))
            eq(len(recs), 2, "nested array at the records-path")
            eq(recs[0].get("b"), 1, "nested record content")
            with open(p, "w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
                f.write(_json.dumps({"x": 9}))
            eq(len(list(apiload._records_from_file(p, None))), 1,
               "a lone object yields one record")
        finally:
            try:
                _os.unlink(p)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def t_api_stream_to_table():
        # end-to-end streaming path via an injected spooler (no network): the
        # response is written to a temp file, parsed from disk, and loaded --
        # ${vars} resolve before the spool, and errors are surfaced.
        import json as _json
        s = Session()
        try:
            captured = {}

            def fake_spool(url, dest, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None,
                           headers=None, **kw):
                captured["url"] = url
                payload = _json.dumps(
                    [{"id": 1, "name": "a"}, {"id": 2, "name": "b"},
                     {"id": 3, "name": "c"}]).encode("utf-8")
                with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(payload)
                return (200, "application/json", None, len(payload))

            s._api_spooler = fake_spool   # streaming path (no _api_fetcher set)
            cfg = {"url": "https://x.test/${region}/items"}
            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "v", "type": "variable", "config": {"vars": [
                    {"name": "region", "value": "eu"}]}},
                {"id": "api", "type": "apinode", "config": cfg}],
                "edges": []}
            r = s.fetch_api_node("api", cfg, graph=g)
            need(r.get("ok"), "stream fetch ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 3, "three records streamed in from disk")
            need("name" in (r.get("columns") or []),
                 "columns parsed from the spooled file")
            need(captured["url"] == "https://x.test/eu/items",
                 "URL resolved before spooling: %s" % captured["url"])

            def fake_nested(url, dest, **kw):
                payload = _json.dumps(
                    {"data": {"items": [{"k": 1}, {"k": 2}]}}).encode("utf-8")
                with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(payload)
                return (200, "application/json", None, len(payload))

            s._api_spooler = fake_nested
            r2 = s.fetch_api_node(
                "api2", {"url": "https://x.test/d", "json_path": "data.items"})
            need(r2.get("ok"), "nested stream ok: %s" % r2.get("error"))
            eq(r2.get("rows"), 2, "nested array streamed via json_path")

            s._api_spooler = lambda *a, **k: (None, "", "spool boom", 0)
            er = s.fetch_api_node("api3", {"url": "https://x.test/d"})
            need(er.get("error") and "boom" in er["error"],
                 "spool error surfaced: %s" % er.get("error"))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_apinode_error_port():
        # the API node's err output: a 0-row fixed-schema table on success, and
        # with continue-on-error a 1-row capture on failure (no hard error),
        # while the out port has no data.
        s = Session()
        try:
            s._api_fetcher = (
                lambda url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw:
                (200, "application/json", [{"id": 1}, {"id": 2}], "", None))
            g = {"nodes": [{"id": "api", "type": "apinode", "config": {
                "url": "https://x.test/d", "continue_on_error": True}}],
                "edges": []}
            cfg = g["nodes"][0]["config"]
            r = s.fetch_api_node("api", cfg)
            need(r.get("ok") and r.get("table"), "success has a data table")
            eq(r.get("err_rows"), 0, "no error rows on success")
            need(r.get("err_table"), "err table exists on success too")
            cfg["table"] = r["table"]
            cfg["err_table"] = r["err_table"]
            eq(s.run_nodeflow(g, "api", "out").get("total_rows"), 2,
               "out port has the 2 data rows")
            eq(s.run_nodeflow(g, "api", "err").get("total_rows"), 0,
               "err port is empty on success")

            # failure + continue-on-error -> captured on err, out empty
            s._api_fetcher = lambda *a, **k: (
                503, "", None, "", "HTTP 503 from the endpoint")
            r2 = s.fetch_api_node("api", cfg)
            need(r2.get("ok") and r2.get("fetched") is False,
                 "soft-fail returns ok with fetched=False")
            eq(r2.get("err_rows"), 1, "one error row captured")
            need(not r2.get("table"), "no data table after a failed fetch")
            cfg["table"] = r2.get("table") or ""
            cfg["err_table"] = r2["err_table"]
            er = s.run_nodeflow(g, "api", "err")
            need(not er.get("error"), "err port runs: %s" % er.get("error"))
            eq(er.get("total_rows"), 1, "err port has the one failure row")
            cols = [c.lower() for c in (er.get("columns") or [])]
            need("error" in cols and "status" in cols,
                 "err table has error+status columns: %s" % cols)
            oo = s.run_nodeflow(g, "api", "out")
            need(oo.get("error"), "out port errors when the fetch failed")

            # failure WITHOUT continue-on-error -> a hard error
            bad = s.fetch_api_node("api9", {"url": "https://x.test/d"})
            need(bad.get("error"), "hard error when continue-on-error is off")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_api_retry():
        # the retry runner: recover after transient failures, give up with an
        # error, never retry a non-transient status, retry network errors, and
        # honor retries=0. Sleep is injected so nothing actually waits.
        from samql_core import apiload
        seq = [(503, "", None, "", None), (503, "", None, "", None),
               (200, "application/json", [{"a": 1}], "", None)]
        calls = {"n": 0}
        slept = []

        def do():
            r = seq[calls["n"]]
            calls["n"] += 1
            return r

        res = apiload._fetch_with_retries(
            do, {"retries": 2, "base_delay": 0.01},
            sleep=lambda s: slept.append(s))
        eq(res[0], 200, "recovered to 200 after retries")
        eq(calls["n"], 3, "three attempts (1 + 2 retries)")
        eq(len(slept), 2, "slept between the two failed attempts")
        need(all(s >= 0 for s in slept), "backoff delays are non-negative")

        c2 = {"n": 0}

        def do2():
            c2["n"] += 1
            return (503, "", None, "", None)

        r2 = apiload._fetch_with_retries(do2, {"retries": 2},
                                         sleep=lambda s: None)
        eq(c2["n"], 3, "1 + 2 retries then stop")
        need(r2[4] and "503" in r2[4], "gives up with an error: %s" % (r2[4],))

        c3 = {"n": 0}

        def do3():
            c3["n"] += 1
            return (404, "", {"e": "nf"}, "", None)

        r3 = apiload._fetch_with_retries(do3, {"retries": 3},
                                         sleep=lambda s: None)
        eq(c3["n"], 1, "404 is not retried")
        eq(r3[0], 404, "404 returned as-is")

        c4 = {"n": 0}

        def do4():
            c4["n"] += 1
            return ((200, "application/json", [{"a": 1}], "", None)
                    if c4["n"] > 1
                    else (None, "", None, "", "TimeoutError: timed out"))

        r4 = apiload._fetch_with_retries(do4, {"retries": 2},
                                         sleep=lambda s: None)
        eq(r4[0], 200, "recovered after a network error")
        eq(c4["n"], 2, "retried the network error once")

        c5 = {"n": 0}

        def do5():
            c5["n"] += 1
            return (503, "", None, "", None)

        apiload._fetch_with_retries(do5, {"retries": 0}, sleep=lambda s: None)
        eq(c5["n"], 1, "retries=0 -> a single attempt")

        d = apiload._backoff_delay(5, base=1.0, cap=3.0)
        need(0 <= d <= 3.0, "backoff stays within [0, cap]: %s" % d)

    def t_api_retry_node():
        # retry wired through the API node, on both the in-memory fetch path
        # and the streaming spool path; injected sleep keeps it instant.
        import json as _json
        s = Session()
        try:
            slept = []
            s._api_sleep = lambda sec: slept.append(sec)

            seq = [(503, "", None, "", None),
                   (200, "application/json",
                    [{"id": 1}, {"id": 2}], "", None)]
            calls = {"n": 0}

            def fetch(url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw):
                r = seq[min(calls["n"], len(seq) - 1)]
                calls["n"] += 1
                return r

            s._api_fetcher = fetch
            r = s.fetch_api_node("api", {
                "url": "https://x.test/d",
                "retry": {"retries": 1, "base_delay": 0.01}})
            need(r.get("ok") and r.get("table"),
                 "recovered fetch: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 2, "loaded after the retry")
            eq(calls["n"], 2, "one retry happened")
            eq(len(slept), 1, "one (injected) backoff sleep")

            c2 = {"n": 0}

            def always503(url, **kw):
                c2["n"] += 1
                return (503, "", None, "", None)

            s._api_fetcher = always503
            r2 = s.fetch_api_node("api2", {
                "url": "https://x.test/d", "retry": {"retries": 2},
                "continue_on_error": True})
            need(r2.get("ok") and r2.get("fetched") is False,
                 "soft-fail after exhausting retries")
            eq(c2["n"], 3, "1 + 2 retries before giving up")

            # streaming spool path retry
            s._api_fetcher = None
            sc = {"n": 0}

            def spool(url, dest, **kw):
                sc["n"] += 1
                if sc["n"] == 1:
                    return (503, "", None, 0)
                with open(dest, "wb") as f:
                    f.write(_json.dumps([{"k": 1}]).encode("utf-8"))
                return (200, "application/json", None, 12)

            s._api_spooler = spool
            r3 = s.fetch_api_node(
                "api3", {"url": "https://x.test/d", "retry": {"retries": 1}})
            need(r3.get("ok"), "spool recovered after retry: %s"
                 % r3.get("error"))
            eq(sc["n"], 2, "spool retried once")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_api():
        # the iterator refreshes an API node in the body each pass, so a
        # ${var}-driven endpoint is called once per value and the results stack.
        s = Session()
        try:
            seen = []

            def fake(url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw):
                seen.append(url)
                return (200, "application/json", [{"u": url, "k": 1}], "", None)

            s._api_fetcher = fake
            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "api", "type": "apinode", "config": {
                    "url": "https://x.test/${region}/data"}},
                {"id": "it", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "var": "region", "table": "acc_api",
                    "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": ["us", "eu"]}}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "api", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "it", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "it")
            need(r.get("ok"), "iterator over API ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("passes"), 2, "two passes (us, eu)")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 2, "one row per region accumulated")
            eq(seen, ["https://x.test/us/data", "https://x.test/eu/data"],
               "API re-fetched per pass with the resolved URL: %s" % seen)
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_row_driver():
        # the rows driver binds several ${vars} per pass (one pass per row); the
        # body -- including a formula -- reads them. Also covers distinct, an
        # optional row-index var, and the empty-columns guard.
        s = Session()
        try:
            def mk(name, sql):
                s.run_nodeflow_to_table({"nodes": [
                    {"id": "s", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql": sql}},
                    {"id": "w", "type": "write",
                     "config": {"name": name, "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                    "edges": [{"from": {"node": "s", "port": "out"},
                               "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}, "w", name)
            mk("rd_jobs", "WITH t(region,yr,endpoint) AS (VALUES "
               "('US','2024','/us'),('EU','2024','/eu'),('US','2024','/us')) "
               "SELECT region,yr,endpoint FROM t")

            def run(driver, acc, extra_nodes=None, extra_edges=None,
                    term="b", **itc):
                nodes = [{"id": "b", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql":
                          "SELECT '${region}' AS region, '${yr}' AS yr, "
                          "'${endpoint}' AS endpoint"}}]
                edges = []
                if extra_nodes:
                    nodes += extra_nodes
                    edges += extra_edges
                nodes.append({"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "table": acc, "driver": driver, **itc}})
                edges.append({"from": {"node": term, "port": "out"},
                              "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "in"}})
                return s.run_iterator({"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}, "IT")

            # one pass per row; all three columns bound (note: no loop var set,
            # which is allowed for the rows driver)
            r = run({"kind": "rows", "table": "rd_jobs",
                     "columns": ["region", "yr", "endpoint"]}, "rd_all")
            need(r.get("ok"), "rows driver: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("passes"), 3, "one pass per row (3 rows)")
            rr = s.run_nodeflow({"nodes": [{"id": "i", "type": "input",
                "config": {"table": r["table"]}}], "edges": []}, "i", "out")
            got = sorted(tuple(x) for x in rr.get("rows"))
            eq(got, sorted([("US", "2024", "/us"), ("EU", "2024", "/eu"),
                            ("US", "2024", "/us")]),
               "each pass bound its row's column values")

            # distinct collapses the duplicate (US,2024,/us) -> 2 passes
            r = run({"kind": "rows", "table": "rd_jobs",
                     "columns": ["region", "yr", "endpoint"],
                     "distinct": True}, "rd_distinct")
            eq(r.get("passes"), 2, "distinct rows -> 2 passes")

            # a formula in the body reads the row vars
            fr = run({"kind": "rows", "table": "rd_jobs",
                      "columns": ["region", "yr", "endpoint"],
                      "distinct": True}, "rd_formula",
                     extra_nodes=[{"id": "f", "type": "formula", "config": {
                         "formulas": [
                             {"name": "tag", "expr": "region||'-'||yr"}]}}],
                     extra_edges=[{"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                                   "to": {"node": "f", "port": "in"}}],
                     term="f")
            need(fr.get("ok"), "formula w/ row vars: %s" % fr.get("error"))
            rr = s.run_nodeflow({"nodes": [{"id": "i", "type": "input",
                "config": {"table": fr["table"]}}], "edges": []}, "i", "out")
            ti = rr["columns"].index("tag")
            eq(sorted(row[ti] for row in rr["rows"]), ["EU-2024", "US-2024"],
               "formula computed a per-row tag from the bound vars")

            # an optional loop var in rows mode binds the 1-based row index
            ri = run({"kind": "rows", "table": "rd_jobs",
                      "columns": ["region"], "distinct": True}, "rd_idx",
                     var="i")
            need(ri.get("ok"), "rows + index var: %s" % ri.get("error"))

            # no columns -> a clear error
            bad = s.run_iterator({"nodes": [
                {"id": "b", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql": "SELECT 1 AS x"}},
                {"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "table": "rd_bad",
                    "driver": {"kind": "rows", "table": "rd_jobs"}}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "in"}}]}, "IT")
            need(bad.get("error") and "column" in bad["error"].lower(),
                 "rows driver with no columns errors: %s" % bad.get("error"))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_reduce():
        # reduce/fold accumulator: each pass contributes a partial aggregate,
        # folded into one row per key. Distributive only (sum/min/max/count);
        # a non-distributive fn is rejected.
        s = Session()
        try:
            def mk(name, sql):
                s.run_nodeflow_to_table({"nodes": [
                    {"id": "s", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql": sql}},
                    {"id": "w", "type": "write",
                     "config": {"name": name, "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                    "edges": [{"from": {"node": "s", "port": "out"},
                               "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}, "w", name)
            mk("rdc_chunks", "WITH t(chunk,region,amount) AS (VALUES "
               "(1,'US',100),(1,'EU',40),(2,'US',50),(2,'APAC',70)) "
               "SELECT chunk,region,amount FROM t")

            # fold partial SUMs per region across the two chunks
            r = s.run_iterator({"nodes": [
                {"id": "b", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql":
                    "SELECT region, SUM(amount) AS amount FROM rdc_chunks "
                    "WHERE chunk = ${chunk} GROUP BY region"}},
                {"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "table": "rdc_total", "var": "chunk",
                    "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": ["1", "2"]},
                    "accumulate": "reduce", "reduce_keys": ["region"],
                    "reduce_aggs": [{"col": "amount", "fn": "sum"}]}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "in"}}]}, "IT")
            need(r.get("ok"), "reduce iterator: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 3, "one row per region after folding")
            rr = s.run_nodeflow({"nodes": [{"id": "i", "type": "input",
                "config": {"table": r["table"]}}], "edges": []}, "i", "out")
            ri = rr["columns"].index("region")
            ai = rr["columns"].index("amount")
            got = {row[ri]: row[ai] for row in rr["rows"]}
            eq(got.get("US"), 150, "US folded 100+50=150 across passes")
            eq(got.get("EU"), 40, "EU folded to 40")
            eq(got.get("APAC"), 70, "APAC folded to 70")

            # a non-distributive aggregation is refused (lands in errors)
            bad = s.run_iterator({"nodes": [
                {"id": "b", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql":
                    "SELECT region, amount FROM rdc_chunks "
                    "WHERE chunk = ${chunk}"}},
                {"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "table": "rdc_bad", "var": "chunk",
                    "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": ["1", "2"]},
                    "accumulate": "reduce", "reduce_keys": ["region"],
                    "reduce_aggs": [{"col": "amount", "fn": "avg"}]}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "in"}}]}, "IT")
            errs = bad.get("errors") or []
            need(not bad.get("ok") and errs
                 and "avg" in errs[0]["error"].lower(),
                 "reduce rejects a non-distributive fn: %s"
                 % (errs or bad.get("error")))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_while_controller():
        # the while/until controller repeats the body until a pass adds no new
        # rows (a fixpoint) or hits the iteration cap.
        s = Session()
        try:
            def mk(name, sql):
                s.run_nodeflow_to_table({"nodes": [
                    {"id": "s", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql": sql}},
                    {"id": "w", "type": "write",
                     "config": {"name": name, "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                    "edges": [{"from": {"node": "s", "port": "out"},
                               "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}, "w", name)
            mk("wc_edges", "WITH t(src,dst) AS (VALUES (1,2),(2,3),(3,4)) "
               "SELECT src,dst FROM t")
            mk("wc_closure", "SELECT src,dst FROM wc_edges")   # seed

            # body: pairs reachable via one more hop, minus those already known
            # (antijoin) -- so the loop stops when nothing new is found
            r = s.run_while({"nodes": [
                {"id": "j", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql":
                    "SELECT c.src AS src, e.dst AS dst FROM wc_closure c "
                    "JOIN wc_edges e ON c.dst = e.src "
                    "EXCEPT SELECT src,dst FROM wc_closure"}},
                {"id": "W", "type": "while", "config": {
                    "table": "wc_closure", "reset_first": False,
                    "replace_keys": ["src", "dst"], "max_iters": 50}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "j", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "W", "port": "in"}}]}, "W")
            need(r.get("ok"), "while closure: %s" % r.get("error"))
            need(r.get("converged"), "closure reached a fixpoint")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 6, "transitive closure has 6 pairs")
            rr = s.run_nodeflow({"nodes": [{"id": "i", "type": "input",
                "config": {"table": "wc_closure"}}], "edges": []}, "i", "out")
            got = sorted(tuple(x) for x in rr["rows"])
            eq(got, [(1, 2), (1, 3), (1, 4), (2, 3), (2, 4), (3, 4)],
               "closure is the full reachability set")

            # a body that always adds a new row never converges -> cap stops it
            mk("wc_seq", "SELECT 0 AS n")
            c = s.run_while({"nodes": [
                {"id": "b", "type": "sql",
                 "config": {"sql": "SELECT ${i} AS n"}},
                {"id": "W", "type": "while", "config": {
                    "table": "wc_seq", "var": "i", "reset_first": True,
                    "replace_keys": ["n"], "max_iters": 5}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "b", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "W", "port": "in"}}]}, "W")
            eq(c.get("iterations"), 5, "stops at the 5-iteration cap")
            need(not c.get("converged"), "cap hit -> not converged")
            need(c.get("note"), "a note explains the cap was hit")

            # no body wired -> a clear error
            bad = s.run_while({"nodes": [
                {"id": "W", "type": "while", "config": {"table": "wc_x"}}],
                "edges": []}, "W")
            need(bad.get("error"), "while with no body errors")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_body_nodes():
        # audit: every kind of body node accumulates correctly in an iterator
        # (single-input transforms, joins, aggregation, set-ops, the
        # force-materialised pivot, and multi-node chains with a ${var} reaching
        # a mid-chain step). Also locks in that a write node inside the body is
        # a pass-through (no per-pass side table).
        s = Session()
        try:
            def mk(name, sql):
                s.run_nodeflow_to_table({"nodes": [
                    {"id": "s", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql": sql}},
                    {"id": "w", "type": "write",
                     "config": {"name": name, "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                    "edges": [{"from": {"node": "s", "port": "out"},
                               "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}, "w", name)
            mk("ib_nums", "WITH t(n) AS (VALUES (1),(2),(3),(4),(5)) "
               "SELECT n FROM t")
            mk("ib_sales", "WITH t(grp,amt) AS (VALUES ('x',10),('x',20),"
               "('y',5)) SELECT grp,amt FROM t")
            mk("ib_lft", "WITH t(g,a) AS (VALUES (1,'a'),(2,'b')) "
               "SELECT g,a FROM t")
            mk("ib_rgt", "WITH t(g,b) AS (VALUES (1,'x'),(3,'y')) "
               "SELECT g,b FROM t")
            mk("ib_t1", "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES (1),(2)) SELECT x FROM t")
            mk("ib_t2", "WITH t(x) AS (VALUES (3)) SELECT x FROM t")
            mk("ib_pv", "WITH t(reg,mon,amt) AS (VALUES ('e','jan',1),"
               "('e','feb',2),('w','jan',3)) SELECT reg,mon,amt FROM t")
            mk("ib_grp", "WITH t(id,score) AS (VALUES (1,50),(2,5),"
               "(3,80),(4,30)) SELECT id,score FROM t")

            def it(body_nodes, body_edges, term, port, vals=("p", "q"),
                   acc="ib_acc", **itc):
                nodes = list(body_nodes) + [
                    {"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                        "var": "k", "table": acc,
                        "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": list(vals)},
                        **itc}}]
                edges = list(body_edges) + [
                    {"from": {"node": term, "port": port},
                     "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "in"}}]
                return s.run_iterator({"nodes": nodes, "edges": edges}, "IT")

            r = it([{"id": "I", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_nums"}},
                    {"id": "F", "type": "filter",
                     "config": {"condition": "n <= ${k}"}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "I", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "F", "port": "in"}}],
                   "F", "true", vals=("2", "4"), acc="ib_filter")
            need(r.get("ok"), "filter body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 6, "filter body accumulates 2+4 rows")

            r = it([{"id": "L", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_lft"}},
                    {"id": "R", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_rgt"}},
                    {"id": "J", "type": "join", "config": {
                        "keys": [{"left": "g", "right": "g"}],
                        "mode": "inner"}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "L", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "J", "port": "left"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "R", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "J", "port": "right"}}],
                   "J", "inner", acc="ib_join")
            need(r.get("ok"), "join body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 2, "join body accumulates 1x2 rows")

            r = it([{"id": "I", "type": "input",
                     "config": {"table": "ib_sales"}},
                    {"id": "G", "type": "summarize", "config": {
                        "group_by": ["grp"],
                        "aggs": [{"col": "amt", "func": "sum",
                                  "name": "total"}]}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "I", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "G", "port": "in"}}],
                   "G", "out", acc="ib_summ")
            need(r.get("ok"), "summarize body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 4, "summarize body accumulates 2x2 rows")

            r = it([{"id": "A", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_t1"}},
                    {"id": "B", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_t2"}},
                    {"id": "U", "type": "union", "config": {}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "A", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "U", "port": "in1"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "B", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "U", "port": "in2"}}],
                   "U", "out", acc="ib_union")
            need(r.get("ok"), "union body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 6, "union body accumulates 3x2 rows")

            r = it([{"id": "I", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_nums"}},
                    {"id": "F", "type": "formula", "config": {
                        "formulas": [{"name": "d", "expr": "n*2"}]}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "I", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "F", "port": "in"}}],
                   "F", "out", acc="ib_formula")
            need(r.get("ok"), "formula body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 10, "formula body accumulates 5x2 rows")

            r = it([{"id": "I", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_pv"}},
                    {"id": "P", "type": "pivot", "config": {
                        "rows": ["reg"], "cols": ["mon"],
                        "values": [{"field": "amt", "agg": "sum"}]}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "I", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "P", "port": "in"}}],
                   "P", "out", acc="ib_pivot")
            need(r.get("ok"), "pivot body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 4, "pivot body accumulates 2x2 rows")

            r = it([{"id": "I", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_nums"}},
                    {"id": "F", "type": "formula", "config": {
                        "formulas": [{"name": "d", "expr": "n*2"}]}},
                    {"id": "FL", "type": "filter",
                     "config": {"condition": "d > ${k}"}},
                    {"id": "S", "type": "select", "config": {"fields": [
                        {"name": "n", "keep": True},
                        {"name": "d", "keep": True}]}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "I", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "F", "port": "in"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "F", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "FL", "port": "in"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "FL", "port": "true"},
                     "to": {"node": "S", "port": "in"}}],
                   "S", "out", vals=("4", "6"), acc="ib_chain")
            need(r.get("ok"), "chain body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 5, "chained body with mid-chain ${k} (3+2 rows)")

            # a write node inside the body is a pass-through: rows flow but its
            # named side table is NOT created per pass
            r = it([{"id": "I", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_nums"}},
                    {"id": "W", "type": "write", "config": {
                        "name": "ib_sidecar", "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "I", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "W", "port": "in"}}],
                   "W", "out", acc="ib_writepass")
            need(r.get("ok"), "write-passthrough body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 10, "write body passes rows through (5x2)")
            need("ib_sidecar" not in s.db.table_columns,
                 "write node inside an iterator does not create a side table")

            # group node body: an internal mini-pipeline whose child filter uses
            # ${k} -- proves resolve_graph substitutes deep into group children
            r = it([{"id": "I", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_grp"}},
                    {"id": "G", "type": "group", "config": {
                        "label": "prep", "children": [
                            {"id": "c1", "type": "filter",
                             "config": {"condition": "score >= ${k}"}},
                            {"id": "c2", "type": "sort", "config": {
                                "sorts": [{"col": "score", "dir": "asc"}]}}]}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "I", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "G", "port": "in"}}],
                   "G", "out", vals=("30", "60"), acc="ib_group")
            need(r.get("ok"), "group body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 4, "group body w/ mid-group ${k} (3+1 rows)")

            # reconcile node body (a blocking UNION-of-three): one row per
            # distinct key across both sides, accumulated each pass
            r = it([{"id": "L", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_lft"}},
                    {"id": "R", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_rgt"}},
                    {"id": "RC", "type": "reconcile",
                     "config": {"keys": ["g"]}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "L", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "RC", "port": "left"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "R", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "RC", "port": "right"}}],
                   "RC", "out", acc="ib_recon")
            need(r.get("ok"), "reconcile body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 6, "reconcile body accumulates 3x2 status rows")

            # antijoin node body (multi-input, left-rows-not-in-right)
            r = it([{"id": "L", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_lft"}},
                    {"id": "R", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "ib_rgt"}},
                    {"id": "AJ", "type": "antijoin", "config": {
                        "mode": "anti",
                        "keys": [{"left": "g", "right": "g"}]}}],
                   [{"from": {"node": "L", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "AJ", "port": "left"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "R", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "AJ", "port": "right"}}],
                   "AJ", "out", acc="ib_anti")
            need(r.get("ok"), "antijoin body: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 2, "antijoin body accumulates 1x2 rows")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_apinode_err_accumulator():
        # the API node's err port works as an iterator body: with
        # continue-on-error a per-pass failure is captured and the error rows
        # accumulate (the iterator refreshes the node's err table each pass,
        # not just its data table -- regression guard for that wiring).
        s = Session()
        try:
            s._api_fetcher = lambda url, **kw: (503, "", None, "", "HTTP 503")
            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "api", "type": "apinode", "config": {
                    "url": "https://x/${k}", "continue_on_error": True}},
                {"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "var": "k", "table": "it_errs",
                    "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": ["1", "2", "3"]}}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "api", "port": "err"},
                           "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "in"}}]}
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "IT")
            need(r.get("ok"), "err-accumulator iterator: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("passes"), 3, "all three passes captured an error row")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 3, "three error rows accumulated")
            rr = s.run_nodeflow({"nodes": [
                {"id": "in", "type": "input",
                 "config": {"table": r["table"]}}], "edges": []}, "in", "out")
            cols = [c.lower() for c in (rr.get("columns") or [])]
            need("error" in cols and "url" in cols,
                 "accumulated error schema: %s" % cols)
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_refresh_scope():
        # only apinodes are refreshed per pass; a filebrowser glob is still
        # re-resolved at compile time (varies per pass), while a directory node
        # keeps its pre-loaded table (its path ${var} is not re-applied).
        from samql_core import applyvars
        s = Session()
        try:
            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "api", "type": "apinode", "config": {"url": "u"}},
                {"id": "fb", "type": "filebrowser",
                 "config": {"pattern": "/d/*_${k}.csv"}},
                {"id": "dir", "type": "directory",
                 "config": {"table": "__nbfile_x", "path": "/d/${k}"}},
                {"id": "U", "type": "union", "config": {}}],
                "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": "api", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "U", "port": "in1"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "fb", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "U", "port": "in2"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "dir", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "U", "port": "in3"}}]}
            eq(sorted(s._api_nodes_upstream(g, "U")), ["api"],
               "only the apinode is refreshed per pass")
            rg1 = applyvars.resolve_graph(g, extra={"k": "2024"})
            rg2 = applyvars.resolve_graph(g, extra={"k": "2025"})

            def cfg_of(rg, nid, key):
                return next(n for n in rg["nodes"]
                            if n["id"] == nid)["config"][key]

            fb1, fb2 = cfg_of(rg1, "fb", "pattern"), cfg_of(rg2, "fb", "pattern")
            need(fb1 != fb2 and "2024" in fb1 and "2025" in fb2,
                 "filebrowser glob varies per pass: %s / %s" % (fb1, fb2))
            eq(cfg_of(rg1, "dir", "table"), "__nbfile_x",
               "directory keeps its fixed pre-loaded table (static per pass)")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_iterator_container():
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb is not installed [QUARANTINE]")
        # NEW container iterator: inner children (a mini-pipeline, like a group)
        # run once per row of the wired "variables" input, with that row's
        # columns bound as scalar ${vars}. An optional side "in" feeds the inner
        # pipeline. Verifies (a) the side data flows in and ${var} surfaces into
        # BOTH a filter and a formula, (b) an API node nested inside still gets
        # ${var} substituted into its URL -- the case API / file nodes can't
        # express through a data port -- with no side input wired, (c) the
        # classic driver + upstream-body iterator keeps working unchanged.
        s = Session()

        def mk(name, sql):
            s.run_nodeflow_to_table({"nodes": [
                {"id": "x", "type": "sql", "config": {"sql": sql}},
                {"id": "w", "type": "write",
                 "config": {"name": name, "mode": "overwrite"}}],
                "edges": [{"from": {"node": "x", "port": "out"},
                           "to": {"node": "w", "port": "in"}}]}, "w", name)
        try:
            mk("c_txns", "SELECT 'US' AS region, 10 AS amt UNION ALL "
               "SELECT 'US',20 UNION ALL SELECT 'EU',5 UNION ALL SELECT 'EU',7")
            mk("c_regions", "SELECT 'US' AS region UNION ALL SELECT 'EU'")
            it = {"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                "table": "c_per_region", "accumulate": "append",
                "reset_first": True, "children": [
                    {"id": "f", "type": "filter",
                     "config": {"condition": "[region] = '${region}'"}},
                    {"id": "fx", "type": "formula", "config": {
                        "formulas": [{"name": "src", "expr": "'${region}'"}]}}]}}
            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "D", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "c_txns"}},
                {"id": "V", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "c_regions"}},
                it],
                "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": "D", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "in"}},      # side data
                    {"from": {"node": "V", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "vars"}}]}    # variables (top)
            r = s.run_iterator(g, "IT")
            need(r.get("ok"), "container iterator runs: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("passes"), 2, "one pass per variables row")
            eq(r.get("rows"), 4, "both regions' matching rows accumulated")
            # Write / Input / iterator accumulate follow DuckDB-default store
            # (same as run_nodeflow_to_table); query the engine the run used.
            eq(r.get("engine"), "duckdb",
               "container iterator accumulates on DuckDB with unpinned writes")
            eng = s.duckdb if r.get("engine") == "duckdb" else s.db
            _c, rows = eng.execute(
                'SELECT region,amt,src FROM "c_per_region" ORDER BY region,amt')
            eq([tuple(x) for x in rows],
               [("EU", 5, "EU"), ("EU", 7, "EU"),
                ("US", 10, "US"), ("US", 20, "US")],
               "side data filtered by ${region} and tagged by the formula")

            # API node nested inside the container -- ${region} must reach its
            # URL even though it takes no data input. Mock fetch_api_node to
            # record the (already-substituted) URL and hand back a table.
            seen = []
            real_fetch = s.fetch_api_node

            def fake_fetch(node_id, config, graph=None, query_id=None,
                           should_cancel=None):
                url = (config or {}).get("url")
                seen.append(url)
                tn = "__apimock_%d" % len(seen)
                ue = url.replace("'", "''")
                # Mock table must land on the flow engine (DuckDB default).
                mock_eng = s.duckdb if s.duckdb is not None else s.db
                mock_eng.execute('DROP TABLE IF EXISTS "%s"' % tn)
                mock_eng.execute(
                    "CREATE TABLE \"%s\" AS SELECT '%s' AS url" % (tn, ue))
                return {"ok": True, "table": tn, "err_table": None,
                        "columns": ["url"], "rows": [[url]]}
            s.fetch_api_node = fake_fetch
            try:
                it2 = {"id": "IT", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                    "table": "c_api", "accumulate": "append",
                    "reset_first": True, "children": [
                        {"id": "api", "type": "apinode",
                         "config": {"url": "https://svc/${region}/x"}}]}}
                g2 = {"nodes": [
                    {"id": "V", "type": "input",
                     "config": {"table": "c_regions"}}, it2],
                    "edges": [{"from": {"node": "V", "port": "out"},
                               "to": {"node": "IT", "port": "vars"}}]}  # no side
                r2 = s.run_iterator(g2, "IT")
                need(r2.get("ok"),
                     "API-child container (optional side) runs: %s"
                     % r2.get("error"))
                eq(sorted(seen), ["https://svc/EU/x", "https://svc/US/x"],
                   "${region} surfaced into the nested API node's URL")
            finally:
                s.fetch_api_node = real_fetch

            # back-compat: a classic iterator (driver + upstream body, no inner
            # children) still runs through the original code path.
            body = {"id": "B", "type": "formula", "config": {
                "formulas": [{"name": "tag", "expr": "'${region}'"}]}}
            it3 = {"id": "IT3", "type": "iterator", "config": {
                "table": "c_classic", "var": "region", "reset_first": True,
                "driver": {"kind": "list", "values": ["US", "EU"]}}}
            g3 = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "S", "type": "input", "config": {"table": "c_txns"}},
                body, it3],
                "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": "S", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "B", "port": "in"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "B", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "IT3", "port": "in"}}]}
            r3 = s.run_iterator(g3, "IT3")
            need(r3.get("ok"),
                 "classic driver+body iterator still works: %s"
                 % r3.get("error"))
            eq(r3.get("passes"), 2, "classic iterator: 2 passes (back-compat)")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_api_pagination():
        # pagination loops the fetch and concatenates records -- all driven
        # through the injected fetcher, so no network is touched.
        from samql_core import apiload
        import urllib.parse as _up

        def qget(url, key, default=None):
            q = _up.parse_qs(_up.urlparse(url).query)
            return (q.get(key) or [default])[0]

        # page-number pagination: pages 1..2 have data, page 3 is empty
        def fake_page(url, **kw):
            p = int(qget(url, "page", "1"))
            if p <= 2:
                return (200, "application/json",
                        [{"p": p, "n": 1}, {"p": p, "n": 2}], "", None)
            return (200, "application/json", [], "", None)

        st, recs, err, pages = apiload.fetch_all_pages(
            "https://x.test/items", pagination={"kind": "page"},
            fetch=fake_page)
        need(not err, "page pagination ok: %s" % err)
        eq(len(recs), 4, "page pagination concatenates two pages")
        eq(pages, 3, "three fetches including the empty probe")

        # offset pagination: a short page ends it without an empty probe
        def fake_offset(url, **kw):
            off = int(qget(url, "offset", "0"))
            if off == 0:
                return (200, "application/json", [{"i": 0}, {"i": 1}], "", None)
            if off == 2:
                return (200, "application/json", [{"i": 2}], "", None)
            return (200, "application/json", [], "", None)

        st, recs, err, pages = apiload.fetch_all_pages(
            "https://x.test/i", pagination={"kind": "offset", "page_size": 2},
            fetch=fake_offset)
        eq(len(recs), 3, "offset pagination stops on a short page")
        eq(pages, 2, "two fetches (short page ended it)")

        # cursor pagination: follow next until it's absent
        def fake_cursor(url, **kw):
            c = qget(url, "cursor", None)
            if c is None:
                return (200, "application/json",
                        {"items": [{"x": 1}], "next": "c2"}, "", None)
            if c == "c2":
                return (200, "application/json",
                        {"items": [{"x": 2}], "next": None}, "", None)
            return (200, "application/json", {"items": []}, "", None)

        st, recs, err, pages = apiload.fetch_all_pages(
            "https://x.test/c", json_path="items",
            pagination={"kind": "cursor", "cursor_path": "next"},
            fetch=fake_cursor)
        eq(len(recs), 2, "cursor pagination follows the next cursor")
        eq(pages, 2, "two cursor fetches")

        # cap: an endpoint that never empties is bounded by max_pages
        st, recs, err, pages = apiload.fetch_all_pages(
            "https://x.test/inf", pagination={"kind": "page"},
            fetch=lambda url, **kw: (200, "application/json", [{"a": 1}], "",
                                     None),
            max_pages=3)
        eq(pages, 3, "max_pages cap stops the loop")
        eq(len(recs), 3, "capped at three pages of records")

        # 'none' (default): a single request, no paging params added
        seen = []

        def fake_none(url, **kw):
            seen.append(url)
            return (200, "application/json", [{"a": 1}, {"a": 2}], "", None)

        st, recs, err, pages = apiload.fetch_all_pages(
            "https://x.test/d", params=[("q", "1")], fetch=fake_none)
        eq(len(recs), 2, "single request loads its records")
        eq(pages, 1, "one fetch in 'none' mode")
        eq(seen, ["https://x.test/d?q=1"],
           "no paging params added in 'none' mode: %s" % seen)

        # integration: a paginated API node loads every page into its table
        s = Session()
        try:
            s._api_fetcher = fake_page
            r = s.fetch_api_node(
                "apg", {"url": "https://x.test/items",
                        "pagination": {"kind": "page"}})
            need(r.get("ok"), "paginated node fetch ok: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r.get("rows"), 4, "paginated node loads all four rows")
            eq(r.get("pages"), 3, "node reports the page count")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_sql_input_keyword():
        # the SQL node can read its wired input as `input`
        s = Session()
        try:
            r = _sql_flow(
                s, "SELECT 1 AS a, 'x' AS b UNION ALL SELECT 2, 'y'",
                {"id": "q", "type": "sql", "config": {
                    "sql": "SELECT a, upper(b) AS B FROM input WHERE a > 1"}})
            need(not r.get("error"), "sql FROM input runs: %s" % r.get("error"))
            eq(r["columns"], ["a", "B"], "projects the query's columns")
            eq([list(x) for x in r["rows"]], [[2, "Y"]], "reads input data")
            # an IN(...) operator must not be mistaken for the input relation
            r2 = _sql_flow(
