                 for t in fl.table_names()}
            fl.close()
            return o

        cols, rows = flat([{"a b": 1, "a_b": 2, "a.b": 3}])["r"]
        eq(len([c for c in cols if c != "_id"]), 3,
           "three colliding keys must yield three columns: %r" % cols)
        eq(rows[0][1:], [1, 2, 3], "colliding-key values dropped: %r" % rows[0])
        # a flat key and a nested path that serialise identically ("a_b_c")
        c2, r2 = flat([{"a_b_c": 1, "a": {"b": {"c": 2}}}])["r"]
        eq(len([c for c in c2 if c != "_id"]), 2,
           "flat/nested path collision: %r" % c2)
        eq(r2[0][1:], [1, 2], "flat/nested values dropped: %r" % r2[0])
        # ragged: row 2 has only the literal "a_b"; it must land in the SAME
        # column it did in row 1 (not the "a b" column), leaving "a b" NULL.
        c3, r3 = flat([{"a b": 1, "a_b": 2}, {"a_b": 9}])["r"]
        eq(r3[0][1:], [1, 2], "row1 alignment: %r" % r3[0])
        eq(r3[1][1:], [None, 9], "ragged alignment broken: %r" % r3[1])
        # a data key colliding with the auto parent-FK name must not clobber it
        kids = flat([{"id": 1, "kids": [{"r id": 7, "v": 1}]}])
        ck, rk = kids["r_kids"]
        need("r_id" in ck and rk[0][ck.index("r_id")] == 1,
             "parent FK clobbered by data key: %r %r" % (ck, rk))

    def t_duckdb_weird_data():
        # Run the strange-data battery through the DuckDB streaming ingester.
        # Skips where DuckDB isn't installed (the sandbox); runs in full on the
        # real machine, covering dedupe/escaping + typed-vs-VARCHAR coercion of
        # awkward values, then a query + reconcile over DuckDB-resident tables.
        from samql_core.engines import HAS_DUCKDB
        if not HAS_DUCKDB:
            skip("duckdb not installed (this test runs on the real machine)")
        import decimal
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            duck = s.get_duckdb()
            cols = ["dup", "dup", "", 'a"b', "amt"]
            rows = [(1, 2, 3, 4, decimal.Decimal("1.50")),
                    (10 ** 30, None, "x", "y", float("nan")),
                    (5, 6, 7, 8, 9.5)]
            name, n = duck.add_table_streaming("dw", cols, iter(rows))
            eq(n, 3, "duckdb weird-data row count")
            got = duck.table_columns.get(name)
            eq(len(set(got)), 5, "duckdb columns disambiguated: %r" % got)
            need('a"b' in got, "embedded-quote column lost on duckdb: %r" % got)
            r = s.run_query('SELECT COUNT(*) FROM %s'
                            % ('"' + name + '"'), target="__duckdb__")
            eq(r["rows"][0][0], 3, "duckdb weird table not queryable")
            # reconcile two DuckDB-resident tables
            duck.add_table_streaming("dl", ["k", "v"],
                                     iter([(1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3)]))
            duck.add_table_streaming("dr", ["k", "v"],
                                     iter([(1, 1), (2, 9)]))
            rep = s.reconcile({"left": "dl", "right": "dr",
                               "keys": ["k"], "compare": ["v"]})
            t = rep.get("totals", {})
            eq([t.get("a_only"), t.get("matching")], [1, 1],
               "duckdb reconcile totals: %r" % t)
            # flattened weird JSON -> DuckDB
            from samql_core.flatten import JSONFlattener
            fl = JSONFlattener(root_name="j")
            fl.flatten([{"a b": 1, "a_b": 2, "nested": {"x": 3}}])
            for tn in fl.table_names():
                duck.add_table_streaming(tn, fl.columns(tn),
                                         fl.iter_rows_aligned(tn))
            fl.close()
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_json_streaming_edge():
        # Angles beyond t_json_streaming_parser: NaN/Infinity literal recovery,
        # a UTF-8 BOM, and assorted whitespace around concatenated objects.
        import math
        from samql_core.flatten import stream_json_records, read_json_any_format
        dd = tempfile.mkdtemp()

        def w(name, text, enc="utf-8"):
            p = os.path.join(dd, name)
            with open(p, "w", encoding=enc) as f:
                f.write(text)
            return p

        recs = list(stream_json_records(
            w("nan.json", '[{"a":NaN,"b":Infinity},{"a":-Infinity}]')))
        eq(len(recs), 2, "NaN/Infinity literals recovered as 2 records")
        need(math.isnan(recs[0]["a"]) and math.isinf(recs[0]["b"]),
             "NaN/Inf values preserved: %r" % recs[0])
        need(math.isinf(recs[1]["a"]) and recs[1]["a"] < 0, "negative Infinity")
        eq(len(list(stream_json_records(
            w("ws.json", '  {"x":1}\n\n\t{"x":2}   {"x":3}\n')))), 3,
            "concatenated objects with assorted whitespace")
        eq(len(list(stream_json_records(
            w("bom.json", '\ufeff[{"x":1},{"x":2}]')))), 2,
            "BOM-prefixed array via streaming parser")
        bom_obj = read_json_any_format(w("bom2.json", '\ufeff{"only":1}'))
        eq(bom_obj, [{"only": 1}],
           "BOM single object via any-format reader (normalised to a list)")

    def t_flatten_array_linkage():
        # Child tables built for arrays must carry a foreign key back to their
        # parent row, and arrays-of-arrays must chain parent -> child -> inner.
        from samql_core.flatten import JSONFlattener
        fl = JSONFlattener(root_name="r")
        fl.flatten([{"id": 1, "items": [{"x": 10}, {"x": 20}]},
                    {"id": 2, "items": [{"x": 30}]}])
        child = [t for t in fl.table_names() if t != "r"][0]
        cc = fl.columns(child)
        need("r_id" in cc, "child table missing parent FK: %r" % cc)
        rows = [list(x) for x in fl.iter_rows_aligned(child)]
        fk = sorted(x[cc.index("r_id")] for x in rows)
        eq(fk, [1, 1, 2], "child FK values don't link to parents: %r" % fk)
        fl.close()
        fl2 = JSONFlattener(root_name="r")
        fl2.flatten([{"id": 1, "m": [[1, 2], [3]]}])
        n2 = fl2.table_names()
        eq(len(n2), 3, "array-of-arrays makes parent/child/inner: %r" % n2)
        inner = n2[-1]
        ic = fl2.columns(inner)
        need("value" in ic, "inner scalar table needs a value column: %r" % ic)
        vals = sorted(x[ic.index("value")]
                      for x in fl2.iter_rows_aligned(inner))
        eq(vals, [1, 2, 3], "inner array scalars lost: %r" % vals)
        fl2.close()

    def t_flatten_deep_arrays_and_depth_guard():
        # Arrays nested three or more deep now explode into chained child
        # tables (previously the third level was stringified); a mixed-type
        # field stays lossless; and a pathologically deep document degrades
        # gracefully instead of raising RecursionError.
        from samql_core.flatten import JSONFlattener

        def tabs(data):
            fl = JSONFlattener(root_name="r")
            fl.flatten(data)
            out = {t: (fl.columns(t),
                       [list(x) for x in fl.iter_rows_aligned(t)])
                   for t in fl.table_names()}
            fl.close()
            return out

        # three-level array -> a deepest *_items_items table of real scalars
        t = tabs([{"a": [[[10, 20]]]}])
        deep = [k for k in t if k.endswith("_items_items")]
        need(deep, "3-level array did not explode into a deep child: %r"
             % sorted(t))
        ic = t[deep[0]][0]
        vals = sorted(x[ic.index("value")] for x in t[deep[0]][1])
        eq(vals, [10, 20], "deep-array scalars must be real values, not JSON "
           "text: %r" % t[deep[0]][1])

        # mixed-type field: scalar in one record, object in another -> both
        # representations survive (no data loss)
        t = tabs([{"x": 5}, {"x": {"a": 1}}])
        cols = t["r"][0]
        need("x" in cols and "x_a" in cols,
             "mixed scalar/object field lost a representation: %r" % cols)
        xs = [row[cols.index("x")] for row in t["r"][1]]
        xas = [row[cols.index("x_a")] for row in t["r"][1]]
        need(5 in xs and 1 in xas,
             "mixed-type values not both preserved: x=%r x_a=%r" % (xs, xas))

        # pathologically deep array must not blow the Python stack
        deep_val = 1
        for _ in range(300):
            deep_val = [deep_val]
        try:
            t = tabs([{"d": deep_val}])
        except RecursionError:
            raise AssertionError("deep nesting raised RecursionError")
        need(len(t) <= JSONFlattener._MAX_NEST_DEPTH + 2,
             "depth guard did not cap child-table explosion: %d tables"
             % len(t))

    def t_reconcile_high_cardinality():
        # Exact set arithmetic over many distinct keys (recursive-CTE built):
        # a_only/b_only/matching/non_matching must reflect the true overlap.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE hc_a AS WITH RECURSIVE s(k) AS "
                "(SELECT 1 UNION ALL SELECT k+1 FROM s WHERE k<2000) "
                "SELECT k, k*2 AS v FROM s", target="__local__")
            s.run_query(
                "CREATE TABLE hc_b AS WITH RECURSIVE s(k) AS "
                "(SELECT 500 UNION ALL SELECT k+1 FROM s WHERE k<2499) "
                "SELECT k, CASE WHEN k%2=0 THEN k*2 ELSE k*2+1 END AS v "
                "FROM s", target="__local__")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "hc_a", "right": "hc_b",
                               "keys": ["k"], "compare": ["v"]})
            need(not rec.get("error"), "high-card reconcile error: %r" % rec)
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq(t["a_only"], 499, "a_only = keys 1..499")
            eq(t["b_only"], 499, "b_only = keys 2001..2499")
            eq(t["matching"], 751, "row matches = even k across the overlap")
            eq(t["non_matching"], 750, "row diffs = odd k across the overlap")
            eq(t["total"], 2499, "total = a_only + b_only + matched keys")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reconcile_composite_keys():
        # Composite (multi-column) keys, plus NULL handling on a *compare*
        # field: two NULLs compare equal (COALESCE), NULL vs a value differs.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE ca (region TEXT, acct INT, amt REAL, "
                        "note TEXT)", target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO ca VALUES "
                        "('E',1,10.0,'x'),('E',2,20.0,NULL),"
                        "('W',1,30.0,'y'),('W',9,5.0,'z')",
                        target="__local__")
            s.run_query("CREATE TABLE cb (region TEXT, acct INT, amt REAL, "
                        "note TEXT)", target="__local__")
            s.run_query("INSERT INTO cb VALUES "
                        "('E',1,10.0,'x'),('E',2,20.0,NULL),"
                        "('W',1,30.0,'CHANGED'),('Z',1,1.0,'q')",
                        target="__local__")
            spec = {"left": "ca", "right": "cb",
                    "keys": ["region", "acct"], "compare": ["amt", "note"]}
            rec = s.reconcile(spec)
            need(not rec.get("error"), "composite reconcile error: %r" % rec)
            t = rec["totals"]
            eq((t["a_only"], t["b_only"]), (1, 1),
               "composite a_only=(W,9), b_only=(Z,1): %r" % t)
            eq(t["total"], 5, "composite total = 1 + 1 + 3 matched")
            byf = {f["field"]: f for f in rec["fields"]}
            eq((byf["note"]["matching"], byf["note"]["non_matching"]), (2, 1),
               "NULL==NULL matches, value change differs: %r" % byf["note"])
            eq(byf["amt"]["non_matching"], 0, "amt agrees on every matched key")
            da = s.reconcile_drilldown({**spec, "bucket": "a_only"})
            eq(da["count"], 1, "composite-key a_only drilldown count")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_duckdb_pivot_chart():
        # Engine-routing fix: a DuckDB-resident table with no engine hint must
        # let pivot + chart aggregate on DuckDB (not fall through to SQLite and
        # come back empty). Gated -- runs on the real machine.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.load_file(CSV, destination="duckdb", base_name="dp")
            pv = s.pivot({"table": "dp", "rows": ["category"],
                          "values": [{"field": "score", "agg": "sum"}]})
            need(not pv.get("error"),
                 "duckdb pivot error: %r" % pv.get("error"))
            eq(pv["row_count"], 3, "pivot over 3 categories on duckdb")
            ch = s.chart_data({"table": "dp", "chart_type": "bar",
                               "x": "category", "y": "score", "agg": "sum"})
            need(not ch.get("error"),
                 "duckdb chart error: %r" % ch.get("error"))
            eq(len(ch["labels"]), 3, "chart has 3 category labels on duckdb")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_duckdb_flow_chart_multiaxis_temp_table():
        # A chart node's input is a TEMP table the flow just materialised on
        # the DuckDB main connection. The multi-axis chart types (multiy /
        # multix / candlestick) fetch rows via _source_rows, whose
        # fresh-cursor read is a SEPARATE connection with its own temp schema
        # and cannot see it -- 'Catalog Error: Table with name __nbflow_...
        # does not exist!' on a SQL Server (DuckDB-pinned) flow while the
        # select node's preview showed data fine. Guards the
        # locked-main-connection fallback. Gated -- runs on the real machine.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.load_file(CSV, destination="duckdb", base_name="dfc")
            g = {
                "nodes": [
                    {"id": "i", "type": "input",
                     "config": {"table": "dfc", "label": "dfc"}},
                    {"id": "sel", "type": "select",
                     "config": {"label": "sel", "fields": [
                         {"name": "category", "keep": True},
                         {"name": "score", "keep": True},
                         {"name": "id", "keep": True}]}},
                    {"id": "c", "type": "chart", "config": {"label": "c"}},
                ],
                "edges": [
                    {"from": {"node": "i", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "sel", "port": "in"}},
                    {"from": {"node": "sel", "port": "out"},
                     "to": {"node": "c", "port": "in"}},
                ],
            }
            r = s.run_nodeflow_chart(
                g, "c", {"chart_type": "multiy", "x": "category",
                         "y": "score", "y2": "id", "agg": "sum"})
            need(not r.get("error"),
                 "multiy chart over a DuckDB flow temp table: %r"
                 % r.get("error"))
            eq(len(r.get("series") or []), 2,
               "multiy over a flow returns both series")
            need(all((x.get("values") or []) for x in r["series"]),
                 "both series carry aggregated values")
            r2 = s.run_nodeflow_chart(
                g, "c", {"chart_type": "multix", "x": "category",
                         "y": "score", "x2": "category", "y2": "id",
                         "agg": "sum"})
            need(not r2.get("error"),
                 "multix chart over a DuckDB flow temp table: %r"
                 % r2.get("error"))
            # The same temp-visibility trap exists on the generic result
            # drain -- run_nodeflow's final read when the Parquet fast path
            # is unavailable (no pyarrow). Force that path so the drain's
            # locked-main-connection fallback is exercised even where
            # pyarrow IS installed.
            s.use_parquet_results = False
            rp = s.run_nodeflow(g, "sel", "out")
            need(not rp.get("error"),
                 "flow read via the generic drain: %r" % rp.get("error"))
            need(int(rp.get("total_rows") or 0) > 0,
                 "drain read returns the select node's rows")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_duckdb_paging():
        # Sorted + filtered paging over a DuckDB-resident result set. Gated.
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.load_file(CSV, destination="duckdb", base_name="dq")
            res = s.run_query("SELECT id, score FROM dq", target="__duckdb__")
            rid = res["result_id"]
            need(rid, "expected a duckdb result id")
            pg = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=5, sort_col="score",
                        descending=True)
            sc = [row[1] for row in pg["rows"]]
            eq(sc, sorted(sc, reverse=True), "duckdb sorted page descending")
            eq(pg["rows"][0][0], ROWS - 1, "top score belongs to the last id")
            pf = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=100,
                        filters=[{"column": "score", "op": "gt", "value": 40}])
            need(pf["rows"] and all(row[1] > 40 for row in pf["rows"]),
                 "duckdb filtered page respects the predicate")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_duckdb_cross_engine_recon():
        # A SQLite table and a DuckDB table can't be reconciled together; the
        # user gets a clear, engine-naming error (not a crash or empty result).
        if not feats["duckdb"]:
            skip("duckdb not installed")
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.load_file(CSV, destination="sqlite", base_name="ls")
            s.load_file(CSV, destination="duckdb", base_name="ld")
            rec = s.reconcile({"left": "ls", "right": "ld",
                               "keys": ["id"], "compare": ["score"]})
            need("error" in rec, "cross-engine reconcile must error: %r" % rec)
            msg = rec["error"].lower()
            need("sqlite" in msg and "duckdb" in msg,
                 "error should name both engines: %r" % rec["error"])
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_source_bundle_roundtrip():
        # Guards the source-bundle contract used by Expand-SamQL[.]ps1: the
        # "===== FILE: <path> =====" markers must split the bundle back into the
        # exact files -- including files with leading whitespace (Python
        # indentation) and intentional unicode (em dash, ellipsis). Mirrors the
        # extractor's split logic in Python so a bundle change that would break
        # reconstruction is caught here.
        import re

        files = {
            "a.py": "def f():\n    return 1\n",                    # indentation
            "b/c.ts": "const x = \"q\";\nconst y = '\u2014';\n",   # em dash
            "d.md": "Title \u2026 done\n",                         # ellipsis
        }
        bundle = "# header (ignored by the extractor)\n\n"
        for path, body in files.items():
            bundle += "===== FILE: %s =====\n%s\n" % (path, body)

        def split_bundle(text):
            rx = re.compile(r"(?m)^===== FILE: (?P<path>.*?) =====[ \t]*\r?\n")
            ms = list(rx.finditer(text))
            out = {}
            for i, m in enumerate(ms):
                start = m.end()
                end = ms[i + 1].start() if i + 1 < len(ms) else len(text)
                out[m.group("path")] = re.sub(r"(\r?\n)+\Z", "",
                                              text[start:end]) + "\n"
            return out

        got = split_bundle(bundle)
        eq(got, files, "bundle does not split back into the source files")
        # the markers must be unique to headers -- no file body may contain one
        for path, body in files.items():
            need("===== FILE:" not in body,
                 "file body unexpectedly contains a FILE marker: %s" % path)

        # --- email-safe "defang" contract -------------------------------
        # For email / URL scanners the bundle can be shipped "defanged": a
        # bracketed-dot token is inserted in front of executable-style
        # extensions, so SamQL[.]exe travels as SamQL<bracketed-dot>exe.
        # Expand-SamQL[.]ps1 reverses only a token immediately followed by a
        # declared dangerous extension. Mirror both halves so drift in either
        # side is caught here and ordinary bracketed-dot source literals remain
        # byte-stable through expansion and repackaging.
        fang = "[" + "." + "]"
        exts = "exe|dll|msi|bat|cmd|scr|vbs|ps1|jar"

        def defang(t):
            return re.sub(r"\.(" + exts + r")(?![A-Za-z0-9])",
                          lambda m: fang + m.group(1), t)

        def refang(t):
            return re.sub(r"\[\.\](" + exts + r")(?![A-Za-z0-9])",
                          lambda m: "." + m.group(1), t)

        sample = ("run signtool" + "." + "exe; build" + "." +
                  "ps1; esbuild" + "." + "cmd; regex.exec(); "
                  "obj.execute(); literal " + fang + " marker; done.")
        d = defang(sample)
        need(("signtool" + "." + "exe") not in d
             and ("signtool" + fang + "exe") in d,
             "defang neutralises executable extensions")
        need(("build" + "." + "ps1") not in d
             and ("build" + fang + "ps1") in d,
             "defang neutralises script extensions")
        need(("esbuild" + "." + "cmd") not in d
             and ("esbuild" + fang + "cmd") in d,
             "defang neutralises command extensions")
        need("regex.exec()" in d and "obj.execute(" in d,
             "defang must NOT touch look-alikes like .exec / .execute")
        need(("literal " + fang + " marker") in refang(d),
             "refang must preserve ordinary bracketed-dot source literals")
        eq(refang(d), sample,
           "the extractor targeted un-defang is the exact inverse")

    def t_filter_op_symbols():
        # Filter ops accept symbolic forms (">", ">=", "=", "!=") as well as the
        # word forms ("gt", "gte", "equals", "ne"); both must filter
        # identically. Guards the silent no-op an unrecognised op used to cause
        # (it fell through to "match everything"). Runs on an in-memory SQLite
        # result, so it exercises the Python _match path directly.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.load_file(CSV, destination="sqlite", base_name="fo")
            rid = s.run_query("SELECT id, score FROM fo",
                              target="__local__")["result_id"]
            word = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=100,
                          filters=[{"column": "score", "op": "gt",
                                    "value": 40}])
            sym = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=100,
                         filters=[{"column": "score", "op": ">", "value": 40}])
            need(word["rows"] and all(r[1] > 40 for r in word["rows"]),
                 "word op 'gt' did not filter")
            eq([r[1] for r in sym["rows"]], [r[1] for r in word["rows"]],
               "symbolic op '>' must match word op 'gt'")
            one = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=100,
                         filters=[{"column": "id", "op": "=", "value": 5}])
            eq(one["total_rows"], 1,
               "symbolic op '=' must select exactly one row")
            eq(str(one["rows"][0][0]), "5",
               "symbolic op '=' selected the wrong row")
            neq = s.page(rid, offset=0, limit=100,
                         filters=[{"column": "id", "op": "!=", "value": 5}])
            need(neq["total_rows"] == ROWS - 1 and
                 all(str(r[0]) != "5" for r in neq["rows"]),
                 "symbolic op '!=' must exclude the matching row")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_store_filter_sort_parity():
        # A result is served by different stores depending on size (in-memory
        # list vs spilled SQLite DiskBackedRows). They MUST filter and sort
        # identically, or the same query returns different rows/order purely
        # because it was bigger. Covers the three historical divergences:
        # ne+NULL, numeric-vs-text comparison, and NULL sort placement.
        from samql_core.session import _CachedResult
        from samql_core.rows import DiskBackedRows
        cols = ["v"]
        data = [[5], [12], [3], ["7"], ["apple"], ["banana"], [None], [0],
                [-2], ["10"]]

        def rows_for(store, filters, sort_desc=None):
            cr = _CachedResult("r", cols, store, len(data), "sql", "t", "e")
            view, _ = cr.filtered_view(
                filters, sort_col=("v" if sort_desc is not None else None),
                descending=bool(sort_desc))
            return [list(r) for r in view]

        def mem(filters, sort_desc=None):
            return rows_for([tuple(r) for r in data], filters, sort_desc)

        def disk(filters, sort_desc=None):
            st = DiskBackedRows(block=2)
            st.extend([tuple(r) for r in data])
            return rows_for(st, filters, sort_desc)

        def key(rowlist):
            return sorted(repr(r) for r in rowlist)

        for f in ([{"column": "v", "op": "ne", "value": "5"}],
                  [{"column": "v", "op": "gt", "value": "5"}],
                  [{"column": "v", "op": "lte", "value": "5"}],
                  [{"column": "v", "op": "equals", "value": "12"}],
                  [{"column": "v", "op": "gt", "value": "apple"}],
                  [{"column": "v", "op": "ne", "value": "apple"}]):
            eq(key(mem(f)), key(disk(f)),
               "in-memory and spilled stores must agree on filter %s" % f)
        # ne excludes NULL (both stores), numeric strings compare numerically
        eq(len(mem([{"column": "v", "op": "ne", "value": "5"}])), 8,
           "ne must exclude the matching row AND NULL")
        eq(len(mem([{"column": "v", "op": "gt", "value": "5"}])), 3,
           "gt 5 matches 12, '7', '10' (numeric strings), not 'apple'")
        # NULL sort placement identical (last ascending, first descending)
        for desc in (False, True):
            eq([r[0] for r in mem([], desc)], [r[0] for r in disk([], desc)],
               "in-memory and spilled stores must sort identically (desc=%s)"
               % desc)

    def t_progress_registry():
        # The heartbeat registry backs the dashboard and the watchdog. A bare
        # beat() (no id) must update the op running on the *calling thread*, so
        # deep engine streaming loops can report progress without an id.
        from samql_core import progress as P
        P.reset_for_tests()
        try:
            oid = P.begin("load", target="big.csv", engine="duckdb")
            P.beat(rows=500)            # thread-keyed: no id passed
            snap = P.snapshot()
            eq(len(snap), 1, "one op expected")
            eq(snap[0]["kind"], "load", "kind")
            eq(snap[0]["rows"], 500, "rows from bare beat()")
            eq(snap[0]["engine"], "duckdb", "engine label")
            # a load streams under a generated id -> not cancel_query-able
            # (it is cancelled via its tray job instead).
            need(snap[0]["cancellable"] is False,
                 "load (generated id) must not be cancellable")
            eq(P.active_kinds(), {"load"}, "active_kinds")
            # nothing is stale right after a beat; everything is stale at thr<=0
            need(P.stale(60.0) == [], "fresh op must not be stale")
            need(len(P.stale(0.0)) == 1, "thr 0 marks the op stale")
            P.end(oid)
            # .516: end() marks finished (linger-visible); nothing ACTIVE
            need(all(o["finished"] for o in P.snapshot()),
                 "op finished on end (lingers observable)")
            eq(P.count(), 0, "no active ops after end")
            eq(P.active_kinds(), set(), "no kinds after end")
            # a foreground run / bg op registered under a real run id IS
            # cancel_query-able (drives the inline Cancel in the activity modal
            # and the stat popover); restore registers with no id -> stays
            # false, so it never shows a cancel control.
            qid = P.begin("query", target="select 1", op_id="q-77")
            _q77 = next(o for o in P.snapshot() if o["id"] == "q-77")
            need(_q77["cancellable"] is True,
                 "run with a real id must be cancellable")
            P.end(qid)
        finally:
            P.reset_for_tests()

    def t_watchdog_decide_and_dump():
        # Pure decision: dump once per stall; forget recovered ids so a re-stall
        # re-dumps. Then scan_once must actually write a thread-stack dump.
        from samql_core import progress as P, watchdog as W
        d, a = W._decide_dumps(["x", "y"], set())
        eq(d, {"x", "y"}, "all newly-stale dump")
        eq(a, {"x", "y"}, "remember dumped")
        d2, _ = W._decide_dumps(["x", "y"], {"x", "y"})
        eq(d2, set(), "already-dumped don't re-dump")
        _, a3 = W._decide_dumps(["y"], {"x", "y"})
        eq(a3, {"y"}, "recovered id forgotten")

        # A Session starts the process-wide daemon. reset_for_tests must stop
        # that thread, not merely clear its state: otherwise its 90-second
        # scan can run between the two threshold-0 scans below, empty
        # _dumped, and make the same stall get written twice. Use a short
        # interval here so the old race is deterministic on every platform.
        P.reset_for_tests()
        W.reset_for_tests()
        bg_log = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "background.log")
        W.start(threshold_s=9999.0, interval_s=0.01, log_path=bg_log)
        need(W._thread is not None and W._thread.is_alive(),
             "watchdog test daemon did not start")
        W.reset_for_tests()
        need(not W._started and W._thread is None,
             "reset_for_tests left the watchdog daemon alive")

        log = os.path.join(tempfile.mkdtemp(), "stall.log")
        try:
            P.begin("query", target="stuck")     # an op with a fresh beat
            stale = W.scan_once(0.0, log)         # thr 0 -> treat as stuck
            eq(len(stale), 1, "scan sees the op")
            need(os.path.exists(log), "watchdog wrote no dump file")
            txt = open(log, encoding="utf-8").read()
            need("STALL" in txt, "dump missing STALL marker")
            need("end stall" in txt, "dump not closed")
            # Give any leaked short-interval daemon enough time to run,
            # then make a second pass. The same stall must still be remembered.
            n1 = len(txt)
            time.sleep(0.04)
            W.scan_once(0.0, log)
            need(len(open(log, encoding="utf-8").read()) == n1,
                 "same stall must not be dumped twice")
            ls = W.last_stall()
            need(ls and ls.get("kind") == "query", "last_stall not recorded")
        finally:
            P.reset_for_tests()
            W.reset_for_tests()

    def t_status_shape_and_busy():
        # status() reports in-flight ops + per-engine lock-held flags + thread
        # count + restore flag. The busy flag must read True only when ANOTHER
        # thread holds the engine lock (it is re-entrant for the holder). Use a
        # fresh (unloaded) session so post-load bookkeeping can't briefly hold
        # the lock and make the idle baseline racy.
        import threading as _th
        import time as _t
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            st = s.status()
            for k in ("operations", "engines", "threads", "restoring",
                      "last_stall"):
                need(k in st, f"status missing {k}")
            need(st["engines"]["sqlite"]["active"] is True, "sqlite active")
            need(isinstance(st["threads"], int) and st["threads"] >= 1,
                 "threads must be a positive int")
            idle = False
            for _ in range(40):
                if s.status()["engines"]["sqlite"]["busy"] is False:
                    idle = True
                    break
                _t.sleep(0.02)
            need(idle, "idle SQLite engine must not report busy")
            grab, rel = _th.Event(), _th.Event()

            def holder():
                with s.db.write_lock:
                    grab.set()
                    rel.wait(2.0)
            t = _th.Thread(target=holder)
            t.start()
            need(grab.wait(2.0), "holder never acquired")
            busy_held = s.status()["engines"]["sqlite"]["busy"]
            rel.set()
            t.join()
            need(busy_held is True, "busy must be True while lock held elsewhere")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_reset_engines_rebuilds():
        # Reset swaps in fresh engines and rebuilds loaded tables from the
        # manifest (recovery without restarting the app).
        import time as _t
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            s.load_file(CSV, destination="sqlite", base_name="data")
            s.record_load("file", CSV, destination="sqlite", base_name="data")
            need(any("data" in n for n in s.db.table_columns), "precondition")
            old_db = s.db
            r = s.reset_engines()
            need(r["ok"] and "sqlite" in r["reset"], "reset result")
            need(s.db is not old_db, "SQLite engine must be a fresh instance")
            for _ in range(80):
                if not s.restoring and list(s.db.table_columns):
                    break
                _t.sleep(0.05)
            need(any("data" in n for n in s.db.table_columns),
                 "reset must rebuild the table from the manifest")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_restore_yields_to_user_ops():
        # restore must defer to a real user op, but ignore its own restore-kind
        # ops, and be bounded so a long user op can't starve it forever.
        import time as _t
        from samql_core import progress as P
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            P.reset_for_tests()
            P.begin("restore", target="own")        # its own work: ignore
            t0 = _t.time()
            s._restore_wait_if_busy(poll=0.02, max_wait=1.0)
            need(_t.time() - t0 < 0.2, "must not wait on its own restore op")
            P.reset_for_tests()
            P.begin("query", target="user")          # a real user op: yield
            t0 = _t.time()
            s._restore_wait_if_busy(poll=0.05, max_wait=0.3)
            dt = _t.time() - t0
            need(0.25 <= dt < 1.0, f"must wait (bounded) for user op, dt={dt}")
        finally:
            P.reset_for_tests()
            s.shutdown()

    def t_get_duckdb_synchronized():
        # #6: concurrent first-ops must build exactly one DuckDB manager (the
        # double-checked lock), so two connections/temp files aren't opened.
        import threading as _th
        import samql_core.session as SS
        s = _fresh_session()
        made = {"n": 0}

        class _FakeDuck:
            ENGINE_KIND = "duckdb"

            def __init__(self, **kw):
                made["n"] += 1
                time.sleep(0.05)        # widen the race window

            def interrupt(self):
                pass
        orig_has, orig_cls = SS.HAS_DUCKDB, SS.DuckDBManager
        SS.HAS_DUCKDB, SS.DuckDBManager = True, _FakeDuck
        try:
            outs = []
            ts = [_th.Thread(target=lambda: outs.append(s.get_duckdb()))
                  for _ in range(8)]
            for t in ts:
                t.start()
            for t in ts:
                t.join()
            eq(made["n"], 1, "exactly one DuckDB manager under concurrency")
            need(all(o is outs[0] for o in outs), "all callers share it")
        finally:
            s.duckdb = None             # detach fake before real shutdown
            SS.HAS_DUCKDB, SS.DuckDBManager = orig_has, orig_cls
            s.shutdown()

    def t_connect_timeout_helper():
        # #5: bound only the connect. A wedged connect returns None (we don't
        # block on the worker); a fast one returns the conn; an error re-raises.
        from samql_core.engines import _connect_with_timeout

        def slow(_p):
            time.sleep(2.0)
            return "conn"

        def fast(_p):
            return "conn"

        def boom(_p):
            raise RuntimeError("nope")
        t0 = time.time()
        need(_connect_with_timeout(slow, "x", 0.2) is None,
             "wedged connect must time out to None")
        need(time.time() - t0 < 1.0, "must not block on the wedged worker")
        eq(_connect_with_timeout(fast, "x", 1.0), "conn", "fast connect")
        try:
            _connect_with_timeout(boom, "x", 1.0)
            need(False, "connect error should re-raise")
        except RuntimeError:
            pass

    def t_cancel_interrupts_engine():
        # #2: cancel must reach engine.interrupt() so a stuck single statement
        # can be broken (not just stopped between batches).
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            hit = {"n": 0}

            class _Eng:
                ENGINE_KIND = "duckdb"

                def interrupt(self):
                    hit["n"] += 1
            s._register_run("q-cancel", _Eng(), kind="query", target="t")
            res = s.cancel_query("q-cancel")
            need(res.get("cancelled") is True, "cancel should report cancelled")
            eq(hit["n"], 1, "cancel must call engine.interrupt()")
            s._unregister_run("q-cancel")
            # an unknown id still interrupts engines + reports cancelled
            # (Stop cancels everything, registered or not)
            need(s.cancel_query("nope").get("cancelled") is True,
                 "Stop interrupts engines + reports cancelled for any id")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_infer_affinity_native_numbers():
        # Native numbers (JSON numbers, or grid cells already coerced to
        # int/float) are typed numeric regardless of the column name, so a
        # strict engine (DuckDB) can do arithmetic on them. String digit-runs
        # (CSV) stay conservative to preserve identifiers / leading zeros.
        from samql_core.inference import infer_affinity
        eq(infer_affinity("col1", [1, 1]), "INTEGER", "native ints -> INTEGER")
        eq(infer_affinity("col2", [1.5, 2.0]), "REAL", "native floats -> REAL")
        eq(infer_affinity("id", [1, 2, 3]), "INTEGER",
           "a native-int id is still a number")
        eq(infer_affinity("col1", [1, "x"]), "", "mixed int+text -> text")
        eq(infer_affinity("flag", [True, False]), "", "bools -> text")
        eq(infer_affinity("big", [10 ** 20]), "",
           "too-wide int -> text (lossless)")
        # CSV string behaviour unchanged
        eq(infer_affinity("col1", ["1", "2"]), "",
           "string digits (generic name) stay text")
        eq(infer_affinity("amount", ["1", "2"]), "INTEGER",
           "string digits with a measure name -> INTEGER (unchanged)")
        eq(infer_affinity("amount", ["007"]), "",
           "leading zero preserved as text")

    def t_createtable_numeric_columns_typed():
        # A grid table of whole numbers must create *numeric* columns, not text
        # -- otherwise a downstream formula (col1 + 1) can't bind on a strict
        # engine (DuckDB: BinderException on VARCHAR arithmetic). Verify the
        # declared SQLite column type is numeric and that arithmetic computes.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            res = s.create_table_from_grid(
                "grid_nums", ["col1", "col2"], [["1", "1"], ["2", "3"]],
                destination="sqlite")
            need(res.get("ok"), "createtable failed: %s" % res.get("error"))
            t = res["table"]
            info = s.db.conn.execute('PRAGMA table_info("%s")' % t).fetchall()
            types = {row[1]: (row[2] or "").upper() for row in info}
            need("INT" in types.get("col1", ""),
                 "col1 must be an integer column, got %r" % types.get("col1"))
            need("INT" in types.get("col2", ""),
                 "col2 must be an integer column, got %r" % types.get("col2"))
            cols, rows = s.db.execute(
                'SELECT col1 + 1 AS c FROM "%s" ORDER BY col1' % t)
            eq([r[0] for r in rows], [2, 3],
               "col1 + 1 must compute numerically")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_explain_node_error_type_hint():
        # The explainer names the node and, for a type/cast mismatch, says how
        # to fix it; an unrelated error gets named but no cast hint.
        from samql_core import nodeflow as nf
        node = {"type": "formula", "config": {"label": "net"}}
        msg = nf.explain_node_error(
            node, "BinderException: No function matches the given name and "
            "argument types '(VARCHAR, INTEGER_LITERAL)'")
        need('formula node "net"' in msg, "names the node + label")
        need("type mismatch" in msg.lower(), "explains the type problem")
        need("cast" in msg.lower(), "suggests a cast")
        plain = nf.explain_node_error({"type": "sort"}, "disk is full")
        need("sort node" in plain, "names the node")
        need("cast" not in plain.lower(), "no cast hint for an unrelated error")

    def t_flow_error_names_failing_node():
        # A run error must name the node that actually failed (and carry its
        # id) -- not the run target -- so the UI highlights the real culprit.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            g = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "src", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                    "label": "t", "columns": ["col1"], "rows": [["1"]],
                    "dest": "sqlite"}},
                {"id": "f1", "type": "formula", "config": {
                    "label": "calc",
                    "formulas": [{"name": "bad", "expr": "NOSUCHFN([col1])"}]}},
                {"id": "sel", "type": "select", "config": {
                    "label": "pick",
                    # Keep the bad derived output live. Dead formula outputs
                    # are intentionally eliminated by projection pushdown.
                    "fields": [{"name": "col1", "keep": True},
                               {"name": "bad", "keep": True}]}},
            ], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "src", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "f1", "port": "in"}},
                {"from": {"node": "f1", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "sel", "port": "in"}},
            ]}
            # run the downstream select; the failure is in the upstream formula
            r = s.run_nodeflow(g, "sel", "out")
            need(r.get("error"), "expected a run error")
            eq(r.get("node"), "f1",
               "error must name the failing formula, not the run target")
            need("formula node" in r["error"], "message names the node type")
            need("calc" in r["error"], "message includes the node label")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_lineage_cast_passthrough_rename_tracked():
        # Lineage: a cast that only changes type is NOT a data change (it passes
        # through), but a rename IS a change we still want to see.
        from samql_core import lineage as _lin
        g = {"nodes": [
            {"id": "src", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "F", "columns": ["col1", "col2"],
                "rows": [["1", "2"]], "dest": "sqlite"}},
            {"id": "sel", "type": "select", "config": {"label": "pick",
             "fields": [
                 {"name": "col1", "type": "integer", "keep": True},   # cast
                 {"name": "col2", "rename": "col2x", "keep": True},   # rename
             ]}},
            {"id": "out", "type": "output", "config": {"label": "out"}},
        ], "edges": [
            {"from": {"node": "src", "port": "out"},
             "to": {"node": "sel", "port": "in"}},
            {"from": {"node": "sel", "port": "out"},
             "to": {"node": "out", "port": "in"}},
        ]}
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            data = _lin.build_field_lineage(s, g)
            pt = {r["data_element"] for r in data["passthrough"]}
            der = {r["data_element"] for r in data["derived"]}
            need("col1" in pt, "cast-only column should pass through")
            need("col1" not in der, "cast-only column must not be a derived hop")
            need("col2x" in der, "renamed column should be a tracked change")
            steps = {r["used_in"]: r["step"] for r in data["derived"]}
            need("rename" in (steps.get("col2x") or "").lower(),
                 "rename hop should be labelled rename, not cast")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_column_lineage_transform_depth():
        # Per-column diagram lineage: each stage exposes inputs → op → output,
        # plus filter/join/summarize/cast specifics from node cfg.
        from samql_core import lineage as _lin

        def edge(a, b, ap="out", bp="in"):
            return {"from": {"node": a, "port": ap},
                    "to": {"node": b, "port": bp}}

        g = {"nodes": [
            {"id": "src", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                "label": "Orders", "columns": ["region", "amount", "qty"],
                "rows": [["east", "10", "2"]], "dest": "sqlite"}},
            {"id": "flt", "type": "filter", "config": {
                "label": "keep east",
                "condition": "[region] = 'east'"}},
            {"id": "sel", "type": "select", "config": {"label": "cast amt",
             "fields": [
                 {"name": "region", "keep": True},
                 {"name": "amount", "type": "integer", "keep": True},
                 {"name": "qty", "keep": True},
             ]}},
            {"id": "agg", "type": "summarize", "config": {
                "label": "totals",
                "group_by": ["region"],
                "aggs": [{"col": "amount", "func": "sum",
                          "name": "sum_amount"}]}},
            {"id": "out", "type": "output", "config": {"label": "out"}},
        ], "edges": [
            edge("src", "flt"), edge("flt", "sel"),
            edge("sel", "agg"), edge("agg", "out"),
        ]}

        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            r = _lin.build_column_lineage(s, g, "sum_amount")
            need(r.get("available"), "sum_amount lineage available: %r" % r)
            stages = r.get("stages") or []
            need(len(stages) >= 2, "expected multiple stages: %r" % stages)
            by_type = {st.get("node_type"): st for st in stages}
            # summarize stage
            agg = by_type.get("summarize") or stages[-1]
            ch = agg.get("change") or {}
            need(ch.get("transform"), "summarize transform line: %r" % ch)
            need("→" in (ch.get("transform") or ""),
                 "transform is inputs → op → output: %r" % ch.get("transform"))
            need((ch.get("op") or "").lower() in ("sum", "agg"),
                 "op names the aggregate: %r" % ch.get("op"))
            need(ch.get("group_by") == ["region"],
                 "group_by from cfg: %r" % ch.get("group_by"))
            need("amount" in (ch.get("inputs") or []),
                 "inputs include amount: %r" % ch.get("inputs"))
            need(ch.get("output") == "sum_amount",
                 "output is sum_amount: %r" % ch.get("output"))

            # Direct unit: _describe_change on the select node for cast.
            sel_node = [n for n in g["nodes"] if n["id"] == "sel"][0]
            rec = {"kind": "passthrough", "srcs": [("flt", "out", "amount")]}
            ch_cast = _lin._describe_change(sel_node, rec, "amount")
            need(ch_cast.get("type_to") == "integer",
                 "cast type_to: %r" % ch_cast)
            need("CAST" in (ch_cast.get("transform") or "").upper()
                 or (ch_cast.get("op") or "") == "cast",
                 "cast transform/op: %r" % ch_cast)

            flt_node = [n for n in g["nodes"] if n["id"] == "flt"][0]
            ch_flt = _lin._describe_change(
                flt_node,
                {"kind": "passthrough", "srcs": [("src", "out", "amount")]},
                "amount")
            need(ch_flt.get("predicate"), "filter predicate: %r" % ch_flt)
            need("filter" in (ch_flt.get("op") or ""),
                 "filter op: %r" % ch_flt.get("op"))
            need("→" in (ch_flt.get("transform") or ""),
                 "filter transform: %r" % ch_flt.get("transform"))

            # join specifics
            gj = {"nodes": [
                {"id": "l", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                    "label": "L", "columns": ["id", "v"],
                    "rows": [["1", "a"]], "dest": "sqlite"}},
                {"id": "r", "type": "createtable", "config": {
                    "label": "R", "columns": ["id", "w"],
                    "rows": [["1", "b"]], "dest": "sqlite"}},
                {"id": "j", "type": "join", "config": {
                    "label": "J", "how": "inner",
                    "keys": [{"left": "id", "right": "id"}]}},
                {"id": "o", "type": "output", "config": {"label": "o"}},
            ], "edges": [
                {"from": {"node": "l", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "j", "port": "left"}},
                {"from": {"node": "r", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "j", "port": "right"}},
                {"from": {"node": "j", "port": "out"},
                 "to": {"node": "o", "port": "in"}},
            ]}
            rj = _lin.build_column_lineage(s, gj, "v")
            need(rj.get("available"), "join lineage available: %r" % rj)
            jstages = [st for st in (rj.get("stages") or [])
                       if st.get("node_type") == "join"]
            need(jstages, "join stage present: %r" % rj.get("stages"))
            jch = jstages[0].get("change") or {}
            need(jch.get("join_how") == "inner",
                 "join_how: %r" % jch.get("join_how"))
            need(jch.get("predicate"), "join predicate: %r" % jch)
            need("→" in (jch.get("transform") or ""),
                 "join transform: %r" % jch.get("transform"))
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_loaders_auto_resolves_to_default_engine():
        # loaders.load_file must honour destination="auto" by resolving it to
        # the session's default engine (DuckDB when available), not silently
        # fall to SQLite -- this is what the appendfolder / directory readers
        # pass, so a folder load lands in DuckDB by default.
        from samql_core import loaders
        import tempfile as _tf
        import os as _os
        seen = []

        class FakeSession:
            def default_destination(self):
                seen.append("asked")
                return "duckdb"

            def get_duckdb(self):
                raise RuntimeError("DUCK_BRANCH")

            @property
            def db(self):
                raise RuntimeError("SQLITE_BRANCH")

        p = _os.path.join(_tf.mkdtemp(), "x.csv")
        open(p, "w").write("a,b\n1,2\n")
        try:
            loaders.load_file(FakeSession(), p, destination="auto")
            need(False, "expected the duckdb branch to be taken")
        except RuntimeError as e:
            need("DUCK_BRANCH" in str(e),
                 "auto must route to the duckdb branch, not sqlite: %s" % e)
        eq(seen, ["asked"], "default_destination must be consulted for 'auto'")

    def t_duckdb_load_interrupt_aborts_no_retry():
        # A cancel during a DuckDB native read must ABORT -- not fall through to
        # the tolerant reader and finish the load the user stopped (the
        # "Cancelling..." that never cancels). DuckDB isn't available here, so
        # drive the loader's retry loop directly with a fake connection.
        from samql_core import engines
        import threading as _th

        class FakeCur:
            description = [("a",)]

        class FakeMgr:
            def __init__(self, conn):
                self.write_lock = _th.RLock()
                self.table_columns = {}
                self.table_sources = {}
                self._conn = conn
                self._cancel = _th.Event()
                self._reserved_names = set()
                self._applied_resource_memory_mb = 2048
                self.concurrent_reads = False
                self._native_ops = {}
                self._native_ops_lock = _th.Lock()

            reserve_table_name = (
                __import__("samql_core.engines", fromlist=["x"])
                .DuckDBManager.reserve_table_name)
            release_table_name = (
                __import__("samql_core.engines", fromlist=["x"])
                .DuckDBManager.release_table_name)
            _unique_name = (
                __import__("samql_core.engines", fromlist=["x"])
                .DuckDBManager._unique_name)

            def _types_cache_drop(self, name=None):
                pass

            @property
            def conn(self):
                return self._conn

            def _unique_name(self, n):
                return n

        # (1) interrupt on the first read -> re-raise, exactly one CREATE
        creates = [0]

        class InterruptConn:
            def execute(self, sql):
                if sql.startswith("CREATE TABLE"):
                    creates[0] += 1
                    raise RuntimeError("INTERRUPT Error: interrupted by user")
                return None

        try:
            engines.DuckDBManager.create_table_from_file(
                FakeMgr(InterruptConn()), "t", "/big.csv", "csv")
            need(False, "interrupt must propagate, not be swallowed")
        except RuntimeError as e:
            need("interrupt" in str(e).lower(), "the interrupt propagates")
        eq(creates[0], 1, "must NOT retry the tolerant reader after a cancel")

        # (2) a genuine parse error DOES fall through to the tolerant reader
        creates2 = [0]

        class ParseConn:
            def execute(self, sql):
                if sql.startswith("CREATE TABLE"):
                    creates2[0] += 1
                    if creates2[0] == 1:
                        raise RuntimeError("Conversion Error: malformed row")
                    return None
                if sql.startswith("SELECT"):
                    return FakeCur()
                return None

        out = engines.DuckDBManager.create_table_from_file(
            FakeMgr(ParseConn()), "t", "/messy.csv", "csv")
        eq(out, "t", "a parse error retries the tolerant reader and succeeds")
        eq(creates2[0], 2, "tolerant fallback still used for real parse errors")

    def t_folder_load_registers_operation():
        # The append-from-folder load must register a progress op so the
        # Activity dashboard shows it -- the bug was DuckDB busy but ACTIVE
        # OPERATIONS empty ("nothing running"). We can't watch it mid-flight,
        # so verify it begins/ends a "load" op targeting the folder.
        from samql_core import session as _sess
        import tempfile as _tf
        import os as _os
        folder = _tf.mkdtemp()
        open(_os.path.join(folder, "a.csv"), "w").write("x,y\n1,2\n")
        open(_os.path.join(folder, "b.csv"), "w").write("x,y\n3,4\n")
        opreg = _sess.opreg
        orig_begin, orig_end = opreg.begin, opreg.end
        calls = {"begin": [], "end": 0}

        def spy_begin(kind, target=None, **kw):
            calls["begin"].append((kind, target))
            return orig_begin(kind, target=target, **kw)

        def spy_end(op_id=None):
            calls["end"] += 1
            return orig_end(op_id)

        opreg.begin, opreg.end = spy_begin, spy_end
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            r = s.load_folder_files(folder)
            need(r.get("ok"), "folder load should succeed: %r" % r)
            loads = [t for k, t in calls["begin"] if k == "load"]
            need(loads, "folder load must begin a 'load' op: %r" % calls["begin"])
            need(_os.path.basename(folder) in loads,
                 "the op target should be the folder name: %r" % loads)
            need(calls["end"] >= 1, "the op must be ended (finally)")
        finally:
            opreg.begin, opreg.end = orig_begin, orig_end
            s.shutdown()

    def t_folder_load_cancelable():
        # The appendfolder folder read must be cancelable: its engine is
        # registered under the query id (so cancel_query can interrupt it), a
        # cancel mid-read stops the WHOLE load with a cancelled marker (not
        # swallowed and skipped to the next file -- the bug), and the id is
        # unregistered afterward. Driven without DuckDB by making the per-file
        # load raise an interrupt.
        from samql_core import loaders as _loaders
        import tempfile as _tf
        import os as _os
        folder = _tf.mkdtemp()
        open(_os.path.join(folder, "a.csv"), "w").write("x\n1\n")
        open(_os.path.join(folder, "b.csv"), "w").write("x\n2\n")
        s = _fresh_session()
        orig = _loaders.load_file
        state = {"calls": 0, "registered": None, "cancel": None}

        def boom(session, path, **kw):
            state["calls"] += 1
            with session._running_lock:
                state["registered"] = "qf" in session._running
            # the user hits Cancel mid-read -> cancel_query finds the engine
            state["cancel"] = s.cancel_query("qf")
            raise RuntimeError("INTERRUPT Error: interrupted by user")

        _loaders.load_file = boom
        try:
            r = s.load_folder_files(folder, query_id="qf")
            need(state["registered"],
                 "the load's engine must be registered under the query id")
            need(state["cancel"] and state["cancel"].get("cancelled"),
                 "cancel_query must find + interrupt the load's engine")
            need(r.get("cancelled"),
                 "a cancelled read returns a cancelled marker: %r" % r)
            eq(state["calls"], 1,
               "must stop at the first file, not skip through all of them")
            with s._running_lock:
                need("qf" not in s._running,
                     "the query id must be unregistered after the load")
        finally:
            _loaders.load_file = orig
            s.shutdown()

    def t_cancel_query_interrupts_all_engines():
        # Stop must cancel EVERYTHING: cancel_query interrupts every engine (not
        # just the one registered under the id), so unregistered work -- a
        # folder read, an iterator / while loop -- is stopped too, and it flags
        # the run so a cooperative loop stops between statements.
        s = _fresh_session()
        hit = {"sqlite": 0}
        orig = s.db.interrupt
        s.db.interrupt = lambda: hit.__setitem__("sqlite", hit["sqlite"] + 1)
        try:
            r = s.cancel_query("run-xyz")
            need(r.get("cancelled"), "cancel_query reports cancelled")
            need(hit["sqlite"] == 0,
                 ".411: an UNREGISTERED id touches nothing by default "
                 "(Stop is per-run; other work keeps going)")
            s.cancel_query("run-xyz", scope="all")
            need(hit["sqlite"] >= 1,
                 'scope="all" restores the everything-sweep')
            need(s._run_is_cancelled("run-xyz"),
                 "cancel_query must flag the run for cooperative loop checks")
            need(not s._run_is_cancelled("other"),
                 "only the cancelled id is flagged")
            s._unregister_run("run-xyz")
            need(not s._run_is_cancelled("run-xyz"),
                 "the flag clears when the run unregisters")
        finally:
            s.db.interrupt = orig
            s.shutdown()

    def t_api_fetch_pages_cancel():
        # A paginated API fetch stops between pages when should_cancel turns
        # true -- Stop aborts an in-flight API node fetch.
        from samql_core import apiload
        calls = {"n": 0}

        def fake(url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw):
            calls["n"] += 1
            return (200, "application/json", [{"a": calls["n"]}], "", None)

        raised = False
        try:
            apiload.fetch_all_pages(
                "https://x.test/d", pagination={"kind": "page"},
                fetch=fake, should_cancel=lambda: calls["n"] >= 1,
                max_pages=10)
        except apiload.FetchCancelled:
            raised = True
        need(raised, "fetch_all_pages raises FetchCancelled when cancelled")
        need(calls["n"] <= 1, "cancel stops before fetching more pages")

    def t_api_spool_cancel():
        # A streaming download aborts mid-stream when should_cancel turns true.
        from samql_core import apiload
        import io
        import tempfile as _tf
        import os as _os
        body = io.BytesIO(b"x" * (5 * 1024 * 1024))   # 5 MB -> several chunks
        fd, dest = _tf.mkstemp(prefix="t_spc_")
        _os.close(fd)
        try:
            seen = {"n": 0}

            def should():
                seen["n"] += 1
                return seen["n"] > 1   # allow the first chunk, cancel after

            raised = False
            try:
                apiload.spool_response(body, dest, chunk=1024 * 1024,
                                       should_cancel=should)
            except apiload.FetchCancelled:
                raised = True
            need(raised,
                 "spool_response raises FetchCancelled when cancelled")
        finally:
            try:
                _os.remove(dest)
            except Exception:
                pass

    def t_api_load_cancel():
        # load_api turns a cancellation into a {cancelled} result so
        # fetch_api_node can report it to the UI instead of erroring.
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            from samql_core import apiload

            def fake(url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw):
                return (200, "application/json", [{"a": 1}], "", None)

            res = apiload.load_api(
                s, "https://x.test/d", base_name="c",
                pagination={"kind": "page"}, fetch=fake,
                should_cancel=lambda: True, max_pages=5)
            need(res.get("cancelled"), "load_api reports cancelled")
            need(not res.get("ok"), "a cancelled load is not ok")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_apinode_fetch_cancel():
        # End to end: when the run is flagged cancelled, the API node fetch
        # stops and reports cancelled, and the flag clears on unregister.
        g = {"nodes": [{"id": "api", "type": "apinode", "config": {
            "url": "https://x.test/items",
            "pagination": {"kind": "page"}}}], "edges": []}
        s = Session()
        try:
            calls = {"n": 0}

            def fake(url, auth_user=None, auth_pass=None, headers=None, **kw):
                calls["n"] += 1
                return (200, "application/json", [{"id": calls["n"]}], "", None)

            s._api_fetcher = fake
            s._cancelled_runs.add("api-run")   # Stop already pressed
            r = s.fetch_api_node("api", g["nodes"][0]["config"], graph=g,
                                 query_id="api-run")
            need(r.get("cancelled"), "api fetch reports cancelled")
            need(calls["n"] == 0,
                 "no page is fetched once cancel is already requested")
            need("api-run" not in s._cancelled_runs,
                 "the run flag clears after the fetch unregisters")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_concurrent_reads_env_flag():
        # The flag is read from SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS, default off.
        import os
        from samql_core import engines
        prev = os.environ.get("SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS")
        try:
            os.environ.pop("SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS", None)
            need(engines._env_truthy("SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS") is False,
                 "unset -> default off")
            for v in ("1", "true", "TRUE", "yes", "on", " On "):
                os.environ["SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS"] = v
                need(engines._env_truthy("SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS") is True,
                     "%r is truthy" % v)
            for v in ("0", "", "off", "no", "nope"):
                os.environ["SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS"] = v
                need(engines._env_truthy("SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS") is False,
                     "%r is falsey" % v)
        finally:
            if prev is None:
                os.environ.pop("SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS", None)
            else:
                os.environ["SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS"] = prev

    def t_concurrent_reads_default_on():
        # Concurrent reads default ON so catalog/page peeks stay live during
        # multi-GB COPY. SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS=0 restores full serialization.
        import os
        prev = os.environ.pop("SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS", None)
        try:
            s = _fresh_session()
            try:
                need(s.concurrent_reads_enabled() is True,
                     "concurrent reads default to on (large-load friendly)")
            finally:
                s.shutdown()
        finally:
            if prev is not None:
                os.environ["SAMQL_CONCURRENT_READS"] = prev

    def t_concurrent_reads_session_toggle():
        # set_concurrent_reads flips the runtime preference and status reports it
        # (with DuckDB absent in the sandbox this exercises the pref path).
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            eq(s.set_concurrent_reads(True), True, "setter returns new state")
            need(s.concurrent_reads_enabled() is True, "enabled after on")
            need(s.status().get("concurrent_reads") is True,
                 "status snapshot reflects the flag")
            s.set_concurrent_reads(False)
            need(s.concurrent_reads_enabled() is True,
                 ".426: off clamps to on")
            need(s.status().get("concurrent_reads") is True,
                 ".426: status stays on after an off attempt")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_db_read_method_sqlite():
        # SQLite read() returns the same as execute() (the locked path -- a
        # single connection can't read concurrently with a write).
        import tempfile
        import os as _os
        s = Session()
        try:
            p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
            open(p, "w").write("a,b\n1,x\n2,y\n3,z\n")
            s.load_file(p, destination="sqlite")
            name = s.tables_tree()[0]["name"]
            sql = 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % name
            eq(s.db.read(sql)[1][0][0], s.db.execute(sql)[1][0][0],
               "DBManager.read matches execute")
            eq(Session._safe_count(s.db, name), 3, "_safe_count via read")
            try:
                _os.remove(p)
            except Exception:
                pass
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_safe_count_routing_and_fallback():
        # _safe_count prefers engine.read() and falls back to execute().
        class Reader:
            def __init__(self):
                self.r = 0
                self.e = 0

            def read(self, sql):
                self.r += 1
                return ["c"], [(5,)]

            def execute(self, sql):
                self.e += 1
                return ["c"], [(9,)]
        a = Reader()
        eq(Session._safe_count(a, "t"), 5, "uses read() when present")
        eq((a.r, a.e), (1, 0), "execute untouched when read works")

        class FailRead(Reader):
            def read(self, sql):
                raise RuntimeError("temp not visible on a fresh cursor")
        b = FailRead()
        eq(Session._safe_count(b, "t"), 9, "falls back to execute on read error")
        eq(b.e, 1, "fallback used the serialized execute()")

        class NoRead:
            def __init__(self):
                self.e = 0

            def execute(self, sql):
                self.e += 1
                return ["c"], [(7,)]
        c = NoRead()
        eq(Session._safe_count(c, "t"), 7, "engine without read() uses execute")

        class Broken:
            def read(self, sql):
                raise RuntimeError("x")

            def execute(self, sql):
                raise RuntimeError("y")
        eq(Session._safe_count(Broken(), "t"), None,
           "both paths failing -> None, no crash")

    def t_duck_read_dispatch_unbound():
        # Exercise the REAL DuckDBManager.read() dispatch + fallback without a
        # live DuckDB connection, by binding the method to a stub self.
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager

        class Stub:
            def __init__(self, on):
                self.concurrent_reads = on
                self.calls = []

            def execute_read(self, sql):
                self.calls.append("read")
                return ["c"], [(1,)]

            def execute(self, sql):
                self.calls.append("exec")
                return ["c"], [(2,)]
        on = Stub(True)
        eq(DuckDBManager.read(on, "SELECT 1")[1], [(1,)],
           "flag on -> concurrent cursor (execute_read)")
        eq(on.calls, ["read"], "flag on did not take the locked path")
        off = Stub(False)
        eq(DuckDBManager.read(off, "SELECT 1")[1], [(2,)],
           "flag off -> serialized execute")
        eq(off.calls, ["exec"], "flag off did not open a concurrent cursor")

        class FailReader(Stub):
            def execute_read(self, sql):
                self.calls.append("read")
                raise RuntimeError("temp")
        fr = FailReader(True)
        eq(DuckDBManager.read(fr, "SELECT 1")[1], [(2,)],
           "a failed concurrent read falls back to execute")
        eq(fr.calls, ["read", "exec"], "tried concurrent, then fell back")

    def t_duck_column_types_concurrent_unbound():
        # The concurrent branch of column_types (now in the raw helper) maps
        # DESCRIBE rows from a separate cursor; verify via the REAL method.
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager

        class Stub:
            concurrent_reads = True

            def execute_read(self, sql):
                need('DESCRIBE "t"' in sql, "describes the requested table")
                return (["column_name", "column_type"],
                        [("id", "BIGINT"), ("name", "VARCHAR")])
        st = Stub()
        st._column_types_raw = DuckDBManager._column_types_raw.__get__(
            st, DuckDBManager)
        eq(DuckDBManager.column_types(st, "t"),
           {"id": "BIGINT", "name": "VARCHAR"},
           "column_types maps DESCRIBE rows on the concurrent path")

        class FailStub:
            concurrent_reads = True

            def execute_read(self, sql):
                raise RuntimeError("temp")
        fs = FailStub()
        fs._column_types_raw = DuckDBManager._column_types_raw.__get__(
            fs, DuckDBManager)
        eq(DuckDBManager.column_types(fs, "t"), {},
           "degrades to {} when the schema can't be read (no real conn)")

    def t_duck_sync_catalog_concurrent_unbound():
        # The concurrent reconcile reads information_schema (+ columns) and
        # selective DESCRIBE on separate cursors, then updates under
        # _catalog_lock. Verify the REAL method: live tables added, vanished
        # ones dropped; unchanged tables with warm types skip DESCRIBE.
        import threading as _th
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager

        class Stub:
            concurrent_reads = True

            def __init__(self):
                self.table_columns = {"gone": ["x"], "keep": ["old"]}
                self.table_sources = {"gone": "", "keep": ""}
                self.table_origins = {"gone": "/tmp/gone.json",
                                      "keep": "/tmp/keep.json"}
                self._catalog_lock = _th.Lock()
                self._types_cache = {}
                self.describe_calls = []

            def _types_cache_drop(self, name=None):
                if name is None:
                    self._types_cache.clear()
                else:
                    self._types_cache.pop(name, None)

            def execute_read(self, sql):
                if "information_schema.tables" in sql:
                    return ["table_name"], [("keep",), ("new",)]
                if "information_schema.columns" in sql:
                    return ["table_name", "column_name"], [
                        ("keep", "k1"),
                        ("new", "n1"),
                        ("new", "n2"),
                    ]
                need("DESCRIBE" in sql, "unexpected catalog SQL: %r" % sql)
                tbl = sql.split('"')[1]
                self.describe_calls.append(tbl)
                cols = {"keep": [("k1", "BIGINT")],
                        "new": [("n1", "VARCHAR"), ("n2", "BIGINT")]}[tbl]
                return ["column_name", "column_type"], cols
        st = Stub()
        DuckDBManager.sync_catalog(st)
        eq(sorted(st.table_columns), ["keep", "new"],
           "reconciles to the live set (vanished table dropped)")
        eq(st.table_columns["new"], ["n1", "n2"],
           "new table columns come from DESCRIBE")
        eq(st.table_columns["keep"], ["k1"], "existing columns refreshed")
        need("gone" not in st.table_columns
             and "gone" not in st.table_sources
             and "gone" not in st.table_origins,
             "a table no longer present is removed from columns/sources/origins")
        need("new" in st.table_sources, "the new table gets a source entry")
        need("keep" in st.table_origins,
             "surviving tables keep their origin path")
        eq(sorted(st.describe_calls), ["keep", "new"],
           "first sync DESCRIBEs tables whose shape is new/changed")
        eq(st._types_cache.get("keep"), {"k1": "BIGINT"},
           "sync seeds types cache from DESCRIBE")
        # Second sync: shapes unchanged + warm types -> no DESCRIBE.
        st.describe_calls.clear()
        DuckDBManager.sync_catalog(st)
        eq(st.describe_calls, [],
           "unchanged catalog skips DESCRIBE on refresh")

    def t_concurrent_reads_source_guards():
        # Structural guarantees on the concurrent-read implementation.
        import inspect
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager
        er = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager.execute_read)
        need(".cursor()" in er, "execute_read uses a separate cursor")
        need("with self.write_lock" not in er,
             "execute_read does NOT acquire write_lock (so it runs "
             "concurrently with a build on the main connection)")
        rd = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager.read)
        need("concurrent_reads" in rd and "execute_read" in rd
             and "self.execute(" in rd,
             "read() dispatches on the flag and falls back to execute()")
        sc = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager.sync_catalog)
        # .464 repoint: the flag-off branch was rewritten to the same
        # non-blocking rule as the sqlite twin -- probe the lock, serve
        # the cached catalog when busy, release in finally. Pin THAT.
        need("self.write_lock.acquire(blocking=False)" in sc
             and "self.write_lock.release()" in sc,
             "sync_catalog's flag-off path probes without parking and "
             "releases in finally")
        # Incremental sync (656+): concurrent work lives in _duck_sync_catalog
        # (use_read=True → execute_read), then reconciles under _catalog_lock.
        need("_duck_sync_catalog" in sc and "use_read=True" in sc,
             "sync_catalog concurrent path delegates to _duck_sync_catalog")
        dsc = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager._duck_sync_catalog)
        need("_catalog_lock" in dsc and "use_read" in dsc,
             "incremental duck sync reconciles under the catalog lock")
        fetch = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager._duck_fetch_catalog_lists)
        need("execute_read" in fetch,
             "catalog list fetch uses execute_read on the concurrent path")
        ct = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager._column_types_raw)
        need('hasattr(self, "execute_read")' in ct and "execute_read(" in ct,
             "schema reads try a separate cursor UNCONDITIONALLY (never queue "
             "behind a build), falling back to the locked connection")
        ini = inspect.getsource(DuckDBManager.__init__)
        need("_catalog_lock" in ini and "concurrent_reads" in ini,
             "the manager initializes the catalog lock and the flag")

    def t_tables_tree_correct_with_flag_sqlite():
        # End to end: toggling the flag never changes correctness on SQLite
        # (single connection -> read() is the locked execute()).
        import tempfile
        import os as _os
        s = Session()
        try:
            p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
            open(p, "w").write("id,name\n1,a\n2,b\n3,c\n4,d\n")
            s.load_file(p, destination="sqlite")
            name = s.tables_tree()[0]["name"]
            for flag in (False, True, False):
                s.set_concurrent_reads(flag)
                row = [t for t in s.tables_tree() if t["name"] == name][0]
                eq(row["row_count"], 4, "row count correct (flag=%s)" % flag)
                eq([c["name"] for c in row["columns"]], ["id", "name"],
                   "columns correct (flag=%s)" % flag)
            try:
                _os.remove(p)
            except Exception:
                pass
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_concurrent_reads_real_duckdb():
        # When DuckDB is present, verify the concurrent read path is
        # functionally correct end to end (count + schema + tables_tree match
        # the serialized path). Dormant in the sandbox (no DuckDB), where the
        # concurrency is reasoned about and validated on the real build.
        from samql_core.engines import HAS_DUCKDB
        if not HAS_DUCKDB:
            return
        import tempfile
        import os as _os
        s = Session()
        try:
            p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".csv")
            open(p, "w").write("id,name\n1,a\n2,b\n3,c\n")
            s.load_file(p, destination="duckdb")
            duck = s.get_duckdb()
            name = [n for n in duck.table_columns
                    if not n.startswith("__")][0]
            sql = 'SELECT COUNT(*) FROM "%s"' % name
            base = duck.execute(sql)[1][0][0]
            duck.concurrent_reads = True
            eq(duck.read(sql)[1][0][0], base, "concurrent count matches")
            eq(duck.execute_read(sql)[1][0][0], base,
               "execute_read returns the same count")
            need(set(duck.column_types(name))
                 == set(duck.table_columns[name]),
                 "concurrent column_types matches the columns")
            s.set_concurrent_reads(True)
            row = [t for t in s.tables_tree()
                   if t["name"] == name and t["engine"] == "duckdb"][0]
            eq(row["row_count"], base,
               "tables_tree count matches under the flag")
            try:
                _os.remove(p)
            except Exception:
                pass
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_concurrent_reads_nonblocking_under_lock():
        # THE async property: with the flag ON a read returns while a build
        # holds write_lock; with it OFF the same read serializes behind the
        # lock. This is decided by the lock, not the engine, so it runs without
        # DuckDB -- it drives the REAL DuckDBManager.read() dispatch against a
        # stub that models the two paths faithfully (execute_read is lock-free,
        # like the real one per the structure guard; execute takes write_lock,
        # like the real one). A generous lock timeout keeps it from raising
        # EngineBusy during the short hold.
