        import threading as _th
        from samql_core.engines import DuckDBManager, _DeadlineRLock

        class LockStub:
            def __init__(self, concurrent):
                self.concurrent_reads = concurrent
                self.write_lock = _DeadlineRLock(timeout=30.0)

            def execute_read(self, sql):       # concurrent path: never locks
                return ["c"], [(1,)]

            def execute(self, sql):            # serialized path: takes the lock
                with self.write_lock:
                    return ["c"], [(2,)]

        # ---- flag ON: read comes back while the lock is held ----
        on = LockStub(True)
        on.write_lock.acquire()                 # simulate a build holding it
        try:
            done, box = _th.Event(), {}

            def do_on():
                box["res"] = DuckDBManager.read(on, "SELECT 1")
                done.set()
            t = _th.Thread(target=do_on, daemon=True)
            t.start()
            need(done.wait(3.0),
                 "flag ON: a read must return while a build holds write_lock "
                 "(it never queues behind the lock)")
            eq(box["res"][1], [(1,)], "flag ON used the concurrent cursor")
            t.join(1.0)
        finally:
            on.write_lock.release()

        # ---- flag OFF: the same read blocks until the lock is released ----
        off = LockStub(False)
        off.write_lock.acquire()
        done, box = _th.Event(), {}

        def do_off():
            box["res"] = DuckDBManager.read(off, "SELECT 1")
            done.set()
        t = _th.Thread(target=do_off, daemon=True)
        t.start()
        try:
            need(not done.wait(0.5),
                 "flag OFF: a read must block while write_lock is held "
                 "(it serializes behind the build)")
        finally:
            off.write_lock.release()
        need(done.wait(3.0),
             "flag OFF: the read completes once the lock is released")
        eq(box["res"][1], [(2,)], "flag OFF used the serialized execute path")
        t.join(1.0)

    def t_hdfs_url_and_dates():
        from samql_core import hdfs
        # URL normalisation -> (base ending at /webhdfs/v1, start path)
        eq(hdfs.parse_webhdfs_url("https://knox:8443/gateway/default/webhdfs/v1/output"),
           ("https://knox:8443/gateway/default/webhdfs/v1", "/output"),
           "marker URL splits at /webhdfs/v1")
        eq(hdfs.parse_webhdfs_url("http://nn:9870/explorer.html#/output/x"),
           ("http://nn:9870/webhdfs/v1", "/output/x"),
           "explorer.html URL -> webhdfs base + fragment path")
        eq(hdfs.parse_webhdfs_url("nn:14000"),
           ("http://nn:14000/webhdfs/v1", "/"),
           "bare host[:port] assumes the standard mount at root")
        try:
            hdfs.parse_webhdfs_url("   ")
            need(False, "empty URL should raise")
        except ValueError:
            pass
    class _FakeFS:
        """Duck-typed WebHDFS client backed by an in-memory directory map."""
        def __init__(self, fs):
            self.fs = fs
        def list_dir(self, path):
            return self.fs.get(path, [])

    def _D(name):
        return {"pathSuffix": name, "type": "DIRECTORY"}

    def _F(name):
        return {"pathSuffix": name, "type": "FILE"}

    def _sample_fs():
        # output/<date>/<feed>/<file>.csv ; compact date folders ; a _tmp to skip ;
        # a feed (txns) that exists on only one date ; two DISTINCT files in one feed.
        return _FakeFS({
            "/output": [_D("20260601"), _D("20260605"), _D("_tmp")],
            "/output/20260601": [_D("creditcardsplit"), _D("txns")],
            "/output/20260605": [_D("creditcardsplit")],
            "/output/20260601/creditcardsplit": [_F("creditcard.csv"), _F("chargeback.csv")],
            "/output/20260605/creditcardsplit": [_F("creditcard.csv"), _F("chargeback.csv")],
            "/output/20260601/txns": [_F("txns.csv")],
        })

    def t_hdfs_client_requests():
        from samql_core import hdfs

        class _Resp:
            def __init__(self, body, ctype="application/json"):
                self._b = body.encode() if isinstance(body, str) else body
                self.headers = {"Content-Type": ctype}
            def read(self):
                return self._b
            def __enter__(self):
                return self
            def __exit__(self, *a):
                return False

        seen = {}

        def make_opener(resp):
            def _open(req, timeout):
                seen["url"] = req.full_url
                seen["timeout"] = timeout
                return resp
            return _open

        # build_url: op + user.name + range params, path percent-encoded
        c = hdfs.WebHDFSClient("http://nn:14000/webhdfs/v1", user="slauri2")
        url = c.build_url("/output/a b", "OPEN", offset=1024, length=4096)
        need("op=OPEN" in url and "user.name=slauri2" in url, "op + user.name present")
        need("offset=1024" in url and "length=4096" in url, "byte-range params present")
        need("a%20b" in url or "a+b" in url, "path is url-encoded")
        # None-valued extras are dropped (no naked offset= when not ranging)
        need("offset" not in c.build_url("/p", "OPEN"), "no range -> no offset param")
        # user omitted -> no user.name
        need("user.name" not in hdfs.WebHDFSClient("http://h/webhdfs/v1").build_url("/p", "LISTSTATUS"),
             "no user -> no user.name param")

        # list_dir parses FileStatuses.FileStatus from a LISTSTATUS reply
        listing = ('{"FileStatuses":{"FileStatus":'
                   '[{"pathSuffix":"20260601","type":"DIRECTORY"},'
                   '{"pathSuffix":"creditcard.csv","type":"FILE"}]}}')
        c2 = hdfs.WebHDFSClient("http://nn/webhdfs/v1", opener=make_opener(_Resp(listing)))
        rows = c2.list_dir("/output")
        eq([r["pathSuffix"] for r in rows], ["20260601", "creditcard.csv"],
           "LISTSTATUS reply parsed to FileStatus list")
        need("op=LISTSTATUS" in seen["url"], "list_dir issues a LISTSTATUS op")
        # a NameNode-UI HTML reply is detected and explained, not JSON-parsed
        c3 = hdfs.WebHDFSClient("http://nn/webhdfs/v1",
                                opener=make_opener(_Resp("<html>NN UI</html>", "text/html")))
        try:
            c3.list_dir("/output")
            need(False, "HTML reply should raise a clear error")
        except ValueError as e:
            need("WebHDFS" in str(e) or "HTML" in str(e), "error explains the URL mistake")
        # open_stream targets OPEN with the range
        c2.open_stream("/output/20260601/x/creditcard.csv", offset=0, length=64)
        need("op=OPEN" in seen["url"] and "length=64" in seen["url"],
             "open_stream issues a ranged OPEN")

    def t_hdfs_connect():
        # hdfs_connect orchestrates: parse the URL -> build a client -> LISTSTATUS
        # the start path -> split entries into sorted folders + files (the
        # 'files' list the picker shows). A malformed URL and an unreachable
        # endpoint both come back as {error}, never a crash. The real client is
        # swapped for a fake so there's no network.
        import samql_core.hdfs as hdfsmod
        s = _fresh_session()
        orig = hdfsmod.WebHDFSClient

        class _FakeClient:
            def __init__(self, base, user=None, **kw):
                self.base, self.user = base, user

            def list_dir(self, path):
                return [
                    {"pathSuffix": "source", "type": "DIRECTORY"},
                    {"pathSuffix": "output", "type": "DIRECTORY"},
                    {"pathSuffix": "readme.txt", "type": "FILE"},
                    {"pathSuffix": "data.csv", "type": "FILE"},
                ]

        class _BoomClient:
            def __init__(self, *a, **k):
                pass

            def list_dir(self, path):
                raise OSError("connection refused")

        try:
            hdfsmod.WebHDFSClient = _FakeClient
            r = s.hdfs_connect("http://nn:9870/webhdfs/v1/output", user="sam")
            need(r.get("ok"), "connect ok: %r" % r)
            eq(r["path"], "/output", "start path taken from the URL")
            eq(r["folders"], ["output", "source"], "folders sorted")
            eq(r["files"], ["data.csv", "readme.txt"],
               "files split out and sorted (the picker's list)")
            hdfsmod.WebHDFSClient = _BoomClient
            rb = s.hdfs_connect("http://nn:9870/webhdfs/v1")
            need(rb.get("error"),
                 "an unreachable endpoint returns {error}, not a crash: %r" % rb)
        finally:
            hdfsmod.WebHDFSClient = orig
        # a malformed URL never reaches the client -> friendly error
        need(s.hdfs_connect("   ").get("error"),
             "an empty/garbage URL is a friendly error")

    def t_hdfs_session_browse():
        # Browse one directory against an injected fake client (no network).
        s = _fresh_session()
        need(s.hdfs_browse("/output").get("error"),
             "browse before connect is an error")
        s._hdfs = _sample_fs()
        br = s.hdfs_browse("/output")
        eq(br.get("dirs"), ["20260601", "20260605", "_tmp"],
           "browse lists child dirs (sorted, raw names)")
        eq(br.get("files"), [], "browse lists files separately (none here)")

    def t_hdfs_load_cancel():
        # The streaming fetch is the cancellation point + progress source for the
        # HDFS load job. (The full job needs DuckDB; here we test the primitive.)
        from samql_core.loaders import LoadCancelled
        import tempfile
        s = _fresh_session()

        class _Resp:
            def __init__(self, chunks):
                self._chunks = list(chunks)
            def read(self, n=-1):
                return self._chunks.pop(0) if self._chunks else b""
            def close(self):
                pass

        class _Client:
            def __init__(self, resp):
                self.resp = resp
            def open_stream(self, path, offset=None, length=None):
                return self.resp

        dst = os.path.join(tempfile.gettempdir(), "hdfs_cancel_test.bin")
        s._hdfs = _Client(_Resp([b"abc", b"de"]))
        seen = []
        n = s._hdfs_fetch_to_file("/p", dst, progress=lambda b: seen.append(b))
        eq(n, 5, "fetch returns the bytes streamed")
        eq(seen, [3, 5], "progress reports cumulative bytes per chunk")
        # progress is offset by base (bytes already streamed by earlier files)
        s._hdfs = _Client(_Resp([b"abc", b"de"]))
        seen2 = []
        s._hdfs_fetch_to_file("/p", dst, base=100,
                              progress=lambda b: seen2.append(b))
        eq(seen2, [103, 105], "progress is offset by base")
        try:
            os.remove(dst)
        except OSError:
            pass
        # cancel() True -> the fetch unwinds with LoadCancelled before reading
        s._hdfs = _Client(_Resp([b"abc", b"de"]))
        try:
            s._hdfs_fetch_to_file("/p2", dst, cancel=lambda: True)
            need(False, "cancel()=True must raise LoadCancelled")
        except LoadCancelled:
            pass
        try:
            os.remove(dst)
        except OSError:
            pass

    def t_hdfs_load_file():
        # Load ONE browsed HDFS file (CSV here, JSON below): stream it to a temp
        # file, then the standard loader dispatches on the extension. mode="view"
        # wants DuckDB; with none available here it falls back to a materialised
        # load (CSV->SQLite, JSON->SQLite flatten) -- so the stream + load wiring
        # is verified end to end and the tables come out queryable.
        s = _fresh_session()
        csv = b"id,name\n1,alice\n2,bob\n3,carol\n"

        class _Resp:
            def __init__(self, data):
                self._data = data

            def read(self, n=-1):
                if n is None or n < 0:
                    d, self._data = self._data, b""
                    return d
                d, self._data = self._data[:n], self._data[n:]
                return d

            def close(self):
                pass

        class _Client:
            def __init__(self, data):
                self.data = data

            def open_stream(self, path, offset=None, length=None):
                return _Resp(self.data)

        s._hdfs = _Client(csv)
        try:
            res = s.hdfs_load_file("/data/people.csv", mode="view")
            need(not res.get("error"),
                 "load returned an error: %r" % res.get("error"))
            tables = res.get("tables") or []
            eq(len(tables), 1, "exactly one table loaded")
            eq(tables[0]["name"], "people", "table named from the file stem")
            names = [t["name"] for t in s.tables_tree()]
            need("people" in names, "loaded table shows in the tree: %r" % names)
            r = s.run_query('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM "people"',
                            target="__local__")
            eq(r["rows"][0][0], 3, "streamed rows are queryable")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
        # JSON loads too (broadened filter): no DuckDB here -> SQLite flatten
        s3 = _fresh_session()
        s3._hdfs = _Client(b'[{"id":1,"name":"a"},{"id":2,"name":"b"}]')
        try:
            res = s3.hdfs_load_file("/data/things.json", mode="view")
            need(not res.get("error"), "json load error: %r" % res.get("error"))
            tables = res.get("tables") or []
            need(tables, "json load produced a table")
            tname = tables[0]["name"]
            r = s3.run_query('SELECT COUNT(*) AS n FROM "%s"' % tname,
                             target="__local__")
            eq(r["rows"][0][0], 2, "json rows are queryable")
        finally:
            s3.shutdown()
        # not connected -> a friendly error, never a crash
        s2 = _fresh_session()
        s2._hdfs = None
        try:
            need(s2.hdfs_load_file("/x.csv").get("error"),
                 "load with no connection is a friendly error")
        finally:
            s2.shutdown()

    def t_hdfs_load_file_cancel():
        # hdfs_load_file WRAPS the streaming fetch: a fired cancel must unwind
        # with LoadCancelled AND delete the temp it created (no leak); a
        # transport error must come back as {error} (not a crash) with the temp
        # cleaned too. Both short-circuit before the loader runs, so no DuckDB
        # is needed. A source-guard also pins the job handler's cancel rollback.
        from samql_core import tmputil
        from samql_core.loaders import LoadCancelled

        class _Resp:
            def read(self, n=-1):
                return b"id\n1\n"

            def close(self):
                pass

        class _OkClient:
            def open_stream(self, path, offset=None, length=None):
                return _Resp()

        class _BoomClient:
            def open_stream(self, path, offset=None, length=None):
                raise OSError("connection reset")

        def hdfs_temps():
            d = tmputil.instance_dir()
            if not os.path.isdir(d):
                return set()
            return set(f for f in os.listdir(d) if f.startswith("hdfs_"))

        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            before = hdfs_temps()
            # (1) cancel mid-fetch -> LoadCancelled, temp removed
            s._hdfs = _OkClient()
            try:
                s.hdfs_load_file("/d/x.csv", cancel=lambda: True)
                need(False, "a fired cancel must raise LoadCancelled")
            except LoadCancelled:
                pass
            eq(sorted(hdfs_temps() - before), [],
               "a cancelled load leaves no temp file behind")
            # (2) transport error -> {error}, not a raise, temp removed
            s._hdfs = _BoomClient()
            res = s.hdfs_load_file("/d/y.csv")
            need(res.get("error"),
                 "a fetch error returns {error}, not a crash: %r" % res)
            eq(sorted(hdfs_temps() - before), [],
               "a failed load leaves no temp file behind")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()
        # the load job still rolls back on cancel (same rail as file loads)
        srv = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "server.py"), encoding="utf-8").read()
        i = srv.find("def hdfs_load_file_start")
        need(i != -1, "hdfs_load_file_start handler exists")
        seg = srv[i:i + 3400]
        need("LoadCancelled" in seg
             and 'job["state"] = "cancelled"' in seg
             and "drop_tables_created_since" in seg,
             "the HDFS load job unwinds a cancel -> cancelled + drops any "
             "tables it created")

    def t_drop_cleans_instance_temp():
        # Dropping a table/view whose source is a SamQL-managed temp (e.g. an
        # HDFS file loaded as a query-in-place view) deletes that temp at once
        # instead of leaking it until the next-start sweep. A user file outside
        # the instance temp dir is left untouched, and odd inputs never raise.
        from samql_core import tmputil
        import tempfile
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            # (a) an instance-dir temp is deleted
            inside = tmputil.new_tempfile("hdfs_", ".csv")
            with open(inside, "w") as f:
                f.write("x\n1\n")
            need(os.path.isfile(inside), "instance temp created")
            s._cleanup_temp_source(inside)
            need(not os.path.exists(inside), "instance-dir source is deleted")
            # (b) a file OUTSIDE the instance dir is preserved
            fd, outside = tempfile.mkstemp(suffix=".csv")
            os.close(fd)
            try:
                s._cleanup_temp_source(outside)
                need(os.path.exists(outside),
                     "a user file outside the instance dir is left alone")
            finally:
                if os.path.exists(outside):
                    os.unlink(outside)
            # (c) odd inputs are safe no-ops
            for bad in (None, "", "/no/such/file.csv", "nodeflow"):
                s._cleanup_temp_source(bad)
            # (d) wiring: drop_table reads the source + cleans an instance temp
            keep = tmputil.new_tempfile("hdfs_", ".csv")
            with open(keep, "w") as f:
                f.write("x\n1\n")
            s.db.conn.execute('CREATE TABLE "vdrop" (x INTEGER)')
            s.db.table_sources["vdrop"] = keep
            r = s.drop_table("sqlite", "vdrop")
            need(r.get("ok"), "drop ok")
            need(not os.path.exists(keep),
                 "dropping a temp-backed table deletes its instance temp")
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_optimize_to_parquet_routing():
        # optimize_to_parquet's gating + re-point + cancel handling, exercised
        # with a fake DuckDB manager so the logic runs without the real engine
        # (the COPY itself is DuckDB-only -- see t_optimize_wiring source-guard
        # and t_optimize_to_parquet_real which runs on the real machine).
        from samql_core import tmputil
        from samql_core.loaders import LoadCancelled
        s = _fresh_session()
        try:
            # no DuckDB -> a clear error, never a crash
            r = s.optimize_to_parquet("anything")
            eq(bool(r.get("error") and "DuckDB" in r["error"]), True,
               "no DuckDB -> needs-DuckDB error")

            def csv_in_instance(txt="a,b\n1,2\n"):
                q = tmputil.new_tempfile("hdfs_", ".csv")
                with open(q, "w") as f:
                    f.write(txt)
                return q

            class FakeDuck:
                def __init__(self, sources):
                    self.table_sources = dict(sources)
                    self.converted = None
                def view_to_parquet(self, name, pq, cancel=None):
                    if cancel and cancel():
                        raise LoadCancelled()
                    open(pq, "wb").close()      # stand in for the real COPY
                    self.converted = (name, pq)
                def drop_table(self, name):
                    self.table_sources.pop(name, None)
                def drop_all(self):
                    self.table_sources.clear()
                def create_view_from_file(self, name, path, kind):
                    self.table_sources[name] = path
                    return name

            # materialized (non-file-backed) table -> still converts: it
            # copies the rows out to Parquet and re-points the view rather than
            # hard-refusing the way it used to.
            s.tables_tree = lambda: [{"name": "t"}]   # skip the real engine walk
            fdm = FakeDuck({"t": "nodeflow"})
            s.duckdb = fdm
            okm = s.optimize_to_parquet("t")
            eq(okm.get("ok"), True,
               "a materialized (non-file) table converts to Parquet")
            need(fdm.table_sources.get("t", "").endswith(".parquet"),
                 "a materialized table is re-pointed at the Parquet file")
            need(bool(fdm.converted), "a materialized table is actually copied")
            # already Parquet -> error
            pqsrc = tmputil.new_tempfile("hdfs_", ".parquet")
            open(pqsrc, "wb").close()
            s.duckdb = FakeDuck({"t": pqsrc})
            need("Parquet" in (s.optimize_to_parquet("t").get("error") or ""),
                 "an already-Parquet table is rejected")
            # unconvertible extension -> error
            xls = tmputil.new_tempfile("hdfs_", ".xlsx")
            open(xls, "wb").close()
            s.duckdb = FakeDuck({"t": xls})
            need("error" in s.optimize_to_parquet("t"),
                 "only csv/tsv/json sources convert")
            # cancel BEFORE any work -> LoadCancelled, original view intact
            src = csv_in_instance()
            fd = FakeDuck({"t": src})
            s.duckdb = fd
            pre = False
            try:
                s.optimize_to_parquet("t", cancel=lambda: True)
            except LoadCancelled:
                pre = True
            need(pre, "a cancel before work raises LoadCancelled")
            need(fd.table_sources.get("t") == src,
                 "a pre-cancel leaves the original view intact")
            need(fd.converted is None, "a pre-cancel does no conversion")
            # success: re-point the view to Parquet + clean the old CSV temp
            src2 = csv_in_instance()
            fd2 = FakeDuck({"t": src2})
            s.duckdb = fd2
            ok = s.optimize_to_parquet("t")
            eq(ok.get("ok"), True, "conversion succeeds")
            need(fd2.table_sources.get("t", "").endswith(".parquet"),
                 "the view is re-pointed at the Parquet file")
            need(not os.path.exists(src2),
                 "the old CSV temp is cleaned up after conversion")
            # interrupted COPY -> partial Parquet removed, original view intact
            class FakeBoom(FakeDuck):
                def view_to_parquet(self, name, pq, cancel=None):
                    self.converted = (name, pq)   # the partial path
                    raise LoadCancelled()
            src3 = csv_in_instance()
            fb = FakeBoom({"t": src3})
            s.duckdb = fb
            boom = False
            try:
                s.optimize_to_parquet("t")
            except LoadCancelled:
                boom = True
            need(boom, "an interrupted conversion propagates the cancel")
            need(bool(fb.converted) and not os.path.exists(fb.converted[1]),
                 "the partial Parquet is deleted when the COPY is interrupted")
            need(fb.table_sources.get("t") == src3,
                 "the original view survives an interrupted conversion")
            s.duckdb = None   # restore so shutdown() doesn't touch the fake
        finally:
            s.shutdown()

    def t_diagnostics_module_and_endpoints():
        # The shared diagnostics registry powers the CLI, the /api/diagnostics
        # endpoints, and the Error log -> Diagnostics tab. Assert: the registry
        # lists the built-in checks; environment + json_load run correctly
        # (json_load on a temp file returns the phase split + tables + write + a
        # cProfile); an unknown name fails gracefully (never raises); the server
        # handlers wrap it; the routes are registered; and a param that would
        # shadow the session argument is dropped rather than crashing.
        import tempfile
        from samql_core import diagnostics as D
        import server
        names = {d["name"] for d in D.list_diagnostics()}
        need({"environment", "json_load"} <= names,
             "registry lists environment + json_load: %r" % names)
        envr = D.run("environment")
        need(envr["ok"] and "version" in envr["result"]
             and "features" in envr["result"], "environment diagnostic runs")

        p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(p, "w").write(
            '[{"a":1,"xs":[{"k":1},{"k":2}]},{"a":2,"xs":[{"k":3}]}]')
        try:
            r = D.run("json_load", None, path=p, max_records=2)
        finally:
            os.unlink(p)
        need(r["ok"], "json_load runs: %r" % r.get("error"))
        res = r["result"]
        for key in ("reader", "read_prod_s", "read_stdlib_s", "flatten_s",
                    "tables", "profile", "write"):
            need(key in res, "json_load result has %r" % key)
        need(any(t["name"].endswith("_xs") for t in res["tables"]),
             "json_load saw the child array table")
        w = res["write"]
        need(w and "seconds" in w and "warm_seconds" in w and "profile" in w,
             "json_load write phase reports cold + warm timing + a cProfile")
        need("fast" in w and "warm_rows_per_s" in w,
             "json_load write verdict is throughput-based (fast + rows/sec)")
        need(w["fast"] is True,
             "a trivially small write is judged fast, not 'slow even warm'")
        # every table is written + timed (not just the largest), with per-table
        # error capture, and the offset window works
        need("per_table" in res and len(res["per_table"]) == res["table_count"]
             and res["table_count"] >= 2,
             "json_load writes EVERY table, not just the largest: %r"
             % [t.get("name") for t in res.get("per_table", [])])
        need(all("seconds" in t or "error" in t for t in res["per_table"]),
             "each per-table write reports timing or an error")
        need(any(t["cols"] >= 3 for t in res["per_table"]),
             "the wide table is among those written")
        import tempfile as _tf
        pw = _tf.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(pw, "w").write('[{"i":0},{"i":1},{"i":2},{"i":3}]')
        try:
            ro = D.run("json_load", None, path=pw, max_records=2, offset=2)
        finally:
            os.unlink(pw)
        need(ro["ok"] and ro["result"]["offset"] == 2
             and ro["result"]["read_prod_n"] == 2,
             "offset skips leading records then samples the window")

        bad = D.run("does_not_exist")
        need(bad["ok"] is False and "Unknown" in bad["error"],
             "an unknown diagnostic fails gracefully (no raise)")

        class _S:
            duckdb = None
            db = None
        got = server.Api.diagnostics(_S(), None, None, None)
        need("diagnostics" in got and "environment" in got,
             "GET /api/diagnostics returns the list + env")
        run_env = server.Api.diagnostics_run(
            _S(), None, {"name": "environment", "params": {}}, None)
        need(run_env["ok"] and "features" in run_env["result"],
             "POST /api/diagnostics/run executes a diagnostic")
        safe = server.Api.diagnostics_run(
            _S(), None,
            {"name": "environment", "params": {"session": "x"}}, None)
        need(safe["ok"], "a 'session' param is dropped, not fatal")
        paths = {rt[1] for rt in server.ROUTES}
        need(r"^/api/diagnostics$" in paths
             and r"^/api/diagnostics/run$" in paths,
             "diagnostics routes are registered")

    def t_json_heaviest_scanner():
        # The find-the-explosion diagnostic: scan records (reading, not
        # flattening) and report the ones with the biggest nested array. A single
        # record with a giant array is what makes a deep-flatten load crawl (it
        # explodes into that many child rows in one add_record); this names the
        # record without paying the flatten, so it stays fast even on the bomb.
        import tempfile
        from samql_core import diagnostics as D
        recs = []
        for i in range(6):
            if i == 3:
                recs.append('{"id":3,"legs":[%s]}'
                            % ",".join('{"k":%d}' % j for j in range(400)))
            else:
                recs.append('{"id":%d,"legs":[{"k":1}]}' % i)
        p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(p, "w").write("[" + ",".join(recs) + "]")
        try:
            r = D.run("json_heaviest", None, path=p, max_records=0, top=5)
        finally:
            os.unlink(p)
        need(r["ok"], "json_heaviest runs: %r" % r.get("error"))
        res = r["result"]
        need(res["scanned"] == 6, "scanned every record")
        need(res["heaviest"] and res["heaviest"][0]["record_index"] == 3
             and res["heaviest"][0]["max_array_len"] == 400,
             "heaviest scan pinpoints the record with the biggest array")
        need("json_heaviest" in {d["name"] for d in D.list_diagnostics()},
             "json_heaviest is registered so the modal lists it")

    def t_full_analysis():
        # The one-shot comprehensive analyzer: whole-file scan (records, biggest
        # array, projected total rows), reader compare, front flatten + per-table
        # write, an auto-profiled flatten of the single heaviest record, a
        # full-load projection, and a named bottleneck. This is the diagnostic
        # meant to replace running the piecemeal checks by hand.
        import tempfile
        from samql_core import diagnostics as D
        recs = []
        for i in range(10):
            if i == 6:
                recs.append('{"id":6,"nm":{"a":1},"legs":[%s]}'
                            % ",".join('{"k":%d}' % j for j in range(2000)))
            else:
                recs.append('{"id":%d,"nm":{"a":1},"legs":[{"k":1},{"k":2}]}' % i)
        p = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=".json")
        open(p, "w").write("[" + ",".join(recs) + "]")
        try:
            r = D.run("full_analysis", None, path=p, sample=10, scan_cap=0)
        finally:
            os.unlink(p)
        need(r["ok"], "full_analysis runs: %r" % r.get("error"))
        res = r["result"]
        need(res["scan"]["records"] == 10, "scan counted every record")
        need(res["scan"]["complete"] is True and "read_mbps" in res["scan"]
             and "est_full_read_s" in res["scan"]
             and "bytes_covered_mb" in res["scan"],
             "scan reports completeness + byte-based read throughput")
        need(res["scan"]["max_array_len"] == 2000,
             "scan found the biggest array across the whole file")
        need(res["scan"]["est_total_rows"] >= 2000,
             "scan projects the total row explosion without flattening")
        need(res["heavy_record"]
             and res["heavy_record"]["record_index"] == 6,
             "the single heaviest record is auto-located and flattened")
        for key in ("est_total_rows", "est_read_s", "est_write_s",
                    "est_total_s"):
            need(key in res["projection"],
                 "projection reports %r" % key)
        need("bottleneck" in res and isinstance(res["verdict"], str)
             and res["verdict"],
             "analysis names a bottleneck + gives a verdict")
        need("full_analysis" in {d["name"] for d in D.list_diagnostics()},
             "full_analysis is registered as a diagnostic")
        src = open(os.path.join(BACKEND, "samql_core", "diagnostics.py"),
                   encoding="utf-8").read()
        need("scan-too-small" in src and "hit_cap" in src,
             "a too-small capped scan is guarded from projecting a fake verdict")
